A Letter to the Librarian.title: A Letter to the Librarian
A Letter to the Librarian.text:
{{BoH_Item |image1=[[File:Letter.generic.png]] |type=[[Readable]], [[Correspondence]] |Location=*[[The Post Office]]}} {{Quote|A letter to me from St Rhonwen's Trust. The Trust's connection with Hush House is probably benevolent, but persistently obscure.}} The Librarian will receive '''A Letter to the Librarian''', alongside a [[Pence|Ten Shilling Note]], after drying the [[Journals|Journal]] and presenting it at the [[Post Office]]. ==== [[Consider]] this: ==== {{Quote|The Letter Reads...

St Rhonwen's Trust wishes to congratulate me on my appointment as Librarian of Hush House. The Trust assures me that it will provide the promised stipend each spring... but reminds me that its resources are limited, and suggests I seek local assistance in restoring the premises. 'Let us know when you're all set up and ready to receive visitors,' the letter concludes. It's signed simply 'the Trustees'.}}
After unlocking a room with a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] and gaining access to [[Ink]], they can be used alongside the letter to write a reply. [[Watchman's Tower: First Floor]] conveniently has both [[Desk: Eva|a Desk]] and [[Yewgall Ink|Ink]]. [[Long Tower: Solomon's Study]], located close to it, does as well. ==Writing a reply== As the game suggests, not all Desks allow all [[Principles]]. Based on the [[Elements of the Soul]] used, the letter varies in tone:
*Using [[Ereb]] or [[Chor]]: {{quote|A Charming Reply to St Rhonwen's Trust
'The journey was difficult, but nothing could keep me from the House, and the place is everything I had imagined! - or will be, once I've restored it to its old glory...'}}
*Using [[Wist]] or [[Phost]]: {{quote|An Inquisitive Reply to St Rhonwen's Trust
'I am here, but my situation is precarious, and there is so much I do not yet know. Is there anything more you can tell me? Of the House, the locals, their pasts? ...}}
*Using [[Trist]] or [[Fet]]: {{quote|An enigmatic Reply to St Rhonwen's Trust
'The sea remains; the House remains; what else remains, we shall learn in time. I am something new, and in time I will learn what that means...'}}
*Using [[Shapt]] or [[Mettle]]: {{quote|A Pragmatic Reply to St Rhonwen's Trust
'The journey was not straightforward, but here I am. Hush House is empty and peaceful. Nothing walks these halls. If something once did, seven years ago... the fire must have purged it.'}}
*Using [[Health]]: {{quote|A Straightforward Reply to St Rhonwen's Trust
'Dear Trustees; I have arrived.'}} {| class="article-table" |+ ! Principle used !! Memory gained |- | [[Ereb]] or [[Chor]] || [[Memory: Satisfaction]] |- | [[Wist]] or [[Phost]] || [[Memory: Revelation]] |- | [[Trist]] or [[Fet]] || [[Memory: Intuition]] |- | [[Shapt]] or [[Mettle]] || [[Memory: Foresight]] |- | [[Health]] || Nothing! |}
After writing a reply, the Ink will be destroyed and the letter will be converted to [[A Reply to the Trust]]. Sending it through the [[Post Office]] will allow the Librarian to receive [[Visitors]], [[Incident|Incidents]] and an yearly stipend, consisting of a [[Pence#Denominations|One Pound Note]] and an [[Spintria#Denominations|Iron Spintria]], at the beginning of every [[Season|Spring]]. It will also allow [[Readable|Books]] to be randomly [[Contamination|Contaminated]] upon cataloguing. If the Librarian delays in sending the letter more than one Season (or if it ''accidentally'' gets burned in a [[Workstations#Fireplaces|Fireplace]] for a free [[Memory: Sight]]), they will eventually receive a second letter, [[A Reminder to the Librarian]], asking why they haven't replied yet. Letters will keep being sent each Season, until the Librarian finally gives in replies. It is uncertain if the tone of the letter has any effect on anything, other than the received [[Memory]]. [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Correspondence]]

An Introduction to Histories.title: An Introduction to Histories
An Introduction to Histories.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=An Introduction to Histories
|image1=File:An_introduction_to_histories.PNG
|mystery=4
|principles={{Lore|Winter}}
|tally_price=3
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Snow Stories]]
|memory=[[Memory: Hindsight]]
|period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}

'''An Introduction to Histories''' is a [[book]] of the [[Winter]] principle written by [[Claude Hersault]].

== Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|The seventeenth-century mystic and antiquarian Claude Hersault describes divergent incidents in five major Histories.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{quote|The prologue warns at length of the iniquities of one Julian Coseley, a former colleague who Hersault now describes darkly as 'a Worm of Worms'. It seems Coseley advised Hersault early in the writing of the book, but Hersault later became suspicious.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{quote|Hersault identifies Blood, Silver, Design and the Worms as the central axes of each of the Histories, and claims that the so-called Second History is the true one.|I've Read...}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of the book provides 1 ''[[Snow Stories|Lesson: Snow Stories]]''. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Hindsight]].

Reading it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Baronial]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Forge]] [[Category:Readable]]

'''A Seventh Voice''' is a [[Books|Book]] of the [[Sky]] principle written by Samuel Savage. 

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Samuel Savage's cycle of comic poems about a band of players who double as footpads seeking a seventh member.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Sir Snatch-Sea is distracted by Mistress Twitch-Shell kissing Mistress Nether-Pearls, and fails to see Master Magglepie making off with the players' funds…|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The whole enterprise almost ends in disaster when Mistress Wander-Eye's family insults her costume, and she burns down their house in a fit of pique, but the day is finally saved by the Seventh Voice, a wandering book-monger who returns the band’s lost music.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides 2 ''[[Preliminal Meter|Lesson: Preliminal Meter]]''. Reading it always provides [[Confounding Parable]].

'''''Black Nephrite''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written by [[Valentine Dewulf]].

== Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|One of Valentine Dewulf's dream-journals, in which he records his visions of 'a place that is no place, beneath the house that is no house.'}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{quote|The dark, inchoate, feral space described by Valentine seems to be the 'Nowhere' of the Invisible Arts - the infra-oneiric lair of the alien Hours sometimes called gods-from-Nowhere.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{quote|Valentine's attitude to the Nowhere-Hours is unexpectedly relaxed. He speaks darkly of their appetites, but he insists they are too alien to penetrate the House of the Sun, let alone the waking world. He even seems to suggest that the Mansus-Hours have exaggerated the threat of the Nowhere-Hours for their own reasons. 'Not all Birds are trustworthy in their Feathers', he warns.|I've Read...}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Wolf Stories|Lesson: Wolf Stories]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]].

'''''An Impertinent Vitulation''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle written by [[Ernestine Peterhans]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description: 
{{Quote|A book of kitchen-garden techniques and aphrodisiac recipes recorded by Ernestine Peterhans, the 'Iron Seneschale' of Hush House for three generations of Dewulfs.|Description}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|Peterhans asserts casually that the rousing liquor called '[[Rubywise Ruin]]', which Leaves & Thorns techniques can brew from flowers, was a favourite of the notoriously severe [[Thomas Dewulf|Baron Thomas]]. If true, this would have raised eyebrows had it been known in his lifetime...|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|Peterhans mentions that one of these Leaves & Thorns techniques, with sufficient Nectar aspect, can supposedly cause 'a marvellous copper fruit' to burst from wood, although she has never managed it herself - but in a 'certain season' the pear-trees in the [[Practic Garden]] will deliver something similar.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Leaves & Thorns|Lesson: Leaves & Thorns]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Satisfaction]].

A True and Complete Accounting of the As.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=A True and Complete Accounting of the Asclepian Mysteries of the Roots of the House
|mystery=4
|tally_price=2

|principles={{Lore|Heart}}
|Period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]
|image1=A_True_and_Complete_Accounting_of_the_Asclepian_Mysteries_of_the_Roots_of_the_House.png

'''''A True and Complete Accounting of the Asclepian Mysteries of the Roots of the House''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle written by [[Rylee Grese]].

==Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Descriptions of the 'Asclepian Mysteries', reproduced by one 'Rylee Grese' from - supposedly - a much older text. It's unlikely to be genuine, but it makes a reference to 'The House without Walls and its Wood' right there in the prologue.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|This is very obviously not an antique text. At the very least, it has been badly mutilated. But it contains substantial intriguing material: especially, a persuasive comparison of the House without Walls, without doors to the human body, with its many portals.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|'The direction of Death is down,' the book explains. 'The Peacock Door has been considered a rent, or an abrasion, but in some respects is more like a mouth - if not a more treasured point of entry.' Discussions of the Doors include a rite which may conjure creatures through those doors, although key incantations are missing.|I've Read...}}
== Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Weaving & Knotworking|Lesson: Weaving and Knotworking]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

'''''Advice on Containment''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written by [[Thirza Blake]].

== Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Thirza Blake discusses ways 'to keep Wood-things out of trouble, and Mansus-things in it.'}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{quote|Thirza is irritatingly light on specifics, insisting above all that the duties of an adept are the duties of a host, and that a conjured spirit should be kept in as luxurious a vessel as possible.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{quote|Thirza notes the similarities between the Lantern-long habit of 'scrining' - returning to the physical world, despite their absence of a body, by entering a mirror or light - and Poemander's techniques of confining Mansus-long to mirrors. She wonders whether Poemander himself might be lured to visit Hush House if provided with a sufficiently alluring scrine.|I've Read...}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting|Lesson: Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Pattern]].

Apollo and Marsyas.text:
{{Book (BoH)

'''''Apollo and Marsyas''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The libretto of a lost opera concerning the contest between Apollo and Marsyas, and its tragic outcome. The librettist is identified only by their initials.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|In the original myth, Marsyas lost the musical contest and was flayed by Apollo, who later regretted it. In this version, Marsyas' skin has a further history...|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Skin of Marsayas gives oracles, and is later smuggled to Phrygia, where the priestesses of Cybele use it for a drum. At the climax, the striking of the drum drive would-be violators of the priestess to suicidal madness. The opera ends with a wistful hymn from the youngest priestess on the beauty of mountain pines.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Surgeries & Exsanguinations|Lesson: Surgeries & Exsanguinations]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Storm]].

==Trivia==
- The lost opera this book is sourced from is recovered in [[The Affair of 'Apollo and Marsyas']]

'''''As the Sun His Course''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} principle written in [[Aramaic]] by [[Joel of the Bridge]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Joel of the Bridge, a retired soldier and sometime tollkeeper, wrote this epic poem about Alexander's famously inexplicable decision at Issus to withdraw from the war with the Achaemenids, and his subsequent return to Macedonia.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Alexander meets at Issus with Darius, King of Kings, for three days and three nights. On the first day, the two men trade threats; on the second, promises; on the third, secrets. Darius tells Alexander something so shattering that he retires to his tent to consider 'matters of strength and matters of mastery'.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|At dawn on the fourth day, Alexander announces: 'the Sun has his course, upon which he returns; and so do I'. He returns to Macedonia, executing two of his captains when they dispute his decision. He brings with him the 'names of a blind God', and a 'rite of sacred betrayal': for, Joel opines, without betrayal there would be an end to war.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Sickle & Eclipse|Lesson: Sickle & Eclipse]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Contradiction]].

'''''A Manual for Departure''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written in [[Vak]] by the Jekadu, who is supposedly one of the [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Great_Hooded_Princes Great Hooded Princes].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|The author, who identifies itself as the Jekadu, claims to be one of the Great Hooded Princes of the Land of the River. The style is informal, even chatty.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|No, these doors shouldn't be recorded, but if we had only recorded things before we'd had to leave the Fifth History, we would be in a much better state. So here I am writing it down, and if you don't like it you can sanction me.'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote| The 'Manual for Departure' lists a number of strategies - occult, martial and political - for quick escapes. Many are irrelevant, obsolete or enigmatic, but the Manual does include a number of powerful techniques for opening portals.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Door & Wall|Lesson: Door & Wall]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Secret Threshold]].

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Some pleasures,' the Formulae Voluptuous attest, 'are so intense they can corrupt the laws of the physical world'. This text catalogues some of those instances.|I'm Reading...}}

'''''A Pale Lady and a Prince of Wines''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|An anonymous biography of Eva Dewulf, last of the Dewulfs, focused rather salaciously on her personal troubles and intrigues.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Eva Dewulf is engaged to one Abraham Wheelock, but he leaves her at the altar. Furious and humiliated, she returns to Brancrug, and is not seen in London again. Three days after her departure, Abraham Wheelock's body is washed up near Gravesend. His face is so badly pecked by birds that he is only identified by his belongings. These include a waxed pouch containing a letter addressed to Wheelock, whose contents seem to show he is a spy in the pay of the Austrians. Subsequent investigations suggest that the letter is a forgery, but the matter remains obscure...|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Lord Franklin Bancroft, sometimes called the Prince of Wines, begins a series of visits to Brancrug House. His relationship with Eva becomes a source of scandal. Eva is by now forty-nine, but rumours persist for years of a Dewulf-Bancroft heir. Eva's biographer claims that before her 'drowning death', her child by Bancroft was adopted by her friends the Southeys - that the child became the sister of the later Poet Laureate, Robert Southey. (No real evidence is provided in support of this claim.)|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Sea Stories|Lesson: Sea Stories]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Salt]].

An Exorcist's Field Manual.title: An Exorcist's Field Manual
An Exorcist's Field Manual.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|mystery=6
|principles={{Lore|Moon}}
|skill=[[Edicts Martial]]
|memory=[[Memory: Contradiction]]
|period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|tally_price=1
|image1=[[File:AnExorcistsFieldManual.png]]}}
'''''An Exorcist's Field Manual''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written by Detective-Ostiary Wheelock of the [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Suppression_Bureau Supression Bureau].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description: 
{{Quote|A practical guide to 'troublesome Dead', grounded in theory but with a clear focus on their disposal, by the redoubtable Detective-Ostiary Wheelock of the Suppression Bureau.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|"The Dead usually avoid Light - as the most immediate manifestation of Eternity, which has no place for death. However those Dead 'uplifted by gold', that is to say touched by an actinic theoplasma, happily bod about in daylight and are perhaps strongest at noon..."|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|"If you are dead but 'uplifted by green', that's the Ring-Yew's blessing. (The Crowned Growth offers a similar but nastier benefit.) This is how Burgeoning Risen come about, but there are different degrees of sentience and freedom depending on which growths are involved. The consciousness of one 'uplifted by green' is always greatly altered, though - they never really seem like the same person. They may have dregs of their original souls, but these are often replaced by something else. The upshot, invariably, is that they need to be set firmly on fire."|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Edicts Martial|Lesson:Edicts Martial]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Contradiction]].

Cardea's Delights.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=Cardea's Delights
|mystery=8

|Period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar Gothic]]}}
'''Cardea's Delights''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written in [[Latin]] by [[Abbot Geffrey]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|The third volume of Abbot Geffrey's hypothetical theological dialogues in the Socratic mode.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|<nowiki/>'If Janus were an Hour, Cardea might be counted among his Names, but the world has never turned in such a manner, and so she is not…'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Geffrey discusses the 'living Signs' - signs which change their shape, and whose flexibility is part of what makes it identifiable. He gives as one example 'the Paradox of the Hinge', and draws comparisons with the 'Names' called Twins (who would be considered Hours beyond the Church). He hints at the 'Amethyst Vessel' which can be sanctified by the Great Signs in the presence of Knock...|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars|Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Pattern]].

An Almanac of Entrances.text:

|title1=An Almanac of Entrances

'''An Almanac of Entrances''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written by [[Willem Harries]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A handbook of sealed and unsealed byways and shortcuts through the Bounds, compiled by Willem Harries in the 1860s - during his term as Librarian of Hush House.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Harries discusses the role played by the 'Légion du Seuil' and the 'Company of the Wolf-in-Gold' in warding the bounds against outside influences. He warns that Bounds-travellers may themselves be considered 'outside influences…'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘The Mansus, as Ys, lacks walls; Ys and the Mansus have both their gates, and there may be no gate without a wall. Thus the paradox resolves, as all those who walk in dream will learn. But the Wood has neither gate nor wall, and so it is the Wood whose roots may creep after us into the hours of our waking.’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Edicts Liminal|Lesson: Edicts Liminal]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Secret Threshold]].

A Tower Falls.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=A Tower Falls
|mystery=16

|memory=[[Confounding Parable]]}}
'''''A Tower Falls''''' is a [[Phonograph Record]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle in Vak. It is thematically related to [[A Tower Rises]]. 

==Description==
Selecting the record provides the following description:
{{quote|The phonograph is packaged in glossy amethyst purple card with the words A TOWER FALLS in nine languages on both sides. There is no other identifying information at all.}}

Upon choosing to master the record at a [[Phonograph]], the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|A recording of uncertain origin: inexplicably compelling poetry recorded by a speaker with a rasping, rumbling, impossibly deep voice... in the language called Vak, which probably isn't spoken by more than a few dozen living scholars.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The poem speaks of a four-winged war, a four-mouthed king, a four-rayed sun, a four-cornered stone. It speaks of a tide-washed hunger of the heart; it speaks, lastly, of its own conclusion, when it might, might, might be spoken in dreams before the Deep Door, by a Messenger of Histories...|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this recording provides ''[[Preliminal Meter|Lesson: Preliminal Meter]]'' x3. Listening to it always provides [[Confounding Parable]].

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Sky]] principle written by [[Abbot Ranulph]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A fourteenth-century treatise on esoteric mechanics and parahydraulics by Abbot Ranulph, best known now as a mason-architect.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Ranulph describes how he tested some of these techniques in the construction of the Winter Tower (now called the Long Tower). He admits to unexpected consequences…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Ranulph mentions that the tower of Ely Cathedral collapsed around the time the Winter Tower was completed… although he stops short of suggesting that one was the cause of another. 'A tower falls, a tower rises,' is all he'll commit to.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides 1 ''[[Lockworks & Clockworks|Lesson: Lockworks & Clockworks]]''. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Pattern]].

'''A True History of Valentine Dewulf''' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Sky]] principle written by [[Valentine Dewulf]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description: 
{{Quote|Written in the third person by Valentine Dewulf. Rarely coherent, though it includes some useful footnotes on falconry and on exotic veterinary medicine.|Description}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Valentine is obssessed with the meaning of the Dewulf coat-of-arms: 'On a field or, a chevron enarched gules between two corby heads erased sable in chief and a wolf sejant sable in base.'…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|'Long have the two birds pursued my blood, yet one is no Crow, yet it is darker. Long has the Wolf rolled itself in gold like a clovered cow, until its slobberings stain our thoughts…'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Furs & Feathers|Lesson: Furs & Feathers]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]].

|image1=Annals of St Brandans.png}}
'''''Annals of St Brandans''''' is a [[Books|Book]] of the [[Winter]] Principle, written in [[Latin]] by an unknown author.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Over a hundred years of the abbey's annals, from 1230 to 1350.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Three events of particular interest are recorded: an endowment by Eva de Braose, widow of the Marcher Lord Gwilym Ddu ('Black William), which enables an expansion of the Abbey; the construction of the Winter Tower, which is dedicated to the Madrugad; and the death 'by poisoning and Arts unsanctioned' of Abbess Nonna...|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|After Abbess Nonna's death, the 'double foundation' is dissolved and the monastery is reformed to accept only male novices. At this point the ink changes. The helpful scribe explains that for the new foundation, the Abbot has mandated stargall, not yewgall, ink. He outlines the differences (use of Inks of Containment techniques with a Sky, not Nectar, context) but doesn't trouble to explain why.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates one ''[[Inks of Containment|Lesson: Inks of Containment]]''. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Regret]].

|memory=[[Memory: Fear]]}}
'''''Book of True Blood''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} principle written in [[Latin]] by Cassius the Thoman.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Cassius the Thoman reveals the deeds of the Unnumbered Legion, the secret army that protected Rome against the Shadowless Empire.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Legion's Legate answered directly to the Hour called the Tribune of Scars, and was promised immortality if he died in battle....|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|In the final part, Cassius confesses to being a former Legate. He recounts his terror of the Tribune, and divulges the secret lore of the Golden General, the champion of the Shadowless Empire, the enemy of the Tribune, in the hope that the Tribune will some day be undone.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards ==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Meniscate Reflections|Lesson: Meniscate Reflections]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]].

== Trivia ==

* The "Golden General" was [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/The_Lionsmith the Lionsmith] prior to ascending as an Hour, while the Tribune is [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/The_Colonel the Colonel], who is known as the Tribune of Scars.

Ambrosial!.text:

|title1=Ambrosial!
|mystery=8

|tally_price=2
|type=[[Codex]]
|image1=[[File:Ambrosial!.png]]

|skill=[[Spices & Savours]]}}
'''''Ambrosial!''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle written by [[Ambrose Westcott]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Ambrose Westcott's inventive - one might say pioneering, or indeed buccaneering - essays into kitchencraft.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Westcott proudly announces his intention to transform cuisine to become 'an Engine of Alchemy, a Fount of War.'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Westcott describes the ferocity of fire with the intensity of appetite as 'in essence, one essence'. A fire's ability to transform and destroy grows when it is offered the correct fuel; so too, he implies, can a sufficiently inspired appetite allow its possessor to consume 'greatly, strangely, unwisely.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Spices & Savours|Lesson: Spices & Savours]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

A Child's Treasury of Golden Afternoons.title: A Child's Treasury of Golden Afternoons
A Child's Treasury of Golden Afternoons.text: {{Book (BoH) |title1=A Child's Treasury of Golden Afternoons |image1=AChildsTreasuryofGoldenAfternoons.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Edge}} |tally_price=8 |language=[[Hyksos]] |type=[[Codex]] |period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]] |memory=[[Numen: Merciless Alteration]] |skill=[[Sharps]]}} '''''A Child's Treasury of Golden Afternoons''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} principle that contains a [[Numen: Merciless Alteration|Numen]]. ==Location == A Child's Treasury of Golden Afternoons is found inside the [[Iron Vault]]. == Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{quote|Once upon a time, a very bad man encoded very bad secrets into the charming illustrations of a book of charming stories. Wake the pictures, and you will see. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote| Lord Jacob Gristwood: surgeon, ethnologist, philanthropist. There is no proof that he ever kept children in hutches beneath his bed. There is no proof he vivisected cats at dinner with his pen-knife. The Suppression Bureau keeps its secrets.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Here is your paint,' whispered the Wolf to the Pale Girl. 'Here is your knife-for-scraping. And here is your face.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sharps|Lesson: Sharps]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Numen: Merciless Alteration]]; a [[Numen]] that can be used to establish a [[history]] and win the game. This numen has a special victory for [[the Artist]] and the [[The Archaeologist|Archaeologist]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Baronial]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Edge]] [[Category:Numen]] [[Category:Readable]]

'''A Novel Method for Invocation & Contrition''' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Rose]] principle written in [[Ericapaean]] by Rory Morrow.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Ingenious and rather beautiful techniques for entreating the Names of the Hours, developed by Rory Morrow, who styled himself 'the Sage-Knight'.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The techniques rely on the unique qualities of the Ericapaean tongue. Morrow professes himself surprised that they serve better to entreat the Names of the Vagabond than the Names of Lantern or Winter Hours…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Morrow demonstrates that Preliminal Meter techniques can be used with sufficient Rose to invoke the Vagabond's Names, transforming an Enduring Reflection into 'something wider of sky.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides 2 ''[[Preliminal Meter|Lesson: Preliminal Meter]]''. Reading it always provides [[Confounding Parable]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle, written by [[Black Elie]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Black Elie, who much later became Damascene Matriarch of the Sisterhood of the Knot, recounts her journey to the Grove of Green Immortals.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|In the Grove, Elie meets with an entity identified as 'Three Faces, Nine Colours' - who may have become her lover.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Three Faces is a Name of the Applebright, the Nowhere Hour of youth, healing and mutation. It offers Elie a form of eternal youth to take back West with her, which she rejects for certain reasons. She does promise, however, to renew their acquaintance 'in the season when the Applebright is the Witch' - not from sentiment, but rather grandly, to ensure the continuity of the Histories.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Orchids & Narcotics|Lesson: Orchids & Narcotics]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Satisfaction]].

'''''A Light in the Inkwell''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle written by [[Musgrave Dewulf]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Musgrave, fourth of the Dewulf line, writes tentatively about the 'Covenant of Brancrug' and the legacy of the sacred inks he calls 'encausta revelationia'.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Words are of the First Importance. So the Book of Suns teaches. But do not Words require Ink? And is the Inkwell not then the Womb of Words?|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Musgrave identifies 'the [[Ichor Auroral]]' as the mother of the encaustum [[Porphyrine]]. He adds that it would be blasphemous to describe the origins of the Ichor itself, although a scrawled marginal note suggests a later reader thought Musgrave was only hiding his ignorance beneath a cloak of piety.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of theis book provides ''[[Inks of Revelation|Lesson: Inks of Revelation]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]].

Amiranis Beteli.title: Amiranis Beteli
Amiranis Beteli.text: {{Book_(BoH) |title1=Amiranis Beteli |principles={{Lore|Forge}} |tally_price=8 |language=[[Fucine]] |type=[[Tablet]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]] |mystery=10 |image1=Amiranis Beteli.png |skill=[[Bells & Brazieries]] |memory=[[Numen: the Bells of Ys]]}} '''''Amiranis Beteli''''' is a [[Books|tablet]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} principle that contains a [[Numen: the Bells of Ys|Numen]]. ==Location== ''Amiranis Beteli'' is found in the [[Iron Vault]]. == Description == Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|A fragment of iron-alloy meteorite carefully inscribed and polished. [This object houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'Who gave us fire? Who gave us steel? What is the sound of dusk? Of what alloy is wind forged?'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Esoteric secrets of metallurgy and resonance are revealed - including directions towards the creation of a terrible Bell. |I've Read...}} == Rewards == Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Bells & Brazieries|Lesson: Bells & Brazieries]]'' x2 . Reading it always provides [[Numen: the Bells of Ys]]; a [[Numen]] that can be used to establish a [[History|history]] and win the game. This numen has a special victory for [[The Prodigal]] and [[The Revolutionary]]. == Trivia == As hints a [[Salon#Salon_Stories|Salon conversation]] between [[The Rector|Timothy]] and [[Mme Olympe Bechet|Olympe]], the Amiranis Beteli is linked to the country of Georgia, and given its name may relate to the Georgian hero [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amirani Amirani]. An Echo of Silence.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=An Echo of Silence

'''''An Echo of Silence''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle written in [[Sabazine]] by a [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Obliviates House of Lethe] Adept known as "The Serenity".

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A very heterodox history of the House of Lethe as recorded by 'the Serenity' - a Lethean adept who declares that the House of Lethe was created explicitly to prevent the ascension of any more mortals to Name or Hour status.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Eternity cannot be escaped; but in History, it may be delayed,’ the Serenity explains. ‘The gods-who-were-flesh, by their nature, are a surrender to Eternity.’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The 'roots of the House' are said to pass into the Wood of dreams through three forests in the Bounds, identified as the Bei Ilai, the Black Cedar Forest, and the Brecheliant. 'While one tree of these may yet stand, one single tree, the Histories continue.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Sacra Limiae|Lesson: Sacra Limiae]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

A Descent of the Shell.title: A Descent of the Shell
A Descent of the Shell.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=A Descent of the Shell
|image1=A Descent of the Shell.png

|period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar Gothic]]}}
'''''A Descent of the Shell''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle written by [[Abbess Melancthe]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|A treatise on eggs, light, and optics by Abbess Melancthe, dazzlingly illuminated with renderings of the Abbess' visions.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The book is unexpectedly challenging to read. The bright glitter of the gold-leaf illuminations acquires a migrainous quality; the eye aches and tires…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|This is, most likely, the 'certain vivid book' that Melancthe once sent to Gunnhlld, daughter of King Harold, which provoked in her 'a dream of eyes' but also caused her to begin to lose her sight (until she was healed by the saint-bishop Wulfstan). To complete it is a kind of test. Its double thesis, at last, seems to be that the Sun is either an eye or an egg; and so the Second Dawn will be either its opening, or its hatching.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Purifications & Exaltations|Lesson: Purifications & Exaltations]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

Bancroft Diaries.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=Bancroft Diaries

'''''Bancroft Diaries''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Lantern]] Principle written in [[Latin]] by [[Lord Franklin Bancroft]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Lord Franklin Bancroft was initiated into the arts of the Flowermaker by the 'rose-witch' Fionna Ayrshire. He rose to become a Society provider of occult services and secret pleasures, before his abrupt disappearance in 1790.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Bancroft seems to have been a talented adept, but devoted his energies to frustratingly whimsical projects: arranging 'grape-fetching races' between Mansus-spirits, teaching Percussigants to juggle, and conjuring storms of imaginary blossoms for the rose-witch Ayrshire, who resolutely refused ever to couple with him. Bancroft spends twenty pages bemoaning this last.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Mantra here recorded is a high and exacting magic which can be used to pledge one's spirit to the Watchman, beginning an ascent to the House. Bancroft boasts of his ability to recite it when in his cups. He also had it set to music for a performance with fireworks at Vauxhall Gardens.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Pyroglyphics|Lesson: Pyroglyphics]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

Book of Miah.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=Book of Miah.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Rose}} |tally_price=5 |language=[[Hyksos]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Sand Stories]] |memory=[[Memory: Intuition]] |Period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Rose}} Principle, written in [[Hyksos]] by an [[The Hours|Hour]] called [[w:c:secret-histories:The_Vagabond|The Vagabond]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{quote|An account of the 'five visits of the Desert Wanderer' - probably the Hour called the Vagabond - to the city Miah. She begins as a delighted child - perhaps even a mortal - but things then go badly…|}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'In her second visit, she came as Laughingthrush. Her heart was bright within, her beak was ripe with song, but in the first moment her feathers touched the city stones, the laughter began….'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The Wanderer's penultimate visit is as Centipede, whose 'venom cracks stone'. Miah is abandoned to the desert. But she returns one last time, again as Laughingthrush, with four other Hours who take the shape of birds, 'to celebrate the First Roost above the bones of her hated kin.'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sand Stories|Lesson: Sand Stories]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Intuition]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Rose]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

'''A Second Glory''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} principle written in [[Deep Mandaic]] by The Priest Juceh.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The priest Juceh celebrates the extirpation of the Gods-who-were-stone, those Hours who preceded humanity.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Juceh engages in an apologia for the destruction of the Hours: they were old, they were cowardly, they were vile, their time had passed, and it was the shining destiny of humankind to seize the House through glorious battle.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Juceh recounts how the Hour called Seven-Coils was slain in battle by the Colonel, how the Grail devoured the Hour called Tide, and how the Egg Unhatching 'fled like a coward'. He's quite vituperative about the Egg Unhatching. He warns darkly against its return.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides 2 ''[[Snow Stories|Lesson: Snow Stories]]''. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Hindsight]].

A Tower Rises is a [[Phonograph Record]] of the [[Rose]] principle.

It is thematically related to [[A Tower Falls]].

==Description==
Selecting the record provides the following description:
{{quote|The phonograph is packaged in glossy card the bright pink of a dog-rose, with the words A TOWER RISES in nine languages on both sides. There is no other identifying information at all.}}

Upon choosing to master the recording at the phonograph, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|A recording of uncertain origin: inexplicably compelling poetry recorded by a speaker with a high, sweet voice that scales up beyond human hearing... in the language called Vak, which probably isn't spoken by more than a few dozen living scholars.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The poem speaks of the Wheel that turns, the Coil that turns, the Tide that returns, Egg that returns; it speaks of a cloven sky, an opened heart, a dream of glittering eyes; speaks, lastly, of its own conclusion, when it might, might, might be spoken in dreams before the Deep Door, by a Messenger of Histories...|I've Read...}}

Completing mastery of the recording generates 3 ''[[Preliminal Meter|Lesson: Preliminal Meter]]''. Listening to it always provides [[Confounding Parable]].

'''''An Investigation of A Foundered Country''''' is a [[Phonograph Record]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle.

== Description ==
Selecting the record provides the following description:
{{Quote|Subtitled 'Recordings from the Atlantic Coast.'}}

Upon choosing to master the record at a [[Phonograph]], the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The phonograph initially seems to consist entirely of wave sounds, and the cries of gulls - but attention to the cries suggests they are not gulls at all - perhaps not even birds.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The bird-cries resolve to possibly-human voices, half-lost in the sound of waves. They lament the absence of a 'city unborn'; they hymn the 'ice behind the wave,' the 'amber cobbles', or perhaps 'amber corals.' The tenor of their song is melancholy but also, increasingly, menacing, as they promise the 'city irresistible.' As the voices fade, distant bells are clearly to be heard among the surf-sounds.|I've Read...}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of the record provides ''[[Hill & Hollow|Lesson: Hill & Hollow]]'' x1. Listening to it always provides [[Memory: A Stolen Secret]].

Journal.title: Journal
Journal.text:
[[File:Journal icon.png|right]] {{Quote|I began before this book, but it'll end when I do.}} __NOTOC__
The '''Journal''' is the only item that the Librarian has at [[The Beginning]] of the game. ==Drowned Book== [[File:Journal Start.png|frame|left|alt=A Drowned Book|The one possession I kept from the shipwreck. It must be important to me.]] When first inspected, it is called "A Drowned Book", which is [[Soaked]]. Once it has been dried out at one of various locations around [[Brancrug Village]], it gains the aspect [[Uncatalogued Book|uncatalogued]]. Once catalogued, it will become a Journal. Which Journal it will become depends on the [[Elements of the Soul]] chosen at The Beginning. The Journal can be [[Mastery|mastered]] using an [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]] and the appropriate [[Principles|Principle]], and upon mastery will yield four [[Memory#Lessons|Lessons]]. {{Clear}} ==Journals== {| class="fandom-table sortable" width="100%" !Librarian !Journal !Principle !3 Lessons of !1 Lesson of |- | rowspan="2" |[[The Archaeologist|Archaeologist]] | rowspan="2" |[[Sand-Scarred Journal]] |{{Lore|Edge}} |[[Ragged Crossroads]] | rowspan="2" |[[Wolf Stories]] |- |{{Lore|Winter}} |[[Inks of Containment]] |- |[[The Artist|Artist]] |[[Bee-Silk Journal]] |{{Lore|Grail}} |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |[[Rites of the Roots]] |- |[[The Cartographer|Cartographer]] |[[Serpentskin Journal]] |{{Lore|Lantern}} |[[Inks of Revelation]] |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |- |[[The Executioner|Executioner]] |[[Horned Journal]] |{{Lore|Edge}} |[[Sickle & Eclipse]] |[[Surgeries & Exsanguinations]] |- |[[The Magnate|Magnate]] |[[Silver-Bound Journal]] |{{Lore|Winter}} |[[Quenchings & Quellings]] |[[Sacra Limiae]] |- |[[The Prodigal|Prodigal]] |[[Hammered Copper Journal]] |{{Lore|Lantern}} |[[Pyroglyphics]] |[[Bells & Brazieries]] |- |[[The Revolutionary|Revolutionary]] |[[Ironclad Journal]] |{{Lore|Edge}} |[[Edicts Martial]] |[[Sky Stories]] |- |[[The Symurgist|Symurgist]] |[[Feather-Decked Journal]] |{{Lore|Winter}} |[[Rhyme & Remembrance]] |[[Sky Stories]] |- |[[The Twice-Born|Twice-Born]] |[[Amber-Flecked Journal]] |{{Lore|Lantern}} |[[Auroral Contemplations]] |[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]] |- |}
==Journal's Use== The Journal is used to reach an [[Endings|ending]]. The simplest ending is reading the journal under [[The Earl's Yew]] with any [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]]. Major endings (or victories) require new pages to be written in the journal. There are two types of entries that can be made in the journal, [[Determination|Determinations]] and [[History|Histories]]. A Determination can be made using 20 of any principle; the principle used decides the determination. A determination adds additional principles to the journal. A History requires a [[Numen]], an [[Ink]] and 25 of any of the Numen's [[Principles]]. The Numen and Principle used both have an impact on the ending that they will achieve. ==Destroying the Journal== The Librarian can choose to destroy their journal in one of three ways: *Burning the journal in any fireplace produces an [[Invincible Audacity]]. *Drowning the journal at the [[Sea's Edge|Sea’s Edge]], the [[Brancrug Boathouse|Boathouse]], or the [[Loading Dock]] produces an [[Old Moment]] and grants an [[Achievements|Achievement]] the first time it’s done. *Flinging the journal down the [[Hush House Well]] produces a [[Memory: Sound]]. All options destroy the journal permanently, rendering the game unwinnable on the current save file. ==Gallery== Journal.archaeologist.unc.png|Uncatalogued Archaeologist's Journal - "Scarred Book" Sand-Scarred Journal.png|Archaeologist's Journal - Sand-Scarred Journal Journal.artist.unc.png|Uncatalogued Artist's Journal - "Silken Book" Bee-Silk Journal.png|Artist's Journal - Bee-Silk Journal Journal.cartographer.unc.png|Uncatalogued Cartographer's Journal - "Scaled Book" Serpentskin Journal.png|Cartographer's Journal - Serpentskin Journal Journal.executioner.unc.png|Uncatalogued Executioner's Journal - "Mottled Book" Horned Journal.png|Executioner's Journal - Horned Journal Journal.magnate.unc.png|Uncatalogued Magnate's Journal - "Silvery Book" Magnate Journal.png|Magnate's Journal - Silver-Bound Journal Journal.prodigal.unc.png|Uncatalogued Prodigal's Journal - "Coppery Book" Hammered Copper Journal.png|Prodigal's Journal - Hammered Copper Journal Journal.revolutionary.unc.png|Uncatalogued Revolutionary's Journal - "Gunmetal Book" Ironclad Journal.png|Revolutionary's Journal - Ironclad Journal Journal.symurgist.unc.png|Uncatalogued Symurgist's Journal - "Feathered Book" Feather-Decked Journal.png|Symurgist's Journal - Feather-Decked Journal Journal.twiceborn.unc.png|Uncatalogued Twiceborn's Journal - "Stone-Studded Book" Amber-Flecked Journal.png|Twiceborn's Journal - Amber-Flecked Journal [[Category:Aspect]] [[Category:Thing]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Journal]] [[Category:Soaked]]

'''Ettery After''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description: 
{{Quote|An anonymous erotic novel occasionally claimed to have been written by Eva Dewulf, although at least two duels were fought in her honour to avenge this slander.|Description}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|The novel graphically details Madame Ettery's various imprisonments, ravishments and escapes in the debauched Commonwealth of Tinctures and its neighbour, the pious Atrament.|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|It becomes apparent that many of Ettery's lovers and pursuers - [[Catwink]], [[Houndsgall]], [[Nillycant|Nilique]] - are transparent allegories for inks, and that Ettery is an embodiment of knowledge pinned to paper - to her mingled delight and dismay. The author only half-commits to the metaphor, though, and is clearly at least as interested in titillation as revelation.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates 2 [[Inks of Containment|''Lesson: Inks of Containment'']]. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Hindsight]].

'''''In the Malleary''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|A lively account of the creation of each jewel at the world's beginning.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Lively, yes; but also almost entirely nonsense. 'Pearl, the tears of the forgotten moon, caught by the Lionsmith in his net. Ruby, the blood of the first bird, stung by the Lionsmith's hammer.'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The author is either terribly misinformed of the nature of the Hours, or - one begins to suspect - intentionally throwing up a smoke-screen to confuse seekers of the Invisible Arts. But there are some useful crumbs of fact to be picked out of the daft and gaping cracks. |I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Anbary & Lapidary| Lesson: Anbary & Lapidary]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

Journal of Thomas Dewulf.text:
{{Book_(BoH) |image1=[[File:JournalofThomasDewulf.png]] |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |tally_price=3 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Ouranoscopy]] |memory=[[Memory: Salt]] |period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} Principle, written in English by [[Thomas Dewulf]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{quote|Thomas Dewulf, 2nd Baron Brancrug, was nicknamed 'Baron Silence of Castle Silence' for his taciturn severity - most likely the origin, eventually, of the name 'Hush House'.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{quote|There are very few personal details here. Thomas, a talented astronomer and ouranoscopist, dispassionately details his observations and the building of the observatory atop the Watchman's Tower.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{quote|As he records the passing of the Great Comet in 1577, the tone finally becomes more animated but also more obscure. Thomas cites his Dawn Period namesake, Abbot Thomas, as an authority on 'Wind, Moon, and Shell in the Heavens Inferior'. He observes: 'My predecessor knew this Truth - three Blossoms hath the Watchman's Tree: Paper; Ink; and Flame. The Great Comet, I now aver, is that Flame.'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Ouranoscopy|Lesson: Ouranoscopy]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Salt]]. De Horis book 3.text: {{Book (BoH) |title1=De Horis book 3 |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Edge}} |skill=[[Disciplines of the Scar]] |memory=[[Memory: Contradiction]] |tally_price=3 |language=[[Latin]] |type=[[Codex]] |Period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]] |image1=De Horis book 3.png}} '''De Horis book 3''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} principle written in [[Latin]], reprinted by [[Nathaniel Darcy-Evers]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|In Latin. A nineteenth-century reprint (by the indefatigable Nathaniel Darcy-Evers) of a fourteenth-century Latin translation of a fourth-century work.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|This is usually described as the third volume of 'De Horis', but Darcy-Evers' foreword argues persuasively that it's a substantial reworking by the original author…|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The Lionsmith makes monsters, the Colonel has his scars, but the De Horis now insists that neither can truly defeat the other; that they must at some level understand these limits in their strategies; and that their enmity is an 'eternal engine of the world.'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Disciplines of the Scar|Lesson: Disciplines of the Scar]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Contradiction]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Baronial]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Edge]] [[Category:Readable]]

'''Exercises in the Continuity of Self''' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Winter]] principle.
==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description: 
{{Quote|Techniques proposed by the Haustorium - the most inaccessible and upsetting of the libraries of the Watchman's Tree - for 'the persistence of memory after the body is discarded'.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|The soul-element wist is regarded as 'the fundamental value of the individual'. All other soul-elements, it is implied, may potentially be discarded, as can the individual itself.|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|The Haustorium expresses grudging respect for the Hour called Elegiast, 'who calls each of the Dead by name', but also concern over the Elegiast's subtlety when it chooses to inspire particular interpretations of Histories. The Haustorium proposes the use of Nowhere-energies in distracting or discouraging the Elegiast, in order to assure that 'the persistence of History remains unalloyed'.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates 2 [[Rhyme & Remembrance|''Lesson: Rhyme & Remembrance'']]. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Hindsight]].

'''''De Horis book 2''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} Principle written in [[Latin]], reprinted by [[Nathaniel Darcy-Evers]]. 

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|In Latin. A nineteenth-century reprint (by the indefatigable Nathaniel Darcy-Evers) of a fourteenth-century Latin translation of a fourth-century work.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|This volume deals mostly with the Hour called Lionsmith, the Hour called the Tribune of Scars, and with their enmity.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:

Collected Hush House Lectures.title: Collected Hush House Lectures
Collected Hush House Lectures.text:
{{Book (BoH) |title1=Collected
Hush House Lectures |image1=CollectedHHL.png |mystery=4 |skill=[[Sickle & Eclipse]] |memory=[[Memory: Intuition]] |tally_price=2 |type=[[Codex]] |principles={{Lore|Moon}} |Period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written by [[Dr Arun Peel]]. == Description == Selecting the book provides the following description: {{quote|In the 1800s, Dr Arun Peel was invited to give a series of lectures to the Curia. They combine his pithy view of the Histories with his particular brand of unhelpfully ironical insight.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|‘1776, the Third History: Louis declares the Masque of Masques, and forbids mention of the Great Writhing within the walls of the Palace of Versailles, although by this point the Worms are observed to move openly along the boulevards of Paris, sometimes even in daylight. The Army is redeployed to defend the Court. The Masque lasts one lunar month, and attracts several of the Long abroad in Western Europe at the time - fleeing the Worms, or hoping to take advantage of the desperate Louis, or seeking access to the sealed mirrors of the Palace - or just eager to attend the most inventive and desperate debauch of the century…’|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|‘Many Know espouse Wormish sympathies. Let a hundred Histories flourish! Tear down the tyranny of eternity! To grow Long is, usually, to cast off these sympathies. There would be no immortality without Eternity, and Eternity, we often seem to decide, is only tyranny as long as we are not eternal.’|I've Read...}} == Rewards == Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sickle & Eclipse|Lesson: Sickle & Eclipse]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Intuition]]. ==Trivia== *Presenting [[Dr Arun Peel]] this book in a consultation provides unique dialogue and rewards the Librarian with [[Wormwood Dream]]. Exorcism for Girls.title: Exorcism for Girls
Exorcism for Girls.text: {{Book (BoH) |mystery=6 |principles={{Lore|Edge}} |tally_price=2 |type=[[Codex]] |Period=[[Curia Period|Curia]] |image1=Exorcism for Girls.png |skill=[[Sickle & Eclipse]] |memory=[[Memory: Fear]]}} '''Exorcisms for Girls''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} principle written by [[Thirza Blake]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{quote|Simple but forceful techniques for 'rousting unbefitting spirits', written in straightforward and colourful language.|}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Blake seems uncertain at points whether the techniques are intended for use by or on girls. She clearly regards children as a nuisance.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Thirza's advice on the shapeless Wood-things known as Raw Prophets is typically practical: (1) discourage them with buckets of water as close as possible to freezing, and with the smoke of dried lemongrass (2) under no circumstances kiss them or receive kisses from them. (3) an effective formula is provided for laundering clothes stained with Prophet-slime.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of the book provides [[Sickle & Eclipse|''Lesson: Sickle & Eclipse'']] x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Curia]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Edge]] [[Category:Readable]]

Chione at Abydos.title: Chione at Abydos
Chione at Abydos.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=Chione at Abydos
|mystery=6

|memory=[[Memory: Regret]]
|tally_price=3

|principles={{Lore|Winter}}
|Period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]
|image1=Chione at Abydos.png}}
'''Chione at Abydos''' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Winter]] principle written by Apollo Fireweaver.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|A play dealing with the nine-year sojourn of a snow-goddess in the Thracian city of Abydos, by 'Apollo Fireweaver'. In English, published in 1892; purportedly from an older Greek text.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The entity called 'Chione' arrives in a blizzard and demands the city gates are barred. As Abydos falls under her spell, the dead return, but do not speak...|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|For eight years the city is a place of slow death, frosty ecstacy and silent beauty, but in the ninth year a Conspiracy of Shouts is mounted against the quiet that Chione demands. The conspirators open the city gates, and a scarred man comes to drag Chione out by the hair. Summer returns, but the conspirators die of remorse.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides 1 ''[[Snow Stories|Lesson: Snow Stories]]'' and [[Memory: Regret]]. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Regret]].

It Is Written.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=It_Is_Written.png |mystery=8 |principles={{Lore|Scale}} |tally_price=3 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Inks of Power]] |memory=[[Confounding Parable]] |period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Scale}} Principle, written in English by [[Musgrave Dewulf]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Musgrave, fourth of the Dewulf line, writes tentatively about the 'Covenant of Brancrug' and the legacy of the sacred inks he calls 'encausta potentialia'.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'As the Light passeth through a Prism into many Colours, so the Great Inks separateth into the Lesser Inks, and the Lesser Inks into Inks Minor…'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Musgrave coyly refuses to talk of the Great Inks (or else refuses to admit he doesn't know much about them). He insists that yewgall and stargall, which can be mixed with sufficient Nectar or Sky aspect, are sufficient for 'most befitting Purposes'.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Inks of Power|Lesson: Inks of Power]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Confounding Parable]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Scale]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]] [[Category:Baronial]]

Damascene Traditions of the House of Let.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=Damascene Traditions of the House of Lethe
|mystery=8
|tally_price=4
|type=[[Codex]]

|skill=[[Sacra Limiae]]

'''Damascene Traditions of the House of Lethe''' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Sky]] principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The House of Lethe was an order of immortals who sought obscurity, rejecting their past and future. If the author of this short text is to be believed, the initiates of the Damascene branch were much more radical than their fellows elsewhere.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The House generally forbade any potentially procreative activities, for fear of the terrible consequences of two Long bearing a child. The Damascene order took this much further…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|At one point, male initiates were required to undergo castration, and female initiates to strangle any children they had previously borne. These measures were so horrific that the Order was shaken by repeated schisms, and eventually absorbed into the local Sisterhood of the Knot as a society of healers and exorcists.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides 2 ''[[Sacra Limiae|Lesson: Sacra Limiae]]''. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

De motu corporum vetitorum.title: De motu corporum vetitorum
De motu corporum vetitorum.text:
{{Book_(BoH) |mystery=10 |tally_price=2 |type=[[Codex]] |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |language=English |Period=[[Curia Period|Curia]] |image1=De motu corporum vetitorum.png |skill=[[Ouranoscopy]] |memory=[[Memory: Storm]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} Principle, written in English by [[Abelard Hubris]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{quote|The author rejoices in the name of 'Abelard Hubris', and the title might be translated as 'On the Forbidden Motions of Bodies' - evidently a reference to Newton's 'De Motu Corporem', published some twenty years previously.|}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Hubris's thesis: that stars, planets and other bodies are the proxies or even essences of the Hours, and that conjunctions and occlusions reveal the outcome of Hour-intrigues in the Mansus.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Hubris declares that the Great Comet of 1577 was the physical embodiment of the Hour named Madrugad; that It disintegrated but its fragments gravitate to bone-marrow, where they can be located even now. He insists that Ouranoscopic techniques can be used with Essential Periost and sufficient Winter to create a 'talisman gerifugic'.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Ouranoscopy|Lesson: Ouranoscopy]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Storm]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Curia]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Sky]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

Gospel of Nicodemus.title: Gospel of Nicodemus
Gospel of Nicodemus.text: {{Book (BoH) |title1=Gospel of Nicodemus |mystery=6 |tally_price=4 |type=[[Codex]] |image1=[[File:GospelofNicodemus.png]] |Period=[[Solar]] |memory=[[Memory: Revelation]] |principles={{Lore|Lantern}} |skill=[[Sacra Solis Invicti]]}} '''''Gospel of Nicodemus''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|An apocryphal account of the works and experiences of the Shepherd Illuminate by one of his supposed companions.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'Inventori Lucis Soli Invicto Nuntio' reads the dedication - loosely translatable as 'I am the herald of the Sun Unconquerable, Light's Contriver'. This is a variation on the more usual 'invicto augusto', the declaration which united the eastern and western traditions of the Church Solar.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The Shepherd Illuminate, the Virgin-Born, warns of the Sun's Division but promises its ultimate reunification in the Second Dawn 'through the ministry of St Uzult'. [[Uzult]] is of course the ink of power used by Librarians of the Tree, but also venerated as a saint in some borderline heterodox solar traditions.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Sacra Solis Invicti|Lesson: Sacra Solis Invicti]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Lantern]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Solar]]

'''Codex Acephali''' is a [[book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written in [[Latin]].

Selecting the book provides the following description: 
{{Quote|Sometimes called 'The Book of the Clean Skull'. The book contains accounts of enlightenments available through the gradual, surgical removal of the lobes of the brain.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|It becomes clear that the processes described are mostly allegorical or metaphorical descriptions of Winter techniques for less revolting occult work. Even the metaphors are pretty horrible, though.|I'm reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|The author explains adaptations of these techniques, with sufficient Winter aspect, to harvest a mysterious substance described as the '[[Essential Periost|rags of the final bone]]' from the remains of almost any animal…|I've read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Snow Stories|Lesson: Snow Stories]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Regret]].

{{Quote|Omar describes his work in the construction of mirrors for the enclosure of a sacred flame, and his slow realisation of 'a Flaw in the Glass'.|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Omar explains how his lightsmithing techniques can be used, in the presence of sufficient Lantern, to enrich [[Xanthotic Essence]] into [[Uzult|'the Great Ink of the First History'.]] But he pleads caution in its use… 'lest the Chandler be Realised.'|I've Read...}}

{{Book (BoH) |mystery=14 |principles={{Lore|Knock}} |tally_price=3 |language=[[Fucine]] |type=[[Codex]] |image1=File:Death_Evasion.png |period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]] |memory=[[Memory: A Stolen Secret]] |skill=[[Edicts Liminal]]}} __NOTOC__
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written in [[Fucine]] by [[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Father Stanislav John Schaller writes of the means and limitation of passage between the orders of the Mansus - Know, Long, Names, Hours. Unusually, Father John has written this book in Fucine - for, he says, especial secrecy.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|He speaks very cautiously of the exceptions that can sometimes be made to the edicts of Chancel and Calyptra, and hints at the means by which he successfully returned a Lantern-long to flesh...|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Schaller mentions most cautiously of all that he has been permitted to see a book that speaks more deeply on the matter, but that it was surrendered 'into the shadow of a covenant-stone of the Watchman's Tree.' It can be retrieved if 'the ninety-ninth wink is reserved under the Edicts Liminal.'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Edicts Liminal|Lesson: Edicts Liminal]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: A Stolen Secret]]. ==Special Interactions== Presenting [[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] this book prompts unique dialogue. {{Quote|I'm surprised that it's found its way here... but that's Hush House, I suppose. May I refresh my memory? I remember that I wrote about the Galmier business - not as cautiously as I might have...}} Schaller will examine the book and return it to you, along with a ''[[Edicts Liminal|Lesson: Edicts Liminal]]''. He will not leave after this interaction. {{Quote|That law I will not name aloud - the law of the three - it can be defied. It is rarely wise to attempt that defiance. The penalty of failure is paid by one - but the penalty of success, by many. I would ask you, Librarian, to remember that, when you decide how to address yourself to Eternity. But I already have faith in your judgement. Thank you for the loan of the book.}} [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Baronial]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Knock]] [[Category:Readable]]

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The poem elliptically describes a war between beasts, weather phenomena, and arcane concepts. It's quite specific about their tactics.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Two-One joined, and the Horned distinguished. Consequently, blood.'|I've Read...}}
==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Disciplines of the Scar|Lesson: Disciplines of the Scar]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Contradiction|Contradiction]].

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Black nephrite and scolecite, for Nowhere; orichalc and amber, for Ys; amethyst for the Night Key of the Spider Door...|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Eva points out - bitterly? - that there is no shortage of uplifting parables and proverbs about the saving graces of a flaw in a jewel; but that no-one, 'not jeweller, not priest, not Hour' has ever found a way to repair such a flaw.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides one ''[[Anbary & Lapidary|Lesson: Anbary & Lapidary]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Foresight]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Sky]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]] [[Category:Baronial]]

Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1927.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=CucurbitPrisonerRecords1927.png |mystery=12 |principles={{Lore|Nectar}} |tally_price=1 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Insects & Nectars]] |memory=[[Memory: Impulse]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Nectar}} Principle, written in English by [[George Collers]]' private secretary of interventions and experiments. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Accounts by Governor Collers' private secretary of interventions and experiments in the last years of the Cucurbit prison, focusing particularly on prisoners he believes might have Carapace Cross lineage.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Two prisoners suspected of oneiric crimes are encouraged to access their inner Carapace Cross tendencies, and develop the attributes of the Seglaz-kind ('sickle-formed pseudocrustacea'). Regrettably they lose the ability to breathe air; one dies and Collers releases the other into the sea.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Collers describes how he's successfully induced an unstable Carapace-larva to develop into a greater form, using Insects and Nectars techniques in the context of considerable Moon-aspect to 'awaken what would rather remain hidden'. He hopes that similar techniques might be used to expedite the moral development of prisoners...|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Insects & Nectars|Lesson: Insects & Nectars]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Impulse]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Nectar]] [[Category:Nocturnal]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

He was in fact hung as a witch at the age of tweny-four, and never inherited the estate…|I'm Reading...}}After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|Bryan describes how a [[Mazarine Fife|'Sky-inspired fife']] can be prepared using these Fur and Feathers techniques, in the presence of greater {{lore|Sky}}-aspect, to 'make of the winds good neighbours.' It's a powerful technique to be described so casually: Brian's main interest seems to be in ensuring good weather for his hunts.|I've Read...}}
