De Ratio Quercuum.title: De Ratio Quercuum
De Ratio Quercuum.text:
{{Book (BoH) |mystery=8 |principles={{Lore|Nectar}} |tally_price=2 |language=[[Latin]] |skill=[[Rites of the Roots]] |memory=[[Earth-Sign]] |period=[[Curia Period|Curia]] |type=[[Codex]] |image1=[[File:DeRatioQuercuum.png]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Nectar}} Principle, written in [[Latin]] by [[Nathaniel Darcy-Evers]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{quote|In English the title translates roughly as 'the Account of the Oaks'; but this is Nathaniel Darcy-Evers' fascinating, if haphazard, survey of the occult properties of every tree he can find, not just oaks.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'In Persia taxus baccata, the yew, is called sorkhdar, which is 'the red tree'. There they had long understood the Grail-Root. In later times, the Great King of Pontus had bee-hives set in the branches of the oldest of the female trees….'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'The berries of the Pontine Yew open the door to death but the honey of their flowers opens a different door entirely. This was not the Great King's mithridate but one who has suckled at the Great Yew fears poison no longer. Perhaps they should…' Nathaniel is here distracted, however, by the toxic properties of certain inks. He does mention more usefully that the minor Ink of Power, Yewgall, can be brewed through the Rites of the Roots with the assistance of the aspect Nectar.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Rites of the Roots|Lesson: Rites of the Roots]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Earth-Sign]]. This is one of only two books that generate this memory, the other being ''[[Rapt in the King]]''. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Nectar]] [[Category:Curia]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

From History to Eternity.title: From History to Eternity
From History to Eternity.text: {{Book (BoH) |title1=From History to Eternity |mystery=10 |tally_price=2 |type=[[Codex]] |principles={{Lore|Moth}} |Period=[[Nocturnal]] |image1=[[File:FromHistorytoEternity.png]] |memory=[[Intuition]] |skill=[[Inks of Revelation]]}} '''''From History to Eternity''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|A contraband manual of the Inks of Revelation. The author explains in a brief foreword that she is a high-ranking officer of 'an agency of the Duties' and that, though she supports its mission, she has concerns about the long-term consequences of its work.|Description}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|‘All Histories braided into a golden loop; a shining ascent to Eternity. I had never imagined I could be afraid that there might be too few Truths. I could be wrong. But I'd like to leave at least one door ajar.’|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|‘‘[[Ichor Auroral]]’ can be brewed into an [[Encaustum Terminale|encaustum terminale]] associated with the Second History, using Inks of Revelation techniques with Rose aspect. The author warns that this is exceptionally difficult, since these techniques aren't aligned with Rose. ‘But that's why I'm hoping the door will stay ajar, even once all the others are closed. I wish you luck.'’|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of the book generates [[Inks of Revelation|Lesson: Inks of Revelation x2]] and [[Memory: Intuition]]. Subsequent [[Consider|consideration]] of the book produces only [[Memory: Intuition]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Moth]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Nocturnal]]

Glimmerings.title: Glimmerings
Glimmerings.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=[[File:Glimmerings.png]] |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Forge}} |tally_price=1 |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Sights & Sensations]] |memory=[[Bittersweet Certainty]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|An anonymous prison diary written by a dreamer convicted of 'oneiric irresponsibility' and confined to the Cucurbit.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The prisoner is plainly terrified and bewildered by their situation, and has been unable to wrangle a coherent explanation out of anyone. But the dreams keep coming, and they keep writing them down…|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Snow; broken mirrors; half-heard sky music; flowers of white, red and black; a blood-streaked winter dawn... the most notorious signifiers of oneiric risk, fantastically vivid and detailed. No wonder they were locked up. Their final recorded dream is of a 'worm-jewel' beneath Brancrug Isle, which they open with a key carved from their finger-bone.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sights & Sensations|Lesson: Sights & Sensations]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Bittersweet Certainty]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Forge]] [[Category:Nocturnal]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]]

Enchiridion Tragularis.title: Enchiridion Tragularis
Enchiridion Tragularis.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|mystery=14
|principles={{Lore|Moon}}
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Greek]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Serpents & Venoms]]
|memory=[[Intuition|Memory: Intuition]]
|image1=[[File:EnchiridionTragularis.png]]
|Period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}}
'''''Enchiridion Tragularis''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written in [[Greek]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The poison-manual of the order of assassins called the Tragulari.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Tragulari - 'dartsmen' - were employed by the Duties in their various incarnations to hunt down inhuman troublemakers. They developed poisons that even the immortals called Long could not withstand…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Immunity to their own poisons was a constant concern for the Tragulari, and they constantly dosed themselves with substances that might built up immunity. Perinculate, the notoriously toxic Unsanctioned Ink, can be used as a base for one of these - Serpent-Milk - with sufficient Scale and with arts of Serpents and Venoms.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides [[Serpents & Venoms|''Lesson: Serpents & Venoms'']] x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Intuition]].

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Dawn]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Moon]]
[[Category:Readable]]

How the End will Begin.title: How the End will Begin
How the End will Begin.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=[[File:How the End Will Begin.png]]
|mystery=14
|principles={{Lore|Edge}}
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Vak]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Ragged Crossroads]]
|memory=[[Memory: Fear]]
|period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} Principle written in [[Vak]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A prophecy of the Wars of the Roads, recorded in the Subcontinent in the days before the Great Hooded Princes.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|In the foretold war, the Children of the Leashed Flame march on the cities of the Continent, but the 'Enactors of Solar Law' and the 'Triple Sisterhood' join forces to hold them back... at tremendous cost.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘In that battle between the Imperishable Legions and the Leashed Flame, the Legions will perish and the Flame will be unleashed.’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Ragged Crossroads|Lesson: Ragged Crossroads]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]]. 

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Edge]]
[[Category:Dawn]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Readable]]

Honey: the Comprehensive Guide.title: Honey: the Comprehensive Guide
Honey: the Comprehensive Guide.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=Honey: the Comprehensive Guide
|mystery=6
|tally_price=1
|language=
|memory=[[Memory: Contradiction]]
|skill=[[Insects & Nectars]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|principles=[[Nectar]]
|image1=[[File:Honey The Comprehensive Guide.png]]
|period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}}
'''''Honey: the Comprehensive Guide''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Nectar]] principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Harvey Hattington - pilot, polymath, confectioner - writes with great enthusiasm about the 'marvellous work of the Bee'.|}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Hattington insists that all the primary aspects - Nectar, Scale, Heart, Lantern, Moth, Grail - are possessed by bees and expressed in honey. (Clearly, he points out, there are only six primary aspects, as a honeycomb has only six angles.)|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|'Yewgall Ink is prepared with these techniques - but so is Skinshuck Mead, and only Skinshuck requires honey. Just as any beverage or foodstuff can be improved with the addition of honey, so any garden is improved with the presence of bees. Even those bloody Blomberende.'|I've Read...}}
==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book gives ''[[Insects & Nectars|Lesson: Insects & Nectars]]''. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Contradiction]].

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Nectar]]
[[Category:Nocturnal]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Readable]]

De Horis book 1.title: De Horis book 1
De Horis book 1.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=De Horis book 1.png |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Nectar}} |tally_price=3 |language=[[Latin]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Rites of the Roots]] |memory=[[Memory: Impulse]] |period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Nectar}} Principle, written in [[Latin]] by an unknown author. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|An occasionally coherent catalogue of the secret gods, organised by hour. This is a reprint, but in the original Latin.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|This volume deals mostly with the Hours of the Wood: the Moth, the Black-Flax, the Ring-Yew, among others.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'The Glory is a question, and the Moth always answers 'Yes'.'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Rites of the Roots|Lesson: Rites of the Roots]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Impulse]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Nectar]] [[Category:Baronial]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

Inaam, Kapigiginlupir, Garkie, Cryppys.title: Inaam, Kapigiginlupir, Garkie, Cryppys
Inaam, Kapigiginlupir, Garkie, Cryppys.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=Inaam, Kapigiginlupir, Garkie, Cryppys.png
|mystery=14
|principles={{Lore|Moth}}
|tally_price=2
|language=[[Phrygian]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Transformations & Liberations]]
|memory=[[Memory: Foresight]]
|period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle written in [[Phrygian]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|In which four enigmatic figures tell the stories they've heard over the years at the Roost, the secret location where the aviform Hours congregate.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|INAAM: Has not the Beach-Crow shared his treasures? GARKIE: Not the rarest. He takes those things most precious, which he claims found, not stolen.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Beach-Crow, Kapigiginlupir suggests, is not only a thief, but also a spy and even a voyeur. He has hidden the memory of secret couplings among the Hours and their Names in the corners of the House, as treasures to gloat over. There is particularly fevered speculation on a liaison between the Ring-Yew, that fervent hour of the Wood, and the Mare-in-the-Tree, who sometimes has been the Witch's Sister.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Transformations & Liberations|Lesson: Transformations & Liberations]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

[[Category:Moth]]
[[Category:Curia]]
[[Category:Codex]]

Isaac of Karth's History of the Shadowle.title: Isaac of Karth's History of the Shadowless Kings
Isaac of Karth's History of the Shadowle.text:
{{Book (BoH) |title1=Isaac of Karth's History
of the Shadowless Kings |image1=Isaac of Karth.png |mystery=14 |principles={{Lore|Rose}} |tally_price=5 |language=[[Aramaic]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Sand Stories]] |memory=[[Confounding Parable]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Rose}} Principle, written in [[Aramaic]] by [[Isaac of Karth]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|'A True and Accurate History of the Shadowless Kings, by Isaac of Karth.' Isaac describes the thousand-year ascendancy of the Shadowless Empire.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'The first and greatest history' is described herein. The Persian Empire - 'the sons of Achaemenes', 'the Shadowless Kings', 'the most Glorious Empire' - survives the assaults of Alexander the Great and flourishes as late as the fifth century.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|
After the fall of Rome, the Shadowless Empire takes Byzantium under its wing, and moves East against the Land of the Great River. Isaac begins to recount the invasion struggling against 'the unskinned armies of the hooded serpents', but ends abruptly with a series of incantations that he claims allowed the Shadowless Empire to persist.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sand Stories|Lesson: Sand Stories]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Confounding Parable]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Rose]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1928.title: Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1928
Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1928.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1928
|mystery=12
|skill=[[Hill & Hollow]]
|memory=[[Memory: Salt]]
|tally_price=1
|type=[[Codex]]
|principles={{Lore|Scale}}
|Period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]|image1=Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1928.png}}
'''Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1928''' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Scale]] principle written by [[George Collers|Governor Collers]]' unnamed secretary.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Accounts by Governor Collers' private secretary of interventions and experiments in the last years of the Cucurbit prison, focusing particularly on the 'hill-children', wild Wood-things that have found a shape in the physical world.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Something called a 'Singlefoot', a horned mountain-dweller, is brought back from some kind of embassy to the Grove of Green Immortals. Collers expresses his irritation that Gervinus van Lauren refuses to assist in its containment.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Singlefoot somehow conjures an earthquake that cracks the tower and enables its escape. Collers determines that it should not have been permitted to dream while kept beneath the earth: it had access to sufficient Scale aspect to use its 'arts of Hill and Hollow' to develop an Old Moment into an Earthquake Name. He mandates above-ground confinement for all hill-children prisoners in the future.|I've Read...}}
==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides 2 ''[[Hill & Hollow|Lesson: Hill & Hollow]]''. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Salt]].

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Nocturnal]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Scale]]
[[Category:Readable]]

EXPERIMENT BEYOND SIGHT.title: EXPERIMENT BEYOND SIGHT
EXPERIMENT BEYOND SIGHT.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=EXPERIMENT BEYOND SIGHT
|mystery=8
|principles={{Lore|Moon}}
|tally_price=1
|type=[[Reel of Film]]
|skill=[[Edicts Inviolable]]
|memory=[[Memory: Revelation]]
|image1=[[File:EXPERIMENT BEYOND SIGHT.png]]
|Period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}}
'''EXPERIMENT BEYOND SIGHT''' is a [[Reel of Film]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} principle by [[Ilse Bischoff]]. As a film, it can only be mastered with the [[Projector]].

==Description==
Selecting the film provides the following description:
{{Quote|Ilse Bischoff's bewildering, widely derided final film.}}

Upon choosing to master the film, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The film is an unrelenting fusillade of apparently unrelated images - birth, mirrors, grain-threshers, animal attacks, crowds at stations… but a single image appears again and again, dominating the rush of images until the film is only a single static shot.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The repeating image is a view through a grimy window-pane of a nearby tower. There is a vague impression of flickering light around the tower-top. Just as the film ends, smoke plumes from the tower. That's it. Nothing of note at all… unless one happens to recognise the view of the Crucible Tower from the window of the Librarian's Quarters, and unless one happens to know that Ilse Bischoff never visited Brancrug, or even Britain, before her untimely death.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the film provides [[Edicts Inviolable|''Lesson: Edicts Inviolable'']] x2. Watching the film always provides [[Memory: Revelation]].


[[Category:Nocturnal]]
[[Category:Reel of Film]]
[[Category:Moon]]
[[Category:Readable]]

Green Jasper Tablet.title: Green Jasper Tablet
Green Jasper Tablet.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=Green Jasper Tablet|mystery=10|category=[[Readable]]|tally_price=5|language=[[Cracktrack]]|type=[[Codex]]|principles={{Lore|Nectar}}|image1=Green Jasper Tablet.png|period=[[Dawn]]|skill=[[Rites of the Roots]]|memory=[[Memory: Impulse]]}}Green Jasper Tablet is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Nectar}} principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:{{quote|Supposedly copied from a tablet of green jasper which serves as the Covenant-stone of the Monastery of the Fifth Cup - the token which gives that Library shelter beneath the Watchman's Tree.|}}Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|Humankind hid itself from the Glory's light in the Roots of the Watchman's Tree. But for every chink we stuffed with cloth and hair, we opened another, and the light crept in. Until we looked below, into Nowhere, and the Eye of the Mare-in-the-Tree winked Red...|I'm Reading...}}After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|The Tablet expounds the dangers of inviting in the Nowhere-Hour called the Mare-in-the-Tree, and also of forbidding her entry, since she can never entirely be denied. Along the way, it reveals the secret of the Sacrament Malachite ('in which the merry Mare merrily spits') - brewed with the Rites of the Roots from the numa-pear, in the presence of sufficient Nectar-aspect.|I've Read...}}
==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates  2 [[Rites of the Roots|Lesson: Rites of the Roots]]. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].


This book suggests a recipe

COLOURS IN THE LIVER.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=COLOURS IN THE LIVER
|mystery=6
|principles={{Lore|Grail}}
|tally_price=1
|type=[[Reel of Film]]
|image1=[[Colours in the Liver.png]]
|Period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]
|memory=[[Memory: Revelation]]
|skill=[[Resurgences & Emergences]]}}
'''''COLOURS IN THE LIVER''''' is a [[Reel of Film]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle by [[Ilse Bischoff]]. As a film, it can only be mastered with the [[Projector]].

==Description==
Selecting the film provides the following description:
{{Quote|Ilse Bischoff's most controversial film, blamed for outbreaks of cannibalistic killings in Tiflis and Leipzig.}}

Upon choosing to master the film, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|A gang of heretic priests agrees to strike the 'fear of the Change' into the infuriatingly atheist citizenry. At night they dress as four-winged angels and crawl down chimneys and through windows to savage members of their congregation.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The priests are caught by unidentified figures wearing heavily mandibled masks, like grotesque caricatures of ants. They are force-fed larvae: a final caption indicates that at dawn the larvae will hatch…|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the film provides ''[[Resurgences & Emergences|Lesson: Resurgences & Emergences]]'' x1. Watching it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]].

[[Category:Nocturnal]]
[[Category:Reel of Film]]
[[Category:Grail]]

In Memory of Gods.title: In Memory of Gods
In Memory of Gods.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=In Memory of Gods.png |mystery=12 |principles={{Lore|Winter}} |tally_price=5 |language=[[Fucine]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Ragged Crossroads]] |memory=[[Memory: Hindsight]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} Principle, written in [[Fucine]] by the [[Barrowchild]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|The 'Barrowchild', a nameless Gaulish adept who joined an organisation identified as the Ordo Limiae, writes regretfully of the destruction of the gods-who-were-stone - the Hours who preceded humanity.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The Barrowchild singles out the Scarred Tribune, the Red Grail, the Forge and the Moth for especial condemnation as murderers of the first gods. 'We live in the shadow of their crime', she writes, 'and we must evade it or repeat it.'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The Barrowchild describes how the Grail drained the Hour called Tide, how the Moth 'usurped the Wheel from within', stealing its skin, and how the Forge first eclipsed then shattered Flint. 'Perhaps these are glories,' she observes, 'but then it cannot be that Glory is merciful.'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Ragged Crossroads|Lesson: Ragged Crossroads]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Hindsight]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Winter]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

Echidnalia.title: Echidnalia
Echidnalia.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=Echidnalia.png |mystery=21 |principles={{Lore|Scale}} |tally_price=2 |language=[[Cracktrack]] |type=[[Codex]], [[Multitudinous]] |skill=[[Stone Stories]] |memory=[[Memory: Impulse]] |period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Multitudinous]] [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Scale}} Principle, written in [[Cracktrack]] by an unknown author. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Part genealogy, part taxonomy, part family gossip - a closely detailed, highly specialised account of one branch of the complex brood of children associated with the Ligeian Echidna.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The gods-who-were-Stone knew the uses of the Biting Key, and now Echidna claims it. She has birthed so many children, and some yet survive.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Echidna's children are of two kinds: 'born' and 'won'. She seems to have had some success in winning over the creations of other powers to her service. In particular she has a habit of giving sustenance to the labhites, who consume what is found in the sky, and seducing them away from the Lionsmith...|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Stone Stories|Lesson: Stone Stories]]'' (x3). Reading always provides [[Memory: Impulse]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Scale]] [[Category:Curia]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Multitudinous]] [[Category:Thing]]

Five Creations.title: Five Creations
Five Creations.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=Five Creations
|mystery=14
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Vak]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|principles={{Lore|Moth}}
|Period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]
|memory=[[Memory: Gossip]]
|skill=[[Resurgences & Emergences]]
|image1=Five Creations.png}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle written in [[Vak]] by [[Shohei]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|The itinerant scholar Shohei debated five possible origins for humanity with a hooded figure since claimed to be the Beach-Crow. Shohei later claimed that all these accounts had proven false, but the debate was, nevertheless, recorded.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|THE CARAPACE ORIGIN: we were born from shell, like the children of the wasp from the spider. THE GLORIOUS ORIGIN: our life-motes descended from Light. THE ORIGIN BEFOULED: we were found naked and smeared with muck in the roots of the Wood...'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Shohei's preferred theories are that we are the children of apes who walked upright, although his tone here is satirical; or that we consumed not only our parents, 'which is not the Crime of the Sky', but also our origin, so that we came from Nowhere.|I've Read...}}
==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Resurgences & Emergences|Lesson: Resurgences & Emergences]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Gossip]].

==Trivia==
*All mentioned origins of humanity except the origin from primates can be written as a [[Determination]] in the [[Journals|Journal]], although only one origin can be written in the Journal at a time. The Carapace origin is {{Lore|Scale}}, the Glorious Origin is {{Lore|Lantern}}, the Origin Befouled is {{Lore|Nectar}} and the Nowhere origin is {{Lore|Sky}}.

Commandments For the Preservation of All.title: Commandments For the Preservation of All That Exists
Commandments For the Preservation of All.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=Commandments For the Preservation of All That Exists
|mystery=14
|principles={{Lore|Heart}}
|tally_price=4
|language=[[Deep Mandaic]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|image1=[[File:CommandmentsForthePreservationofAllThatExists.png]]
|period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar Gothic]]
|skill=[[Stitching & Binding]]
|memory=[[Memory: Satisfaction]]}}
'''''Commandments For the Preservation of All That Exists''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle written in [[Deep Mandaic]] by [[Black Elie]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Black Elie, Damascene Matriarch of the Sisterhood of the Knot, was imprisoned by the emperor Didius Julianus. She reportedly instructed that these secret doctrines be recorded in writing to preserve against their loss. Regrettably, the story goes, Didius Julianus ordered that the work be entombed with her in an unmarked sepulcher.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Elie describes powerful protective incantations to be used in a variety of circumstances.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|'It is essential that these Protections be completed every fourth year, to defend against the entry of the Worms and against the avidity of the Wave and the Wound.' In the current History at least, there is no indication that these Protections have been performed regularly for at least the last thousand years.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Stitching & Binding|Lesson: Stitching & Binding]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Satisfaction]].

In The Mountains As Upon The Plain There.title: In The Mountains As Upon The Plain There May Not Be A Path Where None Has Passed
In The Mountains As Upon The Plain There.text:
{{Book (BoH) |title1=In The Mountains
As Upon The Plain
There May Not Be A Path
Where None Has Passed |image1=In The Mountains As Upon The Plain There May Not Be A Path Where None Has Passed.png |mystery=18 |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |tally_price=5 |language=[[Vak]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Sky Stories]] |memory=[[Memory: Gossip]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} Principle, written in [[Vak]] by [[Nyn|Ninegala of Lagash]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Ninegala of Lagash describes the secrets to be found in mountains.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Ninegala tells a number of lively stories about riddling ogres and wars between mountain tribes, but turns sombre in the tale of the Empty-Handed Hunter: a lover of the Grail who sought to match her appetites and join her as an Hour, but in the end rent and devoured himself, giving his name to the mountains he had once roamed.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Ninegala claims that the Hours who sometimes manifest as birds - the Laughingthrush, the Ivory Dove, the Beachcrow and the Witch-and-Sister - meet at a secret location on a mountaintop to exchange gossip unheard by their peers. Now and then a mortal overhears them. The mortal is always obliterated, and the meeting-place always changed.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sky Stories|Lesson: Sky Stories]]'' (x3). Reading always provides [[Memory: Gossip]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Sky]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

Journal of Sir David Greene, 1903.title: Journal of Sir David Greene, 1903
Journal of Sir David Greene, 1903.text:
__NOTOC__ {{Spoiler Header}} {{Spoilers |caption_element=h3 |content= {{Book (BoH) |title1=Journal of
Sir David Greene, 1903 |image1=[[File:Journal of Sir David Greene, 1903.png]] |mystery=14 |principles={{Lore|Edge}} |tally_price=4 |language=[[Hyksos]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Sharps]] |memory=[[Memory: Fear]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} Principle, written in [[Hyksos]] by [[Sir David Greene]]. == Location == {{Spoilers |caption_element=h3 |content = This item can be found in the [[Librarian's Quarters]] by clicking a hidden panel between the foot of the stairs and the fireplace. A hidden compartment will be opened, revealing a small bookshelf containing the ''{{PAGENAME}}''.}} == Description == Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|A confidential journal kept by Greene, former Nocturnal Branch Superindent but, by 1903, Librarian of the House. Greene has kept his journal in Hyksos, presumably as an extra measure of privacy.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|In 1903, the House co-operated closely with the Branch, and Greene was the public face of that co-operation. In private, however, Greene is clearly disillusioned with the Branch, which he increasingly regards as irresponsible. He is especially concerned about the construction of a 'suppressive mechanism' beneath Brancrug Gaol, and its likely occupant.

'Hours and Names are dangerous,' he writes, 'but at least our dealings have the benefit of long experience. An Hour who acts before she is born - who leaves those places she has never entered - if her Names walk the world already, how can we understand their courses and their capabilities?'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The last entries alternate between calculations (tides, dates, financial calculations) and expressions of fevered longing for 'A.F'. It seems that Greene intends to run away with A.F., and some of the calculations imply that he has been embezzling funds to that end, under cover of the chaos caused by the Ortucchio Incident and the subsequent reorganisation of Nocturnal Branch into the Suppression Bureau...

The entries, however, stop abruptly before the year's end. It's not clear whether Greene did in fact abscond with funds and fond friend, or whether he abandoned this journal for other reasons.|I've Read...}} == Rewards == Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sharps|Lesson: Sharps]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]]. }} [[Category:Secret]] [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Edge]] [[Category:Nocturnal Period]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]]

On Resonance.text:
{{Book_(BoH)
|mystery=6

'''''On Resonance''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} principle by [[Everett Vinzant]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Experiments in ithastry by the 'sky-smith' Everett Vinzant.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Vinzant suggests percussion instruments that might be 'sympathetic' to a number of Hours and Names. Some are more likely than others.|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Vinzant uncontroversially suggests drums of various materials as the sympathetic instrument for the Thunderskin and its 'ascendant duendrazones'. He proposes bells of bronze and iron for the Lionsmith and Colonel. He spends time on the design of a 'bee-rattle' for the Malachite, but doesn't seem entirely confident of his findings...|I've Read...}}
==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides a ''[[Bells & Brazieries|Lesson: Bells & Brazieries]]''. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

Opus Magnum Caeruleum.title: Opus Magnum Caeruleum
Opus Magnum Caeruleum.text:
{{Book_(BoH)
|title1=Opus Magnum Caeruleum
|mystery=14
|principles={{Lore|Lantern}}
|tally_price=3
|type=[[Codex]]
|Period=[[Baronial]]
|image1=Opus Magnus Caeruleus.png
|memory=[[Memory: Foresight]]
|skill=[[Pyroglyphics]]}}
'''''Opus Magnum Caeruleum''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|[[Ambrose Westcott]] used to render the title of this venerable and anonymous work mockingly as 'the Big Blue Business'. A kinder translation would be 'the Great Work in Azure'.
}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The reasons for Westcott's enmity to this work are clear to any pyroglyphicist: it was written at least two centuries before he was born, but anticipates or undermines many of his preferred conclusions.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The 'Work' in question is the creation of the 'blue gold' allegedly necessary for the terrible Rite which allows a Forge-long to become a Name. The book mentions that Pyroglyphics techniques can be used with Forge to create [[Iotic Essence]] as a necessary component; but withholds the final step, insisting that the consequences are too dire, and that any interest should remain only a matter of theory.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Pyroglyphics|Lesson: Pyroglyphics]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]]

Oblations in Iron.title: Oblations in Iron
Oblations in Iron.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=OblationsinIron.png |mystery=6 |principles={{Lore|Winter}} |tally_price=2 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Inks of Containment]] |memory=[[Memory: Hindsight]] |period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} Principle, written in English by [[Little Sophia]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|A Monster-hunting initiate of the Hour named the Colonel, who identifies herself as 'Little Sophia', records the exhibits she has rendered to the Worm Museum in the Mansus.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Little Sophia has never visited the Worm Museum, or even the Mansus, in person, and evidently has no desire to do so. She mixes ink which incorporates the remains of her prey, writes her records in that ink, then burns them before the Colonel's altar…|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'It is essential however to permit no drop of the ink thereby obtained to enter any portal of the body, even a break in the barrier of the skin. Should any fragment of the Worm remain viable, it might enter thereby, and the Hunt's ultimate conclusion be melancholy indeed...'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Inks of Containment|Lesson: Inks of Containment]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Hindsight]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Winter]] [[Category:Curia]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

Kitling Ripe's Tasty Treats.title: Kitling Ripe's Tasty Treats
Kitling Ripe's Tasty Treats.text: {{Book (BoH)|title1=Kitling Ripe's Tasty Treats|mystery=[[Nectar]] 4|category=[[Book]]|tally_price=3|type=[[Readable]], [[Thing]], [[Codex]]|image1=[[File:KitlingRipesTastyTreats.png|thumb]]|Period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]|memory=[[Memory: Satisfaction]]|skill=[[Spices & Savours]]}}''Kitling Ripe's Tasty Treats'' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Nectar]] principle. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description:{{Quote|The Velvet is the Hour of secrets; and so very little is known of the - Moth-long? Nectar-long? - who ascend to immortality under her auspices. But this book (by 'Kitling's Friend') purports to be part cook-book, and part manual for immortality.|Description}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|Kitling Ripe is the name usually given to the speechless 'but never silent' cat-thing that serves as a Name of the Velvet. Kitling Ripe, it seems, enjoys hunting immortals; and the Velvet is very fond of Kitling Ripe.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|The secret, it appears, is to arouse the Kitling's appetite enough to become her quarry, but not quite enough to be caught. The Velvet permits the game, since it culls immortals careless enough to attract attention, and keeps her Name happy. The author bemoans the loss of the Carapace Cross' savour-secrets, which apparently were particularly tempting - but suggests decent spice-substitutes, which also happen to make for excellent pigeon-pie.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of the book generates [[Spices & Savours|Lesson: Spices & Savours]] and [[Memory: Satisfaction]]. Subsequent [[Consider|consideration]] of the book produces only [[Memory: Satisfaction]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Nectar]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Codex]]

One Hundred And Eight.title: One Hundred And Eight
One Hundred And Eight.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=OneHundredAndEight.png |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Scale}} |tally_price=3 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |memory=[[Confounding Parable]] |period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Scale}} Principle, written in English by Eva Dewulf. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Eva Dewulf discurses on the Fifth History, and particularly on those who are said to have 'passed over' from it - the Great Hooded Princes, the Knock-long who ascended under the Mother of Ants but now (so Eva claims) honour the Horned-Axe.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|
'The Great Hooded Princes call their library the Tomb of Lies, and this has given rise to a foolish tradition that the Princes are habitual liars. Of course, in fact, Truth flourishes when Lies are slain. On the other hand, the Princes do not say 'Knowledge is Power', but rather, 'Power is Knowledge.'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Eva has, to her regret, never visited the Library. She notes that it is said to be 'west of the Lion, and north of Victory' - and suggests that, although the Princes are generally associated with India, their library might be farther East…|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Pentiments & Precursors|Lesson: Pentiments & Precursors]]''. Reading always provides [[Confounding Parable]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Scale]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]] [[Category:Baronial]]

Journal of Walter Dewulf.title: Journal of Walter Dewulf
Journal of Walter Dewulf.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=Journal of Walter Dewulf
|mystery=6

'''''Journal of Walter Dewulf''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle written by [[Walter Dewulf]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Walter Dewulf, 3rd Baron Brancrug, was grandson of [[Thomas Dewulf|Thomas]], son of the disgraced [[Giles Dewulf|Giles]], who eloped with 'Pale Hafren'. The Dewulf line might have ended here if the Seneschale [[Ernestine Peterhans|Ernestine]] - by then over eighty - had not managed to reconcile Thomas with a dying Giles.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Walter, though nominally siding with the Parliamentarians, manages to stay out of the war... but in 1642, his son [[Bryan Dewulf|Bryan]] runs away on the night of his sixteenth birthday and joins the Royalist army. He is captured and returned to his father, who pleads for mercy and gives his parole for his son's good behaviour.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|In 1648, Bryan runs away again to join a Royalist uprising. Walter writes of news that Bryan has been seen on the field of battle at Gear Camp, but that his fate is yet unknown. Walter writes one last entry about his fear for his son and the future of his family. There the journal ends; but the extensive account of Walter's collaboration with the architect [[Gregory Wheelock]] includes usefully esoteric information.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Door & Wall|Lesson: Door & Wall]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

[[Category:Forge]]

Selecting the book provides the following description:

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|<nowiki/>'If we should flourish not, let our enemies flourish, in that time when we are no more…'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|One prayer describes how a strong degree of Nectar-aspect can be used with Leathy and Tridesma Hiera rites to bring forth 'the Last Nectar of the Last History, the Living Ink, the Ink-in-Secret…'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the [[Rose]] principle written in [[Phrygian]]. These are the collected letters from [[Lars Westergren]].
==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:{{Quote|Lars Westergren, explorer and murderer, spent seven years escaping justice through his knowledge of byways and shortcuts in the Bounds. Throughout that time he wrote regularly to his daughter, possibly in part to taunt his pursuers.|Description}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|A year with the Légion de Seuil, patrolling the Bounds, until he deserts; a month in the Priory of Captains in Morbihan; seven days, or so he claims, in Ys behind the wave…|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|Cornered at last by his pursuers, Westergren writes that he will 'attempt the Paths of the Sun'. He doesn't seem sanguine about his chances, and indeed, this is his last letter. An editor's note adds that Westergren's whereabouts or end remain unknown, although he was supposedly sighted at the 'Christmas Market' in Vienna - the negotiations between invisible underworld figures that happen each year there - in 1929.|I've Read...}}


==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides [[Path & Pilgrim|Lesson: Path & Pilgrim]]. Reading it always provides [[Confounding Parable]].

'''''Kitling Ripe and the Moldywarp's Grave (and Other Stories)''''' is a [[book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A lusciously illustrated tome of loosely connected children's stories. Few of them are remotely suitable for children.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|The protagonist, a speechless cat-thing called Kitling Ripe, performs a series of elaborate rites to rescue members of her extended family, culminating in the resurrection of her 'other grandmother', Moldywarp.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘When the Snake-Witch killed the horse, Kitling snatched one of its eyes. When the Dry-Witch killed the pig, Kitling stole a cup of its blood. Then she took them to the place Moldywarp lay buried, and she shook out her hair, and she began to dance…’|I've Read...}}

==Reward==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Resurgences & Emergences|Lesson: Resurgences & Emergences]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

Selecting the record provides the following description:

{{quote|Recordings of the folk-dances of the Fucine Marshes.|}}

Upon choosing to master the recording at a [[phonograph]], the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The wailing of flutes, the roaring of drums, cries like birds lost in the marshes…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|These are the songs the Sister sang to the Witch - that the Thunderskin roared to the Sky - the songs with which the duendrazones of the Mansus keep their vigil. Once heard, they are not forgotten.|I've Read...}}

Completing mastery of this record generates ''[[Drums & Dances|Lesson: Drums & Dances]]'' x2. Listening to it always provides [[Beguiling Melody]].

Nyn's Cages (Bruges Text, Illuminated).text:
{{Book (BoH) |title1=Nyn's Cages
(Bruges Text, Illuminated) |image1=Nyns Cages Bruges Text Illuminated.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Winter}} |tally_price=4 |language=[[Ericapaean]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Quenchings & Quellings]] |memory=[[Memory: Hindsight]] |period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} Principle, written in [[Ericapaean]] by the witch [[Nyn]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|The 'merciful measures' of the witch Nyn. This is only a partial version of the original, but it contains illustrations by Nyn's pupil, Mabelie of Bruges, which supplement the original.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Nyn's stated aim was to 'keep beyond the Walls of Sleep that business which should not trouble the world'. This includes fever, madness and delirium as well as spirits identified as 'Devourers' and 'Deceivers'. (Mabelie clearly enjoyed drawing both Devourers and Deceivers, but was less interested in illustrating disease symptoms.)|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|
Nyn warns against invoking the Edicts Liminal or Inviolable before sleep - 'for no matter how secure a lock may be, its key will surely open it.' Mabelie has helpfully illustrated this by drawing a sleepwalker clambering through an open window, about to leap into the jaws of a sea-monster. The sea-monster is goggle-eyed with happy anticipation.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Quenchings & Quellings|Lesson: Quenchings & Quellings]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Hindsight]]. ==Trivia== *This book hints at a secret. Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The first part of the poem describes the ambush of the Seven-Coils by a warrior 'scarred all over by the traitor gods, scarred even unto his eyes, so that the sight of the great coils would not destroy him'.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The battle rages on until the Seven-Coils drowns in its own blood, at which point the narrative turns mystical and allusive. A seven-titled goddess arises from the foam of its blood: she is an armoured queen, a serpent-daughter, a key, a healer, a murderess, an oracle, but her seventh title is not to be revealed.|I've Read...}}

'''''Nix Abolix''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written in [[Fucine]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description: 
{{quote|A grim treatise on 'those feasts that occur, those feasts that are not to be witnessed.'}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|The alukites, who feasted on their children and became monsters. The dragon-kinds among the Carapace Cross, who feasted on Hour-flesh and became monsters. The khalvites, who drank of Echidna's bounty, and became monsters…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|‘Marinette, the Ligeian: so young, so hungry. All her children cannot slake her thirst. When Moth rose, another held the Flaying Key, but at the Grail's bidding did Marinette consume that she.’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Wolf Stories|Lesson: Wolf Stories]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]].

==Trivia==
In [[Nyn|Nina Lagasse]]'s letter to [[Julian Coseley]], she says she will create 3 paintings, the second of which is also called Nix Abolix:

{{Quote|The second I will paint in the hills outside Heraklion where the hawthorn blooms. Gertrude will not want to go to Crete, but I will promise her a hidden mountain in the Zagros and I think she will humour me. If I bring the proper offerings, the Horned-Axe might grant me audience in the Mansus. I doubt it. But if the subject matter opens any doors that I cannot close, the Axe will be on hand to close them. She will not be pleased with me, but at this late stage there is little she can do. And if I am going to paint the Cross’ fate, it is fitting for me to do so beneath her gaze. If they were not her children, they were certainly her servants. I’ll paint all the detail I can, Julian: how the Cross passed into Nowhere, and how they did not, and how they met with Worms, and how you may discern them now. Husher argued for the journey of colours. You disagreed. Perhaps I can still change your mind.|Nina Lagasse}}

These paintings seem to be the three paintings that convinced Coseley to rewrite his magnum opus to create [[Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic: Second Edition]].

On Matthias and the Amethyst Imago: Loss.title: On Matthias and the Amethyst Imago: Loss
On Matthias and the Amethyst Imago: Loss.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=[[File:On Matthias and the Amethyst Imago- Loss.png]]
|mystery=6
|principles={{Lore|Moth}}
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Aramaic]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Solutions & Separations]]
|memory=[[Memory: A Stolen Secret]]
|period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle, written in [[Aramaic]] by Para.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|An account of an occult romance. A certain Para, son of Aaron, claims to have written this in a single night as part of his initiation into the Damascene branch of the House of Lethe - that order of immortals who rejected their past and future.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘The laws of the House forbade Matthias to love. The customs of the Wood forbade the Imago to remain. So he conjured her a final time, when she had uncovered the Shears of Alakapura; and she suffered him to cut the wings from her back, so that she might remain; and he suffered her to cut the parts which hold man's seed, to keep them from the Detestable Act. This was love in all its blood and joy. We have cast out Matthias from the House.’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘In the cradle of the roots, Matthias and the Imago left their names, and though their names were lost, they found their Nameday Riddles. This we recall in Solution and Separation, so that in the presence of the Moth our memories may become our futures. Do this wisely, in memory of the Name and the Long who gave up their past that they might be together forgotten.’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Solutions & Separations|Lesson: Solutions & Separations]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: A Stolen Secret]].

On the White.title: On the White
On the White.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=On the White|mystery=6|category=[[Readable]]|tally_price=2|type=[[Codex]]|image1=[[File:OntheWhite.png|thumb]]|principles={{Lore|Winter}}|Period=[[Curia]]|skill=[[Quenchings & Quellings]]|memory=[[Memory: Regret]]}}''On the White'' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} principle.
==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:{{Quote|Solomon Husher writes, perhaps allegorically, of Winter, and its long slow doomed romance with the Sun. The epigraph is 'Sunset at Noon'.|Description}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|On closer investigation, the work seems to be a theory of aesthetics, or perhaps a set of warnings about the dangers of painting.|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|Husher writes distractedly about his suspicion of colours and his yearning for death. He hints at a Great Work he has envisaged, or begun, where the 'palest of paintings' will enthral the world. He returns again and again to certain compelling phrases which he claims are the 'secret words of Winter'.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates [[Quenchings & Quellings|Lesson: Quenchings & Quellings]] and [[Memory: Regret]]. Reading it again provides [[Memory: Regret]].

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Winter]]
[[Category:Readable]]
[[Category:Codex]]

Operations of a Certain Finality.title: Operations of a Certain Finality
Operations of a Certain Finality.text:
{{Book (BoH) |title1=Operations of
a Certain Finality |image1=[[File:OperationsofaCertainFinality.png]] |mystery=8 |principles={{Lore|Winter}} |tally_price=2 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Putrefactions & Calcinations]] |memory=[[Memory: Hindsight]] |period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} Principle, written in English by an anonymous adept. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Subtitled 'The Hammer's Sundering'. The work of an anonymous adept who violently despised the Invisible Serapeum, the library of the Watchman's Tree in Alexandria.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The author outlines the means they had taken to sabotage the place and its collection, which increasingly seem more poetic than effective, to the point where the whole business may in fact be some kind of allegory.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The author gloats that with the techniques of Putrefaction and Calcination, they have transformed the Library's stocks of asimel to 'a seduction of black sapphire' which will ensure the texts therein contain only 'Moon-truths'.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Putrefactions & Calcinations|Lesson: Putrefactions & Calcinations]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Hindsight]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Winter]] [[Category:Curia]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

Lady Eva's Repose.title: Lady Eva's Repose
Lady Eva's Repose.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=File:LadyEvasRepose.png |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Winter}} |tally_price=3 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Rhyme & Remembrance]] |memory=[[Memory: Regret]] |period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} Principle, written in English by Father Theo. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|A 'meditation' on the drowning of Lady Eva Dewulf and her two grandchildren, written in the years when the estate was abandoned by Father Theo, once the Dewulf family chaplain, one of the few to remain on the Isle in those desolate years.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'There are so many stories of her heritage, so many rumours of her persistence. We might easily choose to believe that the grand-twins escaped - even that they live yet beyond the sea - '|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Father Theo has come to believe that Eva sought an escape from a family curse - the 'pale heritage' of Hafren her forebear, or the curse placed upon the line by the cunning-man Red William in the time of Hendrik Dewulf. He had begun by believing neither curse was real; but as the book concludes, he decides that he has determined to believe in them, rather than accept the three deaths as a futile tragedy. 'One does not so easily escape the long necessity of faith,' he concludes.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Rhyme & Remembrance|Lesson: Rhyme & Remembrance]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Regret]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Winter]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]] [[Category:Baronial]]

Perugian Diaries.title: Perugian Diaries
Perugian Diaries.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=File:Perugian_Diaries.png |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |tally_price=1 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Strings & Songs]] |memory=[[Cheerful Ditty]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} Principle, written in English by Christopher Illopoly. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|In 1907, at the age of eighteen, Christopher Illopoly left Strathcoyne's household to study theology at the University of Perugia in Italy, enrolling under the name 'Christopher Strathcoyne'.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|For four years, since his adoption from a Bristol orphanage, Illopoly served as Strathcoyne's pupil and protégé, but his relationship with this austere and secretive man was always complicated. His journal confides: 'I still think Fraser's intentions are good. Certainly he agrees. But I never understood the final goal of his investigations. He was never prepared to enlighten me. And good intentions or not, I can no longer bear this dream of eyes. We have agreed to part, almost amicably.'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Illopoly left Perugia in 1909 without completing his degree. He had long lost interest in his studies, and the latter half of the journal is concerned with his studies of Umbrian folk-songs, and notes towards his own compositions (which are of widely varying quality). One of the better ones, 'In the Marshes of Night', suggests he visited the site of the old Lake Fucinus near Ortucchio…|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Strings & Songs|Lesson: Strings & Songs]]''. Reading always provides [[Cheerful Ditty]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Sky]] [[Category:Nocturnal Period]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

Opening the Sky.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=Opening the Sky
|mystery=10

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Phonograph Record]] of the [[Sky]] principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:{{quote| An unusual recording of Verro's 'Opening the Sky', composed for the coronation of the New King, Henry IX. The record bears the Suppression stamp EXPUNGE.|}}Upon choosing to master the book at a [[Phonograph]], the Librarian learns:{{Quote| The first movement is soft, autumnal. The second unsettling, febrile. The third is bright, soaring, rapturous. The fourth movement is glassy, slithering, a tintinnabulous icicle rattle…|I'm Reading...}}After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote| The fifth returns to the theme of the third, bright and rapturous once again, but this is a choral movement. It becomes apparent, though, that these are much, much too pure and high to be human voices. They recall birdsong - they recall the sweep of the windswept sky, blue turning black at the edge of the higher heaven - and they wrench the heart in a direction the Bureau does not permit.|I've Read...}}
==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates [[Strings & Songs|x2 Lesson: Strings & Songs]] and [[Cheerful Ditty]]. Subsequent [[Consider|consideration]] of the book produces only [[Cheerful Ditty]].

Letters To My Successor.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=Letters to my Successor.png
|mystery=8
|principles={{Lore|Lantern}}

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle written by [[Gervinus van Lauren]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Advice from Gervinus van Lauren, eleventh Librarian of Hush House, to the one who will come after him.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Some of the advice is practical - don't worry about losing the House Key; always close the seaward windows; make sure you feed the cockatoo. Much more of it is rarefied, specifically about the '[[Inks of Revelation]]'. And some of it relates to van Lauren's own doom...|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘When I was another, I made a foolish wager with the Hooded Princes, to solve seven riddles. I had not realised the riddles would be set by me for the one I would become. Six are resolved. The seventh will be the end of me. It waits now in the cellar of the Gaol, where Collers still believes I can keep it confined. But the first riddle told me I would not see the Second Dawn...’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Inks of Revelation|Lesson: Inks of Revelation]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written by [[Poemander]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Poemander, light-smith and Lantern-long, describes the process of 'transinhabitation', which he calls 'a manifestation of imperfection.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Lantern-long lack bodies, and so cannot normally leave the Mansus - but they can 'steady-glint' in the physical world by establishing a 'road of glass'. Poemander notes with disgust that the order of Long called the Obliviates refer to it as 'scrining', which he considers a 'debased term'.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Poemander explains the benefits of transinhabitation - that a Lantern-long can affect the senses and thoughts of those nearby, that they can even enter their spirits, and that they can 'employ the senses of those inhabited to experience again the scent of blossom and season'. This seems to be what interests him most. He insists that a Lantern-long should only ever inhabit a mirror of silver, not silvered glass, but he declines to explain why.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting|Lesson: Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Pattern]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle written in [[Aramaic]] by Iyavogos.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|An account of an occult romance. A certain Iyavogos claims to have written this in a single night as part of his initiation into the Aleppine branch of the House of Lethe - that order of immortals who would not pledge themselves to any Hour.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘We cast Matthias out, and we pronounced a curse upon the Amethyst Imago, but we watched them in dreams. We saw them pledge themselves to the Forge, to change themselves and ascend anew. Into the fire they fly.’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘This is the first of the practices that the Imago and Matthias used, to begin their ascent to power. They have risen beyond our sight, but their flames may yet burn in the Malleary.’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Spices & Savours|Lesson: Spices & Savours]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written in [[Ramsund]] by [[Gregory Wheelock]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Gregory Wheelock, the master mason and architect employed by Walter Dewulf to construct the Winding Stair and the guest chambers in Hush House, describes a more ambitious and dangerous project.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Gregory marks the bricks of his Roost-touched family home, Treowen, with Ramsund, hoping to open forbidden doors…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Gregory evidently succeeds in opening a way to something he calls the 'Moon-Hall', but here his account becomes erratic. He insists that in the Moon-Hall the Horned-Axe is still an Edge-power; he hopes for an 'eternal rival', but cannot find the one he needs. The narrative is increasingly interspersed with chess notations, and ends abruptly.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Door & Wall|Lesson: Door & Wall]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Pattern]].

'''''Notes on Bindings''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle written by [[Gideon Dewulf]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Gideon Dewulf, 5th Baron Brancrug, discusses techniques shared between medical suturing, tailoring, and - carefully, allusively - the binding of restless spirits.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Gideon's favourite motif is 'the history of the flesh'. He insists obscurely that histories should be woven, not written.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Gideon speaks reverently of the 'wyrd-weft', which he has achieved by applying Stitching and Binding arts to a fabric in the presence of sufficient Winter. He laments however that its complexities only approach those understood by the Sisterhood of the Knot, which in turn are only a shadow of 'the true Braid of Histories'.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Stitching & Binding|Lesson: Stitching & Binding]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Solace]].

On Thirstlies, Ivories and Lovelies.title: On Thirstlies, Ivories and Lovelies
On Thirstlies, Ivories and Lovelies.text:
{{Book (BoH) |title1=On Thirstlies, Ivories
and Lovelies |image1=On Thirstlies Ivories and Lovelies.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Grail}} |tally_price=2 |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |memory=[[Memory: Impulse]] |period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle written by Fionna Ayrshire. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Fionna Ayrshire recounts her visits in dreams to the 'Red Church' in the Mansus, and her conversations with the Names of the Grail.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|An Hour, Ayrshire explains, may usually only have seven Names - but since the Thirstlies, Ivories and Lovelies who usually comprise the Red Grail's Names are constantly attempting to devour one another, and the Names of other Hours, that number fluctuates.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Lovelies, the 'freshest' of the Grail's Names, usually adopt the characteristics of whatever they devour - be it an Ivory, a Thirstly, or, occasionally, an entirely different kind of Name. A practical application of the principle is described. The arts of Resurgences and Emergences, in the presence of sufficiently potent Grail-aspect, can be used to feed a Pale Mommet to its successor-doll, creating something 'notably more avid'.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Resurgences & Emergences|Lesson: Resurgences & Emergences]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Grail]] [[Category:Curia]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]]

On the Matter and the Deeds of Serpents.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=OntheMatterandtheDeedsofSerpents.png
|mystery=12

'''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written in [[Vak]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|This was probably the 'prophecies of the naga' rendered into English, and illustrated, by 'William Midnight' in Paris in the 1880s; but it shows a number of divergences from that text. It's certainly quite recent by the standards of Vak texts.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The serpent-folk called the Great Hooded Princes came to know the order called the House of Lethe, and warred across the miles with them. They made an alliance with the Mother of Ants, 'whose children they had been'...|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The text describes how the Great Hooded Princes escaped (or will escape) from the Fifth History, where they had died (or were doomed to die). They engaged in a secret conquest of 'the land of the Great River', called India in some histories, and have ensured that all other conquests of that land are false conquests.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Edicts Liminal|Lesson: Edicts Liminal]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Secret Threshold]].

[[Category:Knock]]
[[Category:Curia]]

[[Category:Readable]]

Kopralith Omphalos.title: Kopralith Omphalos
Kopralith Omphalos.text: {{Book (BoH) |image1=Kopralith Omphalos.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Moth}} |tally_price=8 |language=[[Killasimi]] |type=[[Tablet]] |skill=[[Weaving & Knotworking]] |memory=[[Numen: Weaving the World]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle that contains a [[Numen]] and is written in [[Killasimi]]. ==Location== ''{{PAGENAME}}'' is found on a shelf inside the [[Ivory Vault]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|What is this? A tufted fossil of silken fibre, big as a child. [This object houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Something consumed, and something was consumed. If we interpret its interweavings, we might understand.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The meaning of this object isn't something that one reads, but rather something that one follows, until at last one has passed three times around it, and one finds the meaning waiting at one's shoulder.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Weaving & Knotworking|Lesson: Weaving & Knotworking]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Numen: Weaving the World]]: a [[Numen]] that can be used to establish a [[history]] and win the game. This numen has a special victory for [[the Symurgist]] and [[the Cartographer]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Moth]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Tablet]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Numen]]

'''''Observations on the Peacock Door''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written in [[Vak]] by [[Nyn|Ninegala of Lagash]]. 

== Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Ninegala of Lagash discusses the Peacock Door, the highest door available to mortals in the Mansus: 'a rent, an imperfection, an abrasion.'.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Notably, the book is written in Vak, which by some accounts is another aspect of the Peacock Door itself. Ninegala addresses this by apologising courteously to the Door, and the language, at the end of every section.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Peacock Door did not exist - Ninegala says - in the days when the gods-from-stone entered the Mansus. They used the 'Fanged Key' to open the Savage Door, a door not usually available to mortals. 'Speech, as the initiates of Chione would have it, is a wound. I fear that through that wound, the blood of the Mansus flows even now, and that one day Speech will be an end to Dream. I fear that; but I fear the alternative far more.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Sickle & Eclipse|Lesson: Sickle & Eclipse]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Contradiction]]

On Matthias and the Amethyst Imago: Purs.title: On Matthias and the Amethyst Imago: Pursuit
On Matthias and the Amethyst Imago: Purs.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=On Matthias and the Amethyst Imago Pursuit.png
|mystery=6
|principles={{Lore|Grail}}
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Aramaic]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Desires & Dissolutions]]
|memory=[[Memory: Gossip]]
|period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle written in [[Aramaic]] by Mek.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|An account of an occult romance. A certain Mek claims to have written this in a single night as part of his initiation into the Theban branch of the House of Lethe - that order of immortals who used the arts of water to conceal themselves.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Matthias defied us to hunt the Names of the Moth in the Wood, to populate his pinned collection. The Amethyst Imago had dallied with the Witch-and-Sister, but she'd returned to the Wood to plead the Moth's pardon. The Moth, as a whim or a penance, sent her out to lure the Long to a slough of nightmares.’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Matthias loved the Imago. (Did he? Can Long love, or has that organ of their soul desiccated beyond repair?) The Imago loved Matthias. (Did she? or did she only enact a whim?) He pursued her through the Wood, but at the last she turned aside from the nightmare-slough, and they lay together where the Bounds grow bright. So they learnt the Grail's pleasures, and this is the lore they won.’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Desires & Dissolutions|Lesson: Desires & Dissolutions]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Gossip]].

Old Coppernose and the Softer Metal.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=Old Coppernose and the Softer Metal
|image1=Old Coppernose and the Softer Metal.png

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A disgraceful compendium of ribald poetry about the habits and corruptions of Henry VIII.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Henry's 'Great Misfortune' - his crushing injury at a jousting bout - has left him unable to stand 'any straighter than a splintered withy'…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The most savage mockery is reserved for Henry's 'Great Debasement', where the corruption of his softer metal is supposed to have crept into the coin of the realm. The last and most serious lampoon makes seditious references to 'the Crucible Revolution'.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Bells & Brazieries|Lesson: Bells & Brazieries]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

My Deeds, My Powers, My Achievements and.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=My Deeds, My Powers, My Achievements and the Injustices Perpetrated Against Me
|mystery=16

|image1=My Deeds My Powers My Achievements and the Injustices Perpetrated Against Me.png
