'''''My Deeds, My Powers, My Achievements and the Injustices Perpetrated Against Me''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle written in [[Deep Mandaic]] by [[Magister Hokobald|Hokobald of Pocsind]].
==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|A diatribe by Hokobald of Pocsind, formerly of the order of immortals called the House of Lethe (later the Ordo Limiae; much latter the Obliviates). He has scores to settle.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Hokobald boasts of his royal descent, and insists that the magics of the Forge are more effective when practised by those of noble blood.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Pocsind complains of his condemnation by the Ordo Limiae. He acknowledges that he has 'undergone alterations' after the 'consummation of that particular delight', but insists that these changes are both elegant and inevitable. 'Who is the fire, and who the fuel?' he asks rhetorically.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Transformations & Liberations|Lesson: Transformations & Liberations]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

== Hidden Interaction ==
Presenting [[Magister Hokobald]] this book prompts unique dialogue where he offers to purchase it for a [[Tally|Gold Spintria]]. He will leave after this discussion and will not return for the current incident (if one is active).
{{quote|'I had feared no copies yet remained! There is so much despite in the world - so much needless contumely - so much contempt for hard-earned wisdom - forgive me. I will purchase this treasure from you - if you are prepared to give it up. A gold spintria?' [Hokobald will take the book and depart, forgetting about any current Incident.]|Upon presentation of the book}}
{{quote|I have been so very greatly wronged. But I am capable of wreaking wrongs yet greater. My dear Librarian, ''bon appetit''|Upon buying the book}}

On What is Contained By Silver.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=On What is Contained By Silver|mystery=[[Sky]] 6|category=[[Book]]|tally_price=3|type=[[Readable]], [[Thing]], [[Codex]]|image1=[[File:OnWhatIsContainedBySilver.png|thumb]]|Period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]|principles=|skill=[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]]|memory=[[Memory: Pattern]]}}''On What is Contained By Silver'' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Sky]] principle originally by [[Poemander]].
==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:{{Quote|A dire bestiary of the horrors to be found in mirrors. This is a recent edition of a third century text by 'Poemander'.|Description}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|Poemander engages in a considerable and pedantic discussion about the particular mirror-alloys that attract particular danger from particular entities. This is less useful, of course, in an era where most mirrors are silvered glass.|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|'The virgins/maidens of the mirror favour orchids. The [behindlings?] favour the rhododendron. Cut flowers of either nature should not be placed before polished bronze.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates [[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting|Lesson: Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]] and [[Memory: Pattern]]. Subsequent [[Consider|consideration]] of the book produces only [[Memory: Pattern]].

'''OGHKOR OGHKOR TISSILAK OGHKOR''' is a book of the {{Lore|Knock}} principle and the [[Baronial Period]] written by 'the Excellency Gnathobasis'.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A surprisingly chatty text by an entity that identifies itself as 'the Excellency Gnathobasis'.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Excellency Gnathobasis explains the 'limbs and extensions' of potent and dangerous 'glyphic achievements'. The sentences are nonsense on first reading, but quickly acquire an insistent meaning on each repetition.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘With adequate Grail,’ the Excellency Gnathobasis explains, ‘the [[Pale Mommet]] wakes to life. With generous Grail, the [[Flushed Mommet]] accepts our beneficence. It may be necessary to overcome scruple! The Excellency Gnathobasis will assure you as to how, and to whom, and with which most perfect instrument.’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars|Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Pattern|Memory: Pattern]].

Naenian Sketches.title: Naenian Sketches
Naenian Sketches.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=[[File:Naenian Sketches.png|thumb]] |mystery=21 |principles={{Lore|Winter}} |tally_price=1 |language=[[Sabazine]] |type=[[Codex]], [[Multitudinous]] |skill=[[Sights & Sensations]] |memory=[[Memory: Hindsight]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Multitudinous]] [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} Principle, written in [[Sabazine]] by various Long. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Travelogues and studies exchanged by raggies and ghouls - that is, the Long who've ascended under the patronage of the Sun-in-Rags and those who won the attention of the Elegiast.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'Naenia is the Elegiast's Name, but she has always stood high in the Sun-in-Rags' favour; and she offers her consolations also to those Long who have taken him as a patron...'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Both kinds of Winter-long know that their death is only deferred, so both tend to seek and treasure beauty. Here they detail their purest experiences - the mountain after the avalanche, the peace after the storm-wreck, the gusted silence of the sun-shadowed hill...|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sights & Sensations|Lesson: Sights & Sensations]]'' (x3). Reading always provides [[Memory: Hindsight]]. '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Multitudinous]] [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle written in [[Killasimi]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Haustorial discussions of Medusa's histories.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|'Medusa's Riddle: 'What Is Not Seen?' She might be the oldest of her kind still living; and she is dead. Once she held the key to the door in the Wood; and though perhaps she lost it, she holds it still…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The scholars of the Haustorium seem to suggest that just as there are always seven Ligeians but they are not always the same, there is always one Medusa but she is not always the same. There does seem to be more of a common thread of identity than simply a series of titled successors, and here the Haustorium's argument becomes harder to follow - especially because the Haustorium and its members themselves have an unusual concept of individual identity...|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Pentiments & Precursors|Lesson: Pentiments & Precursors]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]].

{{Quote|Nyn's stated aim was to 'keep beyond the Walls of Sleep that business which should not trouble the world'. This includes fever, madness and delirium, as well as spirits identified as 'Devourers' and 'Deceivers'.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:

You can order multiple items by re-using the order form before submitting it. Once you complete your order, the total price in Pence and all ordered goods will be displayed in the order form's infobox. Each order will take 5 seconds to complete.
If you make a mistake or go overbudget, you can select the "Begin again" option at the top of the order. Once you have finished, the Order Form will be [[Ready to Post]]. {{Quote|This message will find its destination... once properly sanctioned by the powers of the post-box.
[Take it to the Post Office, with cash for a stamp or a postal order.]}}
All that is left now is to take your form to the [[Post Office]] and part with it, alongside your money. {{Quote|The Postmistress signs and seals the order, and places it in the place that stamped orders are properly placed.
'Wait three days,' she commands.}} ==Delivery== {{quote|Something delightful has arrived!}}
A day and a half later, a [[A Delivery from T.R.N. Limited]] will arrive in your sundries box, which you can open by [[Consider]]ing it. {{quote|Unwrap, unbox, unleash.}} ==Trivia== *This item was added after the DAYMARE update. *In Cultist Simulator, T.R.N. Ltd is a mysterious firm mentioned in the description of [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/The_Seven_Graces The Seven Graces]. [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Ordering]]

Manuscript.title: Manuscript
Manuscript.text:
{{Stub}} [[File:Multitudinous icon.png|right]] {{quote|I wrote this; I won't learn anything new from reading it, but Visitors might.}}
A '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an [[Aspects|Aspect]] of [[Readable]]s written by the Librarian in order to satisfy the [[Skill]] and [[Principles|Principle]] interest of a [[Visitor]]. A Manuscript is written at a [[Workstation#Desks|Desk]] by providing any [[Element of the Soul]] that matches the used desk, a [[Quire of Paper]] and [[Ink]]. [[Perinculate]] cannot be used, as it is dreadfully poisonous. The primary Principle of the Skill used determines what type of mystery is written, and the final mystery value is determined only by the current level of the Skill, not the total power of the provided Principles. Additionaly, using an ink matching the Principle of the used Skill will double the mystery value of the work. For instance, if you write with [[Pyroglyphics]] 2 and a [[Typewriter]], then the resulting mystery level is going to be 2 (skill level) * 2 (matching ink) = 4. Any ink and paper used will be destroyed and the process takes 65 seconds to complete, plus an additional 5 seconds if the Principles match. Note that if the [[Typewriter]] or the [[Silent Typewriter]] are used, they will not be destroyed. ====[[Consider]] this:==== {{Quote|
My Work!

Readable.title: Readable
Readable.text:
[[File:Readable icon.png|64px|right]] __NOTOC__
There are many '''Readable''' items to be found in ''[[Book of Hours]]''. The majority are in the form of standard books, or '[[Codex|codices]]', but there are also [[Tablet|tablets]], [[Scroll|scrolls]], [[Reel of Film|reels of film]], and [[Phonograph Record|phonograph records]]. Each readable can be [[Mastery|mastered]] for [[Skills|lessons]]. Reading or re-reading anything will always produce a [[Memory|memory]]. Films and records will only be accepted at specific [[Workstations|workstations]] - the [[Projector]] and either [[Phonograph]], respectively. All other texts can be mastered at any desk or with the [[Consider|consider]] verb. Readables can be found by cataloguing [[Uncatalogued Book|uncatalogued books]] at a [[Workstations#Desks|desk]] or with the consider verb and an [[Elements of the Soul|element of the soul]]. Reading a non-mastered book takes 2x 1 minute; reading an already mastered one takes just 1 minute. Re-reading completely ignores Principle requirements and always succeeds, which means you shouldn't use neither skills nor other items, and just use any desk of your choice (all desks accepts all Readables themselves, regardless of Principles) with any Principle matching that desk. This page contains lists of all readable items, organised by [[Principles|principle]]. The Admonitory Automata Project.title: The Admonitory Automata Project
The Admonitory Automata Project.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=The Admonitory Automata Project
|mystery=10
|principles={{Lore|Forge}}
|tally_price=2
|type=[[Reel of Film]]
|period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]
|image1=[[File:TheAdmonitoryAutomataProject.png]]
|memory=[[Memory: Foresight]]
|skill=[[Lockworks & Clockworks]]}}
'''''The Admonitory Automata Project''''' is a [[Reel of Film]] of the [[Forge]] Principle. As a film, it can only be mastered with the [[Projector]].

==Description==
Selecting the film provides the following description:
{{Quote|Footage of experimental devices under development in the Cucurbit under [[George Collers|Governor Collers]]' supervision.}}

Upon choosing to master the film, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The 'admonitory automata' are nasty little things of spring and wire, but they all have merry faces of painted tin…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The last item shown is a prototype towards something called a '[[condignator]]', which, Collers says proudly, will allow a prisoner to 'elaborate their own punishment.' He hastens to add that he hopes that in the coming era, 'punishment' will be an entirely obsolete concept.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the film provides ''[[Lockworks & Clockworks|Lesson: Lockworks & Clockworks]]'' x2. Watching it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

[[Category:Reel of Film]]
[[Category:Forge]]
[[Category:Nocturnal]]
[[Category:Readable]]

Stolen Histories.title: Stolen Histories
Stolen Histories.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=StolenHistories.png |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Scale}} |tally_price=3 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Coil & Chasm]] |memory=[[Memory: Fear]] |period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Scale}} Principle, written in English by Alexander Sparrow. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|The agitator and pamphleteer Alexander Sparrow inveighs against the 'monstrous Serpents, Thieves of History.'|}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Sparrow acknowledges five Histories, insists the Third History may be 'overrun by Coils', warns the Fifth History is already lost.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Sparrow, with his usual paranoia, appears to be conflating the horror of the Worm Wars and the Great Writhing with the activities of the Great Hooded Princes. Still, he draws thought-provoking comparisons between the Princes - normally conceived as exotic Knock-long - and the widely feared Worms.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Coil & Chasm|Lesson: Coil & Chasm]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Fear]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Scale]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]] [[Category:Baronial]]

The Carmine Petal: Unexpurgated.title: The Carmine Petal: Unexpurgated
The Carmine Petal: Unexpurgated.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=The Carmine Petal Unexpurgated.png
|mystery=18
|principles={{Lore|Forge}}
|tally_price=3
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Disciplines of the Hammer]]
|memory=[[Memory: Foresight]]
|period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A project proposed by 'Lionel' of the Society of the Noble Endeavour by which, he claims, he succeeded in creating a sanctuary for a fugitive Forge-Name. The unexpurgated version.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|At the time this book was written, a 'fugitive' Forge-Name would have been guilty of heresy, treason, or both.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|'Lionel' suggests that the 'house of iron and fire' so created would include 'hollows of air and night', which would serve as a final hiding-place if the larger sanctuary were uncovered - though, he says, they could be easily revealed with invocations of the Disciplines either of Scar or of Hammer.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Disciplines of the Hammer|Lesson: Disciplines of the Hammer]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

[[Category:Forge]]

Prophecies of Glory.title: Prophecies of Glory
Prophecies of Glory.text:
{{Book_(BoH)
|mystery=8
|tally_price=3
|principles={{Lore|Lantern}}
|Period=[[Baronial]]
|image1=Prophecies of Glory.png
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Watchman's Paradoxes]]
|memory=[[Memory: Revelation]]}}
'''''Prophecies of Glory''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle compiled by William Gore.

== Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Religious and patriotic fables collected, or composed, by William Gore.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|This is much more sober in tone than Gore's previous '[[Wainscot Histories]]'; evidently he became religious in his later years.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Each fable describes the coming of the Second Dawn, when the Hours of the Sun will be united - but in 'Eternity Denied', 'The Vampire Light', and 'The Feast of Rays,' Gore depicts a tainted Dawn which can only be purified by a second Division of the Sun. He insists repeatedly on the dangers and temptations of a false Dawn...|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Watchman's Paradoxes|Lesson: Watchman's Paradoxes]]'' x2. Reading it always provides a [[Memory: Revelation]].

[[Category:Baronial]]
[[Category:Lantern]]

Sunrise Awakenings.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=Sunrise Awakenings.png
|mystery=4
|principles={{Lore|Lantern}}
|tally_price=3
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Auroral Contemplations]]
|memory=[[Memory: Revelation]]
|period=[[Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle, written by {{Lore|Edge}}-Long [[Twrog of Meirionnydd]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|An uncharacteristically poignant meditation by the Edge-long Twrog of Meirionnydd, who later came to Hush House under a variety of other names, often in search of some sort of fight.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘If Light were not silent, it would be Music. If Music were visible, it would be Light…’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Each day's light, Twrog suggests, is faintly touched by the light of every past day; so in the light of every present day, we may begin to understand something of days to come. At least, this appears to be his conclusion, but he stops in mid-sentence, apparently having lost patience with the act of writing, or possibly been ambushed.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Auroral Contemplations|Lesson: Auroral Contemplations]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]].

The Book of Cinders.title: The Book of Cinders
The Book of Cinders.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=TheBookofCinders.png |mystery=6 |principles={{Lore|Forge}} |tally_price=2 |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Pyroglyphics]] |memory=[[Memory: Foresight]] |period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Ostensibly an eighteenth-century fireworks manual, but with some exotic ingredient choices and a substantial section on 'teframancy', divination from ashes.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The text takes as its theme the motto of the Society of the Noble Endeavour, ALITUR PROPRIIS IGNIS CINERIBUS - 'a fire by its own ashes is nourished', and uses this as a way into discussions of alchemical techniques…|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|A surprisingly casual final section mentions that iotic essence, 'the root of the Great and Exultant Ink Orpimental', can be refined with enough Forge from a variety of liquids.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Pyroglyphics|Lesson: Pyroglyphics]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Forge]] [[Category:Curia]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]]

The Book of the Centipede.title: The Book of the Centipede
The Book of the Centipede.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=The Book of the Centipede|mystery=[[Rose]] 6|category=[[Readable]]|tally_price=2|language=[[Greek]]|type=[[Codex]]|principles=[[Rose]]|Period=[[Curia]]|image1=[[TheBookoftheCentipede.png|thumb]]}}''The Book of the Centipede'' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Rose]] principle written in [[Greek]].
==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:{{quote|In the mid 1860s one 'Madam Yi' presented an entertainment based, she claimed, on this book.|}}Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|The Centipede always found her way into the dark places. When she was punished for it, she reacted badly, in the Mansus as in Miah.'|I'm Reading...}}After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|'The River runs through the sands out of myth and into legend. The Painted River runs the other way. One is barred to the Centipede now, but she finds ways back in, sometimes.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates [[Sand Stories|Lesson: Sand Stories]]. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Intuition]].

[[Category:Codex]]

The Alloy of the White Rose.title: The Alloy of the White Rose
The Alloy of the White Rose.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Alloy of the White Rose
|mystery=10
|principles={{Lore|Lantern}}
|tally_price=4
|type=[[Codex]]
|image1=The Alloy of the White Rose.png
|memory=[[Memory: Revelation]]
|skill=[[Purifications & Exaltations]]
|period=[[Solar]]}}
'''''The Alloy of the White Rose''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle written by 'Mistress White-Flower'.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description: 
{{quote|An account by 'Mistress White-Flower' of the alchemical techniques favoured by the House of York, also identified with the 'Dawn Road'. These techniques failed to bring them victory in the War of the Roads, but are 'not to be discounted'.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|The author asserts proudly that the Dawn Road ends in the Second Dawn; and hints darkly that the downfall of the House of York was 'Grail-sabotage'.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|'Mistress White-Flower' urges a 'History of [[Uzult]]', where the Second Dawn may come to pass. She identifies [[Xanthotic Essence]] as Uzult's predecessor; she explains that with sufficient Lantern, [[Bitterblack Salts]] can be Purified to Xanthotic Essence, and [[Iotic Essence]] can be Exalted to Xanthotic Essence.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Purifications & Exaltations|Lesson: Purifications & Exaltations]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]].

[[Category:Lantern]]

Rapt in the King.title: Rapt in the King
Rapt in the King.text:
{{Book_(BoH)
|mystery=8
|type=[[Codex]]
|tally_price=3
|image1=Rapt in the King.png
|title1=Rapt in the King
|principles={{Lore|Heart}}
|skill=[[Drums & Dances]]
|memory=[[Earth-Sign]]
|Period=[[Baronial]]}}
'''''Rapt in the King''''' is a [[book]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle.

== Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:{{Quote|Detailed accounts of secret bachanals and ecstatic dances observed in necropolises and graveyards in Southern Europe, in Egypt and in Anatolia. The author is a self-confessed ghoul, an eater of buried flesh: he claims to have witnessed the dances while at his feasting.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The dances draw from the traditions of the Mysteries, of the cults of Isis and of Cybele, but include both symbolic and literal flayings, and the human heart is always central in the rites. The author punctuates his accounts with queasily sensuous descriptions of his own interrupted feasts.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|"At these greater Feasts a Black Pig is always crowned as King before its Slaying. On this Occasion, its Heart was weighed in the Balance against a Knot of Feathers, and its Skin became a Cape for the Officiant. Its Flesh was left for the Crows, but I must confess my Interest was not in its Carcass but in the Perfumed Flesh of the Milliner laid fresh in the Earth."|I've Read...}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Drums & Dances|Lesson: Drums & Dances]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Earth-Sign]].

[[Category:Heart]]

The Berrybook.title: The Berrybook
The Berrybook.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=The Berry Book.png |mystery=8 |principles={{Lore|Nectar}} |tally_price=2 |language=[[Killasimi]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Leaves & Thorns]] |memory=[[Memory: Satisfaction]] |period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Nectar}} Principle, written in [[Killasimi]] by [[Thirza Blake]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Thirza Blake, seventh librarian of Hush House, talks about fruit. For no other apparent reason but that it was the kind of thing she did, she talks about fruit in the woven language Killasimi.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'Who was it once said, fruit is the womb of a plant? It was me. Take a few moments to think on that enripened wisdom. I shall leave a blank space for your moments, here in this page.'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'Nectar, children mine - cast my words into a sufficiency of Nectar and watch the pyrus pyrissimus burst from wood. Gather more Nectar! Wring it from the trees and earth! And our pyrissimus gushes forth the Sacrament! You will thank me.'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Leaves & Thorns|Lesson: Leaves & Thorns]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Satisfaction]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Nectar]] [[Category:Curia]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

The Account of Kanishk at the Spider's D.title: The Account of Kanishk at the Spider's Door
The Account of Kanishk at the Spider's D.text:
{{Book (BoH) |title1=The Account of Kanishk
at the Spider's Door |image1=TheAccountofKanishkattheSpidersDoor.png |mystery=6 |principles={{Lore|Moon}} |tally_price=5 |language=[[Aramaic]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Sharps]] |memory=[[Memory: A Stolen Secret]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written in [[Aramaic]] by Lok Kahuli. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Lok Kahuli, Kanishk's victim and lover, wrote this account, perhaps posthumously.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Kanishk sought to become a Name. In pursuit of that end, he made Lok Kahuli the vessel of his appetites, promising Lok that they would ascend together. At the Spider's Door, he betrayed his lover...|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The Chiliarch listened to it happen and then forced Kanishk into his service. The Chiliarch cannot be denied. Lok Kahuli remained to write this work, and to describe the outer magics of struggle and contest.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sharps|Lesson: Sharps]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: A Stolen Secret]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Moon]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]]

Seven Faces of Icarus.title: Seven Faces of Icarus
Seven Faces of Icarus.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=File:SevenFacesofIcarus.png |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |tally_price=3 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Furs & Feathers]] |memory=[[Memory: Fear]] |period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} Principle, written in English by Roaring Richard. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|In the early 1530s, the last Abbot of St Brandan's, called 'Roaring Richard',
set down his conversations with the illiterate local cunning-man, Red William.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Red William describes the seven forms in which he 'goes about and under the world' -
viper, cat, fox, eagle, dove, boar and crow. Abbot Richard ingeniously fits these all into a framework of Solar belief…|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|According to Abbot Richard, each of Red William's forms is closer to the Sun, and is increasingly 'winged with virtue'. Richard draws an analogy with the waxen wings of Icarus: hypocrisy and false virtue will melt before the Sun's heat, and so sincerity and untrammelled expression of the Self are the utmost piety. It's worth noting that only a year or two after Richard wrote this book, John Tregonwell was so appalled by the debaucheries of the monks of St Brandan's that he recommended the monastery's immediate dissolution.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Furs & Feathers|Lesson: Furs & Feathers]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Fear]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Sky]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]] [[Category:Baronial]]

The Amalgam of the Red Rose.title: The Amalgam of the Red Rose
The Amalgam of the Red Rose.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Amalgam of the Red Rose
|mystery=8
|principles={{Lore|Forge}}
|tally_price=2
|type=[[Codex]]
|image1=[[File:TheAmalgamoftheRedRose.png]]
|Period=[[Curia]]
|memory=[[Memory: Foresight]]
|skill=[[Meniscate Reflections]]}}
'''''The Amalgam of the Red Rose''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle written by Mistress Red-Flower.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|An account by 'Mistress Red-Flower' of the alchemical operations favoured by the House of Lancaster, also identified with the 'Sunset Road'. These operations ultimately led to their victory in the War of the Roads, but are described as 'now debased'.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The generals of the Houses of Lancaster and York are described as 'brother-enemies' - a term more usually associated with the dyadic, invariably twinned Edge-long…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The author's conclusion is that in the absence of the operations of the Dawn Road, the operations of Sunset inevitably became unbalanced, debased, and ultimately enfeebled. The combination of the two is described, tantalisingly, as 'the Forge's True Alloy'.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Meniscate Reflections|Lesson: Meniscate Reflections]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

Snare of the Tree: Collected Proverbs of.title: Snare of the Tree: Collected Proverbs of Aunt Mopsy
Snare of the Tree: Collected Proverbs of.text:
{{Book (BoH) |title1=Snare of the Tree:
Collected Proverbs
of Aunt Mopsy |image1=Snare of the Tree Collected Proverbs of Aunt Mopsy.png |mystery=8 |principles={{Lore|Grail}} |tally_price=1 |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Applebright Euphonies]] |memory=[[Confounding Parable]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle written by [[Aunt Mopsy]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|‘Once in the Wood, we call a visit. Twice in the Wood, we call a journey. Thrice, we call coming home.’}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|‘Every timber has its knots, the straight and the crooked both. Every weave is more absence than thread. You can't keep Nowhere out any more than you can keep Somewhere in…’|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|‘When the cuckoo learns the nightingale's song, our sleep is sweeter than honey.’|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Applebright Euphonies|Lesson: Applebright Euphonies]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Confounding Parable]]. == Trivia == *Presenting [[Aunt Mopsy]] this book in a consultation rewards the Librarian with another ''[[Applebright Euphonies|Lesson: Applebright Euphonies]]'' and contaminates the book with [[Keeperskin]]. *''Snare of the Tree: Collected Proverbs of Aunt Mopsy'' is named after Alexis Kennedy's real-world book, [https://weatherfactory.biz/snare-of-the-tree-and-other-perilous-seductions/ ''The Snare of the Tree, and Other Perilous Seductions'']; it also has a similar cover to Kennedy's other book, [https://weatherfactory.biz/against-worldbuilding-and-other-provocations/ ''Against Worldbuilding, and Other Provocations'']. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Grail]] [[Category:Nocturnal Period]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]]

The Ceaseless Tantra.text:

|mystery=6

'''''The Ceaseless Tantra''''' is a [[book]] written in [[Sanskrit]].

== Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The avant-garde choreographer Nicholas Keirle supposedly incorporated this Tantra into his menacing ballets.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Ceaseless Tantra is devoted mostly to warnings about the lively creatures called Percussigants, but concludes with a chant which can be used to summon them. It observes that Percussigants can be taught any dance, but they prefer only one.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|That which does not cease, is not ceased.|I've Read...}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Weaving & Knotworking|Lesson: Weaving & Knotworking]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse|Impulse]].

The Ascendant.title: The Ascendant
The Ascendant.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=The Ascendant|principles={{Lore|Edge}}|mystery=10|tally_price=4|language=Hyksos|type=Codex|image1=The Ascendant.png|skill=[[Edicts Martial]]|memory=[[Memory: Contradiction|Contradiction]]|period=[[Solar]]}}

'''''The Ascendant''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} principle written in [[Hyksos]] by the Edge-Long Dardesh.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:

{{quote|The Edge-long Dardesh boasts of her victories over her brother-enemy Tareg in the days of the Shadowless Empire.|The Ascendant}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Sweeter than wine, than nectar is the blood of my brother. We have raised up armies one against another, we have sated the Blackbone with the sinking of our ships…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Dardesh's boasting at length turns melancholy. An Edge-long is half a dyad; she may not defeat her hated brother-enemy without ending herself. She doesn't even want to; but she is aware, to her frustration, that she is 'a piece on the board, an axle on the ox-cart' - an essential part of the eternal engine of contention which the Lionsmith and Colonel use to sustain the world.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Edicts Martial|Lesson: Edicts Martial]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Contradiction]].

[[Category:Edge]]

Seven Shards.title: Seven Shards
Seven Shards.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=[[File:Seven Shards.png]]
|mystery=10
|principles={{Lore|Edge}}
|tally_price=2
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Disciplines of the Hammer]]
|memory=[[Memory: Hindsight]]
|period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} Principle written by [[Natalia Brulleau]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The Lionsmith, one of the two great Hours of struggle, broke his sword into seven shards. Natalia Brulleau, fifth Librarian of Hush House, describes the nature of each of those shards, allegorically and otherwise.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|'The Third Shard then has been identified with 'the cry of pain'. The Lionsmith is a stoic Hour, but we must assume that in the Sundering Moment even he might have been unable to restrain his distress. Now the sound of tin under pressure we call the 'tin cry' - a reason, perhaps, for the further identification of the Third Shard as the 'Shard Royal'...|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘The Seventh Shard we call, informally, the [[Invincible Audacity]], which is struck from the [[Winning Move]] as the Winning Move is struck from a memory - with the application of sufficient Edge.’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Disciplines of the Hammer|Lesson: Disciplines of the Hammer]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Hindsight]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|An apparently theoretical project proposed by 'Lionel' of the Society of the Noble Endeavour which might permit the imprisonment of a renegade Forge-Name. A very heavily revised edition of an earlier and even more controversial work.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The book was evidently revised some time after the Wars of the Roads had ended, but even then this kind of discussion would have been politically difficult.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|'Lionel' suggests that the Disciplines of Scar and Hammer together would be necessary to create such a prison - but that either on its own would serve to release its occupant.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Disciplines of the Hammer|Lesson: Disciplines of the Hammer]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle written in [[Deep Mandaic]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The epic of the final battle of the Lionsmith with the remnant-giant Antaios.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|As always, the Lionsmith drew his strength from metal, and Antaios from stone… but the Lionsmith began to suspect also that this time, Antaios was drawing power from the Moon.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Lionsmith beseeches the Three for their assistance, and the Meniscate favours him with a skin of silver, like water, like mercury, so he too can drink power from the Moon; for, she whispers, he too will one day be drawn into a perfect balance.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Disciplines of the Hammer|Lesson: Disciplines of the Hammer]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]].

Sunset Passages.title: Sunset Passages
Sunset Passages.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=Sunset Passages.png
|mystery=4
|principles={{Lore|Forge}}
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Latin]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Sacra Solis Invicti]]
|memory=[[Memory: Revelation]]
|period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle written in [[Latin]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A miscellany of the funerary prayers, ceremonies and hymns of the Church of the Unconquered Sun, which was ascendant in the Third and Fourth Histories. It schismed during the Intercalate, when the Sun was divided, and has not survived as a significant force.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Church revered the Sun-in-Splendour before it was divided - but even while it was still whole, its later selves were recognised as its Names. The Madrugad, of course, presided over death and the passage into the House.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The White Ceremony was spoken to honour the Madrugad, at funerals held in the chilly space before dawn. The text cautions that all blades should remain sheathed while the Ceremony is spoken, 'lest the corpse be not quiet.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sacra Solis Invicti|Lesson: Sacra Solis Invicti]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle written in [[Phrygian]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A transcription of the play by Menander the Victor, possibly the dramatist of that name, into Phrygian, with commentaries.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The play describes a pilgrimage of smiths and adepts following the trail of the Burning Woman, who has appeared in all their dreams and given each a Wound and a Word.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The smiths and adepts give up on finding the Burning Woman, and resolve to build their own kingdom, 'where our strength will be sufficient to shatter the world.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Transformations & Liberations|Lesson: Transformations & Liberations]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

'''''The Book of Dissolution''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle written in [[Deep Mandaic]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Alexander Probst recovered a copy of this work from a mountain-temple in Persia. Other copies surface now and then, usually seared on rock.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Book consists mostly of prayers to the Unburnt God, the Forge of Days which consumes and transforms. It suggests the Forge's power arises partly from its nature, and partly from its tools.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Book describes an earlier House of the Sun, whose doors and ways were different. It praises the Forge of Days for opening the ways into the house, and for transforming that which was to that which is, despite the screams of stone...|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Transformations & Liberations|Lesson: Transformations & Liberations]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

The Black Book of Brittany.title: The Black Book of Brittany
The Black Book of Brittany.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Black Book of Brittany
|mystery=12
|principles={{Lore|Moon}}
|tally_price=4
|type=[[Codex]]
|Period=[[Solar]]
|image1=[[File:TheBlackBookofBrittany.png]]
|skill=[[Inks of Containment]]
|memory=[[Bittersweet Certainty]]}}
'''''The Black Book of Brittany''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle. It was gifted to St Brandan's Abbey by [[Brian of Brittany]] alongside [[The Red Book of Brittany]] and [[The White Book of Brittany]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|A volume of ink-lore gifted to St Brandan's by Brian of Brittany, who was made Earl of Cornwall after the Norman Conquest.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|"The Black Flower lies heavy, but the roots of the Watchman's Tree run deep, and they may not be hidden forever…"|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Black Flower, spoken of as a doom or geas, can be held at bay with the [[Nillycant|Last Ink of Power]] - brewed from '[[Solomon's Preparation|the Pale Mixture]]' in the presence of sufficient Winter with the arts of Containment.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Inks of Containment|Lesson: Inks of Containment]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Bittersweet Certainty]].

The Bee-Keeper's Ends.title: The Bee-Keeper's Ends
The Bee-Keeper's Ends.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=The Bee-Keeper's Ends|mystery=8|category=Readable|tally_price=3|language=|type=Codex|principles={{Lore|Nectar}}|skill=[[Insects & Nectars|Lesson: Insects & Nectars x2]]|period=[[Baronial]]|memory=[[Memory: Impulse|Impulse]]|image1=The Bee-Keeper's Ends.png}}The Bee-Keeper's Ends is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Nectar}} principle.
==Location==
==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Dialogues with bees and uses for honey, as erratically recorded by Ricardo Milagro, gardener of Hush House in Musgrave's time.|}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Milagro spends an entire chapter on his hatred of wasps, which he describes as 'the Vile Pretenders'.|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Milagro claims that bees retain many traditions passed down from earlier and greater branches of their species, but that they are fiercely jealous of these traditions being passed to lesser insects, and insist above all on an oath of secrecy. Tragically, therefore, he is unable to describe these more substantial and powerful traditions.|I've Read...}}
==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates [[Insects & Nectars|Lesson: Insects & Nectars]] x2 and [[Memory: Impulse]]. Reading it again provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

[[Category:Nectar]]

The Book of the Extinguished Heart.title: The Book of the Extinguished Heart
The Book of the Extinguished Heart.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=The Book of the Extinguished Heart.png
|mystery=16
|principles={{Lore|Heart}}
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Deep Mandaic]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Quenchings & Quellings]]
|memory=[[Bittersweet Certainty]]
|period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle written in [[Deep Mandaic]] by Ennis Lazali.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|In the days of the Shadowless Kings, Ennis Lazali was executed for prophesying the Division of the Sun. If any of his captors grew Long, they probably feel rather abashed now.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Lazali indicates that the Sun will be divided in the Malleary, by the Forge of Days, armed with the love in her heart.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Love will not be the cause of the Sun's death, but rather envy. Envy will not be the cause of the Sun's death, but rather thirst. Thirst shall not be the cause of his death, but curiosity. Curiosity shall not be his end; rather will it be love.’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Quenchings & Quellings|Lesson: Quenchings & Quellings]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Bittersweet Certainty]].

Sunset Celia and the End of Days.title: Sunset Celia and the End of Days
Sunset Celia and the End of Days.text:
{{Book (BoH) |title1=Sunset Celia
and the End of Days |image1=Sunset Celia and the End of Days.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |tally_price=2 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Sacra Limiae]] |memory=[[Memory: Foresight]] |period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} Principle, written in English by 'the Emiliano'. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|An Obliviate adept identified only as 'the Emiliano' rants desperately about the part Sunset Celia played in the Intercalate, as 'the proxy of the Sun'.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'Now she walks behind the Watchman, but did she always? She has many of the characteristics of a Maid-in-the-Mirror, after all. In older texts she has been called Caelia the Elagabaline. Perhaps she was his daughter? Perhaps Tryphon's sister? Perhaps, like the Watchman himself, she is like a shadow cast by two candles.'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'What must be revealed, will be revealed. Our Order's root is tainted, but its branches flourish beneath the shelter of the Watchman's greater Tree. I shall invoke its rites before the Chancel, the Cruciate, and the Rode. I shall write a final History. Or another shall write it for me.'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sacra Limiae|Lesson: Sacra Limiae]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Foresight]]. == Additional Information == Sunset Celia patronizes the library known as Crossrowhttps://weatherfactory.biz/feb-1-curia/, another branch of the Watchman's Tree, described as being in the Far West. Wherever this is the same Sunset Celia described in this book, or another individual taking her name, is unclear. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Sky]] [[Category:Curia]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

Singlefoot Songs.title: Singlefoot Songs
Singlefoot Songs.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=SinglefootSongs.png |mystery=6 |principles={{Lore|Scale}} |tally_price=1 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Hill & Hollow]] |memory=[[Savage Hymn]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Scale}} Principle, written in English by [[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Father Stanislav John Schaller, priest and diplomat, writes of his time on the slopes of Huashan -
'near to the Grove of the Green Immortals, but never too near.'}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Schaller's relations with the Grove are cautious - it's a Library of the Tree, but under the hand of the Hour named Applebright.
In time, however, Schaller comes to be more sympathetic to the Applebright, which he suggests 'causes harm only when so invited.'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The 'Singlefoots' of the title are one-horned, one-footed hill-things with sweet but powerful voices - powerful enough to 'open the mountain.'
The Singlefoots sometimes trample pilgrims; sometimes heal them; sometimes coerce them to 'enter the mountain' and become Singlefoots.
Schaller explains that when he found this last becoming too tempting, he decided to return to his homeland.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Hill & Hollow|Lesson: Hill & Hollow]]''. Reading always provides [[Savage Hymn]]. ==Trivia== *Despite authoring the book, talking to Fr. Stanislav John Schaller about the book does not provide anything. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Scale]] [[Category:Nocturnal Period]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

Recordings from the Althiban Abyss.title: Recordings from the Althiban Abyss
Recordings from the Althiban Abyss.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=Recordings from the Althiban Abyss.png |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Scale}} |tally_price=1 |language=[[Deep Mandaic]] |type=[[Phonograph Record]] |skill=[[Stone Stories]] |memory=[[Memory: Fear]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Phonograph Record]] of the {{Lore|Scale}} Principle, recorded in [[Deep Mandaic]] by [[Juliana Zawistowski]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Recordings from a subterranean space in the mountains near Baghdad of 'conversations' between the entomologist Juliana Zawistowski and an unidentified presence.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Only Zawistowski's part in the 'conversations' is comprehensible to the listener. The other side consists of grating, buzzing and rumbling sounds, perhaps only rock movements or artifacts of the recording process, which Zawistowski nevertheless unhesitatingly translates.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|
Zawistowski seems to believe that the presence identifies itself as a Name or remnant of the lost Hour called Seven-Coils. It pleads with her to assist its rebirth; it begs her to find something for it in the city of Emesa. Towards the end of the interview, Zawistowski grows suspicious, and repeatedly accuses the presence of being not the Seven-Coils at all - only 'an inhabitant.' The recording ends in mid-sentence.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this record provides ''[[Stone Stories|Lesson: Stone Stories]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Fear]]. [[Category:Scale]] [[Category:Nocturnal]] [[Category:Phonograph Record]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

Serpent-Root.title: Serpent-Root
Serpent-Root.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=Serpent-Root.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Nectar}} |tally_price=8 |language=[[Cracktrack]] |type=[[Tablet]] |skill=[[Rites of the Roots]] |memory=[[Numen: Loopholes]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} __NOTOC__'''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Tablet]] of the {{Lore|Nectar}} Principle, written in [[Cracktrack]] by an unknown author. ==Location== {{Spoilers|caption=Secret of the House|content=Can be found in [[Our Lady Beneath]] by using [[Hill & Hollow]] or [[Tridesma Hiera]] with any soul card at the [[Altar of the Knot]].|caption_element=h3}} ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|A mass of root-stock, shiny with age but still somehow viable. Tiny spidery scratchings, marked with embedded egg-shell shards, encode a cryptic message. [This object houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'Sea-born, tide-drawn, Meniscate-sister, Witch-lover. The House of the Moon will always have its messenger, though its messenger is different each time, in eye and flesh and heart…'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Feits, feats, posterns, loopholes, set down against the advent of Eternity by powers favouring imperfection and impermanence.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Rites of the Roots|Lesson: Rites of the Roots]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Numen: Loopholes]]. == Trivia == *A hint for finding this book can be found in ''[[One Thousand Threads]]'', which provides [[Tridesma Hiera|Lesson: Tridesma Hiera]]: {{Quote|Speak these supplications before an altar whose roots have drawn from a sacred spring; perhaps another root will rise towards daylight.}} *Another hint can be found in ''[[The Wonderful Shape]]'', which provides [[Tridesma Hiera|Lesson: Tridesma Hiera]]: {{Quote|The final invocation is one for the 'Restoration of the Roots', to be spoken before an altar of the Triple Knot - but, puzzlingly, it should not be spoken by any priestess of the Knot, or even by one who has been initiated into their Mysteries.}} *Another hint can be found in ''[[The Queen's Turn]]'', which provides [[Hill & Hollow|Lesson: Hill & Hollow]]: {{Quote|The traditions described here - the ones generally described as 'Hill and Hollow' - are associated with Lagiah before her Turn; but now that she's a Name of the Red Grail, they might also be safely used before an altar of the Triple Knot.}} [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Nectar]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Tablet]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]] [[Category:Numen]]

Shuritic Book of Suns.title: Shuritic Book of Suns
Shuritic Book of Suns.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=Shuritic Book of Suns.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |tally_price=8 |language=[[Deep Mandaic]] |type=[[Scroll]] |skill=[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |memory=[[Numen: the Great Counterfeit]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Scroll]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} Principle, written in [[Deep Mandaic]] by [[Hagar]]. ==Location== The book can be found in the [[Silver Vault]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|A radically different text from any of the other versions of the Book of Suns, attributed to Hagar, Queen of Shur, Mother of Wolves. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'Set down with reverence before the Intercalate, by one who understood what would come to pass…'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Apocryphal chapters foretell the means by which the Sun-in-Splendour and the Forge might circumvent the impossibility of their joining, through proxies that are in some sense themselves…|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sacra Solis Invicti|Lesson: Sacra Solis Invicti]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Numen: the Great Counterfeit]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Sky]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Scroll]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

The Carbonek Schism.title: The Carbonek Schism
The Carbonek Schism.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=The Carbonek Schism.png
|mystery=6
|principles={{Lore|Moth}}
|tally_price=3
|language=[[Sabazine]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Sacra Limiae]]
|memory=[[Memory: Hindsight]]
|period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle written in [[Sabazine]] by [[Ambrose Westcott]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The order of Obliviates, on the brink of schism, assembles in a Bounds-house identified only as 'Carbonek', after the Fisher-King's castle of legend. There the Know and the Long of the order debate their long policy of non-involvement in 'matters of Feather and Scale'.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|One of their number - the one recording their debates - describes how in desperation he has found some kind of solution in a 'volume of transcendent heresy', but dares not pursue it alone. He convinces a handful of other Obliviates to depart Carbonek with him, while the others cross the sea to Port Noon.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|In the last few pages, the author reveals himself as the Know-adept Ambrose Westcott, writing in an uncharacteristically serious mode. He informs any who should find this work that he has returned the book he spoke of to 'Abbot Geffrey's Secret', where it can be retrieved with certain invocations of the Sacra Limiae. He hopes that one who has read this far, and understood this much, will find a History to determine.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sacra Limiae|Lesson: Sacra Limiae]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Hindsight]].

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Moth]]
[[Category:Baronial]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Readable]]

The Book of the White Cat.title: The Book of the White Cat
The Book of the White Cat.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=The Book of the White Cat.png |mystery=16 |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |tally_price=5 |language=[[Phrygian]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Watchman's Paradoxes]] |memory=[[Memory: Revelation]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} Principle, written in [[Phrygian]] by [[Penelope of Gordion]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Stories brought by a blind white cat to Penelope of Gordion.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The aviform Hours - the Crow, the Laughingthrush, the Dove, and the twin Kites - have been known to meet in the mountains north of Gordion, at a place called the Roost, to exchange gossip. Penelope indicates that mortals who hear their words directly are obliterated, but claims that her cat goes unnoticed and returns to her with rumours from the Hours' meetings.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The stories that Penelope claims as Hour-gossip are fragmentary and confusing: accounts of contests where Hope and Dread and the Shadowless Empire are used as game-pieces, agendas of ruin and remembrance from no known history. The most interesting element is the protective incantation she records at the end of the book, after she worries that the Hours might in fact learn of her spying.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Watchman's Paradoxes|Watchman's Paradoxes]]'' (x3). Reading always provides [[Memory: Revelation]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Sky]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

The Barrowchild's Elegies.title: The Barrowchild's Elegies
The Barrowchild's Elegies.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=The Barrowchild's Elegies|mystery=10|category=[[Readable]]|tally_price=3|language=[[Latin]]|type=[[Codex]]|principles=[[Winter]]|Period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]|image1=[[File:TheBarrowchildsElegies.png|thumb]]}}''The Barrowchild's Elegies'' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Winter]] principle written by the [[Barrowchild]].
==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|The Barrowchild, a Gaulish adept who won a place in the ranks of the Ordo Limiae, enumerates the 'great shadows' laid to rest in tombs of power, and discusses their various conditions.|}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|The Barrowchild identifies numerous modes that are neither true death nor true life: the 'vitrification of the heart'; 'the corrupt light of the Wood'; 'chor-stasis'; 'the wandering of the fet'…|I'm Reading...}}After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|The Barrowchild warns particularly of the 'avidity of trist', where a remnant-shadow's longing for change survives its sense of self and even devours its wist. That longing may draw the curious into the tomb, where the remnant-shadow changes so that it cannot be distinguished from its visitor - or that the reverse becomes true - and that it is never again possible to say whether it is the shadow or the visitor that exits the tomb.|I've Read...}}
==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates 2x [[Rhyme & Remembrance|Lesson: Rhyme & Remembrance]]. Reading always provides [[Memory: Regret|Regret]].

==Speculation==

The 'avidity of trist' described in the mastery text may describe what happened to the player if one chooses [[The Archaeologist]] for the librarian origin.



[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Winter]]
[[Category:Readable]]
[[Category:Codex]]

Plantagenet Mysteries.title: Plantagenet Mysteries
Plantagenet Mysteries.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=Plantagenet Mysteries.png
|mystery=21
|principles={{Lore|Moth}}
|tally_price=2
|language=[[Deep Mandaic]]
|type=[[Codex]], [[Multitudinous]]
|skill=[[Transformations & Liberations]]
|memory=[[Memory: Foresight]]
|period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Multitudinous]] [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle written in [[Deep Mandaic]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Exhaustive attempts to analyse and renew the Blood of the Sun by one of the numerous occult societies, after the manner of the Endeavour Club, for whatever squalid political motive.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘…until the King fell beneath his great Steed in its Utmost Configuration. By the time he could be cut free, his Alloy had already begun to tarnish, and that Day was ever afterwards known as his Great Misfortune…’|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Since the Sun and the Forge had both bestowed their Favour, one could not remove it without the other - or would not. But neither could the Alloy be renewed by any Power in the Mansus. So the King looked beyond the Mansus - beyond the Bounds…’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Transformations & Liberations|Lesson: Transformations & Liberations]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]]. 

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Moth]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Readable]]
[[Category:Multitudinous]]
[[Category:Baronial]]

Quirinic Meditations.title: Quirinic Meditations
Quirinic Meditations.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=Quirinic Meditations.png
|mystery=21
|principles={{Lore|Lantern}}
|tally_price=4
|language=[[Ericapaean]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Auroral Contemplations]]
|memory=[[Memory: Contradiction]]
|period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Multitudinous]] [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle written in [[Ericapaean]] by Quirinus, a Name of the Colonel.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Battle-apothegms of the Name Quirinus.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Quirinus of the Two-Headed Spear is one of the more approachable Names of the Colonel - still grave and inflexible, but more inclined to divulge occasionally useful advice…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|When Quirinus was honoured in Rome, he was sometimes associated with the enigmatic god Janus - especially in the rites of the Unnumbered Legion. The advice in these pages doesn't confirm any such connection, but does suggest a more philosophical side to this warrior-Name.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Auroral Contemplations|Lesson: Auroral Contemplations]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Contradiction]].

The Book of Masks.title: The Book of Masks
The Book of Masks.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=The Book of Masks.png
|mystery=14
|principles={{Lore|Moth}}
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Phrygian]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Weaving & Knotworking]]
|memory=[[Memory: Impulse]]
|period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle written in [[Phrygian]] by Athena Vana.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Athena Vana's work on the rogue Hour called the Vagabond, who is also known as the Laughingthrush, the Centipede, the Pilgrim, and by many other names - or as Vana has it, 'masks'.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Mask of the Laughingthrush, says Athena Vana, had a great friendship with the Sun-in-Splendour, the highmost Hour of the Mansus (now divided and departed). The Mask of the Sight-Thief painted the river in the Mansus. The Mask of the Vagabond was forbidden the Mansus, not for what she had done, but for what would occur...|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Mask of the Centipede recalled her birth-place, Miah, which had punished her for creeping into the temple precinct. This Mask cursed Miah to drink only dust and to be remembered only by the wind - 'for not beneath any Mask does she forgive, and the Centipede's hunger is not to be forgotten.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Weaving & Knotworking|Lesson: Weaving & Knotworking]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

Petition for a Labyrinth Season.title: Petition for a Labyrinth Season
Petition for a Labyrinth Season.text:
{{Stub}} {{BoH_Item |title1=Petition for a
Labyrinth Season |image1=[[File:Petition for a Labyrinth Season.png]] |type=[[Ready to Post]], [[Readable]] |Location=[[Crafting]]}} {{quote|If this ever reaches its destination, it might bring Numa.

Numa cannot be bidden; but now and then, it has been successfully petitioned.}} {{Tocright}}
The '''Petition for a Labyrinth Season''' is a letter that can summon [[Numa]]. It can be [[Crafting|Crafted]] at some [[Workstations#Desks|Desks]] and requires: * [[Porphyrine]] * A [[Blank]] item * At least 20 {{Lore|Knock}}, {{Lore|Moon}} or {{Lore|Rose}} * ''No'' {{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Edge}} or {{Lore|Winter}} The petition may then be used at [[The Post Office]], along with 3 [[Tally]], to invoke [[Numa]] at the end of the current Season. {{Quote|'By a courier of the Lower Skies?'

The Postmistress accepts the message, weighs the spintria, finds them both sufficient. 'I guarantee nothing,' she tells me.|A Bird-Marked Seal}} ==Recipe breakdown== Porphyrine provides 7 of each [[Principles|Principle]]. Only [[Quire of Paper]], [[Typewriter]], or [[Canvas]] may be used in the Paper slot, as the other items with the Blank [[Aspects|Aspect]] have {{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Edge}}, or {{Lore|Winter}} principles. The item used for writing the petition will be destroyed. The most Principle that may come from [[Memory]] is 5, as [[Wormwood Dream]] includes {{Lore|Winter}}. [[Shapt]], [[Fet]], [[Trist]], or [[Phost]] may be used, though Phost provides no benefits. All other elements contain {{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Edge}}, or {{Lore|Winter}}. A fully upgraded [[Elements of the Soul|Element of Soul]] provides 5 Principle Assuming maximum Principle from other sources, a [[Skills|Skill]] must be at least level 2 to provide the remaining 3 Principle. ==Quotes== Depending on which Principle is used to write the petition, its contents change slightly: ===With Knock=== {{Quote|With the proper arts and signs - and the proper encaustum - a Librarian of the House might find a way to attract the direct attention of an Hour. The Beach-Crow has no dominion over Numa - no Hour does - but he knows it better than some. Perhaps he will find the season.|Compose a Petition to the Beach-Crow}} ===With Moon=== {{Quote|With the proper arts and signs - and the proper encaustum terminale - a Librarian of the House might find a way to attract the direct attention of an Hour. The Sister has no dominion over Numa - no Hour does - but she knows it better than many. Perhaps she will bring the season."|Compose a Petition to the Sister-and-Witch}} ===With Rose=== {{Quote|With the proper arts and signs - and the proper encaustum terminale - a Librarian of the House might find a way to attract the direct attention of an Hour. The Vagabond has no dominion over Numa - no Hour does - but she knows it better than most. Perhaps the season will follow her here.|Compose a Petition to the Vagabond}} All petitions finish the same way: {{Quote|The design is complete. To travel via the Way of the Lower Skies, it must be sanctified with the proper seal, by one charged with the delivery of messages of import...}} ==Memories== These memories are usable to create Petition for a Labyrinth Season. Other memories may be slotted, but will provide no benefit. {| class="sortable mw-collapsible fandom-table" |+Memories !Memory !{{Lore|Knock}} !{{Lore|Moon}} !{{Lore|Rose}} |- |[[Clouds]] |0 |1 |0 |- |[[Fog]] |3 |3 |0 |- |[[Mood|Epiphany]] |0 |2 | 0 |- |[[Mood|Awen]] |2 |0 | 2 |- | [[Wistful Air]] |0 |0 |2 |- |[[Confounding Parable]] | 0 |2 |2 |- |[[Nameday Riddle]] |2 | 0 |0 |- |[[Secret Threshold]] | 2 |0 |1 |- |[[Memory: A Stolen Secret]] |1 |2 |0 |- |[[Memory: Gossip]] |0 |0 |2 |- |[[Memory: Intuition]] |0 |2 |2 |- |[[Memory: Pattern]] |2 |0 |0 |- |[[Horizon-Sight]] |0 |0 |4 |- |[[Occult Scrap]] |2 |0 |2 |- |[[Numen: the Great Counterfeit]] |0 | 5 |0 |- |[[Numen: That Old Lost Music]] |0 |0 |5 |- |[[Numen: Loopholes]] |5 |5 |0 |- |[[Numen: the Paths of the Sun]] |5 |0 |0 |- |} ==Skills== These [[skills]] are listed at base level: "2" indicates that the Principle is primary. {| class="sortable mw-collapsible fandom-table" |+Skills !Skill !{{Lore|Knock}} !{{Lore|Moon}} !{{Lore|Rose}} |- |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |0 |1 |0 |- | [[Door & Wall]] |2 | 0 |0 |- |[[Edicts Liminal]] |1 |0 |0 |- |[[Edicts Liminal]] |2 |0 |0 |- |[[Hill & Hollow]] |0 |2 |0 |- |[[Horns & Ivories]] |1 |0 |0 |- |[[Inks of Power]] |0 |0 |1 |- |[[Insects & Nectars]] |0 |1 |0 |- |[[Lockworks & Clockworks]] |2 |0 |0 |- |[[Ouranoscopy]] |0 |1 |0 |- |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |0 |0 |1 |- |[[Pearl & Tide]] |0 |1 |2 |- |[[Preliminal Meter]] |2 |0 |1 |- |[[Sand Stories]] |0 |1 |2 |- |[[Sea Stories]] |0 |1 |0 |- |[[Serpents & Venoms]] |0 |1 |0 |- |[[Sky Stories]] |0 |0 |1 |- |[[Solutions & Separations]] |1 |0 |0 |- |[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars]] |1 |0 |0 |- |[[Tridesma Hiera]] |0 |1 |0 |- |[[Vak]] |2 |0 |1 |- |[[Wolf Stories]] |0 |1 |0 |- |} [[Category:Ready to Post]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Crafting]] [[Category:Knock]] [[Category:Moon]] [[Category:Rose]]

The High Traditions of the Noble Endeavo.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=[[File:TheHighTraditionsoftheNobleEndeavour.png]]
|mystery=6

|tally_price=3

|period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} Principle, written in [[Latin]] by the Endeavour Club.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A blandly positive work on the Endeavour Club, published by the Endeavour Club. The Club was founded in 1862 but claims to draw from much older traditions.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Club members are assigned names out of noble myth - 'Jaufre', 'Roland', and, unexpectedly, 'Breadbeddel'. They claim to be heirs to the Leashed Flame, which gave the island of Britain such appalling power in some histories.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Their 'Endeavour' itself is a purifying fire which makes its fuel something more than human. This transformation, however, is no longer encouraged by the Club, and perhaps - the work is coy on this - no longer permitted.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Disciplines of the Hammer|Lesson: Disciplines of the Hammer]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]]. 

==Rewards==
The Endeavour is a reference to the Forge victory in ''Cultist Simulator.''

{{Book (BoH) |image1=The Humours of a Gentleman.png |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |tally_price=3 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Sky Stories]] |memory=[[Memory: Gossip]] |period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} Principle, written in English by Samuel Savage. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Samuel Savage's satirical comedy, on the intrigues of the ailing, but cunning John Sonne, his mistress Maevelin, her lover Leo, and the upstart Corvino.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|By the end of the first act, Maevelin has revealed a secret door in the walls of the House to Leo, and Corvino has taken to consuming Worms.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The play is scabrous and occasionally hilarious. The characters are contrary and capricious. Many of the more resonant lines might well be formulae of power, disguised in plain sight.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sky Stories|Lesson: Sky Stories]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Gossip]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Sky]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]] [[Category:Baronial]]

The Crossing to Noon.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=[[File:TheCrossingtoNoon.png]]

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} principle written in Latin by [[Garcia Sauri]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The mystic Garcia Sauri gives a picaresque account of the adventures of Franklin Bancroft, 'Prince of Wines', and Eva Dewulf, 'the Pale Lady', on their way to the hidden island of Noon.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘For a long long time the Blackbone pondered her next move, until the Moon dared to peep from behind a cloud, and the Prince completed the composition of his third sestina. But the Lady met the blind gaze of its open pores, waiting for the tide…’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Garcia Sauri acknowledges in an epilogue that it is widely known that Eva in fact tragically drowned herself - and her twin infant grand-daughters - without ever making such a journey. But he adds contemptuously: 'it is also widely known that the City Unbuilt will so remain, that only one History is ever written, and that Janus is a Mansus-prank.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sea Stories|Lesson: Sea Stories]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Salt]].
