'''''The Incandescent Tantra''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle written in [[Sanskrit]].

==Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Michael Blockley, the eccentric iron magnate, was fond of quoting from this tantra. Blockley died in a factory fire.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Dialogues with an entity called the Crucible Prince. The Prince warns about the appetites of his mistress, the Burning Queen, and the peril of the naked desire she shares with the Sun, but professes his loyalty nevertheless.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|"A rite which changes is necessarily a rite which destroys. But a great change requires a destruction of savage extent."|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Transformations & Liberations|Lesson: Transformations & Liberations]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

{{Book (BoH)
|image1=The Locksmiths Dream Incursus.png
|mystery=6

|type=[[Codex]]

|period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle written by [[Teresa Galmier]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The fifth (and final?) volume of Teresa Galmier's notorious work, which began as an examination of parallels in the mystic dreams of artisans but became an account of her own occult journey. This volume was apparently never published nor, allegedly, even written. Yet here it is.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘The Law goes back all the way to Stone: the Keys cannot be held or owned. This had, I believe, the unexpected consequence that those outside the law may hold and own them. But even they cannot keep them. And of course a Key is no more physical than a spirit. But a spirit may be housed in a body, and I have touched a Key with my own hands.’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘So the Ligeians hold the keys. I had thought the Ligeians only - 'only' - old and powerful transgressors of the Crime of the Sky. But I begin to understand that the Crime of the Sky is more even than it seems. And why a Twin, who unites what is not to be divided, might accept a Ligeian as her Name...’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing|Lesson: Glaziery & Lightsmithing]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Confounding Parable]].

'''''The Kerisham Portolan''''' is a [[book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle.  

== Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|A beautifully illustrated and heavily annotated 'portolan' - a nautical atlas of ports and destinations.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{quote|Two pages have been gummed together. When teased apart they reveal a route to 'Ys Behind the Wave' - marked in red and gold inks with heavily underlined warnings. 'HERE THE FINAL CITY'. 'STRIKE THE HOURS.' 'LEST EARTH AND SKY BREAK OPEN…'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{quote|‘It quickly becomes clear that many of its destinations no longer exist, or never existed in the traditional sense, but the annotations remain fascinating. The routes to Noon, the Long-sanctuary across the Western Sea, may remain viable…’|I've Read...}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Sea Stories|Lesson: Sea Stories]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Gossip]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle written by [[Teresa Galmier]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The first volume of Teresa Galmier's examination of parallels in the mystic dreams of artisans.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The parallels in mystic dreams experienced by carpenters, masons and other artisans, and what they purport to reveal about the architecture of the world. Surprisingly mordant and even funny. No-one has ever explained why Galmier devoted herself to this quixotic exploration of artisan's dreams.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Time and again we hear of the Wood, which rises from the world's foundation. All trees reach for light. What does the Wood reach for? Is there a difference between light and Light? I think the key to dreams of the Wood might be one of these - the one that isn't exactly real.’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Purifications & Exaltations|Lesson: Purifications & Exaltations]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]].

'''The Locksmith's Dream: Trespasses''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written by [[Teresa Galmier]].

== Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|The third volume of Teresa Galmier's examination of parallels in the mystic dreams of artisans.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|In this volume, notoriously, Galmier's prose begins to disintegrate, and it is not clear which dreams are in fact her own.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|<nowiki/>'The woman in the sand-coloured robe has told me: the stairways of the Mansus go ever up. Death is down. The Mother of Ants guards both directions with each of her heads, and so the passage must always be through a wound. I think the White Door might be a wound. That's one reason the Dead sometimes pass it. I think I have the other half of the Secret now, and I hope my reader can put both halves together.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Edicts Liminal|Lesson: Edicts Liminal]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

The Five Letters On Memory.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=[[File:TheFiveLettersOnMemory.png]] |mystery=6 |principles={{Lore|Winter}} |tally_price=2 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Rhyme & Remembrance]] |memory=[[Memory: Regret]] |period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} Principle, written in English by [[Julian Coseley]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Julian Coseley's epistolary treatise on 'matters memorial and mnemonic', addressed to his then-friend Claude Hersault, the mystic and antiquarian.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The book is partly a practical manual, expounding memory-palace-like techniques, and partly an exploration of 'Memory Rarefied' - modes in which sense or experience persist outside a mortal mind.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|This is an early work, and by Coseley's standards it brims with optimism, even enthusiasm. If books, he suggests, are the memory that does not die, then 'perhaps with sufficient Endeavours, Memory's Murderer might be Contain'd'.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Rhyme & Remembrance|Lesson: Rhyme & Remembrance]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Regret]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Winter]] [[Category:Curia]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

The Hissing Key.title: The Hissing Key
The Hissing Key.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=|mystery=[[Scale]] 8|category=Book|tally_price=5|language=[[Greek]]|type=[[Readable]], [[Thing]], [[Codex]]|period=[[Dawn]]|skill=[[Serpents & Venoms]]|memory=[[Memory: Hindsight]]|image1=The Hissing Key.png|principles=}}''The Hissing Key'' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Scale]] principle written in [[Greek]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:{{quote|An account of the ascent of the Hour called the Mother of Ants, by the Bosk-scholar Mek, of the Theban branch of the House of Lethe.|}}Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|Mek is not sympathetic to the Mother of Ants, who he calls 'the Milk-Thief'. He reviles her for her part in the death of the Seven-Coils, which he presents as a treacherous conspiracy.|I'm Reading...}}After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|The Milk-Thief conspires with the Ligeian Echidna and the Hour-to-be called Chiliarch (now more generally rendered as 'Colonel') to unseam the Seven-Coils with feathers and drown her in salt. The Colonel thus ascends to Hour status; the jealous Milk-Thief, once the Colonel's priestess, seduces Echidna into lending her the Hissing Key to enter the Mansus through the Savage Door, beginning her own ascent to Name and ultimately Hour.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates 2 [[Serpents & Venoms|Lesson: Serpents & Venoms]]. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Hindsight]].

The Locksmith's Dream: Stolen Reflection.title: The Locksmith's Dream: Stolen Reflections
The Locksmith's Dream: Stolen Reflection.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=File:TheLocksmithsDreamStolenReflections.png |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |tally_price=1 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Watchman's Paradoxes]] |memory=[[Memory: Revelation]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} Principle, written in English by Teresa Galmier. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|The fourth volume of Teresa Galmier's expansive work - no longer a discussion of the dreams of artisans, but a valuable survey of other works. The tone is calmer than that of 'Trespasses', but occasionally fearful, even paranoid. This volume was published in 1926 but almost immediately recalled and pulped by the publisher - at the request of the author or possibly the authorities, depending which story you believe. A few copies survive.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'Janus is the Gatekeeper, the twin-god, the god that wounds, the presager of changes, the sun, the moon. So we identify him with the Watchman, the Twins, with the Mother, with the Forge, with the Meniscate and the Madrugad. He cannot be all these. Can he? The flamines knew the Church, knew the Dry Land, knew Elagabalus. Is he then synthesis? Or is he something else? In Gallaecia they called him Ianus Lamius, but the Obliviates are notorious for their slanders.'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'Janus has, they say, not one face but two. To which I reply: why only one? Why only two? Hersault and Coseley - according to Thomas Love Denman - once agreed that Janus was 'all the gods and none'. But later, Hersault described him as 'all the gods', and Coseley favoured 'none'. Denman was a sinister dilettante, but this rings true of them both.'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Watchman's Paradoxes|Lesson: Watchman's Paradoxes]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Revelation]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Sky]] [[Category:Nocturnal Period]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

The Debate of Seven Cups.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=The Debate of Seven Cups.png
|mystery=10

|tally_price=2
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Solutions & Separations]]
|memory=[[Memory: Impulse]]
|period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|‘Distillations of Spirit’ recorded by an alchemist who identifies himself in the foreword as ‘But Sir Thomas Browne’s Reflexion.’}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Time is a pure Flame, and we live by an invisible Sun within us.’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Darkness and Light divide the Course of Time, and until that Course is Run, Eternity remains History's Bed-Fellow. Sorrow then is Sense's final Solvent, and even a Tear, should it fall enow, might destroy a Stone…’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Solutions & Separations|Lesson: Solutions & Separations]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

The Gospel of Zacchaeus.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=The Gospel of Zacchaeus.png
|mystery=8

|period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar Gothic]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written in [[Greek]] by [[Zacchaeus]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|An extremely heterodox account of the Nazarene Messiah and his works, describing his ascension to the Mansus through the opening of his body.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Seven were the wounds of His body, seven the doors of the House. Seven the lesser aspects of the Hours, and Knock the aspect above all, for the Mother of Ants is the Mother of Salvation.’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The book includes a description of a rite which can be used to raise a corpse to half-life, 'in memory of He who bled for the Wood'; but the marginalia claim that the Mother of Ants no longer permits use of this rite.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Horns & Ivories|Lesson: Horns & Ivories]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: A Stolen Secret]].

The History of Inks.title: The History of Inks
The History of Inks.text: {{Book (BoH) |image1=The History of Inks.png |mystery=14 |principles={{Lore|Rose}} |tally_price=4 |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Inks of Power]] |memory=[[Intuition]] |period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar Gothic]]}} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Book]] of the {{Lore|Rose}} principle. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|A legendary grimoire of exotic ink-making lore. The cover and some of the pages, unfortunately are stained and crusted with something more like mucus than ink.|Description}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The encaustum Marakat is refined from the liquor named leathy in the presence of Nectar aspect. The Priestesses of the Knot have also learnt to brew Marakat in this wise - yet for the nature of their arts, their task may be easier…|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The History concludes with the admission that the encaustum named 'Orpiment Exultant' was once drawn from the veins of Forge-long. Thankfully, it seems, it can also be refined from Iotic Essence using the techniques in this book - or with 'transformations' and 'the jewel-science'.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of the book generates [[Inks of Power|Lesson: Ink of Power]] (x2). Reading it always provides [[Intuition|Memory: Intuition]]. ==Trivia== * {{PAGENAME}} is referenced in [[The Wakefield Papers]] in ''Prophet and Loss'' and ''Seventy-Seven Winks''. In that paper [[Magister Hokobald]] writes that a [[w:c:cultistsimulator:Raw_Prophet|Raw Prophet]] absconded with {{PAGENAME}} while he was borrowing it. Thus, it is likely that the stains on the page are from the Raw Prophet. 184 years later, the book is retrieved by [[Daymare]] and delivered to [[Serena Blackwood]] * ''Seventy-Seven Winks'' also implies that this Raw Prophet (called "Propsy" by Daymare) wrote the book as well [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Rose]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Solar]]

'''''The Devoured Tantra''''' is a [[Books|scroll]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle written in [[Sanskrit]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|The diplomat-priest [[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller|Stanislav John Schaller]] transcribed this from the library of a Red Long, but his manuscript remains in a private collection in Kerisham.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Devoured Tantra warns of the uses and dangers of appetite, but devotes an entire passage to the 'star-limbed hunger-bringers', who it describes with obvious affection.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote| 'A million blazing fires in the belly engulf what has been swallowed by the multiform mouths.”|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Applebright Euphonies|Lesson: Applebright Euphonies]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Confounding Parable]].

The Chandler's Wish.title: The Chandler's Wish
The Chandler's Wish.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=The Chandlers Wish.png
|mystery=12
|principles={{Lore|Lantern}}
|tally_price=2
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Inks of Revelation]]
|memory=[[Memory: Foresight]]
|period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Formulae and instructions invoking Moth, Lantern and - exceptionally, paradoxically - the liminal and theoretical Hour called the Chandler. The author is anonymous, admitting only that they are 'one who is not yet nameless.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The author makes a passionate argument that the Hour named Chandler is in fact the oldest, even though he does not exist, because he is - supposedly - the culminating event of a plan that precedes even Grail and Moth.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Where the Chandler has passed, the understandings of the Colonel and the Lionsmith will wrench open truth. Where the Chandler will pass, Moth will pass before him.’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Inks of Revelation|Lesson: Inks of Revelation]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

The Locksmith's Dream: Portions and Prop.title: The Locksmith's Dream: Portions and Proportions
The Locksmith's Dream: Portions and Prop.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=[[File:TheLocksmithsDreamPortionsandProportions.png]] |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |tally_price=1 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Lockworks & Clockworks]] |memory=[[Confounding Parable]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}} __NOTOC__
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} principle, written in English by Teresa Galmier. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|The second volume of Teresa Galmier's examination of parallels in the mystic dreams of artisans. The frontispiece has been slashed with a razor.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|In this volume, Galmier records fewer dreams, and explicates more of her own elaborate theories. 'We see this again and again: what is below can't escape what is above.'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'The finest artisans all dream of the White Door in the end. I'm no artisan, only a scholar. I think there's a Secret that all these artisans know, but I think that Secret is only half the story.'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Lockworks & Clockworks|Lesson: Lockworks & Clockworks]]''. Reading it always provides [[Confounding Parable]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Sky]] [[Category:Nocturnal Period]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

The Concursum Diaries.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Concursum Diaries
|mystery=8
|principles={{Lore|Rose}}
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Phrygian]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|image1=The Concursum Diaries.png

|memory=[[Intuition]]
|Period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}}
__NOTOC__
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the [[Rose]] principle written by [[Lars Westergren]].
==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|The diaries of the explorer and murderer Lars Westergren. He's unhelpfully translated them into Phrygian, for privacy.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|There are map-legends, there are maps of legends, and there are legends of maps. Aspects of the Mansus subsist in all of these, in much the same way that you find water in a swamp and in a cup and in the sky.'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Westergren describes a series of expeditions into the Mansus. He focuses on the details of the experience - the colours, the vistas, the textures - rather than the practicalities. He does warn that the Mansus changes each year, although he assures the reader that the Doors have been the same. 'Doors may close, but they never disappear. At least not while there have been mortals in the Mansus. We're like mice.'|I've Read...}}
==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates ''[[Path & Pilgrim|Lesson: Path & Pilgrim]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Intuition]].

==Trivia==
* This book was also in ''[[w:c:cultistsimulator:Cultist_Simulator|Cultist Simulator]]'', however in that game it provided {{Lore|Lantern}}-related lore.

The Instruments of the Heart.title: The Instruments of the Heart
The Instruments of the Heart.text: {{Book (BoH) |title1=The Instruments of the Heart |mystery=10 |principle={{Lore|Heart}} |tally_price=4 |type=[[Codex]] |Period=[[Solar]] |image1=The Instruments of the Heart.png |memory=[[Cheerful Ditty]] |skill=[[Drums & Dances]]}} '''''The Instruments of the Heart''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle written by Sister Isabel. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description:{{quote|Sister Isabel, then Precentress of the Abbey-Church of St Brandan's, engages in dialogues with a Heart-long of a kind called 'duendrazon' that has taken partial possession of her body.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The duendrazon, like all its kind, usually dwells in the Mansus but can enter the physical world by manifesting as music, and take possession of a willing - or semi-willing - mortal who hears and loves that music… like Isabella.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Isabella records her dreams of the high Mansus, where she is accorded the duendrazon's status and titles. In return, the duendrazon enjoys what it calls 'caesura' - a welcome oblivion. 'Our mostly-blessing is that we may never cease - except in caesurae'. There is something more that Isabella refers to as the 'caesura magna', but she laments that her duendrazon will not tell her exactly what that might be.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Drums & Dances|Lesson: Drums & Dances]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Cheerful Ditty]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Heart]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Solar]]

The Intimations of Skin.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Intimations of Skin
|mystery=8
|principles={{Lore|Grail}}
|tally_price=1

|Period=[[Nocturnal]]}}
'''''The Intimations of Skin''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} principle written by Niels Frederik Malskær.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Fiendishly complex, weirdly distorted illustrations of 'congress and anatomy' by the haunted visionary painter Niels Frederik Malskær.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Malskær illuminates the evolutions of the Names of the Grail with unfortunate clarity. It seems that a Lovely who consumes an Ivory becomes an Ivory. A Lovely who consumes a Thirstly becomes a Thirstly. A Lovely who consumes a Name of another Hour might take its place...|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|In the penultimate illustration, a Lovely grapples with a fungoid knot that can only be a Name of the Crowned Growth. The Lovely's mouth and other portals gape wide, and the Growth-Name is already partially engulfed - but it seems that Malskær couldn't bring himself to illustrate the result, and the final illustration is only a scrawled, bloated obscurity.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Desires & Dissolutions|Lesson: Desires & Dissolutions]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Beguiling Melody]].

The Dream of the Conspiracy of the Lower.text:
{{Book_(BoH)
|title1=The Dream of The Conspiracy of The Lower Skies
|mystery=16
|principles={{Lore|Grail}}
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Phrygian]]

|image1=[[File:The Dream of the Conspiracy of the Lower Skies.png]]

'''''The Dream of The Conspiracy of The Lower Skies''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|The disgraced oracle Damaon Azenaten sifts through the tall tales of Penelope of Gordion, the work of the court poet Kalle and the forbidden fragments of the work of the adept Arrettrez, indentifying common themes.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Damaon insists that the Hours, far more than mortals, are subject to their passions - to hatred, and even to love. 'The seasons of famine and plenty, the turn of the Earth, the transformations of the furnace - all these are only the results of the enactment of the lesser passions of the Hours.'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Damaon suggests that the Hours have constrained their rivalry to avoid a war within the House of the Sun. He identifies the 'Fear of the Crime of the Sky' as the reason that Hours do not satisfy other passions. He speculates on the horrifying possibilty of Hours turned alukite. 'What then would they devour?'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars|Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Gossip]].

{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Deeds of the Scarred Captain
|mystery=12

|image1=Deeds of the Scarred Captain.png}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}'' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} principle written in [[Greek]] by Pavel Shulga.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Painstakingly assembled by the soldier of fortune and sometime remittance man, Pavel Shulga, during his years in Greece.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|An account of the founding of Mycenae by a 'Scarred Captain' who first slew seven monsters to make the land safe.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|As the Captain destroys each monster, a flood of blood rises higher, until at last a priestess drowns and is reborn as a serpent-goddess. She blesses the Captain, and he departs for the 'House above the Forest', leaving Mycenae to reign supreme after the flood of blood subsides.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Sharps|Lesson: Sharps]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]].

==Trivia==

* The Scarred Captain is [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/The_Colonel the Colonel], the seven monsters were the seven heads of [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/The_Seven-Coils the Seven-Coils], and the priestess is [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/The_Mother_of_Ants the Mother of Ants].

The Invisible Opera (Unfinished Recordin.text: {{Book (BoH) |title1=The Invisible Opera (Unfinished Recording) |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |tally_price=1 |type=[[Phonograph Record]] |image1=[[File:TheInvisibleOpera(UnfinishedRecording).png|thumb]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]] |memory=[[Cheerful Ditty]] |skill=[[Strings & Songs]]}} '''''The Invisible Opera (Unfinished Recording)''''' is a [[Phonograph Record]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} principle. ==Description== Selecting the record provides the following description: {{quote| A recording of a 1911 attempt at a performance of 'Wings within Wings', the so-called Invisible Opera.|}} Upon choosing to master the book at a [[Phonograph]], the Librarian learns: {{Quote| The singers complete 'the Skewbald Aria', 'Beneath Our Skin', and 'A Rose in Miah' without incident; but the Invisible Opera is dedicated to Ferezeref the Magpie, who delights in unexpected interruptions…|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote| The recording ends with a clamour of horrified voices, a grating metallic screech, and a soft brass buzzing that fades into burring silence…|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of the record generates ''[[Strings & Songs|Lesson: Strings & Songs]]'' x2. Listening to it always provides [[Cheerful Ditty]]. [[Category:Nocturnal]] [[Category:Phonograph Record]] [[Category:Sky]] [[Category:Readable]]

The Ivory Book.title: The Ivory Book
The Ivory Book.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=The Ivory Book.png |mystery=8 |principles={{Lore|Winter}} |tally_price=5 |language=[[Fucine]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Quenchings & Quellings]] |memory=[[Memory: Regret]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} Principle, written in [[Fucine]] by [[Kurenai]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|
A manual of the Ordo Limiae, an order of quasi-immortals who maintained a secret enclave at the source of the river Limia, in the Roman province of Hispania Gallaecia. This manual was compiled by one Kurenai, who claims to have fled 'the tyranny of the Chrysanthemum Throne' to cross the world and join the Ordo.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Members of the Ordo took an oath, the Ivory Chain, not to have commerce with the Hours. Followed literally, this would be almost impossible for an adept, so the manual contains numerous clarifications, exceptions and processes of indulgence.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|
Kurenai describes the Order's burial rites, which include spells to ensure - in theory - that the souls of dead Long are not given to the Hours. The Hour called the Ivory Dove, who memorialises and commemorates, is to be invoked, in secret, in these rites, 'for with that Hour we have made an understanding'.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Quenchings & Quellings|Lesson: Quenchings & Quellings]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Regret]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Winter]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

'''''The Flayed Tantra''''' is a [[scroll]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle written in [[Sanskrit]], written by 'Peel' - possibly [[Dr Arun Peel]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|This Tantra is recorded as being spoken by an enigmatic individual identified as 'Peel', with many of the qualities of the mythological naga. The Flayed Tantra played a notable part in Alexander Sparrow's paranoid pamphleteering.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|'Peel' was numbered among the Great Hooded Princes, but it breaks with its brethren and followed the Thunderskin in the endless dance.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|Once Peel had peeled itself, it had the ink it needed to write the Tantra. It had to face the wrath of its fellows. Here is the invocation it used to fend them off.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Maggephene Mysteries|Lesson: Maggephene Mysteries]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Storm]].

{{Quote|Carlos Garcia Sauri, the ectastic mystic of the Pyrenees, was known to recite this in three languages, though he had never visited the Subcontinent.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Known-Unknown Tantra describes a journey to the White Door of the Mansus, beyond which speech ceases. It describes a mantra which can be used, at the right place and time, to achieve that door.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘The light of a lantern can only ever reveal the space between the forest shadows.’|I've Read...}}

The Deaths of the Moon.title: The Deaths of the Moon
The Deaths of the Moon.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=File:TheDeathsoftheMoon.png
|mystery=8
|principles={{Lore|Moon}}
|tally_price=3
|language=[[Killasimi]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Snow Stories]]
|memory=[[Memory: Salt]]
|period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written in [[Killasimi]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A Haustorial tract on various forms of survival after death.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|When the heart no longer beats, the Grail may keep the spirit in the body, and an appetite is indicated to sustain. (Alukites are the best-known, but not the only, of this nature). This is the waning-moon mode…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The full-moon mode is the intensification of one element of the soul to the point where ordinary sustension is unstable. Our Protector, the Generous of Hosts, began of this nature, and its generosity remains ungentle. It is possible for the body's health or the heart's chor to outpace the other elements, so that a static mode becomes impossible and growth proceeds in dramatic stages until balance remanifests...|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Snow Stories|Lesson: Snow Stories]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Salt]].

'''''The Leonine Tantra''''' is a [[Readable|scroll]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} Principle written in [[Sanskrit]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:

{{quote|In the most notorious translation of the Leonine Tantra, Ashley Phillips is listed as the translator, but their existence is explicitly denied in the prologue. This confusion is characteristic of books which mention the Great Hooded Princes.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:

{{Quote|The Tantra describes, elliptically, the Great Hooded Princes and the multitudinous ways in which they influenced wars against foreign invaders of the Land of the Great River, 'although in a sense they were also invaders'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:

{{Quote|Lions can be created, not as children are created, nor as words are created, but as weapons are created. The Great Hooded Princes learnt to create lions from their spyings on the affairs of the Hours, and not all lions now serve the Golden General.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates ''[[Edicts Martial|Lesson: Edicts Martial]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]].

==Trivia==

* The "Golden General" is [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/The_Lionsmith the Lionsmith].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle written in [[Fucine]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A fragile manuscript, illuminated with twinned shapes of sad and luminous beauty, and with all the phases of the moon. It might be as old as the seventh century, but the language - Fucine - is much older. The cover is tooled goatskin decorated with garnet.}}

r>Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|These pages outline the nature, and the doctrines, of an Hour that weaves together the willing, an Hour that is sought beneath the moon and at the water's edge: the Sister-and-Witch. The language is wilful, knotty, poetic. It'll take some untangling.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The first volume of the Geminiad reminds us that the Sister-and-Witch has been known to manifest as the Witch-and-Sister - and that this face is always hungry, while the other face may heal. It implies connections between the Sister-and-Witch and the Hours of the upper Mansus - especially the lunar Hour called the Meniscate - but it is ambiguous on whether the Sister-and-Witch is a Mansus-Hour proper. And it speaks at length about the sadness of the two-who-are-one, the sadness that remains from their time as flesh.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Weaving & Knotworking|Lesson: Weaving & Knotworking]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Solace]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written in [[Vak]] by [[Burzghash]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The Limian Burzghash's gazetteer of the patterns and rhythms of the Hours' progress through the Mansus, from Concursum to Malleary, Malleary to Wood…}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Each century in the Mansus is a great feasting-hall. In each ninety-ninth year, the hall falls silent; the Elegiast sits alone at the feast.’|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘There are paths in the Mansus that only the Sun has walked. In the time of the Sun's Division, who will know them? When the Second Dawn comes, who will walk them?’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Door & Wall|Lesson: Door & Wall]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Pattern]].

The Iron Book.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=The Iron Book.png

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} Principle, written in [[Fucine]] by Melerai Yivni.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A manual of the Ordo Limiae, an order of quasi-immortals who maintained a secret enclave at the source of the river Limia, in the Roman province of Hispania Gallaecia. This manual was compiled by one Melerai Yivni, who claims to have travelled to join the Ordo from 'the Crossroads of the Waters'.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Members of the Ordo took an oath, the Iron Chain, that required them to remain hidden from the world. This manual includes presumably long-obsolete addresses and pass-phrases that could have been used to find the Ordo's contact in the town of Iria.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The final part of the manual describes the punishments for Ordo members who break their oath of secrecy. This includes an invocation used to summon the spirit called King Crucible as an agent of vengeance. Yivni cautions that this must be a last resort when the oathbreaker would otherwise go unpunished: summoning King Crucible might draw the personal attention of the Forge of Days. (A marginal note suggests, in any case, that King Crucible, 'in a most transcendent Sulk of Sulks', no longer leaves the Mansus.)|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Disciplines of the Hammer|Lesson: Disciplines of the Hammer]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

'''''The Elations of Limentinus''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} principle written in [[Latin]] by [[Abbot Geffrey]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|The second volume of Abbot Geffrey's hypothetical theological debates in the Socratic mode.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|<nowiki/>'If Janus were an Hour, Limentinus might be counted among his Names, but Janus has never passed that threshold, and so Limentinus is not…'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Geffrey discusses 'the signs upon the Threshold', drawing comparisons between the duties of guest and host, and the status accorded to Hours and other powers who dwell in, are permitted in, or are forbidden access to the House of the Sun. (It was of course Geffrey who later invited censure by giving sanctuary to Natan of Regensburg, in an age when the Jews were by royal order unwelcome anywhere in the kingdom.)|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars|Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Pattern]].

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The Encircling Tantra speaks of the Serpent Gate, that hungry portal sometimes known as the Spider's Door, which is sacred to the Mother of Ants, through which the Great Hooded Princes pass.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The tantra includes an invocation but cautions, helpfully, that the invocation is of insufficient power to reach the Serpent Gate from the Hunter's Gate. 'A road which has no destination is itself a destination,' it adds helpfully.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Horns & Ivories|Lesson: Horns & Ivories]]''. '''''The High Mysteries of the Innermost Chamber of our Church Solar''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle written in [[Fucine]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|The secret rites of the Church of the Unconquered Sun, which held power in at least two Histories.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Church chiefly worshipped the Sun-in-Splendour, the original undivided sun; but this text also includes the devotions of its aspects as the chilly winter dawn and the departing sunset, as well as the Meniscate, the Sun's 'night-self'. Priests of the Church were all male, but rites are also included which allowed women to cross ceremonially to manhood.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Church's highest rites were performed in the Concursum, the chamber at the Mansus' heart where the Hours were known to pass. These rites include salutations to non-solar Hours: the Grail, the Ring-Yew, the Horned Axe and the Thunderskin.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Sacra Solis Invicti|Lesson: Sacra Solis Invicti]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]].

{{Quote|Christoph Larquebus claimed to have purchased two hand-written copies of the Codex from a family of witches on the shores of the Sea of Marmara. A third was 'given to the Sea'.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Sister-and-Witch came from the West, where they were born in two wombs, one a princess, one a monster. Nevertheless they loved each other from birth, and met in secret 'to seek union'.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|When the great drought came, the kings of that land tried to sacrifice the princess and the witch, so they sailed across the Sea. When despair took them, they flung themselves into the drowning waters... and so found the Painted River, where they entered the Mansus through the offices of the Red Grail. Nevertheless, the Codex ends with a condemnation of the Grail.|I've Read...}}

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The one known extant copy of this in Western Europe was stolen from the British Library in 1892. One Harvey Hattington confessed to the crime and claimed to have eaten it, with butter and garlic, in a moment of ungovernable whimsy.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Herein the Great Hooded Princes are shown beseeching the Wood to rise and devour an invading Timurid army. The 'Dapple-King', the 'Honey-Tree' and the 'Sea-Twins' all deny their request, until they enlist the help of a burrowing secret-keeper...|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Armed with blackmail material from the 'burrowing secret-keeper', the Great Hooded Princes petition the powers of the Wood for a second time, and are successful. One quarter of the Timurid army is devoured by bees, one quarter drowns themselves, and one quarter 'disrobe themselves until nothing remains'.|I've Read...}}

Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Solutions & Separations|Lesson: Solutions & Separations]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Intuition]].

{{Quote|A fragile manuscript, illuminated with twinned shapes of sad and luminous beauty, and with all the phases of the moon. It might be as old as the seventh century, but the language - Fucine - is much older. The cover is a dark and exotic leather with a smooth, almost chitinous surface, decorated with jasper.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|These pages outline the seven bloody natures of the 'Daughters of Lagiah' - those corrupted immortals who gave birth to children, in defiance of the Laws of the Upper Heaven; who devoured them, in obedience to the Hours' punishment; and who have been left outside the law...|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The second volume of the Geminiad suggests that these seven corrupted immortals have been accorded the privileges of Names of the Witch-and-Sister - or perhaps the Sister-and-Witch. It reminds us that the Twins unite what is apart, and that the 'Crime of the Sky' is in some sense a supreme joining. And it speaks at length about the sadness of the seven, the sadness of mothers whose children are forever lost, and far worse than lost.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Pentiments & Precursors|Lesson: Pentiments & Precursors]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Satisfaction]].

They flush the skin and glow beneath the eyelids after the book is closed.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{quote|‘We must devour to be devoured. We cannot be undevoured, as we cannot be unborn.’|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of the book generates ''[[Desires & Dissolutions|Lesson: Desires & Dissolution]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Intuition]]. ==Trivia== *''The Orchid Transfigurations'' volumes appeared in [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Cultist_Simulator_Wiki Cultist Simulator]. There, its untranslated form is described as:
''"A sixteenth-century alchemical fever-dream, attributed to Robert Fludd, frequently banned for the disturbing allure of its illustrations. This is in the original Latin."''

The Republic of Teeth.title: The Republic of Teeth
The Republic of Teeth.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=[[File:TheRepublicofTeeth.png]] |mystery=6 |principles={{Lore|Scale}} |tally_price=3 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Serpents & Venoms]] |memory=[[Memory: Intuition]] |period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Scale}} Principle, written in English by [[Valentine Dewulf]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|An eccentric political tract by Valentine Dewulf.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Valentine suggests that rulers should be elected to govern by serpents, not their subjects, 'for the Serpent, being cold-blooded in its Nature, is incorruptible.'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Valentine's initial proposal is that a college of electors should subject themselves to the bites of venomous serpents - which he grades and details, preferring the least dangerous - and should allow the resulting deliria to guide them in their choice of people's representatives. He becomes concerned, however, by the practicalities of ensuring equal quantities of venom in each case, and gets half-way into a proposal for using birds instead in the selection process, before giving up mid-sentence.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Serpents & Venoms|Lesson: Serpents & Venoms]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Intuition]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Scale]] [[Category:Baronial]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

'''''The Six Letters on Necessity''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle written by [[Julian Coseley]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Warnings and confessions about the cost of the secret arts, addressed to a student by the seventeenth-century magus (and reputed immortal) Julian Coseley.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Coseley's tone is urgent - as if he suspected he might have little time left.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Even the Sunne can be divided, though it require the Forge of Dayes for its division.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Transformations & Liberations|Lesson: Transformations & Liberations]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

'''''The Skeleton Songs''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle written by Arabella Dusk.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Poems of greedy delight composed by the possibly pseudonymous Arabella Dusk, the rumoured heiress-turned-madam-turned-poetess.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|In Arabella's introduction, she explains that the book was to be illustrated, but that the Suppression Bureau would not permit it. She hints that the illustrations still exist somewhere. The book is dedicated to 'Sir Parsival of the Red Cup'.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Twenty-Six Delightful Fruits; the Seven Chastisements; the Nine Gardens; the Four Regrets.|I've Read...}}

== Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Resurgences & Emergences|Lesson: Resurgences & Emergences]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Beguiling Melody]].

|image1=The Sea Does Not Regret.png}}
'''''The Sea Does Not Regret''''' is a [[book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written by [[Mr Ehsan Fekri|Ehsan Fekri]].

== Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Ehsan Fekri, one-time Secretary Salvant of the Curia of the Isle - responsible for the Curia's healing efforts - writes of his experiences in Brancrug, and hints at his travels elsewhere.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Sea does not regret the tide,' Fekri writes, 'for when the tide has passed, it leaves its traces on the sand; which traces are the Sea's memory.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{quote|Fekri is a keen fisherman, and speaks glowingly of the fish suppers of Brancrug. He also admits that his enthusiasm for 'the bounty of the sea' has altered him - that before he came to Brancrug, he consumed only those things found in the earth. 'I was the greater thereby, but all of us give up what we were, to become what we are.'|I've Read...}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of the book will provide ''[[Pearl & Tide|Lesson: Pearl & Tide]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Salt]].

==Trivia==
* Presenting [[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] this book in a consultation rewards the Librarian with ''[[Spices & Savours|Lesson: Spices & Savours]]''.

The Rose of Waznei.title: The Rose of Waznei
The Rose of Waznei.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=[[File:TheRoseofWaznei.png]]
|mystery=8
|principles={{Lore|Lantern}}
|tally_price=3
|language=[[Greek]]
|type=[[Codex]]

|memory=[[Memory: Revelation]]
|period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle written in [[Greek]] by Waznei.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The heretical teachings of a disgraced offshoot of the Sisterhood of the Knot, that arcane-contemplative order that existed in all histories. This was recorded by 'Waznei', and dedicated to St Respicius.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The offshoot favoured by Waznei - 'the True Sisterhood' - followed St Respicius in pursuing ascension in the name of the Door-in-the-Eye, the merciless Hour of light. St Respicius failed, perhaps because the larger Sisterhood tracked him down and ritually strangled him, but Waznei outlines steps for those who hope to succeed.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Seek in dreams; seek the Mansus. The Third Mark can be achieved only when one has passed the Stag Door. One must pass the Wood. One must rise to the White Door. The Stag Door awaits the light-bearer, in the sight of Ghirbi.’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Auroral Contemplations|Lesson: Auroral Contemplations]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]].

[[THE OPEN HEAD]] is a [[Reel of Film]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} Principle by [[Ilse Bischoff]]. It is in [[Hyksos]]. As a film, it can only be mastered with the [[Projector]].

==Description==
Selecting the film provides the following description:
{{quote|Ilse Bischoff's hallucinatory quasi-documentary, notionally about the Greco-Turkish War of the previous decade.}}

Upon choosing to master the film, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|A hammer-armed Turk and a sword-armed Greek pursue each other through the Pindus, setting traps for each other, robbing peasants, chalking insulting graffiti on walls. The tone is notionally anti-war, but any scholar of the invisible arts would recognise the Edge-hour subtext... and the Hyksos messages in the graffiti.}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The sword-wielder methodically fills a church with candles; lights each one; strips, again, to the waist to reveal his terrible scars; his chest somehow swings open like a cupboard door to reveal a blood-drenched book… and the film ends.}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Disciplines of the Scar|Lesson: Disciplines of the Scar]]'' x2. Watching it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]].

'''''The Sky, the Soul''''' is a [[book]] of the [[Lantern]] principle written in [[Aramaic]] by Kalle, a poet of the Shadowless Kings. 

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|The grand labour of Kalle, an ascetic poet writing at the court of the Shadowless Kings.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Kalle's verses are brief, obscure, and often dominated by images of violence. 'A star is a pin-prick, but the Sun is a wound.' |I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|It's always possible to be deader,' Kalle states. 'The Watchman goes before; none but seven may go after.' 'Yet surely we are born to the Glory as the sparks fly upwards.' |I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Pyroglyphics|Lesson: Pyroglyphics]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

'''''The Moon's Egg''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written by [[Abbot Thomas]]. 

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The third and last volume of the meditations of Abbot Thomas of the Abbey of the Black Dove.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Abbot Thomas speaks of the coming death he hears in the sound of the waves, but rejoices that his blood will water the 'Egg of the Moon' - by which he seems to mean the future.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The last chapter was dictated, not written, by Abbot Thomas. When Thomas' old sword-brother Trygve returned to raid the Abbey, Thomas had broken his monastic oaths and taken up arms to defend the abbey. The two had both been mortally wounded. Thomas' last words are 'The Wheel turns; the Moon sleeps.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Pearl & Tide|Lesson: Pearl & Tide]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Confounding Parable]].

The Queens of the Rivers.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=The Queens of the Rivers|mystery=[[Scale]] 4|category=[[Book]]|tally_price=1|type=[[Readable]], [[Thing]], [[Codex]]|image1=[[File:TheQueensoftheRivers.png|thumb]]|Period=[[Nocturnal]]}}''The Queens of the Rivers'' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Scale]] principle.
==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:{{Quote|A surreal contemporary play by the enigmatic Monica Medina, in which the Queens of the Rivers are murdered, one by one.|Description}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|The Queen of the Vistula is poisoned. The Queen of the Dnieper chokes on a fish-hook. The Queen of the Tagus is burnt alive...|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|The culprit, it transpires, is the audience. The surviving Queens are directed to execute whatever audience members do not escape. A surprisingly lucid epilogue suggests that the correspondence of river-names with historical events does provide clues to secret histories behind our own.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates [[Path & Pilgrim|Lesson: Path & Pilgrim]] and [[Memory: Gossip]]. Subsequent [[Consider|consideration]] of the book produces only [[Memory: Gossip]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written in [[Aramaic]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A priestess of the Sisterhood of the Knot claims to have discerned the true meaning of the Thunderskin's birth.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The writer credits the Red Grail, the Ring-Yew and the Horned-Axe - the powers the Sisterhood reveres - with agreeing a final treaty between the Hours of the House and the Hours they'd displaced: the Thunderskin loved the Yew, and the Grail destroyed him, as restitution for the slaying of the Horned-Axe's sisters and brothers.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Thunderskin entered the Mansus through the Peacock Door, 'a privilege never given to the Witch-and-Sister: but then their merit was much less'. The writer admits that entry through the Peacock Door is unseemly, but insists that under the circumstances, there was no other way.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Tridesma Hiera|Lesson: Tridesma Hiera]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Beguiling Melody]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A volume of collected teachings of the Sisterhood of the Knot, that arcane-contemplative order that existed in all histories, but in some was very powerful indeed. This was recorded by 'Hypatia', and dedicated to St Nympha.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|St Nympha is described as 'not born, but cultivated'. The sentience that became the saint, 'Hypatia' indicates, inhabited a sinner's corpse in order to enable that sinner's redemption.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Not all the Dead enter the Mansus by the Winter Door. Not all the Dead enter the Mansus at all.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Weaving & Knotworking|Lesson: Weaving & Knotworking]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Solace]].

'''''The Temptations of Architecture''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} principle written by [[Ambrose Westcott]].

Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The antiquarian and nyctodromist Ambrose Westcott writes of the 'dangers of doors', with particular reference to a house in the bounds named 'Treowen'.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|<nowiki/>'No doubt they have come to regret the ambitions of their Winding Stair; even now in Treowen, a silver sea is unwisely visible from a rash window…'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|Westcott explains that the Wheelocks, the 'charge-holders of Treowen', have had recourse to dramatic measures to prevent oneiric encroachment, removing the entire top floor of the building. 'Nevertheless,' he writes, 'the business of the Moon-Hall has begun to touch the other business of the house...'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Door & Wall|Lesson: Door & Wall]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Secret Threshold]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle written by Samuel Savage.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|One of Samuel Savage's more thoughtful works: an allegorical play about the City Clarity, a city that is also a book, and the sentences which inhabit it.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Lords Proverbial and Lords Disquisitional war in the streets of Clarity, while the Punctuants get drunk on ink and supply the jokes (though, by Savage's usual standards, there aren't very many jokes.)|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The final act sees the Lords Proverbial unsealing the City Clarity's gate to expel the population into the unknown. (The formula that they use for the unsealing is a real one - it can be used with Knock and Preliminal Meter to create a gate-sign of power.)|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Preliminal Meter|Lesson: Preliminal Meter]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Confounding Parable]].

of the Black Wood |image1=File:TheSerenityoftheBlackWood.png |mystery=12 |principles={{Lore|Moth}} |tally_price=4 |language=[[Greek]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Sacra Limiae]] |memory=[[Confounding Parable]] |period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar Gothic]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle written in [[Greek]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|An allegorical history of the House of Lethe, which it is here implied was inspired by the Centipede. 'Sereno Blackwood' is an occult alias to this day.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'The Proverbial Footloose' gathers travellers in a wood, and leads them through, but abandons them part-way. They find themselves beset by 'glorious monsters'.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The travellers discover they can survive if they close their eyes (they adopt a closed eye as their sign) and that they can go unnoticed if they drink from the clear cold streams. They never forget 'that proverbial footloose, the Centipede' but they never forgive her either.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sacra Limiae|Lesson: Sacra Limiae]]'' (x2). Reading it always provides [[Confounding Parable]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Moth]] [[Category:Solar]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]]

{{Quote|Black Elie, disgraced Damascene Matriarch of the Sisterhood of the Triple Knot, wrote this while fleeing the 'agents of the Duty.'}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Elie writes of the 'secret colours of the Sun' - the blessed 'traces of Error' - weaknesses in sunlight, balancing principles in its reflection.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|A deeper account of these secret colours, Elie reveals, was kept at [[Shrine: the Chancel|a shrine to the Three Hours of the Chancel]] at the 'grey rock in the sea', far from the intrigues of Sisterhood and Church. It is hidden from the common eye, but can be revealed with the arts of Sickle and Eclipse.|I've Read...}}

Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sickle & Eclipse|Lesson: Sickle & Eclipse]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle written in [[Sanskrit]] by C.G. Burial.

Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|C.G. Burial, the temperance campaigner, published elements of this in a pamphlet, which had to be withdrawn and destroyed after it became popular.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|A disquisition on the many varieties of thirst, their uses and their effects.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The tantra describes how the satisfaction of thirsts may allow a mortal to rise into the service of the Thirsting Power, but warns of the consequences of rejecting those rarer thirsts for common ones.“A man who thirsts, O Mighty One, whose mind clings to actions in this world, will return to this world of action from that other place.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Orchids & Narcotics|Lesson: Orchids & Narcotics]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Satisfaction]].

The Queen's Turn.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=[[File:TheQueensTurn.png]]

|principles={{Lore|Moon}}
|tally_price=3
|language=English

|memory=[[Memory: Salt]]

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written by the [[Barrowchild]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A sixteenth-century translation of the Barrowchild's account of 'Lagiah's Turn' - when Lagiah, the Queen Unsated, was offered the opportunity to enter the service of the Hours of the Triple Knot, as long as she repudiated her brother-lover Antaios.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Lagiah accepts, setting aside 'the arts of the low red sun' associated with Antaios. She bargains, however, for freedom for her daughters. The Hours of the Triple Knot accept casually, knowing that Lagiah has devoured her daughters - but wily Lagiah has decided, 'in the secret hollow of her heart', that she will adopt any who ask, if they can prove their fierceness.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The traditions described here - the ones generally described as 'Hill and Hollow' - are associated with Lagiah before her Turn; but now that she's a Name of the Red Grail, they might also be safely used before an [[Altar of the Knot|altar of the Triple Knot]].|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Hill & Hollow|Lesson: Hill & Hollow]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Salt]].

[[Category:Moon]]
[[Category:Baronial]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Readable]]

The Songs of the Carapace Cross.title: The Songs of the Carapace Cross
The Songs of the Carapace Cross.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Songs of the Carapace Cross
|mystery=16
|principles={{Lore|Moth}}
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Fucine]]
|skill=[[Edicts Liminal]]
|memory=[[Memory: Pattern]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|image1=The Songs of the Carapace Cross.png
|Period=[[Dawn]]}}
'''''The Songs of the Carapace Cross''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} principle written in [[Fucine]] by Micah Xi.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Micah Xi, sometimes called the Magus of Quartz, etched this work in acid on stone. It has been reproduced many times in many languages since, but the reproductions are often lost to landslides.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns
:{{Quote|Xi describes the rites of the gods-who-were-stone, the first Hours, as practiced before the existence of human civilisation by the 'Carapace Cross'. He claims a final survivor of the Cross shared the information with him.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|The rites are largely obsolete now. Few have been observed, in the last thousand years at least, to have any effect at all. Nevertheless, Xi identifies at least one invocation of particular power. He warns that it should be used with caution, lest the gods-who-were-stone might find their way back from Nowhere.|I've Read...}}
==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Edicts Liminal|Lesson: Edicts Liminal]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Pattern]].

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Moth]]
[[Category:Dawn]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Readable]]

The Rose of Nuriel.title: The Rose of Nuriel
The Rose of Nuriel.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Rose of Nuriel
|mystery=10
|principles={{Lore|Grail}}
|tally_price=4
|language=[[Greek]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|image1=The Rose of Nuriel.png
|skill=[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars]]
|memory=[[Memory: Satisfaction]]
|period=[[Solar]]}}
'''''The Rose of Nuriel''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|A volume of collected teachings of the Sisterhood of the Knot, that arcane-contemplative order that existed in all histories, but in some was very powerful indeed. This was recorded by 'Nuriel', and dedicated to St Tryphon.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|St Tryphon, Nuriel explains, performed secret miracles in the name of 'She who Bleeds and Bears' and 'She who Opens'. Thus St Tryphon opened the way to the House of the Sun; thus St Tryphon underwent the Great Birth, an ascension to immortality.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|St Tryphon began his ascension by passing the 'Horned Door'. St Tryphon continued his ascension by learning the 'Invocation Thiatic' - which Nuriel does not here record, on account of its extreme holiness. And, Nuriel explains grimly, to achieve the Seven Marks of the Great Birth, St Tryphon consumed 'those whose soul had left them, and even those in whom the soul remained.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars|Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Satisfaction]].

The Red Book of Brittany.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Red Book of Brittany
|mystery=12
|Period=[[Solar]]
|tally_price=4
|type=[[Codex]]
|image1=The Red Book of Brittany.png
|principles={{Lore|Rose}}
|skill=[[Inks of Power]]
|memory=[[Memory: Satisfaction]]}}
'''''The Red Book of Brittany''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Rose}} principle. It was gifted to St Brandan's Abbey by [[Brian of Brittany]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|A volume of ink-lore gifted to St Brandan's by Brian of Brittany, who was made Earl of Cornwall after the Norman Conquest.|}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:{{Quote| 'The Red Flower lies heavy, but the roots of the Watchman's Tree are constant…''|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|The Red Flower is described as 'the temptation of suffering'; but its suffering can apparently be allayed when 'the Copper Fruit' is enspelled with Nectar-aspect and these Herbs and Infusions techniques.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides 2 ''[[Inks of Power|Lesson: Inks of Power]]''. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Satisfaction]].

The Raptures of Forculus.title: The Raptures of Forculus
The Raptures of Forculus.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Raptures of Forculus
|image1=[[The Raptures of Forculus.png]]
|mystery=4
|principles={{Lore|Knock}}
|category=[[Book]]
|tally_price=4

|type=[[Codex]]

|memory=[[Memory: Pattern]]
|period=[[Solar]]}}
'''''The Raptures of Forculus''''' is a [[book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} principle written by [[Abbot Geffrey]].

== Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description: 
{{Quote|The first volume of Abbot Geffrey's hypothetical theological debates in the Socratic mode.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|‘If Janus were an Hour, Forculus might be counted among his Names, but that door remains closed, and so Forculus is not…’|I'm Reading}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|"Geffrey discusses 'the signs that mark Doors', which might permit or forbid access to certain thoughts and dreams, speculating (carefully) on which of the sanctioned Hours might teach or govern each sign."|I've Read}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars|Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Pattern]].
