The Tantra of Worms.title: The Tantra of Worms
The Tantra of Worms.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=Tantra of Worms.png |mystery=8 |principles={{Lore|Scale}} |tally_price=1 |language=[[Sanskrit]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Coil & Chasm]] |memory=[[Memory: Fear]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Scale}} Principle, written in [[Sanskrit]] by an unknown author. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|The entomologist Juliana Zawistowski eventually came to insist that this text was written by insects inhabiting a human skin. She never presented evidence for her claim. There are diagrams. The diagrams are not good to look upon.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The Tantra explains various less than practical countermeasures against the Worms, the 'Serpents Which Are Not Serpents'. Moth and Winter are closest to them, and so understand their weaknesses, but both have their own perils. The Lionsmith crushes them, but that's not recommended for mortals.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'The Worms have always been eager to inhabit us. Here are the practices which make us inhospitable to them.' There are diagrams. The diagrams are not good to look upon, and none of the practices they show would allow the subject to survive.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Coil & Chasm|Lesson: Coil & Chasm]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Fear]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Scale]] [[Category:Nocturnal]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

The Sun Disfigured.title: The Sun Disfigured
The Sun Disfigured.text: {{Book (BoH) |image1=The Sun Disfigured.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Grail}} |tally_price=8 |language=[[Cracktrack]] |type=[[Scroll]] |skill=[[Applebright Euphonies]] |memory=[[Numen: the Sun's Weakness]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[scroll]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle that contains a [[Numen: the Sun's Weakness|Numen]] and was written in [[Cracktrack]] by [[Celia the Elagabaline]]. __NOTOC__ ==Location== {{Spoilers|caption=Secret of the House|content=''{{PAGENAME}}'' is hidden within the [[Chancel of the Abbey Church]], and is uncovered by using [[Sickle & Eclipse]] or [[Sacra Limiae]] with any Element of the Soul at [[Shrine: the Chancel]].|caption_element=h3}} ==Description== Selecting the scroll provides the following description: {{Quote|A scroll of anthropoderm parchment, written in the golden ink called Uzult. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]}} Upon choosing to master the scroll, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The author of the text calls herself 'the Elagabaline'. Sometimes she seems to be Sunset Celia, the Watchman's Name; sometimes she seems to be Lady Tryphon, the Grail-long. It is unclear whether these are separate entities or the same person - it may be unclear even to the writer.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The flaws in the Sun's Plan are elucidated. The Sun's Plan itself is never entirely clear, but it is a project of some kind to enter, possess, or surrender to the Glory - the pure light above the Mansus. This book suggests ways in which that Plan might fail.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this scroll provides ''[[Applebright Euphonies|Lesson: Applebright Euphonies]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Numen: the Sun's Weakness]]; a [[Numen]] that can be used to establish a [[history]] and win the game. This numen has a special victory for [[the Executioner]]. == Trivia == *The method to obtaining this scroll is hinted at in ''[[The Carbonek Schism]]'', ''[[The Secret Colours]]'', and ''[[Sunset Celia and the End of Days]]''. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Grail]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Scroll]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Numen]]

The Orchid Transfigurations: Noon.title: The Orchid Transfigurations: Noon
The Orchid Transfigurations: Noon.text:
{{Book (BoH) |title1=The Orchid Transfigurations: Noon |mystery=4 |principle={{Lore|Heart}} |tally_price=2 |language=[[Latin]] |type=[[Codex]] |image1=[[File:TheOrchidTransfigurationsNoon.png]] |Period=[[Curia]] |memory=[[Memory: Solace]] |skill=[[Maggephene Mysteries]]}} '''''The Orchid Transfigurations: Noon''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle written in [[Latin]], supposedly by [[Robert Fludd]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description :{{Quote|The third volume of a compilation of quasi-Rosicrucian allegories, supposedly by Robert Fludd. This is in the original Latin.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|A long dialogue between the Mountain-Mother and the Vigilant Storm describes the ways in which both mountains and storms end, and the protections they use against those ends.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|‘But we must use the knife,’ said the Lion-Throned One, ‘the noose, the flame, the Waking Word, against those who have passed the Three-Valved Door. And so none may pass: that is our Law, and the Law of the Sun.’|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Maggephene Mysteries|Lesson: Maggephene Mysteries]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Solace]]. ==Trivia== *''The Orchid Transfigurations'' volumes appeared in [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Cultist_Simulator_Wiki Cultist Simulator]. There, its untranslated form is described as:
''"A sixteenth-century alchemical fever-dream, attributed to Robert Fludd, frequently banned for the disturbing allure of its illustrations. This is in the original Latin."''
[[Category:Book]] [[Category:Heart]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Curia]]

The Sevenfold Slaying of the Seven-Coile.title: The Sevenfold Slaying of the Seven-Coiled
The Sevenfold Slaying of the Seven-Coile.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Sevenfold Slaying of the Seven Coiled
|image1=The Sevenfold Slaying of the Seven-Coiled.png
|mystery=16
|principles={{Lore|Edge}}
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Fucine]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Disciplines of the Scar]]
|memory=[[Memory: Fear]]
|period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} Principle written in [[Fucine]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|An account of the destruction of a primaeval Hour, a god-who-was-Stone.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|There are twelve verses. In the first, an ascendant Hour identified as the Scarred One enumerates his justifications for destroying the Seven-Coiled: its appetites, its growth, its enmity to humanity. In the second, a priestess puts out his eyes and scars his skin to protect him against the Seven-Coiled's magics. In each of the next seven verses, he destroys one aspect of the Seven-Coiled...|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|In the tenth verse, the Scarred One bathes his priestess-patron in the blood of the Seven-Coiled, to lend her power. In the eleventh, they assault the 'temple behind the world', entering it by force. In the twelfth, they swear a tripartite oath to protect their ancestors, their descendants, and themselves.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Disciplines of the Scar|Lesson: Disciplines of the Scar]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]].

==Trivia==
The book tells the story of the slaying of the Seven-Coils by the Colonel and the Mother of Ants.

The Three and the Three (Kerisham Manusc.title: The Three and the Three (Kerisham Manuscript)
The Three and the Three (Kerisham Manusc.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Three and the Three (Kerisham Manuscript)
|mystery=10
|tally_price=2
|type=[[Codex]]
|principles={{Lore|Moon}}
|Period=[[Curia]]
|memory=[[Intuition]]
|skill=[[Edicts Inviolable]]
|image1=The Three and the Three (Kerisham Manuscript).png}}
'''''The Three and the Three (Kerisham Manuscript)''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|A more recent version of a much older text, this book describes the operations of the Chancel and the Calyptra, two triads of Hours with subtle, far-reaching powers and responsibilities. It has been heavily censored, but even so contains potent secrets.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The deepest knowledge is safeguarded by the Covenant of the Watchman's Tree, whose patrons are Calyptra - the three flowers on the Watchman's Tree - blood, soot, and snow…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Calyptra may be known, as Night, Dawn, Eclipse. The Chancel may be known, as Threshold, Mirror, Shell. Calyptra and Chancel then are two: is Janus a third?'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Edicts Inviolable|Lesson: Edicts Inviolable]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Intuition]].

[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Moon]]
[[Category:Curia]]

The Most Sorrowful End of the Lady Nonna.title: The Most Sorrowful End of the Lady Nonna
The Most Sorrowful End of the Lady Nonna.text:
{{Book (BoH) |title1=The Most Sorrowful End
of the Lady Nonna |image1=The Most Sorrowful End of the Lady Nonna.png |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Nectar}} |tally_price=4 |language=[[Henavek]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Herbs & Infusions]] |memory=[[Memory: Impulse]] |period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar Gothic]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Nectar}} Principle, written in [[Henavek]] by [[Eusebia]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|An unauthorised account of the death of Abbess Nonna, written by Eusebia, one of the two sisters accused of having murdered Nonna through 'poisoning and Arts unsanctioned.' Eusebia, awaiting execution, intends to hide this account in her cell...}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Nonna has introduced Eusebia to an unsanctioned Thunderskin-cult which meets in the caves below the Abbey; there she and others perform sacred dances for 'the Preservation of the Kingdom.'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|
Eusebia claims that Nonna asked her and another sister to prepare her a leathy-draught (which can be brewed from another beverage with Herbs and Infusions techniques, and a sufficient quantity of Nectar) for a rite all three of them would perform below the Abbey. Something goes awry, Nonna is 'possessed of a tenebrous spirit', and the Abbey-brethren are forced to 'quell her with star-iron'. The other two are implicated: as scapegoats, Eusebia implies, although she acknowledges her fault also...|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Herbs & Infusions|Lesson: Herbs & Infusions]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Impulse]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Nectar]] [[Category:Solar Gothic Period]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

The Shaven Lock Tantra.title: The Shaven Lock Tantra
The Shaven Lock Tantra.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=shaven lock.png
|mystery=6
|principles={{Lore|Moth}}
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Sanskrit]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Rites of the Roots]]
|memory=[[Memory: Impulse]]
|period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle written in [[Sanskrit]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Also known as 'The One Who Has Shaven His Hair'. This, the story goes, is the lore that even the shapechanging Vanaras rejected.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Tantra speaks glowingly of those who are prepared to abandon their old self to seek a new and higher self. It warns that once the change has truly begun - 'past the Third Mark' - a return to the old self is dangerous and painful.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|'Whisper your secrets into the earth, burn them in fire, scatter them in the sea. Still they will cling to your hair,' the Tantra cautions. It provides an occult riddle that it claims is sometimes the answer to the Riddle of the Hunter's Gate.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Rites of the Roots|Lesson: Rites of the Roots]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

[[Category:Moth]]
[[Category:Dawn]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Readable]]

The Shadow in the Stair.title: The Shadow in the Stair
The Shadow in the Stair.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=File:TheShadowintheStair.png |mystery=6 |principles={{Lore|Nectar}} |tally_price=3 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Coil & Chasm]] |memory=[[Memory: Impulse]] |period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Nectar}} Principle, written in English by Ernestine Peterhans. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Ernestine Peterhans records her conversations with the 'little darkness' in Hush House's Stair Tenebrous, which she calls 'Donkerling'.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Ernestine's business in the cellars of Hush House often took her up and down the Stair Tenebrous, although it is avoided by every other servant. 'Donkerling' attempted first to consume her and then to demand sacrifices from her; Ernestine consented to bring it mice, but became very stern when it asked for a 'new-drowned child...'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'Donkerling' claims to be an imprisoned Long under the protection of 'the deepest power of the Sea'. It is prone to occasional bouts of raving about how, when it has its freedom, its patron will drown the Isle. Ernestine renders most of these long speeches as '...', but is very interested in what it can tell her about the circumstances of shipwrecks; there are hints that she may have been planning a salvage expedition.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Coil & Chasm|Lesson: Coil & Chasm]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Impulse]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Nectar]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]] [[Category:Baronial]]

The Origins of Hours.title: The Origins of Hours
The Origins of Hours.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=[[File:The Origins of Hours.png]] |mystery=16 |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |tally_price=5 |language=[[Vak]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Sacra Limiae]] |memory=[[Confounding Parable]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} Principle, written in [[Vak]] by [[Soham]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|The sage and ecstatic Soham, a frequent visitor to the Mansus, claimed to have discoursed with the Beachcrow in person. Soham later insisted on a sky-burial.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Soham's writings veer from poetry to confession. He identifies from flesh (those who were mortal), from blood (those who arose from sacrifice), from Light (entry from the Glory) and from stone (those who arose before his knowledge.) He insists that the Moth was the first god-who-was-blood, but later contradicts himself and claims it was the Red Grail.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'The Mansus was different before the first god came from Light, but never doubt it existed, even then.'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sacra Limiae|Lesson: Sacra Limiae]]'' (x3). Reading always provides [[Confounding Parable]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Sky]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

The Scar in the Sky.title: The Scar in the Sky
The Scar in the Sky.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=The Scar in the Sky.png |mystery=14 |principles={{Lore|Winter}} |tally_price=5 |language=[[Fucine]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Quenchings & Quellings]] |memory=[[Memory: Regret]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} Principle, written in [[Fucine]] by [[Nyn]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Nyn wrote this, and came to regret it.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Each page of this book contains one word only, but as each page is turned, a knowledge creeps in.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The final page is crowded. Each reader of the book records the same word. Now it is my turn.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Quenchings & Quellings|Lesson: Quenchings & Quellings]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Regret]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Winter]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

The Road to Janus.title: The Road to Janus
The Road to Janus.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=The Road to Janus.png
|mystery=18
|principles={{Lore|Knock}}
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Vak]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Door & Wall]]
|memory=[[Memory: Pattern]]
|period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written in [[Vak]] by [[Burzghash]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The Limian Burzghash makes a series of prophecies regarding 'the Initiates of the House of Silence', with intricate, if unhelpful, predictions on their passage through the House.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘The Sixth Initiate is Priest and Key, Gate and Church. He shall cross the sea and open the tide. He shall not be the Eleventh, yet shall there be Seven between them. In the first Year of his Time, the Flower-Door is opened…’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘The Twelfth Initiate is Salvation and Wrack, Steed and Rider, who chooseth one Blossom of Three, who casteth away the Key and whom the Key shall not cast away, who comes after the Flame and before the Snow…’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Door & Wall|Lesson: Door & Wall]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Pattern]].

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Knock]]
[[Category:Dawn]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Readable]]

The Sun's Design.title: The Sun's Design
The Sun's Design.text: {{Book (BoH) |image1=The Suns Design.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Lantern}} |tally_price=8 |language=[[Cracktrack]] |type=[[Tablet]] |skill=[[Watchman's Paradoxes]] |memory=[[Numen: the Paths of the Sun|Numen: the Paths of the Sun]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} __NOTOC__'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Tablet]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle, which contains a [[Numen]]. It is written in [[Cracktrack]] by [[Elagabalus]] and an unknown author. ==Location== {{Spoilers|caption=Secret of the House|content=''{{PAGENAME}}'' is hidden within the [[Oubliette]], and is uncovered by using [[Disciplines of the Hammer]] or [[Disciplines of the Scar]] with any Element of the Soul in the [[Oubliette Containment]].|caption_element=h3}} ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{quote|A scorched slab of black corundum, minutely scratched on every side with intricate ideoglyphs. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]|}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|In the city of Emesa, beneath the Church of the Holy Belt, in a sarcophagus of black corundum, Elagabalus lies: accursed of Janus, neither Long nor mortal, neither man nor woman, neither a liar nor a speaker of truth, neither real nor imagined. On his light-suffused skin is made manifest the Sun-in-Splendour's grand design...|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Elagabalus is the source of one-half of this text. The source of the other-half is obscure, but its power is evident. It is impossible to be certain if the Sun really planned for us to enter Eternity. It is impossible to be sure if the Grail, the Vagabond, and the Forge, stole this birthright from us, or saved us from it. But there is a great secret here.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Watchman's Paradoxes|Lessons: Watchman's Paradoxes]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Numen: the Paths of the Sun]]: a [[Numen]] that can be used to establish a [[history]] and win the game. This numen has a special victory for [[the Cartographer]] and [[the Twice-Born]]. ==Trivia== *The method for obtaining this tablet is hinted at in ''[[The Carmine Petal: Unexpurgated]]'', ''[[The Carmine Petal: Revised]]'', and ''[[The Chandler's Wish]]''. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Lantern]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Tablet]] [[Category:Numen]] [[Category:Readable]]

The Radical Measure.title: The Radical Measure
The Radical Measure.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=The Radical Measure.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Rose}} |tally_price=2 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Preliminal Meter]] |memory=[[Memory: Pattern]] |period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Rose}} Principle, written in English by [[Dr Arun Peel]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Manifesto for experimental and dangerous-sounding invocatory poetry, written some time in the nineteenth century by Dr Arun Peel. A notoriously inconsistent and incoherent text, apparently produced in a tearing hurry.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'The Hours have little time for poetry,' Dr Peel avers, 'but they have a tremendous amount of time for poets.'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'As the Rose opens,' Dr Peel explains, 'an Enduring memory opens to the Horizon. This is a way of saying something that cannot otherwise be said, and is best only written with one's eyes firmly closed.'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Preliminal Meter|Lesson: Preliminal Meter]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Pattern]]. ==Hidden interactions== {{Spoilers|caption=This section contains information on hidden interactions.|content=
Presenting Dr Arun Peel with this book rewards the Librarian with a [[Preliminal Meter|Lesson: Preliminal Meter]] and a [[Horizon-Sight]] memory.}}
[[Category:Book]] [[Category:Rose]] [[Category:Curia]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

The Sky in the Scar.title: The Sky in the Scar
The Sky in the Scar.text: {{Book (BoH) |title1=The Sky in the Scar |mystery=10 |tally_price=8 |language=[[Sabazine]] |type=[[Codex]] |principles={{Lore|Edge}} |image1=The Sky in the Scar.png |memory=[[Numen: Back Into Balance]] |skill=[[Sickle & Eclipse]] |period=[[Dawn]]}} '''''The Sky in the Scar''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} principle that contains a [[Numen: Back Into Balance|Numen]]. ==Location== ''The Sky in the Scar'' is found inside the [[Ivory Vault]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{quote|Gnomic exhortations that might be described as 'emergency procedures' for the return of the travelling kinds of the Carapace Cross. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]|}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Each page of this book except the last bears a single sign, clear and irrefutable as a gem...|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|…the final page is empty. The travelling kinds of the Carapace Cross might never return.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of the book generates ''[[Sickle & Eclipse|Lesson: Sickle & Eclipse]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Numen: Back Into Balance]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Numen]] [[Category:Edge]]

The Sun's Lament.title: The Sun's Lament
The Sun's Lament.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Sun's Lament
|mystery=4
|tally_price=4
|type=[[Codex]]
|image1=[[File:TheSunsLament.png]]
|Period=[[Solar]]
|principles=[[Edge]]
|memory=[[Memory: Fear]]
|skill=[[Ragged Crossroads]]}}
'''''The Sun's Lament''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} Principle written by [[Abbot Thomas]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The first volume of the meditations of Abbot Thomas of the Abbey of the Black Dove.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The thorn-beaked crows took my eyes from me in justice for my crimes, but though I lost my Sight, I found my Light.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Abbot Thomas speaks of the breaking of his oaths to his sword-brother Trygve, and to the 'Lord of Scars' that he served before he came to the Abbey. He writes of the power of oath-bonds, and considers the means and morality of their sundering|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Ragged Crossroads|Lesson: Ragged Crossroads]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]].

==Trivia==

* The Lord of Scars is [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/The_Colonel the Colonel].

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Edge]]
[[Category:Readable]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Solar]]

The Orchid Transfigurations: a Birth.title: The Orchid Transfigurations: a Birth
The Orchid Transfigurations: a Birth.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=File:TheOrchidTransfigurationsaBirth.png |mystery=8 |principles={{Lore|Grail}} |tally_price=3 |language=[[Latin]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |memory=[[Memory: Satisfaction]] |period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle written in [[Latin]], supposedly by [[Robert Fludd]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|The second volume of a compilation of quasi-Rosicrucian allegories, supposedly by Robert Fludd. This is in the original Latin.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Fludd, or pseudo-Fludd, suggests alignments between the alchemical tradition of rubedo and the older Grail traditions, through the Pine-Knight's quest for the Cinnabar Cup.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Seek the Cup in the birthing-bed,' the Pine-Knight is told. The Midwife at the birthing-bed, to his amazement, is the Mountain-Mother. In a fit of awe, he both gelds and flays himself. The Vigilant Storm bursts joyfully from the remains.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Resurgences & Emergences|Lesson: Resurgences & Emergences]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Satisfaction]]. ==Trivia== *''The Orchid Transfigurations'' volumes appeared in [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Cultist_Simulator_Wiki Cultist Simulator]. There, its untranslated form is described as:
''"A sixteenth-century alchemical fever-dream, attributed to Robert Fludd, frequently banned for the disturbing allure of its illustrations. This is in the original Latin."''
[[Category:Book]] [[Category:Grail]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Baronial]]

The Mirror of Melancthe.title: The Mirror of Melancthe
The Mirror of Melancthe.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=The Mirror of Melancthe.png |mystery=12 |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |tally_price=4 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Sights & Sensations]] |memory=[[Memory: Solace]] |period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar Gothic]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} Principle, written in English by [[Abbess Melancthe]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|The day-book and dream-journal of Abbess Melancthe, venerated as a saint and respected as an alchemist.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Melancthe speaks longingly of 'those we would call from behind the sky…'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Melancthe claims that the Sights and Sensations arts that she describes can be used to invoke 'the Dream of a Star', when sufficient Sky-aspect is invoked to uplift an Ascendant Harmony.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sights & Sensations|Lesson: Sights & Sensations]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Solace]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Sky]] [[Category:Solar Gothic Period]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

The Silver Book.title: The Silver Book
The Silver Book.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Silver Book
|mystery=8
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Fucine]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|principles={{Lore|Moth}}
|image1=The Silver Book.png
|skill=[[Edicts Liminal]]
|memory=[[Memory: Impulse]]
|period=[[Dawn]]}}
'''''The Silver Book''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle written in [[Fucine]] by [[Burzghash]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|A manual of the Ordo Limiae, an order of quasi-immortals who maintained a secret enclave at the source of the river Limia, in the Roman province of Hispania Gallaecia. This manual was compiled by one Burzghash, who explains that he came to join the Ordo from the 'city of messenger eagles' after he abandoned the service of the Ivory Dove.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Members of the Ordo took an oath, the Silver Chain, that forbade men to lie with woman, or women with men: 'for what may come is not always the Crime of the Sky, yet that is a furious danger.' It was apparently permissible for men to lie with men, and women with women - in fact, Burzghash suggests that should be encouraged, to distract from other temptations.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The manual prescribes potential countermeasures to protect those who might be tempted to go against the oath: masks, disfigurement, severe poetic disciplines. Those who do break it are to be punished with death, although there are lesser punishments prescribed for various acts that don't involve actual coitus. Death is to be administered with 'the Glassfinger Toxin', which can be created with the assistance of the techniques described earlier in the manual, and with sufficient Knock aspect.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Edicts Liminal|Lesson: Edicts Liminal]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Readable]]
[[Category:Dawn]]
[[Category:Moth]]

Wainscot Histories.text:
{{Book_(BoH)
|image1=File:Wainscot_Histories.PNG
|mystery=6

|tally_price=3
|type=[[Codex]]
|memory=[[Memory: Contradiction]]
|skill=[[Auroral Contemplations]]
|Period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''Wainscot Histories''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle written by William Gore.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Subtitled 'Stories from Behind the Walls': a miscellany of non-traditional histories, including battles not generally acknowledged and countries which appear on no map, told in a playful, apparently fictional manner.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Gore does not mention the Mansus directly, but constant coy metaphorical references to 'Ascending the Staircase of Years', to 'the Doors of Sleep', and to 'the Blue Light of Dawn' suggest he had commerce with the unseen world.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|It was common in that time to speak of the Division of the Sun; by which Contemporaries understood, the irruption of Barbarian Forces, and of their uncouth Gods.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates [[Auroral Contemplations |Lesson: Auroral Contemplations]] and [[Memory: Contradiction]]. Reading it again provides [[Memory: Contradiction]].

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Lantern]]
[[Category:Codex]]

{{Book_(BoH)
|image1=File:The_world_despoil'd.PNG

|skill=[[Maggephene Mysteries]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written by [[Gideon Dewulf]].

== Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Subtitled 'the Flowers in the Waste': an epic poem that presents a medical treatise through allegory. The author is Gideon Dewulf, 5th Baron Brancrug, sometimes unkindly called 'the Cutter'.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The poem is a substantial variation on the Fisher-King tale. A wounded wasteland monarch learns that he and his land can be cured, but that the cure is their own response to ever more savage maladies…|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Gideon concludes with a concrete example: that the Mysteries can be used to despoil '[[Gideon's Soaks|mine own Soaks]]', but then the Soak can then be refined with sufficient Heart into '[[January Sanguinary|the sanguis saltandis]]'.|I've Read...}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Maggephene Mysteries|Lesson: Maggephene Mysteries]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Solace]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} Principle written in [[Killasimi]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|'A history of a hundred wars', sewn into a design of metallic threads that pursues itself across every page...}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Darius and Alexander at Issus - the incandescent strivings of the Houses of Lancaster and York - the Second Worm War - |I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The final page of the book depicts the first battles of a war among Hours, but the threads fray into alternatives, unbraiding from History. One of those threads is a coarse iron wire whose twists suggest the Disciplines of the Scar invoked before a subterranean configuration of iron, fire, and night...|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Disciplines of the Scar|Lesson: Disciplines of the Scar]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Regret]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle written in [[Killasimi]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Blessings and invocations of the Triple Knot recorded at a sanctuary in Cyprus notable for its weavers, sculptors, and gardeners.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘The roots go deep. The knots remain…’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The final invocation is one for the 'Restoration of the Roots', to be spoken before an altar of the Triple Knot - but, puzzlingly, it should not be spoken by any priestess of the Knot, or even by one who has been initiated into their Mysteries.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Tridesma Hiera|Lesson: Tridesma Hiera]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Satisfaction]].

Travelling at Night, vol 2.title: Travelling at Night, vol 2
Travelling at Night, vol 2.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=TravellingatNightvol2.png |mystery=6 |principles={{Lore|Sky}} |tally_price=1 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Sights & Sensations]] |memory=[[Memory: Solace]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}} __NOTOC__
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} Principle, written in English by [[Christopher Illopoly]]. ==Location== It is always located in [[Keeper's Lodge]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|The annotated dream-journals of Christopher Illopoly, sometimes called 'the only readable occultist': literate, entertaining, bewildering.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|There is an extensive discussion of the comparisons between Illopoly's own dreams and those of the Emperor Elagabalus, who Illopoly regards as a dupe or avatar of the Sun-in-Rags. 'The White is west of the world,' Illopoly remarks, 'and Winter does not wait forever.'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'Elagabalus found his way to the White Door at last, thankfully. Speech can't pass the White Door, and honestly, Elagabalus never had anything very interesting to say. I tried to follow in his footsteps, but I never learnt enough of the White. I suppose I'm thankful for that, too. But here's what I do know...'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sights & Sensations|Lesson: Sights & Sensations]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Solace]]. ==Trivia== *[https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Travelling_at_Night(Vol._2) This book originally appears in Cultist Simulator]. '''''Travelling at Night, vol 1''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} principle written by [[Christopher Illopoly]].
__NOTOC__
==Location==
''{{PAGENAME}}'' is always located in [[Keeper's Lodge]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The annotated dream-journals of Christopher Illopoly, sometimes called 'the only readable occultist': literate, entertaining, bewildering.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|"The Wood lies outside the walls of the Mansus. As any student of the Histories knows, the Mansus has no walls."|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Illopoly describes how he came to make repeated visits to a dream-Wood via what he calls silver dreams. 'Trying to think your way to the Wood,' he explains, 'is like thinking your way to being in love. But I did find a Secret that helped.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Edicts Liminal|Lesson: Edicts Liminal]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

* This book also appears in [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Travelling_at_Night(Vol._1) Cultist Simulator], where it is associated with [[Moth]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Forge}} Principle written by [[Everett Vinzant]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The metallurgist and 'sky-smith' Everett Vinzant speaks of 'the sacred alloys', 'the alloys eternal', 'the alloys sufficient', 'the alloys intendant'…}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Everett describes the voices and powers of mortals and immortals based on their composition by analogy to the sounds and strengths of bells based on the metals of their casting…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Vinzant warns that the mingling of metals of 'too great a nobility' can produce 'the alloys incestuous'. He suggests very cautiously that the means used by the Sovereigns of the Leashed Flame to produce their heirs may have analogous issues: 'for though the Crime of the Sky might be circumvented, yet the Law remaineth the Law, in Spirit as in Letter'.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Bells & Brazieries|Lesson: Bells & Brazieries]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

Those Indignities Perpetrated By the Dec.title: Those Indignities Perpetrated By the Deceitful Fraternity of Obliviates
Those Indignities Perpetrated By the Dec.text:
{{Book (BoH) |title1=Those Indignities Perpetrated By the Deceitful Fraternity
of Obliviates |image1=Those Indignities Perpetrated by the Deceitful Fraternity of Obliviates.png |mystery=6 |principles={{Lore|Winter}} |tally_price=3 |language=[[Latin]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Ragged Crossroads]] |memory=[[Memory: Contradiction]] |period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} Principle, written in [[Latin]] by [[C.R.O.D]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|It's not clear whether 'C.R.O.D', who is identified only by his initials, was in fact an initiate of the Obliviate order of immortal adepts. He wrote in the sixteenth century, after the order - if he is to be believed - had passed the height of its power.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'FIFTY-EIGHT. That they did claim inheritance of the traditions of the House of Lethe, but that they have DISREGARDED both its most sacred and its most beautiful ceremonies where they are not found CONVENIENT. FIFTY-NINE...'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'SEVENTY-ONE. The Glassfinger Toxin is no mere assassin's convenience for the Obliv-IDIOTS to confine to the disposal of their enemies. It has higher uses! Certainly it is a great matter of Winter, but I have already outlined the technique by which it may be fitted for its ultimate destiny...'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Ragged Crossroads|Lesson: Ragged Crossroads]]''. Reading always provides [[Memory: Contradiction]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Winter]] [[Category:Baronial]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

The Treatise on Underplaces.title: The Treatise on Underplaces
The Treatise on Underplaces.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=[[File:The Treatise on Underplaces.png]]
|mystery=4
|principles={{Lore|Knock}}
|tally_price=3
|language=English
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Horns & Ivories]]
|memory=[[Memory: Fear]]
|period=[[Baronial Period|Baronial]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written by [[Claude Hersault]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Herein, the seventeenth-century mystic and antiquarian Claude Hersault describes the 'Bounds' or 'Underplaces' on the borders of dream. He warns that they shift over time.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|'The walls of the Mansus,' Hersault begins, 'are the size of starlight.' Many of his directions are equally unhelpful, but common relationships do emerge.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|A picaresque account of a journey through nightmare, interspersed with what might be partial rites. 'On the eighteenth Ascent is the bud. On the thirty-sixth Ascent, the blossom.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Horns & Ivories|Lesson: Horns & Ivories]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]].

Three Flowers Hath the Tree.title: Three Flowers Hath the Tree
Three Flowers Hath the Tree.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=Three Flowers Hath the Tree|mystery=4|category=[[Book]]|tally_price=3|type=[[Readable]], [[Thing]], [[Codex]]|image1=Three Flowers Hath the Tree.png|Period=[[Baronial]]|principles={{Lore|Nectar}}|skill=[[Leaves & Thorns]]|memory=[[Memory: Gossip]]}}''Three Flowers Hath the Tree'' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Nectar}} principle written by [[Ernestine Peterhans]].
==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:{{Quote|Ernestine Peterhans records her observations of the growths of trees and flowers around the Isle, and the omens and portents she attempts to draw from them - particularly the yew-tree in Earl Brian's Meadow, whose flowerings are sometimes eccentric.|Description}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|Ernestine observes that in years when the tree flowers black, 'troubling Secrets arise'; when it flowers red, war and fires follow; and that no Dewulf heir has ever been born in a year when it flowers white...|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|Ernestine attempts to use the tree's growths to advantage in her business affairs, but it fails. She is evidently very concerned when Hendrik Dewulf's grandson Giles runs off with 'the Pale Trollop Hafren' in a year when the tree flowers white - she begins to fear she has entirely misinterpreted all the relevant omens. She is deeply concerned for the continuation of the Dewulf line, and prays for Giles' return.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates [[Leaves & Thorns| Lesson: Leaves & Thorns]] and [[Memory: Gossip]]. Reading it again provides [[Memory: Gossip]].

{{Book_(BoH)

|memory=[[Memory: Salt]]}}
'''''To A Pale Lady''''' is a [[Book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written by [[Lord Franklin Bancroft]]. 

== Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|A collection of Franklin Bancroft's letters to Eva Dewulf.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{quote|There is a substantial body of erotic pleading and half-finished poetry, but also learned discursions on matters mythical and marine, as well as notes towards a comic opera on which Franklin and Eva were apparently collaborating.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{quote|‘Do not return, O my Light, to the Sea. None of us can be what we were; that is History’s curse. None of us know what we may be; that is History’s gift. Your mothers, and the mothers of your mothers, are caught in Eternity’s jaws like a robe-hem in a trap. It is the pearl that shines; but the tide that returns.’|I've Read...}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Pearl & Tide|Lesson: Pearl & Tide]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Salt]].

The Victory of Crowns.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=[[File:The Victory of Crowns.png]]
|mystery=4

|period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} Principle written in by 'Arun' - which may or may not be [[Dr Arun Peel]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Erratic accounts by 'Arun' of the hunting and consumption of supposed immortals by shadowy assassins. Published in the late nineteenth century.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The assassins are, according to 'Arun', the agents of a power called the Coronel, a 'soldier of the Secret Masters'. The accounts date back to Roman times.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Arun's scholarship is dubious, but he (she?) writes pithily. Incidents of sudden and violent death are interspersed with aphorisms: 'Hours don't dream. Long try not to.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sharps|Lesson: Sharps]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Contradiction]]. 

==Trivia==
If you show this book to [[Dr Arun Peel]], he will offer to trade it for two other books:
{{quote|'You know, I can never quite remember if that's actually one of mine. Or one of, um, another mine. Do you mind if I take it away with me? I'll swap you the other books I happen to be carrying. No, I won't tell you what those might be. Rocks are no sharper in the dark.' [Peel will take 'Crowns' and give you two books of unpredictable nature and origin. He won't leave until his other business is concluded.]|}}

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written by [[Julian Coseley]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Julian Coseley's epistolary treatise on 'what may come after', addressed to his once-friend Claude Hersault, the mystic and antiquarian.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|By the time he wrote these letters, Coseley was identified with the oneiropolitical 'Worms' movement, and Hersault with the 'Birds' - meaning roughly that Hersault held the order of the Hours to be desirable, and Coseley held it to be oppressive.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Many of Coseley's arguments about consequence and finality are couched in erudite and practical alchemical terms. Others appear to be thinly-veiled threats directed at Hersault. Some are both.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Putrefactions & Calcinations|Lesson: Putrefactions & Calcinations]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Regret]].

Travelling at Night, vol 3.text: {{Book (BoH) |image1=TravellingatNightvol3.png| |mystery=4 |principles={{Lore|Knock}} |tally_price=1 |language=English |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Door & Wall]] |memory=[[Memory: Pattern]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written by [[Christopher Illopoly]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|The annotated dream-journals of Christopher Illopoly, sometimes called 'the only readable occultist': literate, entertaining, bewildering.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Illopoly's disquisitions on fire and the Unburnt God are interrupted by passages of distractingly erotic poetry addressed to 'Baldomera'.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|‘To reach the Stag Door, I believe that all you really need is to want something enough. But I've never wanted anything that much, except of course Baldomera, and I'm very much afraid that the knot in the story is this: what Baldomera wants is the Stag Door. But here's something I learnt in Persia. Perhaps it'll teach you what you want.’|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Door & Wall|Lesson: Door & Wall]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Pattern]]. == Trivia == * [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Travelling_at_Night(Vol._3) This book originally appears in Cultist Simulator]. '''''The Wind's Ruin''''' is a [[book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle written by [[Abbot Thomas]].

== Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description: 
{{quote|The second volume of the meditations of Abbot Thomas of the Abbey of the Black Dove.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: 
{{quote|Abbot Thomas speaks of his time as a raider, when his name was not Thomas but Toke, 'scything the sea, striving for plunder'…|I'm Reading...}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a Desk or with the Consider verb, the Librarian learns: 
{{quote|Abbot Thomas clearly regrets his 'storm-years', and much of the book is taken up with his thoughts on penitence; but there are hints also that he misses those years, and the companionship of his 'sword-brother, ship-brother' Trygve.|I've Read...}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Applebright Euphonies|Lesson: Applebright Euphonies]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Beguiling Melody]].

'''''The Watchful Tantra''''' is a [[Scroll]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle written in [[Sanskrit]].

Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Notorious for its involvement in the deaths of Dafydd Jones and Meredith Blaine, two early physicists who each claimed to have the only copy and who ultimately fought a duel over it in 1840.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Tantra describes processes of occult illumination, including a formula which may show the way from the 'Hunter's Gate' to the 'Serpent Gate' - which in the West is usually called the Spider's Door.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Sun passes through the House at the appointed time. Since the Sun's division, the time has become uncertain.|I've Read...}}

Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Purifications & Exaltations|Lesson: Purifications & Exaltations]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]].

'''''The Vinzant Inscriptions''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the [[Forge]] principle written in [[Phrygian]] by [[Everett Vinzant]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description: 
{{quote|Everett Vinzant transcribed these from a cliff in Anatolia, where he famously survived a lightning-strike. He died seven years later to the day. His bones, the legend has it, were hot to the touch.|Description}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|Long ago, the Sisterhood of the Knot recounted, the Forge loved the Hour called the Sun-in-Splendour. The Red Grail long anticipated their union, and the Grail-priestesses prophesied it...|Study start}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: 
{{Quote|The remainder of the text consists of gloating remarks by the Grail-priestesses of the Shaping that will come, interpolated with warnings and laments from those of the Sisterhood who serve the Ring-Yew and especially the Horned Axe. Nevertheless, an invocation to the Forge is included as part of an attempt to urge it onwards.|Study end}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Transformations & Liberations|Lesson: Transformations & Liberations]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]].

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle, written by Van Driel.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Van Driel describes odd events in Vienna - the disappearance of children; epidemics of parasite activity; animal mutilations; nightmares of worms; the activities of a charitable organisation, the New Ligeians, that funds the burial of the poor. She proposes peculiar connections between these activities.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘When the individual K. attends the meetings, black dogs are sacrificed and quartered. When the element M. is in attendance, black mares are found with their throats slashed. I propose that these sacrifices are not necessary, but that our Ligeian friends may consider them 'fitting'. Herewith diagrams of the mutilations -’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Medusa's Riddle, then, I choose to render as 'What is Not Seen?' There is another riddle, one I have heard rendered as 'What may be Lost?' I will delineate some historic attempts to answer it- these are in themselves, in some sense, sacrifices - ’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Wolf Stories|Lesson: Wolf Stories]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Fear]].

'''''The Time of Division''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle written by Amira Zahra. 

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|In which Amira Zahra prophesies the events later known as the Intercalate, when the Hour called Sun-in-Splendour will be divided.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Sun will be divided that it might not sire children. Still its children shall be Four in number and its children shall be Seven in number and its children shall also be Numberless. The Numberless shall open the way for the Seven, and the Seven shall consume the Four...'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Amira prophesies four great wars before the Second Dawn, when the Sun-in-Splendour shall rise again. She cautions: 'Sunrise is blood, and I foretell now that the Sun shall rise from blood, yet not the colour of the blood, nor the hour of Night.' She includes a rite that she speculates will be necessary for the Second Dawn.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards ==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Surgeries & Exsanguinations|Lesson: Surgeries & Exsanguinations]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Pattern]].

{{Quote|"The White Flower lies heavy, but the roots of the Watchman's Tree run deeper than snow..."|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The White Flower is described as the 'death of wisdom' - but wisdom can pass into sleep, not death, when 'the Rage of Glass' is subjected to sufficiently powerful Winter-aspect while the Ragged Crossroads arts are invoked..|I've Read...}}

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle written in [[Killasimi]] by [[Thirza Blake]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|A fanciful account by Thirza Blake of the early life of the Twins - their time as mortals before they became Hours or even Long, in a 'dry kingdom beyond the Western Sea' which Thirza suggests might have been ancient Mexico.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘It is widely known that the Sister was rich and the Witch poor. It is widely known that the Witch loved the Sister first. It is not widely known that the Witch was first employed to teach the Sister the arts of embroidery…’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Although Thirza is very probably just making up much of the story, there are long passages expounding notable techniques of weave-work and thread-feit. In particular, when Witch and Sister flee across the Sea to be together, Thirza explains how they fashioned a '[[Frith-Weft|peace-weave]]' with Heart and these arts, and then, to tame the winds, called on Heart again to [[Swaddled Thunder|swaddle the thunder]] in the peace-weave.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Stitching & Binding|Lesson: Stitching & Binding]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Satisfaction]].

The Three and the Three (Vatican Manuscr.text: {{Book (BoH) |title1=The Three and the Three (Vatican Manuscript) |mystery=14 |tally_price=4 |type=[[Codex]] |principles={{Lore|Moon}} |Period=[[Solar]] |image1=The Three and the Three (Vatican Manuscript).png |skill=[[Edicts Inviolable]] |memory=[[Memory: Intuition]]}} '''''The Three and the Three (Vatican Manuscript)''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{quote|A Church-authorised version of an older text, this book describes the Chancel and the Calyptra, two triads of Hours with subtle, far-reaching powers and responsibilities. It has clearly been reworked to fit Church doctrine.|}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|'The deepest knowledge is forbidden to all mortals except those who seek it beneath the Watchman's Tree. It is Calyptra that planted that tree, but it is the Chancel, the Cruciate, that has elected Calyptra. Who then elected the Cruciate? Or is this, as the saying goes, 'a matter of Janus'?|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|The Sister-and-Witch is Cruciate, but the Witch-and-Sister is not. Even those powers that demand a conjunction are not always conjoined. When the Sister is Nowhere, does this mean Nowhere sits in crucem?'|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Edicts Inviolable|Lesson: Edicts Inviolable]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Intuition|Memory: Intuition]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Moon]] [[Category:Solar]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]]

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} Principle written in [[Fucine]] by Niels Frederik Malskær.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The painter Niels Frederik Malskær, notoriously, attempted a series of paintings based on the Torments. By the Fifth Torment, the demands of the painting had grown so dire that he died of blood loss. The diagrams in this text are thankfully less detailed.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘The Enticements of the Grail outnumber its Torments, but its Torments are its final nature. Birth is the First Torment, and Thirst the Seventh’.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Through the enumeration of the Grail's enticements and torments winds the sorrowful history of the Witches of the Dry Land: the ordeal of birth from two wombs, their struggle from and supplication of the Grail, the yearning for union which drives them all.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Resurgences & Emergences|Lesson: Resurgences & Emergences]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].
