Unhatched Hymns.title: Unhatched Hymns
Unhatched Hymns.text: {{Book (BoH) |title1=Unhatched Hymns |mystery=10 |tally_price=4 |language=[[Sabazine]] |type=[[Codex]] |Period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar Gothic]] |image1=[[Unhatched Hymns.png]] |principles={{Lore|Lantern}} |skill=[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |memory=[[Savage Hymn]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Lantern}} Principle written in [[Sabazine]] by [[Saint Lucia|Saint Lucia the Eyeless]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{quote|Hymns attributed to Saint Lucia the Eyeless, patron of glassworkers and Name of the Hour called Meniscate.}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The hymns venerate every sanctioned Hour, celebrating them as the Sun Undivided, but also suggesting that each Hour may become the next - Madrugad to Watchman, Watchman to Wolf, and so on.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The Hymn of the Phases celebrates the Meniscate 'from whom we do not turn', for the truth which is beauty, the beauty which is truth, and the perfect balance between the two. The Hymn of the Reflections, more puzzlingly, celebrates the Meniscate as the 'Sister of Janus, Mother of Shadow', whose 'visage wondrous in emptiness' can reveal all truths.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Sacra Solis Invicti|Lesson: Sacra Solis Invicti]]'' (x2). Reading it always provides [[Savage Hymn]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Lantern]] [[Category:Solar]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]]

The World Does Not Weep.title: The World Does Not Weep
The World Does Not Weep.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=The World Does Not Weep.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Winter}} |tally_price=4 |language=[[Aramaic]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Putrefactions & Calcinations]] |memory=[[Memory: Hindsight]] |period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar Gothic]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} Principle, written in [[Aramaic]] by an unknown author. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|'Brown' Joshua found this in a well in Hamath. There's an unlikely story that it was abandoned by Alexander during his retreat from Issus.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The unknown adept who wrote this proclaims: the world forgets, but the Ivory Dove does not. The text contains a number of prescriptions for ensuring that certain acts are remembered, including a rite which requires a sacrifice in a particularly monstrous mode...|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The Hours tried to bury the memory of what happened to the Wheel, the Flint, the Tide, and the Seven-Coiled, but the Dove won't permit it. Nor will he permit what happened to the First Egg to be forgotten, although it is perhaps the one thing that the Watchman might ever forgive...|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Putrefactions & Calcinations|Lesson: Putrefactions & Calcinations]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Hindsight]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Winter]] [[Category:Solar Gothic Period]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic.title: Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic
Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic.text: {{Book (BoH) |image1=Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Knock}} |tally_price=8 |language=[[Ericapaean]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]] |memory=[[Numen: Inescapable Confinement]] |period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle that contains a [[Numen: Inescapable Confinement|Numen]] and was written in [[Ericapaean]] by [[Julian Coseley]]. ==Location== ''{{PAGENAME}}'' is found in the [[Crucible Tower: Governor's Quarters|Governor's Quarters]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Or, 'The House of Glass'. Julian Coseley considered this his masterwork. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Techniques for perception and analysis which permit invidious and apocalyptic conclusions. Probably the most assiduously suppressed book in history. The entire run was destroyed - even the presses were melted and dispersed - but the manuscript edition has survived.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The perfect hegemony of the Hours is, perhaps, eternal. But Coseley proposes and describes 'Confinement Inescapable', aesthetic and optical techniques which might contain even an Hour, profoundly disrupting the order of the Mansus. He presents this as his own work, but there are hints here and there that he received inspiration or even assistance from the Nowhere-Hour named Snow.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting|Lesson: Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Numen: Inescapable Confinement]]; a [[Numen]] that can be used to establish a [[history]] and win the game. This numen has a special victory for [[the Prodigal]] and [[the Archaeologist]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Knock]] [[Category:Curia]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]]

The Wakefield Papers.title: The Wakefield Papers
The Wakefield Papers.text:
[[File:Hush House Visitor's Guide.png|300px|right]]
'''''The Wakefield Papers'''''  are a series of further reading PDF files that can be found in the place beyond the Watchmen's reach your local game files. Excerpts from ''the Wakefield Papers'' provide context and background about [[Hush House]] and its [[People|Visitors]]. All papers date from before your arrival at Hush House and contain foreshadowing, rather than spoilers. ==Papers== Of particular note is 1930 - "A Visitor's Guide to Hush House". * 1722 - "Prophet and Loss" * 1815 - "Kissing the Twins" * 1857 - "Behold I Stand at the Door and Knock" * 1866 - "Illumination" * 1902 - "Skolekosophy" * 1906 - "Seventy-Seven Winks" * 1924 - "Suppression" * 1925 - "Nyctodromy" * 1929 - "The Sea and the Tide" * 1930 - "A Visitor's Guide" * 1932 - "A Proposition at Noon" [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Readable]]

Warming Draughts to Uplift the Heart.title: Warming Draughts to Uplift the Heart
Warming Draughts to Uplift the Heart.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=Warming Draughts to Uplift the Heart
|mystery=8
|principles={{Lore|Heart}}
|tally_price=2
|language=[[Greek]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|Period=[[Curia]]
|image1=[[File:WarmingDraughtstoUplifttheHeart.png]]
|skill=[[Herbs & Infusions]]
|memory=[[Memory: Impulse]]}}
'''''Warming Draughts to Uplift the Heart''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle written by [[Natan of Regensburg]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|A wonderful compendium of healing tisanes compiled by Natan of Regensburg.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Natan and his family sought sanctuary at Brancrug but were confined to the Barber's Tower (as it was then known) by the suspicions of the monks, but won more freedom over time…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Natan records his delight on the day he was finally permitted access to [[Earl Brian's Field|Earl Brian's Meadow]]. He speaks very carefully of the black bird he met in its branches, and the 'treasures of music and history' that it brought him when he healed its wing.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Herbs & Infusions|Lesson: Herbs & Infusions]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Heart]]
[[Category:Readable]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Curia]]

Those Who Do Not Sleep.title: Those Who Do Not Sleep
Those Who Do Not Sleep.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=Those Who Do Not Sleep.png
|mystery=12
|principles={{Lore|Heart}}
|tally_price=5
|language=[[Fucine]]
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Surgeries & Exsanguinations]]
|memory=[[Memory: Storm]]
|period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle written in [[Fucine]] by Brodnax.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The mystic Brodnax discusses the origins of the Sister-and-Witch, and of the Thunderskin.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘The Sister-and-Witch were born in two wombs, one poor one rich, across the sea. The Sister was stronger in the aspect of Heart, and so their survival was assured; the Witch was stronger in the aspect of Grail, and so they were not satisfied...’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘When the Sister and Witch came West, the Red Grail permitted their ascension, but then grew jealous of their power. It lured a great musician into the ranks of its Names, and caused him to be reborn from blood as a Heart-hour, so that the Grail might maintain dominion there also. But its victory is not assured.’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Surgeries & Exsanguinations|Lesson: Surgeries & Exsanguinations]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Storm]].

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Heart]]
[[Category:Dawn]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Readable]]

Ud Rocashaas.title: Ud Rocashaas
Ud Rocashaas.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=[[Ud Rocashaas.png]] |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Scale}} |tally_price=4 |language=[[Henavek]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Stone Stories]] |memory=[[Memory: Impulse]] |period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar Gothic]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Scale}} Principle, written in [[Henavek]] by an unknown author. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|An anonymous confessional account of unsanctioned activities by the nuns of St Brandan's. The title is a Henavek phrase that might be translated as 'the spirit flees the shadowed places.'}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The author writes guiltily of her dealings with hill-children and Carapace-relics - she suggests she herself has a connection with one of the Carapace-kinds. Most of these dealings are trivial, but she claims to have arranged the death of the Marcher Lord William de Braose, called Black William...|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|De Braose' wife, Eva, evidently seeks the Abbey's help to free her from her hated husband. Subsequently he is found in the bed-chamber of the wife of Llywelyn the Great, Prince of the Welsh, while attempting to negotiate the marriage of his daughter (also Eva) to Llywelyn's son. Llywellyn takes this badly, de Braose is hanged, the elder Eva inherits his estates and makes a substantial endowment to St Brandan's. In the author's telling, de Braose was 'innocent of all but cruelty' and the adulterer found in the bed-chamber was a shape-changing 'undergoer'...|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Stone Stories|Lesson: Stone Stories]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Memory: Impulse]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Scale]] [[Category:Solar Gothic Period]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic: Second.title: Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic: Second Edition
Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic: Second.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic Second Edition.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Winter}} |tally_price=8 |language=[[Ericapaean]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Sights & Sensations]] |memory=[[Numen: a Final Understanding]] |period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}} __NOTOC__'''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Winter}} Principle, written in [[Ericapaean]] by [[Julian Coseley]]. ==Location== {{Spoilers|caption=Secret of the House|content=Can be found at the [[Rowenarium (Room)]] by using the [[Hush House Key]] at the [[Rowenarium (Workstation)]].|caption_element=h3}} ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Or, 'The Refinements of Light'. Julian Coseley had never wanted or expected to write a second edition of his masterwork... [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Julian Coseley long regarded Solomon Husher as a charlatan. But his friend Nina Lagasse painted three paintings before her death in 1895… and these paintings apparently convinced Coseley to change his mind. With considerable irritation, he revised his magnum opus.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The perfect hegemony of the Hours is, perhaps, eternal. Coseley had always championed History rather than Eternity - the exceptions, limitations, contradictions of freedom. But Husher's and Lagasse's work convinced him to believe in the 'paradox of the eternal ending', a means in which perfection might be reconciled with freedom. He's not happy about it. This is perhaps the angriest book ever written in support of a peaceful philosophy of acceptance. But Coseley was always scrupulous about his conclusions.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sights & Sensations|Lesson: Sights & Sensations]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Numen: a Final Understanding]]. == Trivia == *A hint for finding this book can be found in ''[[Glimmerings]]'': {{Quote|Their final recorded dream is of a 'worm-jewel' beneath Brancrug Isle, which they open with a key carved from their finger-bone.}} [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Winter]] [[Category:Nocturnal]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]] [[Category:Numen]]

The Three and the Three (St Chiavi Manus.title: The Three and the Three (St Chiavi Manuscript)
The Three and the Three (St Chiavi Manus.text: {{Book (BoH) |image1=The Three and the Three St Chiavi Manuscript.png |mystery=18 |principles={{Lore|Moon}} |tally_price=8 |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Edicts Inviolable]] |memory=[[Numen: Three Rules]] |period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar Gothic]]}} __NOTOC__'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle. ==Location== {{Spoilers|caption=Secret of the House|content=''{{PAGENAME}}'' can be uncovered by placing the [[Inscribed Stone]] found in the [[Librarian's Quarters]], along with either [[Edicts Inviolable]] or [[Edicts Liminal]] and any soul card, in an occupied [[Workstation#Beds|Bed]].|caption_element=h3}} ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|This book describes the operations of the Chancel and the Calyptra, two triads of Hours with subtle, far-reaching powers and responsibilities. Of all the extant versions, this one has best survived the interventions of the Calyptra. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]}} Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|‘Certain knowledge cannot be learnt by any entity below the rank of Know - outside the covenant of the Watchman's Tree. The enforcement of this rule is Calyptra. The three who enforce it are Calyptra also. It is said that Janus elects Calyptra, that the Chancel is the judgement of Janus, that Janus is the wound in the Law...’|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|‘The Watchman's Tree is a compromise. If Calyptra could end it, they would. If the Watchman could end Calyptra, he might. Between their planes conflicting, sparks illuminate the angles of unmade law…’|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Edicts Inviolable|Lesson: Edicts Inviolable]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Numen: Three Rules]]. == Trivia == *The method to obtaining this book is hinted in ''[[Deaths and their Evasions]]'', ''[[Nyn's Cages (Avignon Text)]]'' and ''[[Nyn's Cages (Bruges Text, Illuminated)]]''. *Unlike all other books that contain Numina, this book has an aspect of 18 (rather than 10), and is not written in one of the esoteric languages. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Moon]] [[Category:Solar Gothic Period]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Numen]]

The Writing on the Wall.title: The Writing on the Wall
The Writing on the Wall.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=The Writing on the Wall.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Nectar}} |tally_price=8 |language=[[Vak]] |type=[[Readable]] |skill=[[Spices & Savours]] |memory=[[Numen: an Irresistible Feast]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} __NOTOC__'''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|'Book']] of the {{Lore|Nectar}} Principle, written in [[Vak]] by an unknown author. ==Location== {{Spoilers|caption=Secret of the House|content=Can be found at the [[Shrine to St Tentreto]] by using [[Preliminal Meter]] or [[Resurgences & Emergences]] with any [[Ink]] at [[Altar: St Tentreto]].|caption_element=h3}} ==Description== Selecting the 'book' provides the following description: {{Quote|The most delicious traditions of the Carapace Cross, as recorded on the walls of the Mansus and transcribed into a book of ninety-nine pages by one known only as 'cc'. Although this book does not exist, it is read to a sleeper under certain very specific circumstances - and certain fragments jotted down on waking. [This 'book' houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]}}
Upon choosing to master the 'book', either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'It was Hunger that made Worms of Dragons - when they consumed the corpses of Hours. Without the savour-secret of the Carapace, their hunger would not have been sufficient…'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Here is outlined the savour-secret of the Carapace, which harnesses hunger to permit impossible hybridisations. With this secret, even the most potent and fundamental entities have devoured and been devoured. And this, no doubt, is why it's secret.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this 'book' provides ''[[Spices & Savours|Lesson: Spices & Savours]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Numen: an Irresistible Feast]]. == Trivia == *A very obscure hint to finding this secret may be found in ''[[A Tower Rises]]'' and ''[[A Tower Falls]]'' with the phrases "Deep Door" and "four-winged", but even then that would only account for the location. One half of the requirements would have to be guessed and the other isn't even mentioned. *Another very obscure reach for a hint might be in ''[[COLOURS IN THE LIVER]]'' with the phrase "four-winged". Again, one half of the requirements would have to be guessed and the other isn't even mentioned. *A more obvious hint may be found in [[Glimmerings]], where it is mentioned that "their final recorded dream is of a 'worm-jewel' beneath Brancrug Isle, which they open with a key carved from their finger-bone." The art of [[Resurgences & Emergences]] depicts finger-bones, thus giving a hint towards the secret. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Nectar]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]] [[Category:Numen]]

The Turquoise Hand.title: The Turquoise Hand
The Turquoise Hand.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=The Turquoise Hand.png |mystery=10 |principles={{Lore|Rose}} |tally_price=8 |language=[[Ramsund]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |memory=[[Numen: That Old Lost Music]] |period=[[Solar Gothic Period|Solar Gothic]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Rose}} Principle, written in [[Ramsund]] by an unknown author. ==Location== The book can be found in the [[Silver Vault]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|A calligraphic manual of Ramsund which employs as exemplar-text Farid ud-Din's 'Conference of the Birds'. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|'At noon the Sun moves like the beating of a wing. At sunset he sends the herald-child with her candle. At midnight, he sends the wind that extinguishes the candle-flame…'|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|Commentary, illustrations and interleavings carry revelations never intended in the original: a sense of history, and the senses of Histories.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Pentiments & Precursors|Lesson: Pentiments & Precursors]]'' (x2). Reading always provides [[Numen: That Old Lost Music]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Rose]] [[Category:Solar Gothic Period]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]] [[Category:Numen]]

Velletri Interviews.title: Velletri Interviews
Velletri Interviews.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=Velletri Interviews
|mystery=6
|tally_price=1
|type=[[Phonograph Record]]
|principles={{Lore|Heart}}
|Period=[[Nocturnal]]
|image1=Velletri Interviews.png
|skill=[[Edicts Inviolable]]
|memory=[[Memory: A Stolen Secret]]}}
'''''Velletri Interviews''''' is a [[Phonograph Record]] of the {{Lore|Heart}} Principle.

==Description==
Selecting the record provides the following description:
{{quote|Interrogation of a man named Lacombe, a former Nocturnal Branch inspector now identified as 'terminally robigoid'.}}

Upon choosing to master the at a [[Phonograph]], the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Lacombe is not especially lucid, and the state called 'robigoia' evidently includes a malady of the lungs which causes coughing fits: he weakens audibly over the course of the interrogation. He is questioned about the disposition of various unsanctioned items recovered from a Nocturnal Branch raid on a castle at Ortucchio, in the region of the Fucine Marshes. He is, however, defiant as well as incoherent.|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Lacombe insists the items have been put to good use; he derides Nocturnal Branch as 'the lackeys of Calyptra'. Alarmingly, during the last few minutes of the interrogation, he begins to insist that his interrogator should 'burn the Library'. He waxes enthusiastic about the fire he wants to see, leading to a final coughing fit after which the interview abruptly ends.|I've Read...}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of this record provides ''[[Edicts Inviolable|Lesson: Edicts Inviolable]]'' x1. Listening to it always provides [[Memory: A Stolen Secret]].

== Trivia ==
* The robigoia mentioned in this interview might be an infection by the nowhere hour the Crowned Growth. [https://weatherfactory.biz/to-superintendent-wynford-of-nocturnal-branch/ This blogpost] is of a manifest relating to a raid on Ortucchio castle with the inspector later running from the Nocturnal Branch to Velletri, Italy. One 'Dottore Robigo' is mentioned often and convinces the inspector to retain multiple dangerous artifacts. Supposedly, the Inspector became acquainted with Robigo after interacting with a painting that describes the Crowned Growth tarot card.

[[Category:Phonograph Record]]
[[Category:Nocturnal]]
[[Category:Readable]]

The Twin-Serpent Tantra.title: The Twin-Serpent Tantra
The Twin-Serpent Tantra.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Twin-Serpent Tantra
|mystery=8
|principles={{Lore|Knock}}
|tally_price=1

'''''The Twin-Serpent Tantra''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} principle written in [[Sanskrit]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Just before the outbreak of the Great War, 'Alexander Sparrow' - almost certainly a pseudonym - published leaflets claiming the influence of 'Snake Princes' on world affairs. The text called the Twin-Serpent Tantra was his primary inspiration.|Description}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Tantra describes the Great Hooded Princes - a dynasty of unclear origin - engaging in prayers, sacrifices and poetry in honour of the Key-Serpent, the Crossroads-Twins and the Mirror-Queen. 'Nagi encircles; Nagi arises from wounds; Nagi spares those who are already harmed.'|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Great Hooded Princes are described as having 'escaped from the history of their death to a history where they yet live'. The text claims that there are now one hundred and eight of them, but - in one of many instances of twinnedness - before they crossed from their death chronicle, there were only fifty-four.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Edicts Liminal|Lesson: Edicts Liminal]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Pattern]].

The War of the Roads, 1451-1551.title: The War of the Roads, 1451-1551
The War of the Roads, 1451-1551.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=File:TheWaroftheRoads14511551.png
|mystery=4
|principles={{Lore|Edge}}
|tally_price=2
|type=[[Codex]]
|skill=[[Meniscate Reflections]]
|memory=[[Memory: Foresight]]
|period=[[Curia Period|Curia]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} Principle written by Willis-Ford.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Willis-Ford describes the War of the Roads, an event in a History other than our own, in detail - from its beginnings as a martial-philosophical dispute between the Dawn and Sunset Roads of alchemy, to a war which ravaged half of Europe.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘It is not now widely believed that the sons and daughters of the Red Rose were forged into immortals. Understandably: they are, after all, now all long dead. The Forge itself devoured the greatest among them.’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The royalty of England, according to Willis-Ford, became the Sovereigns of the Leashed Flame, destroying or transforming their enemies, conquering Europe, establishing grand cathedrals to St Spark. The alliance with the Forge begins to take its toll. At last, the Bronze King undergoes his 'Great Misfortune' and 'Great Debasement', and is afterwards known as the Copper King. His attempt to cheat the Forge ends badly, the Leashed Flame is released, and the King's heirs are merely mortal sovereigns.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Meniscate Reflections|Lesson: Meniscate Reflections]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Foresight]]. 

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Edge]]
[[Category:Curia]]
[[Category:Codex]]
[[Category:Readable]]

The Tripled Heart.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|title1=The Tripled Heart
|mystery=4
|tally_price=4

'''''The Tripled Heart''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Grail}} principle.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|Sacred poems composed in honour of the Hours venerated by the Sisterhood of the Triple Knot.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Grail is celebrated for her colours, the Malachite for her sweetness, the Axe for her constancy…|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Thunderskin, least of the Hours of the Knot when he is even counted among their number at all, is celebrated with an unexpectedly poignant elegy. 'What lives, departs; what is dead, remains.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Tridesma Hiera|Lesson: Tridesma Hiera]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Intuition|Memory: Intuition]].

[[Category:Grail]]

|skill=[[Sea Stories]]
|language=[[Fucine]]}}
'''''The Voyages of Ferninshun of Oreol''''' is a [[book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written in [[Fucine]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|The impossible travels of a sea-captain of the late Phoenician era. Suppressed throughout recorded history: those who read it were said to disappear.|Description}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Ferninshun clearly visited the Mansus, sailing the length of the Painted River. He also claims to have traversed a sea of finest sand, to have dared the blazing waves of the Sun's surface, and to have descended to an underworld ocean lit by lamps of black nephrite...|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Ferninshun's final voyage is to retirement on a peaceful island across an evening sea, where he identifies a spring whose waters will keep him safe. 'I will be forgotten,' he declares, 'and this work my only trace.'|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides ''[[Sea Stories|Lesson: Sea Stories]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Salt]].

Uncatalogued Book.title: Uncatalogued Book
Uncatalogued Book.text:
[[File:Uncatalogued.png|64px|right]] {{quote|'There's nothing as safe as ignorance — or as dangerous.' - Nero Wolfe}}
'''Uncatalogued''' is an [[Aspects|Aspect]] on most [[Books]] found in [[Hush House]]. These are books that must be catalogued before they can be read or mastered. Cataloguing requires an [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]], and can be done at any [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb. The only books which cannot be acquired through cataloguing are books that house [[Numen]], which are found by exploring the house, and ''[[Plantagenet Mysteries]]'', which can be bought from [[Oriflamme's Auction House]]. ==How Cataloguing Works== When a book is catalogued, the game pulls a random book from a "deck" corresponding to the time period of the uncatalogued book. It can pull any book from that deck which is not currently owned. Once all books from a deck are collected, all subsequent uncatalogued books from that period will contain their respective [[Multitudinuous]] book. ==Contamination== There is a chance when cataloguing books that they might be [[Contamination|Contaminated]]. The chance depends on the time period the book is from. {| class="wikitable" |+ Chance of a book having a contamination |- ! Period !! % Chance |- | [[Dawn Period]] || 20% |- | [[Solar Gothic Period]] || 10% |- | [[Baronial Period]] || 5% |- | [[Curia Period]] || 5% |- | [[Nocturnal Period]] || 2% |} ==Periods== It is possible to tell at a glance which time period an uncatalogued book is from by the colour. Dawn books are green, Solar yellow, books from the Baronial period are pink, Curia period books are blue, and Nocturnal books are purple. For lists of all books for each period, please see the relevant period page. What Does Not Bark.title: What Does Not Bark
What Does Not Bark.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=File:WhatDoesNotBark.png

|tally_price=1
|type=[[Codex]]

|period=[[Nocturnal Period|Nocturnal]]}}
'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Moon}} Principle written by Alexander Probst.

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Alexander Probst writes warily of 'Calyptra' - a law, principle or society which prevents the dissemination of dangerous knowledge.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Calyptra, like the planet that occludes the star, or the Doylian dog that fails to bark, can be identified only by its absence. Even the name, I think, must be a mask…’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘Calyptra is said to make exceptions specifically for the libraries of the Watchman's Tree. Does it make those exceptions so the Hours can make use of them?’|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Edicts Inviolable|Lesson: Edicts Inviolable]]'' x1. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Storm]].

White Jade Tablet.text:
{{Book (BoH)
|image1=White Jade Tablet.png
|mystery=14

'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Moth}} Principle written in [[Cracktrack]].

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Supposedly copied from a tablet of white jade which serves as the Covenant-stone of the Grove of the Green Immortals - the token which gives that Library shelter beneath the Watchman's Tree.}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|‘When humankind emerged from the weft of the Roots, we were smeared with the filth of crumbled ages. The foolish sought to wash it from themselves, but our skins were yet soft, and fell easily from us…’|I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Tablet expounds the dangers (and pleasures) of abandoning appearances in search of essence. Along the way, it reveals the secret of Skinshuck Mead, which can be brewed from honey by application of the Rites of the Roots, if enough Moth-aspect is present.|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Rites of the Roots|Lesson: Rites of the Roots]]'' x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Impulse]].

Xenodicene Odes.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1=[[File:Xenodicene Odes.png]] |mystery=21 |principles={{Lore|Knock}} |tally_price=5 |language=[[Vak]] |type=[[Codex]], [[Multitudinous]] |skill=[[Preliminal Meter]] |memory=[[Confounding Parable]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn ]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Multitudinous]] [[Readable|book]] of the {{Lore|Knock}} Principle written in [[Vak]] by various members of the [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/House_of_Lethe House of Lethe] and attributed to Xenodice. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|Poetry attributed to Xenodice, Name of the Horned-Axe.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|In the House of Lethe's heyday, it held an annual competition where its initiates competed to produce the best ode in Xenodice's honour. So there are still a lot of odes out there.|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|It has never been clear why the Letheans, who avoided traffic with the Hours with the occasional exception of the Elegiast, would devote effort to a Name of the Horned-Axe. Perhaps Xenodice was just a suitably challenging subject…|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Preliminal Meter|Lesson: Preliminal Meter]]'' x3. Reading it always provides [[Confounding Parable]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Knock]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Multitudinous]]

{{Book (BoH) |image1=Where Has She Gone.png |mystery=16 |principles={{Lore|Rose}} |tally_price=5 |language=[[Vak]] |type=[[Codex]] |skill=[[Sand Stories]] |memory=[[Memory: Intuition]] |period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}} '''''{{PAGENAME}}'''''  is a [[Readable|Book]] of the {{Lore|Rose}} Principle, written in [[Vak]] by [[The Speeth]]. ==Description== Selecting the book provides the following description: {{Quote|'The Speeth' - perhaps a single adept, perhaps a council of scholars - hypothesises secret events from limited evidence with persuasive accuracy.}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Workstations#Desks|Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|The Vagabond is recorded to have travelled not only the Mansus and the Wood, not only all nine continents, but also places forbidden to other Hours...|I'm Reading...}} After completing mastery, the Librarian learns: {{Quote|From Hour-gossip and invisible lore, Speeth deduces that the Vagabond has visited Nowhere, but that she will not return. He also asserts that she has yet to visit the Glory, but that inevitably, this must be her goal.|I've Read...}} ==Rewards== Completing mastery of this book provides ''[[Sand Stories|Lesson: Sand Stories]]'' (x3). Reading always provides [[Memory: Intuition]]. [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Rose]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Codex]] [[Category:Readable]] [[Category:Thing]]

{{BoH Skill |title1=Disciplines of the Scar |image1=File:Disciplines_of_the_scar.PNG |wisdoms=[[Illumination]]

The Scar marks wisdom and regrets; one is often born from the other.}} Disciplines of the Scar is a [[Skills|Skill]] card. It starts with 2 {{Lore|Edge}} and 1 {{Lore|Lantern}}. This skill is connected to the [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/The_Colonel Colonel], or Tribune of Scars. ==Wisdom Attunement== {{quote|The Mansus is the fortress of dream where the true Hours rule, and Nowhere is the scar beneath it where the Nowhere hours lair. Without the Hours above, that scar would be an open wound. So the Bright Arts teach us.|The Scar}} Committing Disciplines of the Scar to [[Illumination]] provides [[Phost]] (2 {{Lore|Lantern}}, 1 {{Lore|Sky}}), which can be evolved at [[Practice Equipment]] or [[Shrine: the Watchman]]. {{quote|The Mansus is the fortress in dream raised by the gods-who-were-stone. Nowhere is the inevitable scar beneath it. Monstrous, the gods-from-Nowhere; but cruel, the gods-who-were-stone.|The Crime}} Committing Disciplines of the Scar to [[Hushery]] provides [[Trist]] (2 {{Lore|Moth}}, 1 {{Lore|Moon}}), but cannot be used to evolve Trist by itself. It will need a memory with the [[Memories that can evolve Elements of the Soul|Evolve via Hushery]] aspect to upgrade, for example [[Didumos]], can then be evolved at any workstation that accepts the relevant principles, for example, [[Chancel of the Abbey Church|Shrine: the Chancel]]. If after the conclusion of [[The Affair of the Messenger's Casket]] the Librarian received the ''[[Mihail in Chains]]'' painting and put it in the [[Columbic Sarcophagus]], Disciplines of the Scar can be used to evolve Trist there. ==Acquiring the Skill== ''Lesson: {{PAGENAME}}'' can be acquired by studying the following books. {| class="fandom-table" style="width: 100%" |- ! Lockworks & Clockworks.text:
{{BoH Skill
|primary_principle={{Lore|Knock}}

|image1=File:Lockworks_&_Clockworks.PNG

{{quote|The little ways of little machines.}}

'''Lockworks & Clockworks''' is a [[Skills|Skill]] card that starts with {{Lore|Knock|2}} and {{Lore|Sky|1}}.

==Wisdom Attunement==
{{quote|The clocksmith's first duty: when the time comes, the device should speak its purpose. Since the Sun was sundered, Noon is not as it was. Perhaps, if we found the true hour of Noon, we'd know how the Sun might return. Ithastry might give us that answer.|Of Clocks}}

Committing Lockworks & Clockworks to [[Ithastry]] provides [[Wist]] ({{Lore|Winter|2}}, {{Lore|Lantern|1}}), which can be evolved at [[Shrine: the Madrugad]] or the [[Exercise Yard]].

{{quote|The locksmith's first duty: a key for every lock, and a lock for every key. If a key were an Hour, what lock would it open? Skolekosophy might hold the answer.|Of Locks}}

Committing Lockworks & Clockworks to [[Skolekosophy]] provides [[Shapt]] ({{Lore|Knock|2}}, {{Lore|Forge|1}}), which can be evolved at the [[Condignator]]. It can also be evolved at the [[Rowenarium (Workstation)|Rowenarium]] if the [[The Affair of the Endless Guest|Affair of the Endless Guest]] is concluded with Spencer Hobson entering the Rowenarium.

== Notes ==
Lockworks & Clockworks is THE skill to get access to the [[Chronsichord]], the most powerful and useful [[Tools|tool]] in the game, providing all the required elements neatly packed in a single bundle; even better if you got it from [[Against Vitruvius]], since you will also get the [[Memory: Pattern]].

You can craft the Chronsichord already at level 5, or even level 3 if you have also access to [[Curious Hunch]] or [[Glassfinger Toxin]]. The [[Foundry (Workstation)|Foundry]] is the perfect place to craft everything you need, since it accepts [[Knock]], [[Glass]] and [[Metal]]; in addition, since the [[Amethyst Ampoule]] is both [[Glass]] and [[Liquid]], you can slot it in the second slot along with [[Gervinite]].

Once you reach level 6 and evolve [[Shapt]] (which you can do if you commit this skill to [[Skolekosophy]]), you won't even need a memory.

Crafting a Chronsichord with [[Wire (Silver)]] is tricky, since it can be difficulty to put together enough {{Lore|Sky}} in the [[Foundry]], and usually unnecessary, since you'll likely be able to reliably produce Gervinite on demand by the time you can obtain the high-level {{Lore|Sky}} memories required. Since the Silver is taking up the Metal slot and [[Phost]] cannot be used in the Foundry, you are limited to the {{Lore|Sky}} principle of the Skill itself, the Memory slot, and the Fuel slot. Useful memories are limited to [[Numen: That Old Lost Music]], [[Didumos]], and [[Wind-in-Waiting]]: no other Sky memories have the aspects necessary to cheat them into the Memory slot of the Foundry. Useful [[Liquid|Liquids]] (since there are no [[Fuel|Fuels]] with {{Lore|Sky}}) include [[Orpiment Exultant]], [[Uzult]], [[January Sanguinary]] and [[Stargall Ink]]. With Didumos (or Wind-in-Waiting) and Orpiment Exultant (or Uzult) adding up to 13 {{Lore|Sky}}, the Skill must be at least level 2 to for that recipe.{{Skills Navbox}}

Drums & Dances.text:
{{BoH_Skill| primary_principle=[[Heart]] |secondary_principle=[[Nectar]] |image1=Drums_&_Dances.png |wisdoms=[[Horomachistry]]
[[The Bosk]]}} {{quote|The first musics were not made by mortals, but taken; from sand-coil and sea-thorn, from flint-heart and dragon-womb.}} '''Drums & Dances''' is a [[Skills|Skill]] card that starts with 2 {{Lore|Heart}} and 1 {{Lore|Nectar}}. ==Wisdom Attunement== {{quote|The Thunderskin, the eternal drum that beats to preserve the skin of the world, is a god-from-flesh, which is to say he was once mortal. But the Horned-Axe, last of the gods-from-stone, required his death, and so the Grail gave him up, though he loved her. Love is always subject to the will of the Hours, as all horomachists know.|The Heart}} Committing Drums & Dances to [[Horomachistry]] provides [[Mettle]] (2 {{Lore|Forge}}, 1 {{Lore|Edge}}), but cannot be used to evolve Mettle by itself. It will need a memory that has the [[Memories that can evolve Elements of the Soul|Evolve via Horomachistry]] aspect, for example Didumos, and can then be evolved at any workstation that accepts the relevant aspects, for example, [[Practic Garden|Practic Garden Dummy]]. {{quote|The Thunderskin, the eternal drum that beats to preserve the skin of the world, is a god-from-flesh, which is to say he was once mortal. He died to preserve the last god-from-stone; he died for love; he died for necessity. In matters of Bosk, these three are often intertwined.|The Root}} Committing Drums & Dances to [[The Bosk]] provides [[Health]] (1 {{Lore|Heart}}, 1 {{Lore|Nectar}}, 1 {{Lore|Scale}}), which can be upgraded at [[Altar of the Knot]], [[Calicite Altar]], or [[Deeplight Corals]]. ==Acquiring the Skill== ''Lesson: {{PAGENAME}}'' can be acquired by studying the following books. {| class="fandom-table" style="width: 100%" |- ! Books !! Principle !! Language !! Lessons |- | [[Rapt in the King]] || 8 {{Lore|Heart}} || N/A || 2 |- | [[The Instruments of the Heart]] || 10 {{Lore|Heart}} || N/A || 2 |- | [[Lake Fucino Recordings]] ([[Phonograph Record|Record]]) || 12 {{Lore|Heart}} || N/A || 2 |} ==Crafting== {{PAGENAME}} can be used for the following recipes. {| class="fandom-table" style="width: 100%" !Principle !Challenge !Requirements !Result |- | rowspan="3" |{{Lore|Heart}} |Prentice | |[[Cheerful Ditty]] (2 {{Lore|Heart}}, 1 {{Lore|Sky}}, [[Memory]], [[Sound (Aspect)|Sound]]) |- |Scholar |[[Instrument]] or [[Instrumental Workstations]] |[[Thunderskin's Paean]] (1 {{Lore|Grail}}, 4 {{Lore|Heart}}, 1 {{Lore|Scale}}, [[Memory]], [[Sound (Aspect)|Sound]]) |- |Keeper |[[Thunderskin's Paean]] |[[Swaddled Thunder]] (6 {{Lore|Heart}}, 4 {{Lore|Sky}}, [[Tool]], [[Device]], [[Fabric and Fibre]]) |- | rowspan="3" |{{Lore|Nectar}} |Prentice | |[[Savage Hymn]] (2 {{Lore|Scale}}, 2 {{Lore|Sky}}, [[Memory]], [[Sound (Aspect)|Sound]]) |- |Scholar |[[Instrument]] |[[Hive's Lament]] (2 {{Lore|Moth}}, 4 {{Lore|Nectar}}, 2 {{Lore|Winter}}, [[Memory]], [[Sound (Aspect)|Sound]], [[Persistent]]) |- |Keeper |[[Pyrus Auricalcinus]] |[[Sacrament Malachite]] (6 {{Lore|Nectar}}, [[Liquid]], [[Beverage]]) |- |{{Lore|Scale}} |Prentice | |[[Savage Hymn]] (2 {{Lore|Scale}}, 2 {{Lore|Sky}}, [[Memory]], [[Sound (Aspect)|Sound]]) |} == Notable uses == *This is the only skill that can craft [[Hive's Lament]], a strong {{Lore|Nectar}} memory. It is difficult to craft it without levelling this skill. It is possible to acquire the memory in other ways, but crafting it is the least resource-intensive method. *This is one of the only two skills that can craft [[Thunderskin's Paean]], a strong {{Lore|Heart}} memory. The other skill is [[Strings & Songs]]. Drums & Dances is a marginally better option for crafting it, as its primary principle is {{Lore|Heart}}. *The same two aforementioned skills and Thunderskin's Paean can be used to craft [[Swaddled Thunder]], providing a way to craft fabric without using any fabric in the process. Once again, as a {{Lore|Heart}} recipe, Drums & Dances is the better choice.

{{BoH_Skill|wisdoms=[[Illumination]]

'''Glaziery & Lightsmithing''' is a [[Skills|Skill]] card that starts with {{Lore|Lantern|2}} and {{Lore|Sky|1}}. ==Wisdom Attunement== {{quote|A paradox of Illumination: light reveals, light blinds. This is the lesson of the White Flower of the Watchman's Tree:
even the most dangerous of knowledge is no danger at all when it is forgotten.|The White Flower's Paradox}}

even the most dangerous of knowledge is no danger at all when it is given to the fire.|The Red Flower's Lesson}}

Applebright Euphonies.text:
{{BoH Skill |primary_principle=[[Sky]] |secondary_principle=[[Grail]] |title1=Applebright Euphonies |image1=File:Applebright_euphonies.png |wisdoms=[[Illumination]]
[[Bosk]]}} {{quote|‘Breath is the temptation of the soul.’ Pleasures and insights that the Church would call ‘the Secrets', the Sisterhood ‘the Mysteries’, and the Bureau 'unsanctioned.’}} '''Applebright Euphonies''' is a [[Skills|Skill]] card that starts with 2 [[Sky]] and 1 [[Grail]]. ==Wisdom Attunement== {{quote|Calyptra is the law that requires secret knowledge to be forgotten - except in the libraries of the Watchman's Tree. The number of the Hours of the Calyptra is three, and we do not trust the third Hour, though we heed her. This paradox is a matter of Illumination.|What May Be True}} Committing Applebright Euphonies to [[Illumination]] provides [[Mettle]] (2 {{Lore|Forge}}, 1 {{Lore|Edge}}), but cannot evolve Mettle by itself. It will need a memory that has the [[Memories that can evolve Elements of the Soul|Evolve via Illumination]] aspect, such as [[Invincible Audacity]], and can then be upgraded at any workstation that accepts the relevant principles, for example, [[Shrine: the Madrugad]]. {{quote|Calyptra is the law that requires secret knowledge to be concealed - except in the libraries of the Watchman's Tree. The number of the Hours of the Calyptra is three, and we do not speak of the oldest Hour. This observance is a matter of Bosk.|What May Be Known}} Committing Applebright Euphonies to [[the Bosk]] provides [[Ereb]] (2 {{Lore|Grail}}, 1 {{Lore|Edge}}), which can be upgraded at the [[Calicite Altar]]. ==Acquiring the Skill== ''Lesson: {{PAGENAME}}'' can be acquired by studying the following books. {| class="fandom-table" style="width: 100%" |- ! [[Skolekosophy]] |primary_principle={{Lore|Moth}} |secondary_principle={{Lore|Knock}} |image1=Edicts Liminal.png}} {{quote|The precepts of limitation and division; established by the enigmatic conclave of Hours sometimes called the Chancel.}} '''Edicts Liminal''' is a [[Skills|Skill]] card that starts with 2 {{Lore|Moth}} and 1 {{Lore|Knock}}. ==Wisdom Attunement== {{quote|There is a prophecy of a glorious City that mortals could raise, but the Hours of the Chancel have decreed that it will not exist. The decrees of the Chancel are not defied, but now and then they have been circumvented… and we might conceive that a City with walls of shining flint could be raised in dreams; in the Mansus.|Sapphire}} Committing Edicts Liminal to [[Nyctodromy]] provides [[Fet]] (2 {{Lore|Rose}}, 1 {{Lore|Moth}}), and can be evolved at [[Shrine: St Januarius]] or [[Altar: St Tentreto]]. {{quote|There is a prophecy of a glorious City that mortals could raise, but the Hours of the Chancel have decreed that it will not exist. {{BoH Skill |title1=Edicts Martial |wisdoms=[[Horomachistry]]
[[Illumination]] |primary_principle={{Lore|Moon}} |secondary_principle={{Lore|Edge}} |image1=Edicts Martial.png}} {{quote|The precepts of struggle and conflict which drive the cosmic engine of change sometimes called the Corrivality.}} __NOTOC__
'''Edicts Martial''' is a [[Skills|Skill]] card that starts with 2 {{Lore|Moon}} and 1 {{Lore|Edge}}. ==Wisdom Attunement== ===Horomachistry=== {{quote|All the Hours are defined by their opposition to other Hours... just as we are defined by the battles we choose. This is a matter of the Horomachistry Wisdom.|Conflict Creates Gods}} Committing Edicts Martial to [[Horomachistry]] provides [[Mettle]] ({{Lore|Forge|2}}, {{Lore|Edge|1}}), and can be [[Evolve]]d at [[Shrine: the Chancel]] and the [[Telescope]] with no additional requirements. Where there are no names, there are no enemies. This is a matter of the Illumination Wisdom.|Understanding Creates Conflict}} Committing Edicts Martial to [[Illumination]] provides [[Phost]] ({{Lore|Lantern|2}}, {{Lore|Sky|1}}), and can be [[Evolve]]d at the [[Practice Equipment]] with no additional requirements. It can also be Evolved at the [[Condignator]], [[Instrument: Sunset Harp]], [[Oubliette Containment]] or [[Telescope]], with the use of the following [[Memory|Memories]]: *[[Invincible Audacity]] *[[Winning Move]] ==Acquiring the Skill== ''Lesson: {{PAGENAME}}'' can be acquired by studying the following books. {| class="fandom-table" style="width: 100%" |- ! Horns & Ivories.title: Horns & Ivories
Horns & Ivories.text:
{{BoH Skill |primary_principle={{Lore|Scale}} |secondary_principle={{Lore|Knock}} |title1=Horns & Ivories |wisdoms=[[Skolekosophy]]
[[The Bosk]] |image1=Horns & Ivories.png|level_1=}} {{Quote|The Hunter, the Way, and their memories.}} '''Horns & Ivories''' is a [[Skills|Skill]] card that starts with 2 {{Lore|Scale}} and 1 {{Lore|Knock}}. ==Wisdom Attunement== {{quote|When the Moth goes a-hunting in the dark of the Wood, he remembers a time when the Wood was bright, but he uses his horns to find the way, and we may follow him if we choose. After all, a trophy is nothing without a hunt: that's the lesson of the Wood.|The Moth's Way}} Committing Horns & Ivories to [[The Bosk]] provides [[Ereb]] (2 {{Lore|Grail}}, 1 {{Lore|Edge}}), but cannot evolve Ereb by itself. It will need a memory that has the [[Memories that can evolve Elements of the Soul|Evolve via Bosk]] aspect, for example [[Wind-in-Waiting]], and can then be evolved at any workstation that accepts the relevant principles, such as [[Practic Garden Dummy]]. {{quote|When the Chandler goes a-hunting in the dark of the Wood, he shields his candle so his prey is not forewarned, but he leaves a trail of ivory wax so we may follow him and purchase his prizes. After all, the goal of every hunt is to bring home a trophy, and when we understand Skolekosophy, we know how to bargain.|The Chandler's Path}} Committing Horns & Ivories to [[Skolekosophy]] provides [[Shapt]] (2 {{Lore|Knock}}, 1 {{Lore|Forge}}), which can be evolved at the [[Condignator]]. It can also be evolved at the [[Rowenarium (Workstation)|Rowenarium]] if the [[The Affair of the Endless Guest|Affair of the Endless Guest]] is concluded with Spencer Hobson entering the Rowenarium. ==Acquiring the Skill== ''Lesson: {{PAGENAME}}'' can be acquired by studying the following books. {| class="fandom-table" style="width: 100%" |- ! Inks of Containment.title: Inks of Containment
Inks of Containment.text:
{{BoH Skill |primary_principle={{Lore|Winter}} |secondary_principle={{Lore|Moon}} |title1=Inks of Containment |caption1=The inks in which the Histories are preserved. |wisdoms=[[Horomachistry]]
[[Preservation]] |image1=Inks of Containment.png |special_ability=Effective Against [[Theoplasmic Contamination]]}} {{Quote|The inks in which the Histories are preserved.}} '''Inks of Containment''' is a [[Skills|Skill]] card that starts with 2 {{Lore|Winter}} and 1 {{Lore|Moon}}. ==Wisdom Attunement== {{quote|Certain knowledge is forbidden to mortals… unless it's wisely contained. This law is named Calyptra; the enforcement of this law is named Calyptra also; the three Hours who enforce it share that name. They permit that knowledge to persist only in certain sanctioned places, and the most dangerous secrets must only be recorded in the inks called encaustum terminale. Horomachistry teaches us Calyptra's importance.|When It Is Permitted}} Committing Inks of Containment to [[Horomachistry]] provides [[Mettle]] (2 {{Lore|Forge}}, 1 {{Lore|Edge}}), which can be evolved at the [[Telescope]], [[Shrine: the Chancel]], or the [[Great Clock]]. {{quote|Certain knowledge is forbidden to mortals… except in nine great libraries protected by the covenant-stones they hold, where this knowledge can be safely recorded in the inks called encaustum terminale. These libraries are together called the Watchman's Tree, and the covenant marked by these stones shares that name. All this, then, is a matter of Preservation.|When It Is Safe}} Committing Inks of Containment to [[Preservation]] provides [[Health]] (1 {{Lore|Heart}} 1 {{Lore|Nectar}}, 1 {{Lore|Scale}}), but cannot evolve Health by itself. It will need a memory that has the [[Memories that can evolve Elements of the Soul|Evolve via Preservation]] aspect, for example [[Old Moment]], and can then be evolved at any workstation that accepts the relevant principles, such as [[Practic Garden|Practic Garden Dummy]]. ==Acquiring the Skill== ''Lesson: {{PAGENAME}}'' can be acquired by studying the following books. {| class="fandom-table" style="width: 100%" |- ! Inks of Revelation.title: Inks of Revelation
Inks of Revelation.text:
{{BoH Skill |primary_principle={{Lore|Lantern}} |secondary_principle={{Lore|Moth}} |title1=Inks of Revelation |wisdoms=[[Hushery]]
[[Ithastry]] |image1=File:Inks_of_Revelation.png}} {{quote|The inks in which the Histories are revealed.}} '''Inks of Revelation''' is a [[Skills|Skill]] card that starts with 2 {{Lore|Lantern}} and 1 {{Lore|Moth}}. ==Wisdoms== {{quote|The inks called encaustum terminale are permitted only to the Librarians of the Watchman's Tree. Those inks can be used to reveal truths - even truths that are no longer so, not since the dawn times when the sun hung red and low and we felt its warmth like autumn. If that first and gentlest sun returned, the truths might return with it. Hushery remembers.|Truths that Were}} Committing Inks of Revelation to [[Hushery]] provides [[Wist]] (2 {{Lore|Winter}}, 1 {{Lore|Lantern}}), which can be evolved at the [[Solar Altar]] or the [[Columbic Sarcophagus]]. {{quote|The inks called encaustum terminale are permitted only to the Librarians of the Watchman's Tree. Those inks can be used to reveal truths - even truths too great for daylight. Perhaps, then, daylight is not bright enough; perhaps we must find a way to kindle a light bright enough to reveal those greater truths. This would be a matter for Ithastry.|Truths that Will Be}} Committing Inks of Revelation to [[Ithastry]] provides [[Phost]] (2 {{Lore|Lantern}}, 1 {{Lore|Sky}}), which can be evolved at [[Oubliette Containment]]. == Acquiring the Skill == ''Lesson: {{PAGENAME}}'' can be acquired by studying the following books. {| class="fandom-table" style="width: 100%" |- ! [[Nyctodromy]] |image1=File:Path_&_Pilgrim.png}} {{quote|The traveller is always returning. One who does not is no traveller.|Arun Peel}} '''Path & Pilgrim''' is a [[Skills|Skill]] card that starts with 2 {{Lore|Rose}} and 1 {{Lore|Scale}}. ==Wisdom Attunement== {{quote|Every traveller crosses a threshold twice. The Horned-Axe is the Hour who faces both ways at every threshold. Find the answer to her riddles in Birdsong.|The Threshold}} Committing Path & Pilgrim to [[Birdsong]] provides [[Chor]] (2 {{Lore|Heart}}, 1 {{Lore|Grail}}), but cannot evolve Chor by itself. It will need a memory that has the [[Memories that can evolve Elements of the Soul|Evolve via Birdsong]] aspect, for example [[Ascendant Harmony]], and can then be evolved at any workstation that accepts the relevant principles, such as [[Practice Equipment]]. {{quote|Speech is the key to dream, and because we are speaking apes, every night is a journey. Nyctodromy is the wisdom of the paths of night.|The Path}} Committing Path & Pilgrim to [[Nyctodromy]] provides [[Fet]] (2 {{Lore|Rose}}, 1 {{Lore|Moth}}), which can be evolved at [[Shrine: St Januarius]] or [[Altar: St Tentreto]]. ==Acquiring the Skill== ''Lesson: {{PAGENAME}}'' can be acquired by studying the following books. {| class="fandom-table" style="width: 100%" |- ! Hyksos.title: Hyksos
Hyksos.text:
[[File:Hyksos Icon.png|right|64x64px]] {{Quote|A sly language.}} '''Hyksos''' is a [[Languages|Language]]. Though few [[Readable|Readables]] require Hyksos, most of them require {{Lore|Edge}}, which it provides. [[Aunt Mopsy]], [[Mrs E]], and [[Sr. Corso Reverte]] understand Hyksos, and can teach it for 1 [[Tally]]. If Corso is present at a [[Salon]], random conversation with him may produce a language [[Memory|Lesson]]. ==Skill== {{BoH Skill |title1=Hyksos |wisdoms=[[Nyctodromy]]
[[Skolekosophy]] |primary_principle={{Lore|Grail}} |secondary_principle={{Lore|Edge}} |image1=Hyksos.png}} {{Quote|The Shepherd-Kings brought this speech west from Canaan to use in their wards and snares. Had they never come to Egypt, they might never found a way to write it; given its addictive qualities, that might have been for the best.}} As a skill Hyksos starts with 2 {{Lore|Grail}} and 1 {{Lore|Edge}}. Languages cannot be used in crafting recipes, but can be used to explore the [[The Tree of Wisdoms|Tree of Wisdoms]]. == Wisdom Attunement == {{Quote|The veterans of the Légion du Seuil, who guard the boundaries of the waking world, tell stories of the labyrinths under the Mansus, above the Wood, and inside the Moon, where the first fallen Hours sleep, or hide, or rot: the gods-from-stone. Why the labyrinths? Because, the legionnaires say, there are Hours ruling now who would fight to consume the last scraps of their old enemies; and those who feast would eclipse those who abstain. The legionnaires have been known to boast that if they were only offered a great enough prize, they could guide the hungry Hours to their feast.|The Watchmen}} Committing Hyksos to [[Nyctodromy]] provides [[Shapt]] (2 {{Lore|Knock}}, 1 {{Lore|Forge}}), which can be evolved at [[Mirrors]] or [[Altar: Ascite]]. {{Quote|The assassins of the Tragulari, who end the long lives of Long, tell stories of the wars between the Hours in the dawn of the world, when the sun was red and low - wars where the savage sound of savage bells unravelled the light of moon and sun - wars where dreams burned on pyres where Long were the fuel. All this ended, the Tragulari say, once the Worms came, and the Hours had a common enemy. And so the Tragulari fear Worms; hate Worms; and make offerings to Worms.|The Dartsmen}} Committing Hyksos to [[Skolekosophy]] provides [[Ereb]] (2 {{Lore|Grail}}, 1 {{Lore|Edge}}), which can be evolved at the [[Nocturnary]], the [[Condignator]], or the [[Rowenarium (Workstation)|Rowenarium]]. ==Books== The following books are written in Hyksos. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Book !! Principle !! Lesson !! Memory |- | [[THE OPEN HEAD]] ([[Reels of Film|Film]]) || 8 {{Lore|Edge}} || 2x [[Disciplines of the Scar]] || [[Memory: Revelation]] (2 {{Lore|Lantern}}) |- | [[The Ascendant]] || 10 {{Lore|Edge}} || 2x [[Edicts Martial]] || [[Memory: Contradiction]] (2 {{Lore|Edge}}, 1 {{Lore|Moon}}) |- | [[Book of Miah]] || 10 {{Lore|Rose}} || 2x [[Sand Stories]] || [[Intuition]] (2 {{Lore|Moon}}, 2 {{Lore|Rose}}) |- | [[A Child's Treasury of Golden Afternoons]] || 10 {{Lore|Edge}} || 2x [[Sharps]] || [[Numen: Merciless Alteration]] (5 {{Lore|Edge}}, 5 {{Lore|Forge}}, 5 {{Lore|Grail}}) |} ==Trivia== *Hyksos was not an available language in [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Cultist_Simulator_Wiki Cultist Simulator]. *It is implicitly the language spoken by the Canaanite rulers of the Fifteenth Dynasty of Lower Egypt, whom the Egyptians called "''heqau khasut''", "rulers from foreign lands," which is rendered Hyksos in English. Long after their rule, subsequent (non-Canaanite) dynasties portrayed the Hyksos as brutal and cruel, but the modern consensus among Egyptologists paints a more nuanced picture.https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyksos {{Skills Navbox}} [[Category:Language]] [[Category:Skill]] [[Category:Forge]] [[Category:Grail]]

Killasimi.title: Killasimi
Killasimi.text:
[[File:Killasimi Icon.png|right|64x64px]] {{Quote|A woven language.}} '''Killasimi''' is a [[Languages|Language]]. [[MCO Constance Lee]], [[Mlle Margot Matutine]], and [[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] understand Killasimi, and can teach it for 1 [[Tally]]. If any of these Visitors are present at a [[Salon]], random conversation with them may produce a language [[Memory|Lesson]]. ==Skill== {{BoH_Skill |title1=Killasimi| primary_principle={{Lore|Winter}} |secondary_principle={{Lore|Moon}} |wisdoms=[[The Bosk]]
[[Skolekosophy]] |image1=Killasimi.png}} {{Quote|If there is speech in Nowhere; if there is a language used by the Dead; if the House of the Moon has a native tongue; then it must be Killasimi. If none of this is true, it is still not a language to be spoken in daylight. Each word breathes woe. Read it, as they say, and weep.}} As a skill, Killasimi starts with 2 {{Lore|Winter}} and 1 {{Lore|Moon}}. Languages cannot be used in crafting recipes, but can be used to explore the [[The Tree of Wisdoms|Tree of Wisdoms]]. == Wisdom Attunement == {{quote|There is a prophecy among weavers: of one who will unwisely seek to find the future in a tapestry of her own hair. Her house will grow dark, shrouded in the labyrinths of her tresses. Pilgrims will seek her in the cellar of her house, where she will plead with them to cut her free. They will always fail, and she will always devour them. At last one will come who will ask instead to stay with her. Others will join them, until the house becomes a palace and the palace a city, below the world, where all are welcome and in the tapestry all truths are revealed.|The Weaver's Tale}} Committing Killasimi to [[The Bosk]] provides [[Health]] (1 {{Lore|Heart}} 1 {{Lore|Nectar}}, 1 {{Lore|Scale}}), which can be evolved at [[Altar of the Knot]], [[Calicite Altar]], or [[Deeplight Corals]]. {{quote|There is a prophecy of a master-carpenter who will resolve, unwisely, that the coffins he shapes are too beautiful to sully with corpses. He will steal trinkets from the dead, he will ask the help of smiths and jewellers, and day and night he will labour to shape something worthy of his work. At last he will tire of his task and offer his breath to the shape in the casket. When it accepts, it will rise from the coffin and pronounce itself King. It will rule by fear, or fear will destroy it. In either case, its maker will have no coffin and no grave, and his name will lost.|The Carpenter's Tale}} Committing Killasimi to [[Skolekosophy]] provides [[Ereb]] (2 {{Lore|Grail}}, 1 {{Lore|Edge}}), which can be evolved at the [[Nocturnary]] or the [[Rowenarium (Workstation)|Rowenarium]]. ==Books== The following books are written in Killasimi. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Book !! Principle !! Lesson !! Memory |- | [[The Berrybook]] || 8 {{Lore|Nectar}} || 2x [[Leaves & Thorns]] || [[Memory: Satisfaction]] (2 {{Lore|Grail}}, 1 {{Lore|Heart}}) |- | [[The Deaths of the Moon]] || 8 {{Lore|Moon}} || 2x [[Snow Stories]] || [[Memory: Salt]] (1 {{Lore|Knock}}, 1 {{Lore|Moon}}, 1 {{Lore|Winter}}) |- | [[Two Wombs, One Heart]] || 8 {{Lore|Heart}} || 2x [[Stitching & Binding]] || [[Memory: Satisfaction]] (2 {{Lore|Grail}}, 1 {{Lore|Heart}}) |- | [[The Wonderful Shape]] || 10 {{Lore|Grail}} || 2x [[Tridesma Hiera]] || [[Memory: Satisfaction]] (2 {{Lore|Grail}}, 1 {{Lore|Heart}}) |- | [[Kopralith Omphalos]] || 10 {{Lore|Moth}} || 2x [[Weaving & Knotworking]] || [[Numen: Weaving the World]] (5 {{Lore|Heart}}, 5 {{Lore|Moon}}, 5 {{Lore|Nectar}}) |- | [[One Thousand Threads]] || 12 {{Lore|Grail}} || 2x [[Tridesma Hiera]] || [[Memory: Fear]] (1 {{Lore|Edge}}, 2 {{Lore|Scale}}) |- | [[The Wound-Wounds]] || 18 {{Lore|Edge}} || 3x [[Disciplines of the Scar]] || [[Memory: Regret]] (1 {{Lore|Forge}}, 2 {{Lore|Winter}}) |- | [[Medusan Commentaries]] || 21 {{Lore|Grail}} || 3x [[Pentiments & Precursors]] || [[Memory: Fear]] (1 {{Lore|Edge}}, 2 {{Lore|Scale}}) |} ==Trivia== *The most direct inspiration for Killasimi is probably the Quechua language of Peru, which Southern speakers term as "Runasimi" ('people's language'). Further, the Inca Empire is known for its ''quipu'', a partially deciphered system of recording information using knotted strings of cotton or wool.https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quechuan_languages "Killa" means "moon" in Quechua (as seen with Mama Killahttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama_Killa), which follows the description of Killasimi as possibly being the native tongue of "the House of the Moon". *Killasimi may be inspired by Ikat, an Indonesian practice of telling stories through woven or dyed fabric.Orientations. Apr 21, 2015. [https://www.orientations.com.hk/highlights/woven-languages-an-interview-with-peter-ten-hoopen Woven Languages: An Interview with Peter ten Hoopen] ==References== {{Skills Navbox}} [[Category:Language]] [[Category:Skill]] [[Category:Moon]] [[Category:Winter]]

Fucine.title: Fucine
Fucine.text:
[[File:Fucine Icon.png|right|64px]] {{Quote|A dry language.}} '''Fucine''' is a [[Languages|Language]]. Books written in Fucine are primarily from the [[Dawn Period]]. [[Dr Serena Blackwood]], [[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]], [[Mr Peter Agdistis]] and [[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] understand Fucine, and can teach it for 1 [[Tally]]. If any of these Visitors are present at a [[Salon]], random conversation with them may produce a language [[Memory|Lesson]]. == Skill == {{BoH Skill |title1=Fucine |image1=Fucine Skill.png |wisdoms=[[Ithastry]]
[[Hushery]] |primary_principle={{Lore|Heart}} |secondary_principle={{Lore|Knock}}}} {{Quote|A people lived east of the lost lake Fucino. Horace warned that theirs was the land of witches. This was their language, called by some 'the dry tongue' and by others 'the tongue of witches'.}} As a skill, Fucine starts with 2 {{Lore|Heart}} and 1 {{Lore|Knock}}. Languages can not be used in crafting recipes, but can be used to explore the [[The Tree of Wisdoms|Tree of Wisdoms]]. ==Wisdom Attunement== {{Quote|There is a story known to painters: of a Queen who could love no other, neither woman nor man, but only her own image. She sought nine colours to grace the image, and the last was the turquoise of her eyes, a gift from the Shadowless King. Her court poet hymned his Queen and her image, and in his poem she heard the truth: that the image was greater. So she fled into the Wood, and the image ruled her domain with the poet as its consort, but it always remembered her kindly.|The Queen's Wound}} Committing Fucine to [[Hushery]] provides [[Trist]] (2 {{Lore|Moth}}, 1 {{Lore|Moon}}), but cannot be used to evolve Trist by itself. It will need a memory with the [[Memories that can evolve Elements of the Soul|Evolve via Hushery]] aspect, for example [[Didumos]], and can then be evolved at any workstation that accepts the relevant principles, such as [[Altar: St Tentreto]]. {{Quote|There is a story known to smiths: of a Queen whose realm was invaded by a great army. When she learnt that there were nine invaders for every defender, she ordered her army to surrender its swords. Night and day her smiths laboured to melt down the swords to bronze, while her generals threatened mutiny and the enemy advanced unhindered. They used the bronze to cast a Bell, but each time the Bell was rung, it cracked and had to be recast. At last on the night before the invaders reached the city, the Queen surrendered her crown to the casting. When at dawn the smiths rang the Bell, it cracked the moon like an egg and drove the sun from the sky. The invaders fled. But the Queen without a crown was no longer any queen at all.|The Queen's Weapon}} Committing Fucine to [[Ithastry]] provides [[Wist]] (2 {{Lore|Winter}}, 1 {{Lore|Lantern}}), the skill can be used to evolve Wist at the [[Exercise Yard]]. == Books == The following books are written in Fucine. {| class="wikitable" |- !
