Grand Ascent - Ground Floor.title: Grand Ascent - Ground Floor
Grand Ascent - Ground Floor.text:
{{BoH_Room |title1=Grand Ascent -
Ground Floor |image1=Grand Ascent ground floor.png |era=[[Baronial Period]] |required_aspects=* [[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Edge|4}}, {{Lore|Heart|4}},
{{Lore|Moon|4}} or {{Lore|Winter|4}}}} {{Quote|The staircase that served as the spine of the House: Baron Walter's great project, executed by the master mason Gregory Wheelock.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]], which can be unlocked early into the midgame. ==Grand Ascent - Ground Floor (Locked)== {{Quote|The stairs here are clear, but the air here is thick with old magics. I should move carefully, and I should not go alone.

Still no sign of any fire. Why then was the House abandoned?}} Before unlocking, it has the same name and requires {{Lore|Edge|4}}, {{Lore|Heart|4}}, {{Lore|Moon|4}} or {{Lore|Winter|4}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose: *[[Grand Ascent - First Floor]] *[[Servants' Hall]] *[[Reading Room]] *[[Entrance Hall]] ==Contents== ===Comfort=== *[[Delightful Repose]] *[[Ambrose's Favourite Chair]] *[[Paradise Palm]] ===Wall Art=== *[[Hokobald]] *''[['Dr Serena Blackwood']]'' ==Niches== There are five niches here, where the [[Busts]] of their respective owners can be placed in:
====1st Baron Brancrug==== {{Quote|A niche with a plaque: 'Who returned loyalty for loyalty and curse for curse'}} ====2nd Baron Brancrug==== {{Quote|A niche with a plaque: 'Who saw what had not yet passed'}} ====3rd Baron Brancrug==== {{Quote|A niche with a plaque: 'Who commanded the raising of this stair'}} ====4th Baron Brancrug==== {{Quote|A niche with a plaque: 'Who was mocked more than he merited'}} ====5th Baron Brancrug==== {{Quote|A niche with a plaque: 'Who was feared more than he merited'}} [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Baronial]]

Grand Ascent - First Floor.title: Grand Ascent - First Floor
Grand Ascent - First Floor.text:
{{BoH_Room |title1=Grand Ascent -
First Floor |image1=Grand ascent first floor.png |era=[[Baronial Period]] |required_aspects=* [[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Forge|4}}, {{Lore|Heart|4}},
{{Lore|Sky|4}} or {{Lore|Winter|4}}}} {{Quote|By long tradition, each Baron Brancrug had their image set in a niche in the Grand Ascent. Later, the Curia of the Isle continued the tradition for their Librarians.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Grand Ascent - First Floor (Locked)== {{Quote|The windows are tightly closed, the carpets surprisingly clean, but my skin prickles at the watchful presence in the stairwell. We will need to placate it before we go higher.}} Before unlocking, it has the same name and requires {{Lore|Forge|4}}, {{Lore|Heart|4}}, {{Lore|Sky|4}} or {{Lore|Winter|4}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose: * [[Grand Ascent - Second Floor]] * [[Westcott Room]] * [[Physic Garden]] * [[Grand Ascent - Ground Floor]] == Contents == ===Leaf=== *[[Potted Monstera]] ==Niches==
There are five niches here, where the [[Busts]] of their respective owners can be placed in:
====6th Baron Brancrug==== {{Quote|A niche with a plaque: 'Who knew cages'}} ====7th Baroness Brancrug==== {{Quote|A niche with a plaque: 'Not to be crossed, and not to be found'}} ====First Librarian of the Curia of the Isle==== {{Quote|A niche with a plaque: 'Who often purified, but was not often pure'}} ====Second Librarian of the Curia of the Isle==== {{Quote|A niche with a plaque: 'Who was born of three nations, and of none'}} ====Third Librarian of the Curia of the Isle==== {{Quote|A niche with a plaque: 'Whereof we cannot speak, thereof we must remain silent'}} [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Baronial]]

Chapel Ascite.title: Chapel Ascite
Chapel Ascite.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Chapel Ascite.png |era=[[Dawn Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Edge|14}} or {{Lore|Knock|14}} |workstations=*[[Altar: Ascite]]}} {{Quote|The Horned-Axe says: Never speak of this Mystery. When the Thunderskin was mortal, he served the Hours who slew my kind. I required the Thunderskin's death, and so the Grail gave him up. There is always a reckoning, and nothing is truly forgiven.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==A Wintry Forbidding (Locked)== {{Quote|Icy mists coil and drift.}} Before unlocking, it is called "A Wintry Forbidding" and requires {{Lore|Edge|14}} or {{Lore|Knock|14}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose [[Chapel Malachite]]. ==Workstations== * [[Altar: Ascite]] ({{Lore|Edge}}, {{Lore|Scale}}, {{Lore|Winter}}, {{Lore|Knock}}) - Can [[Evolve via Nyctodromy]]. == Contents == ===Books=== *[[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Dawn]]) (x4) ===Materials=== *[[Granite Slab]] *[[Serpentinite Slab]] ===Things=== *[[Cat of Depths]] *[[Owl of Spirals]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Dawn]]

Cucurbit Bridge.title: Cucurbit Bridge
Cucurbit Bridge.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=File:Cucurbit Bridge.png |era=[[Nocturnal Period]] |required_aspects=* [[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Forge|1}}, {{Lore|Lantern|1}}
or {{Lore|Sky|1}}}} {{Quote|Hush House has been many things over the centuries - including, in the Nocturnal Period of 1896-1929, a gaol. No-one remembers that period fondly, but at least it meant Nocturnal Branch paid for a new bridge..}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an area outside [[Hush House]]. ==Mist-Cloaked Bridge (Locked)== {{Quote|Every so often, someone builds a bridge to the Isle; each bridge lasts a hundred years, or two hundred; then the sea disposes of it. This was built in the 1890s, and that makes it the newest bridge - but that doesn't mean it's new.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Mist-Cloaked Bridge" and requires {{Lore|Forge|1}}, {{Lore|Lantern|1}} or {{Lore|Sky|1}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose [[Keeper's Lodge]]. == Contents == There are no items inherently, however if you are already carrying 5 items and receive a 6th one, it will be deposited right outside [[Watchman's Tower: Gatehouse]]. Items will continue accumulating in a straight line, eventually ending up on the bridge. [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Out of Bounds]] [[Category:Nocturnal Period]]

Chapel Calicite.title: Chapel Calicite
Chapel Calicite.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Chapel Calicite.png |era=[[Dawn Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Grail|14}} or {{Lore|Nectar|14}} |workstations=*[[Calicite Altar]]}} {{Quote|The Red Grail says: Never speak of this Mystery. I was always the first, and I must always be greatest. When we spilt the blood of the Thunderskin, I feasted and I grew strong, stronger again than the Twins. There is always a feast, and nothing is truly wasted.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==A Red Forbidding (Locked)== {{Quote|Crimson mists beckon and sway.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "A Red Forbidding" and requires {{Lore|Grail|14}} or {{Lore|Nectar|14}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose [[Chapel Ascite]]. ==Workstations== * [[Calicite Altar]] ({{Lore|Moon}}, {{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Grail}}) - Can [[Evolve via The Bosk]]. == Contents == ===Books=== * [[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Dawn]]) (x4) ===Beverages=== * [[Sacrament Calicite]] * [[Lambig Broceliande]] (Chalice) ===Light=== * [[Widow's Candle]] (x4) ===Material=== * [[Ambergris Chunk]] ===Things=== * [[Bobos of Spring]] * [[Goddess-who-changes-skin]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Dawn]]

Crucible Tower: Interview Laboratory.title: Crucible Tower: Interview Laboratory
Crucible Tower: Interview Laboratory.text:
{{BoH_Room |title1=Crucible Tower:
Interview Laboratory |image1=Crucible Tower Interview Laboratory.png |era=[[Nocturnal Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Knock|14}}, {{Lore|Moth|14}}
or {{Lore|Winter|14}} |workstations=*[[Condignator]]}} {{Quote|When a prisoner resisted all other interventions, Collers would bring them here, to test and refine their worth. His successes might be transferred to Zurich, or turned over to the Légion du Seuil to earn their humanity, or even, at least once, released. But his successes were not numerous.

Here, at last, is where the fire began and where it ended. When the power below the prison was released, it came here to interview Collers. Perhaps it intended to put him in his own device; but it seems there was not nearly enough left of him for that.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Charred Chamber (Locked)== {{Quote|The iron door here stands ajar - but it still glows faintly red, even after all these years. This is not a natural heat, and there is no entirely natural way to quell it.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Charred Chamber" and requires {{Lore|Knock|14}}, {{Lore|Moth|14}} or {{Lore|Winter|14}} [[Assistance]] to access. ==Workstations== * [[Condignator]] ({{Lore|Edge}}, {{Lore|Forge}}, {{Lore|Knock}}, {{Lore|Lantern}}) - Can [[Evolve via Skolekosophy]]. == Contents == ===Liquids=== * [[Black Sapphire Wash]] * [[Gideon's Soaks]] * [[Wolf-Snow Ampoule]] * [[Regensburg Balm]] ===Material=== * [[Labhitic Tincture]] ===Remains=== * [[Phosphorescent Scrapings]] * [[Heart in a Jar]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Nocturnal Period]]

Cell: ?.title: Cell: ?
Cell: ?.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Cell(Unknown).png |era=[[Nocturnal Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Grail|14}}, {{Lore|Moth|14}}
or {{Lore|Scale|14}} |workstations=*[[Chrysalis]]}} {{Quote|This was the last prisoner to be admitted to the Gaol, but only the date has been recorded. No record of its origin, crime, or arrest remains. Collers was a man of many secrets. Sometimes, however, he was also a generous man, and he insisted it be provided with a bed and with writing materials, should it ever feel the need for them.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Mazed Cell (Locked)== {{Quote|A leathery burgundy mesentery has spread out of and around the doorway of this cell. Chitin? Fungus? It crumbles beneath my hands, emitting choking fumes. It will be impossible to enter the cell without clearing it.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Mazed Cell" and requires {{Lore|Grail|14}}, {{Lore|Moth|14}} or {{Lore|Scale|14}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose [[Cell: Worm-Inhabited]]. ==Workstations== * [[Chrysalis]] ({{Lore|Nectar}}, {{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Scale}}, {{Lore|Moth}}) - Can [[Evolve via The Bosk]]. == Contents == ===Ink=== * [[Asimel]] ===Beverage=== * [[Rubywise Ruin]] ===Flower=== * [[Vase of Lilies]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Nocturnal Period]]

Chapel Malachite.title: Chapel Malachite
Chapel Malachite.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Chapel Malachite.png |era=[[Dawn Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Heart|14}} or {{Lore|Nectar|14}} |workstations=*[[Altar: Malachite]]}} {{Quote|The Ring-Yew says: Never speak of this Mystery. When the Thunderskin was mortal he loved me first, and so the Grail destroyed him. Now the Thunderskin delights forever in my succulence. There is always a renewal, and nothing truly ends.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==A Honeyed Forbidding (Locked)== {{Quote|The air is thick with the scents of honey and yew-berries - enough to daze the heart and mind.}} Before unlocking, it is called "A Honeyed Forbidding" and requires {{Lore|Heart|14}} or {{Lore|Nectar|14}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose the [[Smuggler's Den]]. ==Workstations== * [[Altar: Malachite]] ({{Lore|Moth}}, {{Lore|Nectar}}, {{Lore|Heart}}) - Can [[Evolve via Preservation]]. == Contents == ===Books=== * [[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Dawn]]) (x2) ===Tool=== * [[Mortar & Pestle]] ===Beverages=== * [[Skinshuck Mead]] * [[Rubywise Ruin]] * [[Leathy]] ===Liquid=== * [[Wolf-Snow Ampoule]] ===Materials=== * [[Curious Seashell]] * [[Quartz Chunk]] * [[Beeswax]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Dawn]]

Gaol Kitchen.title: Gaol Kitchen
Gaol Kitchen.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Gaol Kitchen.png |era=[[Nocturnal Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Grail|12}}, {{Lore|Heart|12}}
or {{Lore|Winter|12}} |workstations=*[[Kitchen Range: Gaol]]}} {{Quote|'There are no Hours at Brancrug,' Collers used to say - even before he was Governor of Brancrug Gaol, when he was only Secretary Vigilant of the Curia. By way of reminder, the hands were confiscated from every timepiece within the prison walls. The warders could still rely on the chimes of the great Clock in the abbey spire. But it did make life harder for the cooks.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Worm-Gnawed Kitchen (Locked)== {{Quote|This kitchen has clearly been penetrated and polluted by Worms - the 'parasites of the Sun'. The Worms are long gone. But the kitchen will need scouring, it will need decontaminating, and then it will definitely need all its food throwing out. Even if it's tinned.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Worm-Gnawed Kitchen" and requires {{Lore|Grail|12}}, {{Lore|Heart|12}} or {{Lore|Winter|12}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose the [[Gaol Cellar]]. ==Workstations== * [[Kitchen Range: Gaol]] ({{Lore|Scale}}, {{Lore|Lantern}}, {{Lore|Nectar}}, {{Lore|Grail}}) == Contents == ===Tools=== * [[Kitchen Bowls]] ===Beverages=== * [[Skinshuck Mead]] * [[Mist-Kissed Water]] (Pitcher) * [[Dawnlion Coffee]] (Half-Pot) * [[Elderflower Cordial]] * [[Eigengrau]] ===Sustenance=== * [[Cuckoo-Honey]] * [[Rosehip Jam]] * [[Pickled Pilchards]] * [[Blackberry Jam]] * [[Honey]] * [[Flour]] ===Material=== * [[Labhitic Tincture]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Nocturnal Period]]

Deeplight Caves.title: Deeplight Caves
Deeplight Caves.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Deeplight Caves.png |era=[[Dawn Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Moon|14}} or {{Lore|Nectar|14}} |workstations=*[[Deeplight Corals]]}} {{Quote|When the gods-from-stone were swept away, the Carapace Cross who had served them were swept away too. The Seglaz-kind, the Wyrmefota-kind, the Glaeterfloge-kind, all those wise and mighty ones are gone, into Nowhere or hiding or us. Here in the fire-warmed waters, away from the justice of sunlight, their legacy quietly thrives.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in the depths underneath [[Hush House]]. ==Menacing Phosphorescence (Locked)== {{Quote|The pumps have drained enough water to splash through, but everything is spatched and splotted with sickly, alien, wonderous, mesmeric light. When I retreat, I find the same glow on my boots. Whatever I do, I should not do it hastily.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Menacing Phosphorescence" and requires {{Lore|Moon|14}} or {{Lore|Nectar|14}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose the [[Shrine to St Tentreto]]. ==Workstations== * [[Deeplight Corals]] ({{Lore|Nectar}}, {{Lore|Rose}}, {{Lore|Scale}}, {{Lore|Moon}}) - Can [[Evolve via The Bosk]]. [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Dawn]]

Gaol Hall.title: Gaol Hall
Gaol Hall.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Gaol Hall .png]] |era=[[Nocturnal Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Forge|11}}, {{Lore|Moth|11}}
or {{Lore|Winter|11}} |workstations=*[[Serve Here]]}} {{Quote|Here the guards and the prisoners would take their meals. Sometimes Collers, too, would descend from his tower and discuss philosophy with poisoners, ethics with Antaians, theology with labhites. Afterwards he would generally burn his notes.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Worm-Eaten Hall (Locked)== {{Quote|This place bears the unmistakable traces of Worms - the 'serpents which are no serpents'. They are almost certainly gone... but we'll take no chances. Worms are difficult to evict from buildings, but much harder to evict from people.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Worm-Eaten Hall" and requires {{Lore|Forge|11}}, {{Lore|Moth|11}} or {{Lore|Winter|11}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose the [[Gaol Kitchen]]. ==Workstations== * [[Serve Here]] == Contents == ===Books=== * [[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Nocturnal]]) (x4) ===Tool=== *[[Mop and Bucket]] ===Beverages=== * [[Dawnlion Coffee]] (Cup x2) * [[Isle-Water]] (Pitcher, Glass x2) ===Thing=== * [[Lacquered Bone Chess Set]] ===Comfort=== * [[Spartan Chair]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Nocturnal Period]]

Boathouse.title: Boathouse
Boathouse.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Boathouse.png |era=[[:Category:Open Air|Open Air]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Moon|13}} or {{Lore|Rose|13}} |workstations=*[[Brancrug Boathouse]]}} {{Quote|The best way to come to Brancrug unnoticed. Most recently, an unofficial means for Suppression Bureau officials to come and go.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an [[:Category:Open Air|Open Air]] location below [[Hush House]]. ==Perilous Path (Locked)== {{Quote|This route was never safe, even before the last round of storms had their way with it.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Perilous Path" and requires {{Lore|Moon|13}} or {{Lore|Rose|13}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose the [[Sea-Caves]]. ==Workstations== *[[Brancrug Boathouse]] - Can be used to discard objects, release beasts or go for a swim. [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Open Air]]

Cell: Worm-Inhabited.title: Cell: Worm-Inhabited
Cell: Worm-Inhabited.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Cell Worm-Inhabited.png |era=[[Nocturnal Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Forge|15}}, {{Lore|Knock|15}}
or {{Lore|Sky|15}}}} {{Quote|The occupant of this cell could not be allowed fresh air and exercise. It could not have reasonably expected to leave this cell ever again, even while it wore human shape. But it could not be confined forever; in the end, somehow, it found its way into the walls.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Impermeable Cell (Locked)== {{Quote|A sign outside this cell reads WARNING: NOT TO BE SPOKEN WITH, NOR LOOKED UPON. The protections that still hang in the air lend force to the injunction.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Impermeable Cell" and requires {{Lore|Forge|15}}, {{Lore|Knock|15}} or {{Lore|Sky|15}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose [[Cell: Long]]. == Contents == ===Ink=== * [[Stargall Ink]] ===Materials=== * [[Desiccated Witchworms]] * [[Whispering Sand]] ===Mark=== * [[Midnight Mark]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Nocturnal Period]]

Columbic Crypt.title: Columbic Crypt
Columbic Crypt.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Columbic Crypt.png |era=[[Dawn Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Moon|15}} or {{Lore|Winter|15}} |workstations=*[[Columbic Sarcophagus]]}} {{Quote|St Columba, with twelve companions, brought the word of the Unconquered Sun to Scotland, where he founded a monastery on the blessed isle of Iona. There he died and there his bones remained until the Northmen came.

But in Cornwall they speak of his thirteenth companion, a 'hybrid beauty' called Rowena who was perhaps his tutor, perhaps his seducer, or perhaps his daughter. At his death, the monks sought to stone her for her impurities. She bore Columba's bones away so the monks would not have them - substituting, out of tact or mischief, the bones of a horse. She brought the bones to a hidden Isle, where she made a double foundation of nuns and monks, and became its first abbess: but she would admit none to her order who was a virgin, nor innocent of any crime. Since then, the Isle has been a refuge for all the world might consider impure.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Fluttering Crypt (Locked)== {{Quote|The darkness here beats with wings. Bats? The sound is more like birds, but there is a timpani quality that suggests more bones than feathers. One more step, and I sense the possibility of talons.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Fluttering Crypt" and requires {{Lore|Moon|15}} or {{Lore|Winter|15}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose: *[[Catacombs]] *[[Ivory Vault]] ==Workstations== * [[Columbic Sarcophagus]] ({{Lore|Moth}}, {{Lore|Winter}}; also {{Lore|Forge}} and {{Lore|Lantern}}, see the Workstation's page) - Can [[Evolve via Hushery]]. [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Dawn]]

Catacombs.title: Catacombs
Catacombs.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Catacombs.png |era=[[Dawn Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Grail|15}} or {{Lore|Winter|15}} |workstations=*[[Catacombs Altar]]}} {{Quote|In the days of honey, those who remembered brought the bones of their dead to the grey rock in the sea. In the time of the Eagles, those who remembered brought the bones of their dead to the grey rock in the sea. In the time of the Bear-king, the clans brought the bones of their dead to the grey rock in the sea. When the Wolf-kings came, those who remembered brought the bones of their dead to the grey rock in the sea. Through all the years of Sun and Bronze, those who remembered brought the bones of their dead to the grey rock in the sea. Much is taken; much abides.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Rattling Tunnels (Locked)== {{Quote|The dead do not walk here; but their eyes are upon me. I can quell them, or I can feed them.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Rattling Tunnels" and requires {{Lore|Grail|15}} or {{Lore|Winter|15}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose the [[Iron Vault]]. ==Workstations== * [[Catacombs Altar]] ({{Lore|Moon}}, {{Lore|Scale}}, {{Lore|Winter}}) - Can [[Evolve via Hushery]]. == Contents == ===Beverages=== *[[Sacrament Ascite]] *[[Lambig Broceliande]] (Chalice) ===Light=== *[[Widow's Candle]] (x2) ===Materials=== *[[Atlantic Amber]] *[[Sea-Glass]] ===Leaf and Flower=== *[[Eva's Locks]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Dawn]]

Gaol Cellar.title: Gaol Cellar
Gaol Cellar.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Gaol Cellar.png |era=[[Nocturnal Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Forge|13}}, {{Lore|Scale|13}}
or {{Lore|Winter|13}}}} {{Quote|The entrance to the sub-cellar was barred, locked, chained, warded, both physically and otherwise. Whatever was kept down there, they took it extremely seriously.

It looks very much as if the questing Worms broke the seals, drawn by the power below. It looks very much as if they regretted it.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Ravaged Cellar (Locked)== {{Quote|This room too has been visited by Worms, the 'abomination of the relict-kind'... but almost no traces remain.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Ravaged Cellar" and requires {{Lore|Forge|13}}, {{Lore|Scale|13}} or {{Lore|Winter|13}} [[Assistance]] to access. Gaol Yard.title: Gaol Yard
Gaol Yard.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Gaol yard.png |era=[[Nocturnal Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Grail|10}}, {{Lore|Heart|10}}
or {{Lore|Winter|10}} |workstations=*[[Exercise Yard]]}} {{Quote|The gaol was nicknamed the 'Cucurbit', for the alchemist's flask that distils and refines. Prisoners would become better versions of themselves, realigned to responsibility. Hence, though it would have been much safer to confine the more potent inmates to their sealed cells, Governor Collers insisted that even they should be allowed fresh air and exercise.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Blackened Yard (Locked)== {{Quote|A ferocious heat has scorched, even melted, the stones. But as at the bridge, it's only here and there. Horribly, 'here' and 'there' mostly seem to be where people happened to be standing. Charred, cracked bones scatter the yard.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Blackened Yard" and requires {{Lore|Grail|10}}, {{Lore|Heart|10}} or {{Lore|Winter|10}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose: *[[Staff-Room]] *[[Gaol Hall]] ==Workstations== * [[Exercise Yard]] ({{Lore|Winter}}, {{Lore|Edge}}, {{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Knock}}) - Can [[Evolve via Ithastry]]. [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Nocturnal Period]]

Cell: Long.title: Cell: Long
Cell: Long.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Cell Long.png |era=[[Nocturnal Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Edge|13}} or {{Lore|Knock|13}} |workstations=*[[Guest Bed: Long Cell]]}} {{Quote|The few Long at Brancrug were kept in cells triple-buttressed with silver and steel and sanctioned spells. The Bureau knew their weaknesses, but never relied upon them. This cell last housed two immortals - an Edge-long dyad. This would have required not only ferocious and eternal vigilance, but also frequent replacement of shattered furniture.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Trapped Cell (Locked)== {{Quote|A sign outside this cell reads WARNING: DO NOT ENTER WHILE SAFETY MEASURES ARE ARMED.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Trapped Cell" and requires {{Lore|Edge|13}} or {{Lore|Knock|13}} [[Assistance]] to access. ==Workstations== * [[Guest Bed: Long Cell]] ({{Lore|Scale}}, {{Lore|Lantern}}, {{Lore|Edge}}, {{Lore|Heart}}) - Can be camped in, or used by [[Visitors]] with an interest in {{Lore|Edge}}. == Contents == ===Books=== * [[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Curia]]) * [[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Nocturnal]]) ===Wall Art=== * [[Cudgels: Dyddgu and St Twrog]] (x2) * [[Wasters: Darling-Dear and Father Turk]] (x2) * [[Bokken: Captain Torgue and Mistress Dearday]] (x2) [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Nocturnal Period]]

Foundry.title: Foundry
Foundry.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Foundry (Location).png]] |era=[[Baronial Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Forge|6}} or {{Lore|Scale|6}} |workstations=[[Foundry (Workstation)|Foundry]]}} {{Quote|This room was set aside for metalworking by Hendrik Dewulf. There's always been a smithy in Brancrug Village, but Hendrik wanted to make sure he could have his pistol-balls cast and his prisoner-shackles mended, even if the villagers were feeling rebellious. When Ambrose Westcott arrived, he had little use for shackles and less for pistols; he refurbished the place for his metallurgical experiments. A bad place to be in summer, a good one in winter.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Ravaged Foundry (Locked)== {{Quote|This room has not only been abandoned, but vandalised. Someone has smashed the place up and scrawled W-signs on the wall in blood and soot. I'll need skilled assistance to return it to use.}}
Before unlocking, it is called the "Ravaged Foundry" and requires {{Lore|Forge|6}} or {{Lore|Scale|6}} [[Assistance]] to access. Fludd Gallery.title: Fludd Gallery
Fludd Gallery.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Fludd Gallery.png]] |era=[[Curia Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Forge|6}} or {{Lore|Winter|6}} |workstations=*[[Alchemist's Glassware]]}} {{Quote|Thirza Blake, seventh Librarian of the House, extended this space, decorating it with semi-precious materials and filling it with the finest art Hush House's money could buy. (Of course, after her enthusiasms brought the House to the brink of penury, much of it had to be sold off.)}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Despoiled Laboratory (Locked)== {{Quote|This was an alchemist's workshop and a picture gallery, but the pictures have been flung down, the vessels overturned, the solvents and reagents spilt. It will be time-consuming and dangerous to repair.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Despoiled Laboratory" and requires {{Lore|Forge|6}} or {{Lore|Winter|6}} [[Assistance]] to access. Duelling Hall.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Duellist Hall.png]] |era=[[Curia Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Edge|8}} or {{Lore|Grail|8}} |workstations=*[[Practice Equipment]]}} {{Quote|In Baronial times, this was a ballroom, but in the nineteenth century, during Brulleau's time as Librarian, a dyad of eternally duelling Edge-long agreed to stay at Hush House for a year and a day to allow Natalia to study them, if she satisfied certain conditions. Their names are recorded as 'Mistress Dearday' and 'Father Torgue'.}} __NOTOC__

As I essay the threshold, a whisper troubles the still air, and a pair of wall-hung swords glints menacingly. More of van Lauren's protections. Back Stairs.title: Back Stairs
Back Stairs.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Back Stairs.png |era=[[Baronial Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Heart|9}}, {{Lore|Knock|9}}, {{Lore|Lantern|9}}, {{Lore|Moon|9}}, {{Lore|Rose|9}} or {{Lore|Scale|9}}}} {{Quote|The secret artery of the House. All those abbots and barons and all their crowds of retainers needed their chamber pots emptying and their boots cleaning. These are the stairs that the boots and the chamber pots went up and down. They were notoriously cramped and treacherous. It was a rare year some poor scullion didn't crack an ankle. It was the Suppression Bureau, at very long last, who remodelled the stairs and put in electric lights. And people say the Suppression Bureau never did Hush House any good!}} __NOTOC__

Earl Brian's Field.title: Earl Brian's Field
Earl Brian's Field.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Earl Brian's Field.png]] |era=[[Solar Gothic Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Nectar|11}}, {{Lore|Rose|11}}
or {{Lore|Sky|11}} |workstations=*[[The Earl's Yew]]}} {{Quote|'Brian' is another one of those leitmotif names that recur all through Brancrug's long histories. This one was Brian of Brittany, who is named Earl of Cornwall by King William after the Conquest. In 1068, the sons of the deposed King Harold mount raids on Cornwall and Brian funds the construction of a fortified gate and the Watchman's Tower - initially in wood - to protect the abbey. In return, the Abbey 'gives shelter' to a yew tree he's brought from Brittany, that flowers in 'divers colours'. This is that tree, hollow now and rotting slowly from within, taking its time to die gracefully.

It has not flowered in living memory and the colours of its flowers cannot now be told; but Brian's brothers were called Alan the Red and Alan the Black.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Mist-Sunk Meadow (Locked)== {{Quote|There's grass beneath my feet and a mingle of wildflower scents, but above all the damp salt vapours of a thick sea-fog. Somewhere in the fog I think I hear a distant bell - far away - as it were beneath the sea...

Perhaps this can be blown away, perhaps sung away, if I bring the right powers and the right assistance.}}

Hush House.title: Hush House
Hush House.text:
{{Location |title=Hush House |image=[[File:Hush House.png]] |type=Library |location=Brancrug Isle, Cornwall |inhabitants=The Librarian}} {{Quote|Hush House is one of the nine great libraries of the Watchman's Tree - the select few places where the Hours sanction the preservation of forbidden knowledge.}}
'''Hush House''' is the main location in ''[[Book of Hours]]''. It is one of the nine libraries that comprise [[w:c:secret-histories:Watchman's_Tree|The Watchman's Tree]]. {{Quote|Crossrow and the Haustorium; the Grove of the Green Immortals and the Tomb of Lies; the Yeshiva Tigris and the Monastery of the Fifth Cup; the Invisible Serapeum and the Labyrinth of Lions; and here.}} {{Tocright}}
Above the [[Watchman's Tower: Gatehouse|gated entrance]], the inscription "BOOKS ARE THE MEMORY THAT DOES NOT DIE" can be seen. St Rhonwen's Trust has an obscure connection to the House. The Madrugad tolerates Hush House for her own reasons. Traditionally, [[Sea Holly]] was seen as the flower of Hush House. It can sometimes be found along the dunes and cliff-tops. Its history can be read in "Hush House - A Visitor's Guide" by [[The Rector|Reverend Timothy MacDonald]], part of ''[[The Wakefield Papers]]''. ==History== Hush House has been through five eras: [[Dawn Period]], [[Solar Gothic Period]], [[Baronial Period]], [[Curia Period]] and [[Nocturnal Period]].https://weatherfactory.biz/reverend-timothy-on-the-history-of-hush-house/ ===Dawn Period=== The earliest inhabitants of what is now Hush House were an order of monks and nuns, known as the Abbey of the Black Dove, or the Abbey of the White Crow, founded in 599 AD. Their first Abbess, [[Professor Rowena Hengerst|Rowena]], "a hybrid beauty", fled persecution from Iona in Scotland, to the then-hidden Brancrug Isle, and made a double foundation of nuns and monks, as chaste as they had always been, but each nun had her brother-twin and none could enter alone. She admitted none to her order who was a virgin, nor innocent of any crime. Since then, the Isle has been a refuge for all the world might consider impure. They were known for their [[Frith-Weft|'peace-weaving']]. Stories continue to persist of Rowena as the enigmatic protectress of Hush House.[['Lady Rowena']] The Sisterhood of the Triple Knot had first built their temples there much earlier than that. They worshipped the Red Grail, Ring-Yew (or Malachite), Horned-Axe, and the Thunderskin. Before them, either the Romans or Phoenicians had dug tunnels beneath the House grounds, in search of tin and gold. ===Solar Gothic Period=== St Brandan's Abbey was founded in the 11th century, and was part of the Church of the Unconquered Sun. Brian of Brittany, who was made Earl of Cornwall in 1068 by King William after the Norman Conquest, built the [[Watchman's Tower: Gatehouse|Watchman's Tower]], and its fortified gate. It was initially built in wood, later in stone, to protect St Brandan's Abbey (as Hush House was then known), from raids on Cornwall, mounted by the sons of the deposed Saxon king, Harold Godwinson. In return, the Abbey "give shelter" to [[The Earl's Yew|a yew tree]] he had brought from Brittany, that flowered in "divers colours" of red, black and white. The Abbey underwent a substantial expansion in the 13th century, following a generous donation from Lady Eva de Braose, the widow of the Marcher Lord Gwilym Ddu (William de Braose, or "Black William"), who never visited the Isle herself. An anonymous confessional account by a nun written in [[Henavek]], ''[[Ud Rocashaas]]'', suggests that William de Braose's death was arranged by the author, on Eva de Braose's orders, seeking help from the Abbey "to free her from her hated husband". After he was hanged for alleged adultery with the wife of Llywelyn the Great, Prince of the Welsh, Eva gained his estates and made a substantial endowment to the Abbey. The author insists William de Braose was "innocent of all but cruelty", and the adulterer was a shape-changing "undergoer". A notable addition to the monastery includes the construction of the [[Long Tower: Solomon's Quarters|Winter Tower]] in 1322, now known as the Long Tower, dedicated to the Madrugad. It was constructed by the mason-architect [[Abbot Ranulph]], who wrote a ''[[Against Vitruvius|treatise]]'' in which he mentions that Ely Tower collapsed around the time the Winter Tower was completed. [[Earth Cellar|A shrine to St Lucia the Eyeless]] was also built. Since the heresies of the Intercalate, the Church of the Unconquered Sun considers her an aspect of the Hour called Meniscate, but back then she was just the patron saint of stained-glass workers and eye doctors. The yew tree in [[Earl Brian's Field]] outside was traditionally hung with stained-glass ornaments on St Lucia's day. In 1349, the last abbess of St Brandans, Abbess Nonna, was murdered with "perversions of the healing arts" and "by poisoning and Arts unsanctioned". An [[The Most Sorrowful End of the Lady Nonna|unauthorised account]] of her death, written by one of the accused sisters, Eusebia, claims that the Abbess had introduced them to an unsanctioned Thunderskin-cult, which met in the caves below the Abbey, where she and others would perform sacred dances "for the Preservation of the Kingdom". She further claims that the Abbess asked her and the other sister to prepare a [[Leathy|leathy-draught]], for a rite all three of them would perform in the caves. However, something goes wrong, Nonna is "possessed of a tenebrous spirit", and the brethren are forced to "quell her with star-iron". Eusebia claims she and the other sister were implicated as scapegoats, although acknowledging her own fault.
After the two were executed, the abbey ceased to accept nuns and was reformed to accept only male novices. In the fifteenth century, Natan of Regensburg, a physician, came to Brancrug. He was granted sanctuary, but the brothers of the Abbey would not permit a Jew - and his family! - to live on abbey grounds. In an age when the Jews were, by royal order, unwelcome anywhere in the kingdom, Abbot Geffrey invited censure by giving him sanctuary. The Barber's Tower, as the Motley Tower was then known, was constructed in 1450, for Natan to dwell in and practice his healing arts. He was confined there by the suspicions of the monks, but he won more freedom over time. It housed Natan and his descendants, until their eviction by Baron [[Hendrik Dewulf]] a century later, shortly after he gained control of the estate. The monks of St Brandan's were recorded to have expressed concerns about Natan's [[Regensburg Menorah|'many-headed device']]. In the early 1530's, the last Abbot of St Brandan's, "Roaring Richard", wrote a [[book]], called ''[[Seven Faces of Icarus]]'', in which he details his conversations with the illiterate local cunning-man, Red William. Only a year or two after Richard wrote this book, John Tregonwell, after being appointed to investigate the Abbey, was so appalled by the debaucheries of the monks of St Brandan's that he recommended the monastery's immediate dissolution. ===Baronial Period=== This era began when The Bronze King, "Old Coppernose", King Henry VIII, dissolved St Brandan's monastery in 1536, exiled the brethren and granted Brancrug Isle to [[Hendrik Dewulf]], a Guelders mercenary and one of John Tregonwell's captains. The grant came with the title of Baron, and rights sicut regale - "like a king", the quasi-independence traditionally accorded to Marcher Lords. The first Baron Brancrug, Hendrik Dewulf, expanded the House accordingly. The [[Practic Garden]] became the favourite place of the martial, quarrelsome Dewulfs. The [[Violet Chamber]] was reserved for the lady of the House, and all Dewulfs were born there (except for [[Walter Dewulf]], who is said to have been born in a cow-byre outside Kerisham). In 1549, the Prayer Book Rebellion was in full swing. Hendrik Dewulf used [[Stores|a room as a prison cell]] for unfortunate locals, including the rebel ringleader, Red William, who had boasted of a curse he had placed on the Dewulf family line. It is believed that, after an exchange between them, Red William was gelded and thrown in the darkness of the caves below the House. Another version suggests that Red William was an initiate of the Thunderskin, secretly maintained by Hendrik to prophecy for him "in the ancient manner". [[Thomas Dewulf]], second Baron Brancrug, a talented astronomer and [[Ouranoscopy|ouranoscopist]], was nicknamed "Baron Silence of Castle Silence" for his taciturn severity, which is likely the origin of the name "Hush House". He had the [[Watchman's Tower: Observatory|Observatory]] constructed in 1576, just in time to witness the Great Comet in 1577. The [[Severn Chamber]] was reserved for the heir of the House, although it was originally furnished for Hafren Waters - a pale woman from Bristol of "uncertain lineage". Giles Dewulf, Thomas's son, ran away with her, but he later reconciled with his father, Thomas. She was [[Walter Dewulf|Walter Dewulf's]] mother and bequeathed her unusual pale eyes and hair to him and his descendants. Walter Dewulf transformed Hush House "from a draughty castle, to a stately home" with the assistance of Gregory Wheelock, a master mason and architect. He built the [[Grand Ascent - Ground Floor|Winding Stair]] and the guest chambers, as well as a more ambitious and dangerous project, opening a forbidden way to something he calls the "Moon-Hall", where - he insists, the Horned-Axe is still an Edge-power and his account becomes increasingly erratic. Later, [[Ambrose Westcott]] would remark on it in ''[[The Temptations of Architecture]]''. Hush House remained in [[Dewulf Family|his family]]'s hands until the tragic death of [[Eva Dewulf]], seventh of the line, and her twin grandchildren, sometime after 1759 (when her son, Sebastian is drowned in Quiberon Bay in battle against the French, aboard the [[HMS Kerisham|HMS ''Kerisham'']]). The estate was abandoned and the caves below became [[Smuggler's Den|a smuggler's haunt]]. ===Curia Period=== In 1785, a secretive cabal of adepts and scholars of note acquired the deed to the Dewulf estate and established the "Curia of the Isle" to manage Hush House, which became a haven of knowledge. The first Librarian was [[Ambrose Westcott]]. He had [[Librarian's Quarters|a cosy nook]] constructed for himself on the seaward side, above the north wing, to fit his preferences. The Curia used to issue gloves and slippers of soft leather to protect the books and premises. Visitors were often asked to remove their shoes. They were permitted no further than the [[Reading Room]], and in the days when Librarians commanded the services of the Fine-Takers, they were sometimes even left unsupervised. The whole Curia used to meet in the [[Refectory]], including the Librarian, and the Secretaries Salvant, Vigilant and Enigmatic - sometimes even the Secretary Nunciant, though he was often away from the House, due to the duties of that office. There has only ever been one Secretary Persistent, and she never liked to eat in company. In later years, the Governor of the Gaol would sit at one end, the Librarian at the other, with long periods of silence between words. In the 19th century, a ball room was converted into a [[Duelling Hall]] by the fifth Librarian, [[Natalia Brulleau]]. After she retired in 1861, the Curia found itself short on promising candidates, until the arrival of [[Willem Harries]], a former Dutch Lutheran priest. He won the position of sixth Librarian by presenting the Curia with "a key long lost", opening the way to exploring the House's [[Hidden Stair|deeper, forgotten parts]]. The [[Fludd Gallery]] was extended, decorated with semi-precious metals and filled with the finest art money could buy by [[Thirza Blake]], seventh Librarian. ===Nocturnal Period=== The Nocturnal period began at the turn of the century in 1896 when, in order to cover Hush House's considerable debts accrued under [[Thirza Blake]], the Curia of the Isle agreed to submit to yearly inspections by Nocturnal Branch and surrender a portion of the Isle for the construction of a prison. It came to be known as The Cucurbit, led by Governor George Collers. Much of the art in the Fludd Gallery had to be sold off. After Nocturnal Branch was restructured into the Suppression Bureau in 1901, an old [[Boathouse]] was used by their officials as an unofficial means to come and go. In the days of the brethren, the [[Windlit Gallery]] would ring with the Liturgy of the Hours every day. In the times of the Dewulfs and of the Curia, there were services there every Sunday. All those times were long gone. In 1903, [[Oubliette Containment|"a suppressive mechanism"]] was constructed beneath Brancrug Gaol, with the intent of holding a being of great power. At this time, [[Sir David Greene]], eighth Librarian, former superintendent of Nocturnal Branch, was cooperating closely with the Suppression Bureau and was the public face of that cooperation. In private, he found this development increasingly irresponsible and deeply concerning. Relations between the Curia of the Isle and the Suppression Bureau were badly strained after 1918, leading [[Dr Serena Blackwood]], who was the tenth Librarian at the time, to seek allies against Governor George Collers. After the Great War, Christopher Illopoly (poet, painter, archivist, ruiner of seances) was possibly one of those allies. After recuperating in the [[Infirmary]], along with Zachary Wakefield and Harvey Hattington, he was housed in the [[Motley Tower: Illopoly's Nook|Motley Tower]] for some time, ostensibly so he could help with the collection. The Nocturnal period ended in 1929 when Hush House was abandoned after an alleged fire.
