The Sweet Bones.title: The Sweet Bones
The Sweet Bones.text:
{{BoH Room |image1=[[File:The Sweet Bones.png]] |required_aspects= *Either [[Assistance]],
a [[Shilling]], [[Mettle]], [[Chor]]
or [[Shapt]] *Forbidden - [[Reluctant]]}} {{Location |location=[[Brancrug Village]] |inhabitants=Silent landlady}} {{Quote|The 'Sweet Bones' has been the public house in Brancrug since Cromwell's time. Its history is notable; its beer is not. Guests looking for discreet employment, or for discreet assistance, congregate in the snug.}}{{Tocright}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a location in [[Brancrug Village]], available after unlocking the village at the [[The Beginning|Beginning of the game]]. It is home to everyone looking for a good time, hosted by a silent landlady. It has various uses: *The [[Journals|Journal]] can be dried here. *[[Elements of the Soul]] can be used: **To gain [[Memory|Memories]] or [[Pence]] - either Sixpence, or Twopence (or a [[Tally|Silver Spintria]] in [[Numa]]). **To restore Fatigued Soul cards for Twopence (or for free during Numa, plus a [[Memory]], at the cost of a [[Elements of the Soul#Maladies|Malady]]). **To dry out a [[Soaked]] [[Basket of Damp Towels]] for free. **To hire [[Assistance#Unusual Helpers|Unusual helpers]] to help with restoring [[Hush House]] for a Florin. *[[Pence]] can be used without a Soul card: **To hire less skilled [[Assistance#Seasonal Workers|Seasonal workers]] for a Shilling. **To clean a [[Soiled]] [[Basket of Dirty Laundry]] for a Shilling. ==The Sweet Bones [Locked]== {{Quote|After the Restoration of 1930, the New King's agents came looking for his enemies in these parts... and they weren't gentle about it. Since those days, the locals are suspicious of foreigners. No-one in the Sweet Bones will talk to me.

A Sea of Hostile Faces
Diplomacy? Or bribery?}}
Before unlocking, it has the same name and requires either [[Assistance]], a [[Shilling]], [[Mettle]], [[Chor]] or [[Shapt]] to access. When unlocked, the Librarian receives a [[Memory: Solace]]. == Rest and Refreshment == {{Quote|
It is Spring; and the landlady has served me a slice of her starygazy pie, with the pilchard-heads poking cheekily through the hot crust.

It is Summer; I am sitting on the bench outside the Sweet Bones, eating crumbly cheese in nettle wrappings and good black rye bread, soaking up the sun.

It is Autumn when the leaves rustle. The silent landlady has served me apple pie with steamed cream in the window-nook.

It is Winter and the storms have tightened the seas. I am sitting before the fire in the Sweet Bones with a beef and potato pasty in one hand, and a hot ale posset in the other.}}
Using a fatigued [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]] will restore the Soul card in 60 seconds if Twopence is added during the countdown. Twopence can also be used alongside the fatigued element before the countdown starts, but putting in a shilling or greater will hire a Seasonal Worker instead of restoring the Soul card. Therefore, put bigger denomination only after you already started the Rest action. Note that paying with any coin or note other than an exact Twopence is the simplest way to obtain a [[Pence|Penny]] (due to how the change is calculated) for easy Memory generation. If attempting to rest a fatigued Soul card during [[Numa]], it will receive a [[Elements of the Soul#Maladies|Malady]] and the Librarian will draw a single Memory from the following: *[[Memory: Contradiction]] *[[Hive's Lament]] *[[Old Moment]] *[[Curious Hunch]] *[[Confounding Parable]] *[[Old Wound]] *[[Wild Surmise]] *[[Horizon-Sight]] This can either be avoided by using [[Mettle]] (which does not get maladied), or to purposefully inflict a Malady upon an Element of choice (as maladied cards do not get fatigued, and can be used repeatedly). The action takes 70 seconds. ==Work== Soul cards can be used to conduct odd jobs at the pub for money or [[Memory|Memories]]. The Soul card is fatigued. {| class="article-table" !Element of the Soul !Job !Reward !Start Quote !End Quote |- |style=white-space:nowrap|[[Chor]] or [[Health]] |Manual Labour |rowspan=3|Sixpence |rowspan=2|''There's not much work on offer in Brancrug, but I can find sixpence worth of odd jobs.'' |rowspan=2|''As they used to say in my youth, 'The day is done, and so am I; but I've earned my pay.''' |- |style=white-space:nowrap|[[Mettle]] or [[Shapt]] |Fixing and Mending |- |style=white-space:nowrap|[[Phost]] or [[Wist]] |Help with Letters |''I could offer help with correspondence and arithmetic. There's no school in Brancrug, and not everyone here knows their letters.'' |''An afternoon spent profitably, reading newspapers to the curious, writing affectionate letters for the lonely, steering farmers through the requirements of the Ministry of Agriculture.'' |- |style=white-space:nowrap|[[Fet]] or [[Trist]] |Fortune-Telling |Twopence |''I've garnered enough mystique to tell fortunes for pennies. Undignified, perhaps, for the Librarian of Hush House, but times are hard.'' |''The fortunes I tell may be true, and they may be real. The money, at least, is real.'' |- |style=white-space:nowrap|[[Ereb]] |A Little Respect |Memory |''I am the Librarian of Hush House. I will question the villagers of Brancrug, and I will add whatever they tell me to my store of knowledge.'' |''I've learnt something. Something useful? Too early to tell.'' |} Placing [[Ereb]] creates the "A little respect" action, which supplies certain [[Memory|Memories]] as reward: {{#lst:Decks|d.chat.sweetbones}} Using a Soul card at the Sweet Bones during Numa will provide a [[Tally|Silver Spintria]], but afflict the Soul with a Malady, unless Mettle was provided. This action will take a full day (6 minutes). {{quote|
The inn is crowded with Numa's heralds and pilgrims. They will be gone by morning. Until then, I could offer my services for payment. I might regret it.

Afterwards I don't remember what work I performed, except in scents and sensations - leaf-mould, a rhythmic musical clicking like melodious castanets, soft blue flame like antique gaslight. And cold; I remember that where we went, it was cold.}} ==Seek Assistance== Villagers can be employed from the Sweet Bones for use in clearing the Library. Villagers are a type of [[Assistance]]. ===Seasonal Workers=== Can be sought by offering at least a [[Pence|Shilling]] (12p) in the "Mine" slot with ''no'' [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]] card. Seasonal workers do not have any unique collaborations. This action takes 5 seconds. {| class="article-table" !Season !Assistant !colspan=2|Principles !Quote |- |Spring |[[The Miner]] |{{Lore|Forge}}
{{Lore|Moon}}
{{Lore|Scale}} |1
1
2 |''In spring, the local miners often travel to the Feast of Lights Below. If one breaks his journey at the Sweet Bones, a shilling will buy his labour for a day.'' |- |Summer |[[The Barber]] |{{Lore|Moth}}
{{Lore|Rose}} |2
1 |''In summer, the barber comes by to keep the villagers kempt. A shilling will buy his services.'' |- |Autumn |[[The Orchard-Keeper]] |{{Lore|Heart}}
{{Lore|Nectar}} |1
2 |''In autumn, the orchard-keepers come to sell their wares at Brancrug. A shilling will buy one's help.'' |- |Winter |[[The Fisherman]] |{{Lore|Moon}}
{{Lore|Sky}} |2
1 |''In winter when the storms close the seas, the fishermen will offer their services for a shilling a day.'' |} ===Unusual Helpers=== {{Quote|What visitors might be passing through?}} Can be found by using an [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]] with any amount of Pence (the initial currency offering is not consumed). [[Talk]] can then be used to hire them for a Florin (24p). This action takes 60 seconds and a further 5 seconds if you choose to hire them. Unusual helpers always have three [[Principles]], each with a power of 4. Like Villagers, they are a type of [[Assistance]]. Post Office.title: Post Office
Post Office.text:
{{BoH Room |image1=[[File:Post_Office.png]] |required_aspects= *[[Readable]] or [[Journal]] *Forbidden -
[[Soaked]] or [[Reluctant]]}} {{Location |location=[[Brancrug Village]] |inhabitants=The Postmistress}} {{Quote|The Postmistress keeps the gate to the wider world. In her left hand is the lightning (which is to say, the telegraph) and in her right, the thunder (which is to say, the only telephone in Brancrug). Before her lies the cash-register, which accepteth the greater currency and returneth its lesser children.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a location in [[Brancrug Village]], available after unlocking the village at the [[The Beginning|start of the game]]. It is home to the Postmistress. After drying out their [[Journals|Journal]], the Librarian can show it to the Postmistress, who will present them with [[A Letter to the Librarian]] and a [[Ten Shilling Note]]. The Postmistress can perform various services: *If given [[Pence]] of sufficently high denomination, she can break them up into various lower coins or notes. *If given [[Tally]], it can be exchanged for Pence. The higher the denomination of the Spintria, the better the exchange rate. *If given a letter or an [[Ordering|Order Form]] that is [[Ready to Post]], she will send it in exchange for a Penny for postage. *If given a [[Petition for a Labyrinth Season]], she can send the letter in exchange for a Tin Spintria, ensuring the next [[Season]] will be [[Numa]]. ==The Post Office [Locked]== {{Quote|The postmistress may have something for me - once I know what to ask for.

Post Office Counter
A place of power, a place of knowledge, beneath the sheltering hand of his Majesty the King.}}
Before unlocking, it is called "The Post Office [Locked]" and requires a [[Readable]] or [[Journals|Journal]] that isn't [[Soaked]] to access. [[Category:Locations]]

St Brandan's Cove.title: St Brandan's Cove
St Brandan's Cove.text:
{{Location |title=St Brandan’s Cove |image=[[File:St Brandan’s Cove.png]] |location=[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornwall Cornwall, England]}} {{Quote|Here the sea ends and the world begins (or the other way around). After storms, the fishermen of Brancrug Village find oddities washed up here.}} __NOTOC__
'''St Brandan’s Cove''' is a beach near [[Brancrug Village]] and [[Crowcross Sands]]. This is where the [[Librarians|Librarian]] starts the game, washed up on the shore [[The Beginning|after a storm]]. After choosing the starting [[Elements of the Soul]], the Librarian can call for help and gain the (reluctant) [[Assistance]] of a [[The Fisherman|Fisherman]] to lead them to the village and safety. [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Out of Bounds]]

Severn Chamber.title: Severn Chamber
Severn Chamber.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Severn Chamber.png]] |era=[[Curia Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Moon|5}} or {{Lore|Rose|5}} |workstations=*[[Guest Bed: Severn Chamber|Guest Bed:
Severn Chamber]] *[[Thirza's Phonograph]]}} {{Quote|In the days of the Dewulfs, this chamber was reserved for the heir of the House - though it was originally furnished for Hafren, the woman of 'uncertain lineage' who became Baron Walter's mother and bequeathed her unusual pale eyes and hair to Walter and his descendants.}} __NOTOC__
The '''Severn Chamber''' is a room in [[Hush House]], which is unlocked early into the midgame. ==Abandoned Bedroom (Locked)== {{Quote|A crooning whisper haunts this room. It must once have been luxurious, and will be again once I have it restored, but I will need help to lay the restless presence that drifts here.}} Before unlocking, the room is called "Abandoned Bedroom" and requires {{Lore|Moon|5}} or {{Lore|Rose|5}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening the Severn Chamber will expose the [[Violet Chamber]]. ==Workstations== *[[Guest Bed: Severn Chamber]] ({{Lore|Grail}}, {{Lore|Moon}}, {{Lore|Rose}}, {{Lore|Heart}}) - Can be camped in and accept visitors with an interest in {{Lore|Grail}}. *[[Thirza's Phonograph]] ({{Lore|Knock}}, {{Lore|Moon}}, {{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Sky}}) ==Contents== ===Books=== *[[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Baronial]]) *[[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Curia]]) (x2) ===Ink=== *[[Ashartine]] ===Beverage=== *[[Veiled Goddess Lapsang Souchong]] (Cup) ===Lights=== *[[Moth-Orchid-Scented Candle]] *[[Bedside Candleholder]] *[[Fringed Lamp]] (x2) ===Thing=== *''[['Abduction, Salvation']]'' ===Comfort=== *[[Nighted Chair]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Curia]]

Scent Garden.title: Scent Garden
Scent Garden.text:
{{BoH_Room |era=[[Solar Gothic Period]] |required_aspects=* [[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Grail|4}} or {{Lore|Nectar|4}} |workstations=*Garden x2
(Moth Orchid,
Honeyscar Jasmine) *Garden x2
(Fragrant Chalice,
Lenten Rose, Moly) *Garden x2
(Agave Aeterna) |image1=[[Scent garden.png]]}} {{Quote|This too dates from the time of the Abbey... but in summer, neither sisters nor brothers were permitted to spend more than a single hour here, lest the 'temptation of savours' overwhelm them.}} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]], which can be unlocked early on. ==Tangle of Thorns (Locked)== {{Quote|A flower garden, now overrun with thorned weeds and briar rose.}} Prior to unlocking, the room is called "Tangle of Thorns" and requires {{Lore|Grail|4}} or {{Lore|Nectar|4}} [[Assistants|Assistance]] to access.
Opening it exposes the [[Servants' Hall]]. ==Gardens== There are six gardens to gather from in the Scent Garden, with three variations and varying [[Flower]]s depending on the [[Season]].
In [[Numa]], gathering [[Agave Aeterna]] will harvest two instead of one. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Garden !! Spring !! Summer !! Autumn !! Winter !! Numa |- | ''Fragrant chalice in summer and autumn, lenten rose in winter.
Rarer plants might flourish in Numa.'' || [[Lenten Rose]] || [[Fragrant Chalice]] || [[Fragrant Chalice]] || [[Lenten Rose]] ||| [[Moly]] |- | ''Moth orchids in spring and summer, honeyscar jasmine in autumn.'' || [[Moth Orchid]] || [[Moth Orchid]] || [[Honeyscar Jasmine]] ||| - || [[Honeyscar Jasmine]] |- | ''The 'history plant', agave aeterna, flowers here in summer.'' ||| - || [[Agave Aeterna]] ||| - ||| - || [[Agave Aeterna]] (x2) |} ==Contents== *[[Skinshuck Mead]] *[[Hurricane Lamp]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Gardens]] [[Category:Gathering]] [[Category:Solar Gothic Period]] [[Category:Open Air]]

The Rectory.title: The Rectory
The Rectory.text:
{{BoH Room |image1=[[File:The Old Rectory.png]] |required_aspects= *[[An Introduction]] or
[[An Old Friend's Address]] *{{Lore|Knock}}, {{Lore|Lantern}} or {{Lore|Sky}}}} {{Location |location=[[Brancrug Village]] |inhabitants=[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]],
Terrence}} {{Quote|Reverend Timothy's words always run ahead of him, but his thoughts always catch up.

Reverend Timothy is always pleased to see you.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a location in [[Brancrug Village]], available after unlocking the village at the [[The Beginning|start of the game]]. It is home to [[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] and his housekeeper, Terrence. Reverend Timothy can be [[Assistance|hired]] by using an [[Element of the Soul]] with {{Lore|Knock}} or {{Lore|Lantern}}. If the location was unlocked with [[An Old Friend's Address]], he can be hired for free. Otherwise, his services will cost a [[Shilling]]. ==The Rectory [Locked]== {{Quote|Reverend Timothy is a hospitable soul, but Terrence, his housekeeper, guards her employer fiercely. She doesn't want his innocent theological enthusiasms getting him in trouble with the New King's men.
[You need an Introduction, or a mutual acquaintance marked with Lantern, Knock, or Sky - perhaps someone who shares his interests in theology or poetry.]}}
Before unlocking, it has the same name and requires a {{Lore|Knock}}, {{Lore|Lantern}} or {{Lore|Sky}} [[An Introduction|Introduction]] to access. If [[An Old Friend's Address]] is used, it must be a specific one. [[Category:Locations]]

Practic Garden.title: Practic Garden
Practic Garden.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Practic garden.png |era=[[Solar Gothic Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Edge|4}} or {{Lore|Nectar|4}} |workstations=*[[Practic Garden Dummy]] *[[Garden]] (x2)}} {{Quote|In the early days of St Brandan's Abbey, the brothers practiced the arts of war here. So it was that in Baronial times the garden became a favourite of the martial, quarrelsome Dewulfs.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Walled Garden (Locked)== {{Quote|Iron spikes march along the top of the wall. The gate is rusted shut, but what I can see through the bars is as ruinous as I might expect.}} Before unlocking, it is called "Walled Garden" and requires {{Lore|Edge|4}} or {{Lore|Nectar|4}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose: *[[Scent Garden]] ==Workstations== *[[Practic Garden Dummy]] ({{Lore|Edge}}, {{Lore|Scale}}, {{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Winter}}) - Can [[Evolve via Illumination]]. *Garden (x2) - Can be harvested with [[Chor]] or [[Health]] and a {{Lore|Nectar}} [[Skill]]. == Gathering == The fruit trees' yields are dependent on the [[Season]], they can be harvested during Summer and Autumn for [[Bowl of Sea-Blest Pears]] or [[Numa]] for [[Pyrus Auricalcinus]]. [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Gardens]] [[Category:Gathering]] [[Category:Solar Gothic Period]] [[Category:Open Air]]

St Brandan's Cloister.title: St Brandan's Cloister
St Brandan's Cloister.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=St Brandan's Cloister.png |era=[[Solar Gothic Period]] |required_aspects=* [[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Lantern|2}} or {{Lore|Nectar|2}} |workstations=*[[Garden]] (x2)
([[Sea Holly]], [[Blue Crown]])}} {{Quote|The sisters and brothers of the Abbey built these gardens in the thirteenth century - at the height of the period we now call Solar Gothic. Walk here a while and breathe the peace they left.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Cloistered Garden (Locked)== {{Quote|I can make out a green and shaded space, but it's choked with weeds and thorns. I'll need help to clear the space.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Cloistered Garden" and requires {{Lore|Lantern|2}} or {{Lore|Nectar|2}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it exposes [[Long Tower: Solomon's Study]], [[Practic Garden]] and the [[Entrance Hall]]. ==Workstations== This room contains two [[Gathering|flower bushes]], which yield either [[Blue Crown]] or [[Sea Holly]], depending on the season. {| class="fandom-table" style="text-align:center" ! Spring !! Summer !! Fall !! Winter !! Numa |- | Blue Crownnote that the Workstation description mentions only Summer and Winter explicitly|| Sea Holly || Sea Holly|| Blue Crown || Sea Holly |}
[[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Gardens]] [[Category:Gathering]] [[Category:Open Air]] [[Category:Solar Gothic Period]]

Radiant Stair.title: Radiant Stair
Radiant Stair.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Radiant Stair.png]] |era=[[Solar Gothic Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Edge|6}}, {{Lore|Forge|6}},
{{Lore|Knock|6}} or {{Lore|Lantern|6}} |workstations=*[[Shrine: the Watchman]]}} {{Quote|The Watchman's shrine here is decorated with the Eye Elagabaline - a controversial variant of the Watchman's Eye. The Elagabaline rites have always had a shaky doctrinal status. It would not often have been seen, of course. These stairs were reserved for the choir monks who sang the liturgy of the Hours, the only ones permitted to enter the Chancel. Still, it is a little surprising that the Eye was allowed to remain, when the monastery was dissolved and the Isle given to the Dewulfs.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Shrouded Stair (Locked)== {{Quote|This has long been a holy place, but the Meniscate has withdrawn her favour now. Someone has shattered a mirror on the floor. The shards wink from the gloom - something half-seen flits from shard to shard, avoiding my gaze, unseen no matter how quickly I turn my head. Only once it's pacified will I be able to pass safely.}}
Before unlocking, it is called the "Shrouded Stair" and requires {{Lore|Edge|6}}, {{Lore|Forge|6}}, {{Lore|Knock|6}} or {{Lore|Lantern|6}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose the [[Windlit Gallery]]. ==Workstations== *[[Shrine: the Watchman]] ({{Lore|Rose}}, {{Lore|Sky}}, {{Lore|Lantern}}) - Can [[Evolve via Illumination]]. == Contents == *[[Beeswax Candle]] (x3) [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Solar Gothic Period]]

Windlit Gallery.title: Windlit Gallery
Windlit Gallery.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Windlit Gallery.png]] |era=[[Solar Gothic Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Forge|8}}, {{Lore|Lantern|8}}
or {{Lore|Sky|8}} |workstations=* [[Windlit Workbench]] * [[Instrument: Hunter's Harp|Instrument:
Hunter's Harp]]}} {{Quote|In the days of the brethren, every day this gallery would ring with the Liturgy of the Hours. In the times of the Dewulfs and of the Curia, there were services here every Sunday. All those times are long gone. This is a house of echoes now.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Wind-Prowled Gallery (Locked)== {{Quote|This has long been a holy place, but the rites have gone too long unperformed. The windows are shattered and only the wind walks here now.}}
Before unlocking, it is called the "Wind-Prowled Gallery" and requires {{Lore|Forge|8}}, {{Lore|Lantern|8}} or {{Lore|Sky|8}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose: * [[Church Tower]] * [[Chapter House]] * [[Glorious Stair]] * [[Radiant Stair]] ==Workstations== * [[Windlit Workbench]] ({{Lore|Forge}}, {{Lore|Lantern}}, {{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Knock}}) * [[Instrument: Hunter's Harp]] ({{Lore|Sky}}, {{Lore|Scale}}) - Can [[Evolve via Nyctodromy]]. == Contents == {| width="45%" class="table" style="text-align: left;white-space: pre;" |- !Books !Materials |- |● [[Driftwood Fragment]] |- | |● [[Curious Seashell]] |- |● ''[['Gideon Dewulf']]'' |- |● [[Sol Invictis Symbol]] (x2) |- |● [[Eva's Locks]] !Comforts |- |● [[Carpenter's Stool]] |- | | |- | !Fixed in Place |- | |

Solarium.title: Solarium
Solarium.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Solarium.png]] |era=[[Solar Gothic Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Heart|10}}, {{Lore|Lantern|10}}
or {{Lore|Winter|10}}}} {{Quote|This room was once for the meditation of favoured visionaries. Here White Matilda prophesied the victory of the Iron King in the Wars of the Roads, much as it would occur three hundred years later. (She got his name wrong, though.) }} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Glaring Room (Locked)== {{Quote|This has long been a holy place, but now the Sun-in-Rags has withdrawn his peace from it, and the light here cannot be borne. In the day the sun's light dazzles, in the night the moon's light freezes. Only once a peace has been laid on the room will I be able to enter safely.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Glaring Room" and requires {{Lore|Heart|10}}, {{Lore|Lantern|10}} or {{Lore|Winter|10}} [[Assistance]] to access. == Contents == ===Books=== * [[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Solar]]) (x4) * [[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Dawn]]) (x2) ===Things=== * [[Awakened Feather]] * [[Bisclavret's Knot]] * [[Tall Candlestick]] (x2) * [[Potted Pink Orchid]] * [[Potted Snake Plant]] * [[Potted Bamboo]] * [[Ninewink Clock]] ===Bust=== * [['Willem Harries']] ===Wall Art=== * [[Sol Invictis Symbol]] ===Comforts=== * [[Paradise Palm]] * [[Restful Seat]] * [[Contemplative Seat]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Solar Gothic Period]]

Tower Clock.title: Tower Clock
Tower Clock.text:
{{BoH_Room |era=[[Solar Gothic Period]] |image1=[[File:Tower Clock.png]] |required_aspects=* [[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Forge|10}}, {{Lore|Sky|10}}
or {{Lore|Winter|10}} |workstations=[[Great Clock]]}} {{Quote|George Collers, governor of Brancrug Gaol, oversaw the design and installation of this great clock, with the reluctant help of the Librarian Serena Blackwood. She might have refused outright, had she known how he intended to reuse the horologist's techniques for his so-called 'condignator'.

An inscription on the greatest wheel reads 'STRIKE THE HOURS'. }} The '''Tower Clock''' is a room in [[Hush House]], which can be reached after unlocking the [[Church Tower]]. ==Stopped Clock (Locked)== {{Quote|With maniacal but methodical care, someone has disassembled the clock and scattered it round the room. Wheels and parts have been piled and leant on every surface. A W has been marked on the stairs in soot.}} Prior to unlocking, the room is called the "Stopped Clock" and requires {{Lore|Forge|10}}, {{Lore|Sky|10}} or {{Lore|Winter|10}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose the [[Bells]]. ==Workstations== *[[Great Clock]] ({{Lore|Forge}}, {{Lore|Knock}}, {{Lore|Sky}}, {{Lore|Winter}}) - Can [[Evolve via Horomachistry]]. ==Contents== *[[Umbrous Oil]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Solar Gothic Period]]

Spire.title: Spire
Spire.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Spire.png]] |era=[[Solar Gothic Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Lantern|12}}, {{Lore|Moth|12}}
or {{Lore|Sky|12}} |workstations=*[[Spire Prospect]]}} {{Quote|Here Hendrik Dewulf met in secret with King Henry - once the Bronze King, now 'Old Coppernose', for the Great Debasement had ended the supremacy of the Leashed Flame, and Henry's heirs were no more than human. There is a story that Hendrik's son Thomas listened from the rafters - that three times he heard Henry ask his father to break a certain promise in the matter of Caer Ys beyond the wave, and the third time, the father did not refuse the king. This, says the story, is why Thomas never liked to make a promise thereafter, for fear of breaking it.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Wyrd-Cursed Spire (Locked)== {{Quote|Seven years ago, someone pronounced a curse here, in the name of the Sun and its many selves. This place was not the curse's target, and nor was I, but its poison fills the air around me. I should not enter here until it's cleansed.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Wyrd-Cursed Spire" and requires {{Lore|Lantern|12}}, {{Lore|Moth|12}} or {{Lore|Sky|12}} [[Assistance]] to access. ==Workstations== *[[Spire Prospect]] ({{Lore|Moth}}, {{Lore|Sky}}) - Can [[Evolve via Hushery]]. == Contents == * [[Houndsgall]] * [[Evening Isles Coffee]] (Pot, Cup) * ''[['Brian Levinsen']]'' [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Solar Gothic Period]]

Watchman's Tower: Gatehouse.title: Watchman's Tower: Gatehouse
Watchman's Tower: Gatehouse.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Watchman's Tower gatehouse.png |era=[[Baronial Period]] |required_aspects=* [[Hush House Key]]}} {{Quote|Back in the eleventh century, Brian of Brittany built the Tower and its gate to protect St Brandan's Abbey - as Hush House was then known. Later, the Barons Dewulf strengthened the gate against their many enemies. But it's a long time now since Hush House was any kind of fortress... and by the time the scholars of the Curia took possession, this place had long been a comfortable waiting room for visitors to the House too minor to merit immediate attention.}} __NOTOC__
'''Watchman's Tower: Gatehouse''' is the first room in [[Hush House]] proper. ==The great gate of the House (Locked)== {{Quote|The walls of the House tower above me. I had been told that it was abandoned after a fire - but there is no sign of any such thing. The building will no doubt need restoration, but it's in better shape than I'd feared.

'BOOKS ARE THE MEMORY THAT DOES NOT DIE', reads the inscription above the gate.}}
Before unlocking, it is called "The great gate of the House" and requires the [[Hush House Key]] to access. Opening it will expose [[Watchman's Tower: First Floor]] and [[St Brandan's Cloister]]. ==Contents== ===Thing=== *[[Vase of Gorse]] *''[['Serena Blackwood']]'' ===Comfort=== *[[Expansive Chair]] (x2) *[[Lingering Repose]] *[[Treasury of Shelters]] ===Wall Art=== *[[Yeth-Hound Horns]] (x2) *[[Red Deer Antlers]] *''[['The Tattered Outlaw']]'' *''[['Raveline Summer']]'' [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Baronial]]

Watchman's Tower: First Floor.title: Watchman's Tower: First Floor
Watchman's Tower: First Floor.text:
{{BoH_Room |title1=Watchman's Tower:
First Floor |image1=File:Watchman's Tower- First Floor.png |era=[[Baronial Period]] |required_aspects=* [[Assistance]] * {{Lore|Forge|2}} or {{Lore|Lantern|2}} |workstations=*[[Desk: Eva]]}} {{Quote|The notorious Eva Dewulf, first and last Baroness Brancrug, liked this room. Because this side of the house carried fewest memories of her poor father Valentine? So she could eavesdrop on the conversations of visitors waiting below? Or just because of how the pale light slanted through the windows in the last days of winter?}}
__NOTOC__'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]], which gives the Librarian access to one of their first [[Workstations]] - [[Desk: Eva]],
as well as a number of useful objects. ==Gatehouse Stairs (Locked)== {{Quote|The stairs to the room above are blocked with debris, and the plaster is peeling from the walls.
I'll need help from the village to clear and restore the place.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Gatehouse Stairs" and requires {{Lore|Forge|2}} or {{Lore|Lantern|2}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose [[Watchman's Tower: Observatory]]. ==Workstations== *[[Desk: Eva]] ({{Lore|Edge}}, {{Lore|Grail}}, {{Lore|Moon}}, {{Lore|Winter}}) ==Contents== ===Books=== *[[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Curia]]) (x2) *[[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Baronial]]) (x3) ===Tool=== *[[Mirrorscope]] *[[Baron Silence's Astrolabe]] ===Thing=== *[[Yewgall Ink]] *[[Quire of Paper]] *''[['Walter Dewulf']]'' ===Comfort=== *[[Starstrewn Chair]] *[[Nightsky Chair]] ===Wall Art=== *''[['As Above, So Below']]'' {{Spoilers |caption=Hidden items |caption_element=h3 |content=

}} [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Baronial]]

Watchman's Tower: Observatory.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=watch tower observatory.png |era=[[Baronial Period]] |required_aspects=* [[Assistance]] * {{Lore|Grail|2}} or {{Lore|Sky|2}} |workstations=*[[Telescope]]}} {{Quote|Thomas Dewulf, second Baron Brancrug, who they called 'Baron Silence', built this observatory in 1576 - by happy coincidence, just in time to observe the passage of the Great Comet in 1577.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. It contains the first workstation that can be used to upgrade [[Elements of the Soul]]. == Watchman's Tower: Top Floor (Locked) == {{Quote|The ceiling bows worryingly under a damp patch. There must be a leak in the observatory. The Sun above knows what state it's in. I should seek help, and enter carefully.}} Before unlocking, it is called "Watchman's Tower: Top Floor" and requires {{Lore|Grail|2}} or {{Lore|Sky|2}} [[Assistance]] to access. ==Workstations== *[[Telescope]] ({{Lore|Forge}}, {{Lore|Moon}}, {{Lore|Rose}}, {{Lore|Sky}}). Can be used to [[Evolve via Horomachistry]]. == Contents == ===Books=== *[[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Baronial]]) (x4) ===Thing=== *[[Mist-Kissed Water]] (Glass) ===Comfort === *[[Kitty's Armchair]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Baronial]]

Violet Chamber.title: Violet Chamber
Violet Chamber.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Violet Chamber.png]] |era=[[Curia Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Knock|6}} or {{Lore|Scale|6}} |workstations=*[[Guest Bed: Violet Chamber|Guest Bed:
Violet Chamber]]}} {{Quote|In the days of the Dewulfs, this chamber was reserved for the lady of the House. Later, the Librarians Willem Harries and Gervinus van Lauren both preferred it to the Librarian's Quarters. Harries established a little shrine to St Agnes in the far corner, and there it remained for many years until van Lauren ordered it to be removed.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Serpent-Haunted Bedroom (Locked)== {{Quote|Bright-scaled, watchful snakes lie coiled on every surface. I think some of them might be real.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Serpent-Haunted Bedroom" and requires {{Lore|Knock|6}} or {{Lore|Scale|6}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose the [[Pale Chamber]]. ==Workstations== *[[Guest Bed: Violet Chamber]] ({{Lore|Grail}}, {{Lore|Moth}}, {{Lore|Knock}}, {{Lore|Heart}}) - Can be camped in, or used by [[Visitors]] with an interest in {{Lore|Knock}}. == Contents == ===Things=== * [[Strathcoyne Whisky]] (Bottle, Glass) * [[Watchful Candle]] * [[Bedside Candleholder]] ===Comforts=== * [[Violet Stool]] * [[Chair of Challenges]] * [[Chaise-Longue of Conclusions]] ===Wall Art=== * ''[['Mlle Matutine']]'' * ''[['The First Birth']]'' [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Curia]]

Silver Vault.title: Silver Vault
Silver Vault.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Silver Vault PNG.png]] |era=[[Curia Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Grail|14}} or {{Lore|Knock|14}}}} {{Quote|Did the Curia of the Isle construct this vault? They were not Long - most of them were not Long. So they were not the Obliviates, that society of unseen immortals bound by three oaths. But this vault does seem to reference the oath called the Silver Chain, which forbade men to lie with woman, or women with men: 'for what may come is not always the Crime of the Sky, yet that is a furious danger.'}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Sealed Vault (Locked)== {{Quote|A heavy marble door sealed with red wax; a triple lock chased with silver.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Sealed Vault" and requires {{Lore|Grail|14}} or {{Lore|Knock|14}} [[Assistance]] to access. == Contents == ===Readable=== * [[The Turquoise Hand]] * [[Shuritic Book of Suns]] * [[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Dawn]]) ===Cache=== * [[Royal Casket]] * [[Mottled Casket]] * [[Ambered Casket]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Curia]]

Rowenarium (Room).title: Rowenarium (Room)
Rowenarium (Room).text:
{{BoH_Room |title1=Rowenarium |image1=Rowenarium.png |era=[[Dawn Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Rose|13}} or {{Lore|Winter|13}} |workstations=[[Rowenarium (Workstation)|Rowenarium]]}} {{quote|Once there was a brother and sister who loved each other greatly. They resolved that they were one soul split into two bodies, and their greatest wish was to become one. They found the hidden isle where the Twins, the Sister-and-Witch, had arrived when they crossed the great ocean, and a sacred pool on which the moon shone only once a year. There they spoke with the Twins in dreams, and they learnt how they might become conjoined as one flesh, and immortal.


Now the brother's resolution failed him, and though he loved his sister, he could not choose to spend eternity joined in one flesh. The sister could not persuade him, and she would not abandon him or force him. So they used their arts to live long lives, close but separate, and they made a double foundation of monks and nuns, as chaste as they had always been, but each nun had her brother-twin and none could enter alone.

In time, the sister found her own immortality, and to this day she walks the world by moonlight. The brother died, and his bones are buried in the room beneath the well. But his children live on.}}
The '''Rowenarium''' is a room in [[Hush House]], which is unlocked in the late game. ==Crystallised Chamber (Locked)== {{quote|My path is blocked by shining surfaces like curdled light. Dark shapes shift beneath. We can tap away the crystal if we're careful. But we must, we must be careful.}} Prior to unlocking, the Rowenarium is called the "Crystallised Chamber" and requires {{Lore|Rose|13}} or {{Lore|Winter|13}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose the [[Silver Vault]]. ==Workstations== *[[Rowenarium (Workstation)|Rowenarium]] ({{Lore|Rose}}, {{Lore|Winter}}, {{Lore|Grail}}, {{Lore|Moth}}) - Can [[Evolve via Skolekosophy]]. {{Spoilers |caption=Spoilers |caption_element=h2 |content=Using the [[Hush House Key]] with the [[Rowenarium (Workstation)]] will reveal ''[[Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic: Second Edition]].'' }}
[[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Dawn]]

Sea-Caves.title: Sea-Caves
Sea-Caves.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Sea-Caves.png |era=[[Dawn Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Circumstance]] *{{Lore|Moon|3}} or {{Lore|Scale|3}} |workstations=*[[The Sea-Caves]]}} {{Quote|The Curia's last secret. Right under Governor Collers' nose, Levinsen, Blackwood and van Lauren all continued their careful investigations of the Brancrug sea-caves. Many of the species here are unknown to Cornwall. Some have not been seen anywhere under this Sun.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' are located in the depths below [[Hush House]]. ==Submerged Sea-Caves (Locked)== {{Quote|The sea has claimed these caves. The tide thunders below. I'll need to find some way to lower the water level before I can enter.}} Before unlocking, they are called the "Submerged Sea-Caves" and require a [[Circumstance]] ([[Uncovered Depths]]) with {{Lore|Moon|3}} or {{Lore|Scale|3}} to access. Opening them will expose the [[Deeplight Caves]]. ==Gathering== * [[The Sea-Caves]] ({{Lore|Moon}}, {{Lore|Scale}}) [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Dawn]]

Smuggler's Den.title: Smuggler's Den
Smuggler's Den.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Smuggler's Den.png |era=[[Baronial Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Forge|12}} or {{Lore|Grail|12}}}} {{Quote|In the last years of the eighteenth century, the Dewulf line ended and the estate lay empty. Enterprising smugglers spread rumours of the ghosts that walked the Isle, and quietly brought their tea, brandy and tobacco in through the old mines on the seaward side of the Isle. But the remnants here are much newer than the eighteenth century. Perhaps even after the Curia took possession, they permitted the smugglers to use this place. Ambrose Westcott did love his baccy so. Perhaps even the Suppression Bureau found the smugglers useful enough to turn a blind eye. }} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Wing-Haunted Cave (Locked)== {{Quote|A drunken whirl of bats drives me back! Perhaps literally drunken. There's a faint but definite brandy smell.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Wing-Haunted Cave" and requires {{Lore|Forge|12}} or {{Lore|Grail|12}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose: *[[Hermit Cell]] *[[Our Lady Beneath]] == Contents == ===Cache=== * [[Crate of Supplies]] * [[Forsaken Packages]] ===Light=== * [[Hurricane Lamp]] * [[Bottled Candle]] ===Beverages=== * [[Dandelion Wine]] * [[Lambig Broceliande]] (Bottle) * [[Schloss Jannings]] (Bottle x2) * [[Domaine Raveline]] (Bottle x2) [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Baronial]]

Shrine to St Tentreto.title: Shrine to St Tentreto
Shrine to St Tentreto.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Shrine to St Tentreto.png |era=[[Dawn Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Moth|15}} or {{Lore|Scale|15}} |workstations=*[[Altar: St Tentreto]]}} {{Quote|The Carapace Cross, the hybrid race who in their many kinds were winged, legged, eyed, bright, dark, scaled, feathered, chitinous... and us? The Cross are gone; the Cross were always History; but to their children, their enemies, they leave this hushed legacy.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room on the lowest level in the depths beneath [[Hush House]]. ==Pulsing Darkness (Locked)== {{Quote|If the Isle had a heart, we would hear its pulse.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Pulsing Darkness" and requires {{Lore|Moth|15}} or {{Lore|Scale|15}} [[Assistance]] to access. ==Workstations== * [[Altar: St Tentreto]] ({{Lore|Moon}}, {{Lore|Moth}}, {{Lore|Knock}}, {{Lore|Scale}} (optionally {{Lore|Heart}}, see the workstation page) - Can [[Evolve via Horomachistry]] and [[Evolve via Nyctodromy|Nyctodromy]]. {{Spoilers |caption=Spoilers |caption_element=h2 |content= The Librarian can use [[Preliminal Meter]] or [[Resurgences & Emergences]], an [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]] and any [[Ink]] with the [[Altar: St Tentreto]], in order to unveil ''[[The Writing on the Wall]]''.
"If I know what I'm doing - or perhaps acknowledge that I have no idea what I'm doing - I could curl up in the cold beneath the silent statue's shadow, and see what surfaces in sleep."
"I recall how in sleep I heard the changeling's carven churrings. I recall how in sleep I curled my fingers into the forms I found. I recall how in sleep I scratched the signs of secrets spoken to my other self. Here I hold them in my hands."
- Elucidate Enlightenment from an Earlier Era
}} ==Trivia== *Altar: St Tentreto is the only current [[Workstation]] with two evolution aspects. [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Dawn]]

Upper Pump Room.title: Upper Pump Room
Upper Pump Room.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Upper Pump Room.png |era=[[Dawn Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Forge|11}} or {{Lore|Scale|11}} |workstations=*[[Pumps: Upper Level]]}} {{Quote|See the pickaxe marks on the walls. Before the Sisterhood came to the Isle, the Romans or the Phoenicians dug these tunnels, scratching in the ground for tin and for gold. For centuries those pumps kept the sea at bay, driven by slaves or votaries who saw the sun one day in nine. When those pumps fell silent, the sea crept in - until, much later, the Curia brought in their own machines to open up the lower levels again.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Room of Rusts (Locked)== {{Quote|The ceiling has collapsed. Rusting machinery pokes out here and there through the rubble.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Room of Rusts" and requires {{Lore|Forge|11}} or {{Lore|Scale|11}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose: *[[Hall of Voices]] *[[Rowenarium]] *[[Lower Pump Room]] ==Workstations== * [[Pumps: Upper Level]] ({{Lore|Forge}}, {{Lore|Knock}}) - This [[Workstation]] is required to create a [[Circumstance]] ([[Receding Waters]]) to open up the [[Lower Pump Room]]. [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Dawn]]

Sacred Spring.title: Sacred Spring
Sacred Spring.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=Sacred Springs.png |era=[[Dawn Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Moon|10}} or {{Lore|Nectar|10}} |workstations=*[[Sacred Spring (Workstation)]]}} {{Quote|The Eye marked on the rocks here is not the Watchman's Eye that decorates the church above, but the Eye that marks the Temple of the Wheel in dreams. The priests of the Sun would tell you there was no sight before the rising of the Sun; but those who've drunk from this spring will dream of another sun, one that swung lower in the sky, one that would speak with us, one that would accept friendly gifts of blood from us.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Wheel-Filled Spring (Locked)== {{Quote|The pool here is filled with rusting and rotting wheels. Was this some attempt to block it? Or were the wheels thrown down the well above as offerings? In either case, it'll need to be cleaned out, and suitable offerings made to appease the powers to whom this place is holy.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Wheel-Filled Spring" and requires {{Lore|Moon|10}} or {{Lore|Nectar|10}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose: *[[Deep Well Descent]] *[[Narthex]] *[[Upper Pump Room]] ==Workstations== * [[Sacred Spring (Workstation)]] ({{Lore|Nectar}}, {{Lore|Grail}}, {{Lore|Moon}}) [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Dawn]]

Well.title: Well
Well.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Well.png]] |era=[[Dawn Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Moon|7}} or {{Lore|Nectar|7}} |workstations=*[[Hush House Well]]}} {{Quote|There's been a well here since the days of the Sisterhood, and superstitions have gathered around it like leaves in drifts. Its water has a healing virtue if drawn on a night of the new moon. It's ill luck to draw from it if you hear an owl. If you drip the blood of a living enemy into the well, they'll drown. And so on. Certainly, when Numa comes, the mists lie thick here.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. == Deserted Well (Locked)== {{Quote|The well is choked and filthy. It'll need to be purified inside and out.}}
Before unlocking, it is called the "Deserted Well" and requires {{Lore|Moon|7}} or {{Lore|Nectar|7}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose: *[[Kitchen Garden]] *[[Well Descent]] *[[Foundry]] ==Workstations== *[[Hush House Well]] ({{Lore|Heart}}) [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Dawn]] [[Category:Open Air]]

Servants' Hall.title: Servants' Hall
Servants' Hall.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Servants' Hall.png]] |era=[[Baronial Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Heart|5}} or {{Lore|Scale|5}} |workstations=*[[Loom]] *[[Instrument: Piano]] *[[Servants' Hall Fireplace]]}} {{Quote|Hendrik Dewulf, 1st Baron Brancrug, was granted Hush House after the dissolution of St Brandan's by 'Old Coppernose', King Henry VIII. In an act of unusual generosity for that tight-fisted King, the grant came with the title of Baron, and rights sicut regale - 'like a king', the quasi-independence traditionally accorded to Marcher Lords. Hendrik was clearly determined to live as befitted his new rank, and he expanded the house accordingly to support sufficient staff.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Ruinous Hall (Locked)== {{Quote|This place was bright and busy once. It can be again. But it'll be gruelling work to make it so - not suitable work for a Librarian.}} Before unlocking, it is called "Ruinous Hall" and requires {{Lore|Heart|5}} or {{Lore|Scale|5}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose the [[Kitchen]] and the [[Grand Ascent - Ground Floor]]. ==Workstations== *[[Loom]] ({{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Moth}}, {{Lore|Nectar}}, {{Lore|Rose}}) *[[Instrument: Piano]] ({{Lore|Sky}}, {{Lore|Moth}}) *[[Servants' Hall Fireplace]] == Contents == ===Cache=== * [[Slim Parcel]] * [[Contraband Flotsam]] ===Knife=== * [[Bronze Knife]] ===Sustenance=== * [[Misshapen Fruit]] ===Light=== * [[Moth-Orchid-Scented Candle]] * [[Widow's Candle]] (x2) ===Mark=== * [[Midnight Mark]] ===Fabric and Fibre=== * [[Warmly Coloured Yarns]] ===Things=== * [[Inscribed Clock]] * [[Pigeon Statuette]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Baronial]]

Reading Room.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=File:Reading room.png |era=[[Curia Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Lantern|5}} or {{Lore|Rose|5}} |workstations=*[[Desk: Reading Room]]}} {{Quote|Visitors were usually permitted this far into the House, and no further. In the days when the Librarians commanded the services of the Fine-Takers, visitors were sometimes even left unsupervised.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. == Dimly Lit Chamber (Locked)== {{Quote|Van Lauren's old protections hang heavy in the air here, clotting the air with shadows. I'll need counter-influences to unwind them.)}}
Before unlocking, it is called "Dimly Lit Chamber" and requires {{Lore|Lantern|5}} or {{Lore|Rose|5}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose: *[[Mazarine Room]] *[[Grand Ascent - Ground Floor]] ==Workstations== *[[Desk: Reading Room]] ({{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Lantern}}, {{Lore|Moon}}, {{Lore|Sky}}) == Contents == ===Books=== *[[Uncatalogued Book]]s: **[[Solar]] (x5) **[[Curia]] (x4) **[[Dawn]] (x3) **[[Baronial]] (x4) **[[Nocturnal]] (x3) ===Ink=== *[[Houndsgall]] ===Beverages=== *[[Veiled Goddess Lapsang Souchong]] (Pot, Cup) ===Light=== *[[Watchful Candle]] *[[Reading Lamp]] ===Blank=== *[[Quire of Paper]] ===Comforts=== *[[Moon Stool]] *[[Moon Footstool]] (x2) *[[Grand Reading Armchair]] *[[Imposing Reading Armchair]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Curia]]

Westcott Room.title: Westcott Room
Westcott Room.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=File:Westcott room.png |era=[[Curia Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Forge|5}} or {{Lore|Lantern|5}} |workstations=*[[Desk: Ambrose]] * [[Westcott Room Fireplace]]}} {{Quote|'By God, Sir, we shall have no Cigars in the Library, and we shall have no House without a Smoking-Room.'|Dr Ambrose Westcott (1734-1797)}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Smoking-Room (Locked)== {{Quote|A tarnished brass sign on the door clearly reads 'SMOKING-ROOM'. Rags of very old smoke sway restlessly, hazing the room beyond: what remains of the protections van Lauren once placed on it. (And yet, still, no sign of a fire.)}}
Before unlocking, it is called the "Smoking-Room" and requires {{Lore|Forge|5}} or {{Lore|Lantern|5}} [[Assistance]] to access. }} [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Curia]]

Refectory.title: Refectory
Refectory.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Refectory.png]] |era=[[Curia Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Grail|7}} or {{Lore|Nectar|7}} |workstations=[[Refectory Fireplace]]
[[Salon|A Salon in the Refectory]]}} {{Quote|Here, the whole Curia used to meet - the Librarian, and the Secretaries Salvant, Vigilant and Enigmatic. Sometimes even the Secretary Nunciant, though the duties of that office usually kept him away from the House. But there has only ever been one Secretary Persistent, and she has never liked to eat in company.

That was in the good times of the Curia's heyday. In later years, the Governor of the Gaol would sit at one end, the Librarian at the other, and the clock would tick away the long silences between their words.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Rose-Haunted Hall (Locked)== {{Quote|The room is rife with climbing roses, tangled in the lamps, sprawled across the table. The blossoms are a deep, deep red - one of those colours not often seen in waking life - and their perfume makes my head swim. Another of van Lauren's protections? Or something else? In any case, it'll be arduous, careful work to clear it.}}
Before unlocking, it is called the "Rose-Haunted Hall" and requires {{Lore|Grail|7}} or {{Lore|Nectar|7}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose the [[Stores]] and the [[Mazarine Room]]. ==Workstations== *[[Refectory Fireplace]] ==Salon== {{Main|Salon}} ''The room where once the Curia met: a fitting venue for a Salon. [Here one might serve Lunch in the afternoon, or Supper in the evening. A good host will provide at least one first course, one main course, one side dish, and one pudding.]'' The Refectory can be used to host a Luncheon or Supper for up to five guests. == Contents == ===Thing=== * [[Tall Candlestick]] (x2) * [[Vase of Lilies]] (x2) * [[Masquewatch Clock]] ===Wall Art=== *''[['Portrait of a Behatted Lady']]'' *''[['The Hatching']]'' * [[Night Mirror]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Curia]] [[Category:Salon]]

Servants' Quarters - South.title: Servants' Quarters - South
Servants' Quarters - South.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Servants' Quarters - South.png]] |era=[[Baronial Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Heart|8}} or {{Lore|Rose|8}} |workstations=*[[Guest Bed: Servant's Quarters|Guest Bed:
Servant's Quarters]] (x4)}} {{Quote|When Hendrik Dewulf left behind the life of a mercenary, he appointed his quartermaster as head of his new household. This would have drawn little comment, except that his quartermaster was a woman - the soft-spoken, steely-willed Ernestine Peterhans. For more than five decades, these rooms were her unchallenged domain. Even in her eightieth year, she still walked her rounds every day, and the servants would fall silent at the distant jingle of her keys.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Maze-Crazed Room (Locked)== {{Quote|Wires are strung tightly and crazily through this room, snaring the bed-legs to the window-latches, the window-latches to the wardrobe-handles. Every movement brings a ripple of musical pings. It'll need time and patience to unravel.}}
Before unlocking, it is called the "Maze-Crazed Room" and requires {{Lore|Heart|8}} or {{Lore|Rose|8}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose: *[[Servants' Quarters - North]] *[[Pantry]] *[[Well]] ==Workstations== *[[Guest Bed: Servant's Quarters]] ({{Lore|Forge}}, {{Lore|Nectar}}, {{Lore|Scale}}, {{Lore|Heart}}) (x4) - Can be camped in and accept visitors with an interest in {{Lore|Heart}}. == Contents == *[[Slim Parcel]] *[[Contraband Jetsam]] *[[Widow's Candle]] *[[Basket of Clean Linen]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Baronial]]

Servants' Quarters - North.title: Servants' Quarters - North
Servants' Quarters - North.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Servants' Quarters - North.png]] |era=[[Baronial Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Heart|8}} or {{Lore|Knock|8}} |workstations=*[[Guest Bed: Servant's Quarters|Guest Bed:
Servant's Quarters]] (x2)}} {{Quote|This was once the private chamber of the formidable Ernestine Peterhans, Seneschale of Brancrug. Baron Hendrik, and afterwards his son Thomas, would both descend the back stairs to visit her in person. For counsel, most said; for prayers, others insisted. Only the very foolish ever suggested there was any improper motive for their visits.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Wounded Room (Locked)== {{Quote|Blood drips from wet-edged cracks in the ceiling here, pooling on the floor. Another rage-fuelled presence that I could use help to lay.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Wounded Room" and requires {{Lore|Heart|8}} or {{Lore|Knock|8}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose: *[[Back Stairs]] *[[Kitchen Garden]] *[[Servants' Quarters - South]] ==Workstations== *[[Guest Bed: Servant's Quarters]] ({{Lore|Forge}}, {{Lore|Nectar}}, {{Lore|Scale}}, {{Lore|Heart}}) (x2) - Can be camped in and accept visitors with an interest in {{Lore|Heart}}. == Contents == ===Things=== * [[Uncatalogued Book]] ([[Baronial]]) * [[Investigator's Suitcase]] * [[Shadowless Silk]] * [[Bolt of Buttercup Linen]] * [[Shaving Mirror]] * [[Severe Chair]] ===Beverage=== * [[Dawnlion Coffee]] (Cup) * [[Isle-Water]] (Glass) ===Candle=== * [[Weighty Bedside Candleholder]] * [[Bedside Candleholder]] * [[Widow's Candle]] (x2) [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Baronial]]

Vestibulum Transitus.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Vestibulum Transitus.png]] |era=[[Baronial Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Ink]] *{{Lore|Heart|2}}, {{Lore|Knock|2}}, {{Lore|Lantern|2}}, {{Lore|Moon|2}}, {{Lore|Scale|2}}, {{Lore|Winter|2}}
or {{Lore|Edge|2}}}} {{Quote|'Vestibulum Transitus' was the wry name the Curia gave this structure. Before that it was 'Valentine's Bridge', the sheltered crossing beyond which Baron Valentine's solitude was assured.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Rattling Bridge (Locked)== {{Quote|Each time the wind makes its rounds, the whole bridge shakes. On its threshold, there's a serpentine knot-mark in browned blood. The mark is fading, but it still trembles with the power of the spirit that waits in it - a great servant of the old House, perhaps the last of the Fine-Takers themselves. I must pacify it with a suitable offering before I can pass.}}
Before unlocking, it is called the "Rattling Bridge" and requires an [[Ink]] with {{Lore|Heart|2}}, {{Lore|Knock|2}}, {{Lore|Lantern|2}}, {{Lore|Moon|2}}, {{Lore|Scale|2}}, {{Lore|Winter|2}}, or {{Lore|Edge|2}} to access. Stores.title: Stores
Stores.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Stores.png]] |era=[[Baronial Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Grail|8}}, {{Lore|Heart|8}}
or {{Lore|Moon|8}}}} {{Quote|At the time of the Prayer Book Rebellion, in 1549, Hendrik used this room as a prison cell for unfortunate locals - including the cunning-man and rebel ringleader, Red William, who had boasted of the curse he placed on Hendrik's heirs: 'There will be no seventh of his line.'

There is a story told in Brancrug Village that Hendrik came to speak with the imprisoned William in person. 'There will be no second of your line,' he told him - and had him gelded here in this very cell, and cast into the darkness of the caves below the House.

There is another story, that Eva Dewulf once answered an importunate suitor by bringing him here to this room and pointing out a stain upon the stones...}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Heart-Haunted Room (Locked)== {{Quote|The light in this room dims in pulses of sunset red, over and over, in a half-heard heartbeat that matches the crashing of the waves below. It'll need careful exorcism from someone attuned to these influences.}}
Before unlocking, it is called "Heart-Haunted Room" and requires {{Lore|Grail|8}}, {{Lore|Heart|8}} or {{Lore|Moon|8}} [[Assistance]] to access. Opening it will expose the [[Back Stairs]] and the [[Refectory]]. == Contents == {| width="65%" class="table" style="text-align: left;white-space: pre;" |- !width=250px|Cache !width=190px|Tool !width=320px|Beverage !Fuel |- |● [[Saw]] |● [[Kerosene]] |- |● [[Hurricane Lamp]] |● [[Paraffin]] |- |● [[Cucurbit Burette]] |● [[Scintillate Oil]] |- | | |● [[Eigengrau]] | |- |} {| width="65%" class="table" style="text-align: left;white-space: pre;" !width=250px|Thing !width=190px|Pigment !width=320px|Comfort |- |● [[Paint: Palest Blue]] |● [[Bolt of Moss-Green Velvet]] |● [[Wire (Steel)]] |● [[Basket of Towels]] |● [[Bottled Candle]] |● [[Glue]] |

It may be that the servants of the Dewulf family still came here in secret, even while they paid lip service to the rites of the Unconquered Sun.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Creeper-Crowded Descent (Locked)== {{Quote|Leaves, flowers, and thorns. Especially thorns. Could I clear them, I might find something beneath.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Creeper-Crowded Descent" and requires {{Lore|Moon|8}}, {{Lore|Nectar|8}} or {{Lore|Scale|8}} [[Assistance]] to access. {{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Wine Cellar.png]] |era=[[Baronial Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Grail|10}} or {{Lore|Moth|10}}}} {{Quote|Ricardo Milagro, traveller, rascal, Musgrave's gardener, managed a creditable wine from Brancrug grapes. Cornwall has never really been wine country, and the tradition was unevenly maintained, but the Curia of the Isle kept a good cellar.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Infested Wine-Cellar (Locked)== {{Quote|Something much bigger laired here. The walls and ceiling are smeared with its slimes. It's gone, but its children remain, wriggling in every shadow. We'll have to clear, lure or drive them out.}}

Stair Tenebrous.title: Stair Tenebrous
Stair Tenebrous.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Stair Tenebrous.png]] |era=[[Curia Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Memory]] without
the [[Weather]] Aspect *{{Lore|Heart|3}}, {{Lore|Lantern|3}}, {{Lore|Moon|3}}, {{Lore|Rose|3}}, {{Lore|Sky|3}}, {{Lore|Winter|3}} or {{Lore|Edge|3}}}} {{Quote|There were shadows here in the earth, long before the foundations of the House were laid. They retreated before the Romans' burrowings, they quailed before the sun-hymns of the brethren, they slunk away before the blades and pistols of the Barons Dewulf. Over all those centuries they shrank, until at last when the Curia of the Isle sunk this stair, they could recruit one as a watch-dog.}} __NOTOC__
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Shadowed Stair (Locked)== {{Quote|The shadow here is a sentinel. To enter it unprepared is to risk dissolution. I must bear a memory, like a torch in the dark.}}
Before unlocking, it is called the "Shadowed Stair" and requires a {{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Lantern}}, {{Lore|Moon}}, {{Lore|Rose}}, {{Lore|Sky}}, {{Lore|Winter}} or {{Lore|Edge}} [[Memory]] of 3 to access. It forbids the use of the [[Weather]] Aspect. The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a room in [[Hush House]]. ==Riddling Stair (Locked)== {{Quote|Half-seen faces mouth half-heard riddles. This is none of van Lauren's work - these defences are much older than the Curia. But the Curia found a way to answer these riddles, and so will we.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Riddling Stair" and requires {{Lore|Moon|12}} or {{Lore|Rose|12}} [[Assistance]] to access. Staff-Room.text:
{{BoH_Room |image1=[[File:Staff-Room.png]] |era=[[Nocturnal Period]] |required_aspects=*[[Assistance]] *{{Lore|Grail|11}} or {{Lore|Heart|11}} |workstations=*[[Staff-Room Stove]]}} {{Quote|The warders at Brancrug were a cut above your usual prison warder - former Bureau constables, repentant Know, turncoat Tragulari, veterans of the Légion du Seuil. When the end came, none of that mattered. But here, for a while, when the winter storms battered the walls, they hunkered close to this glowing stove to share tea and comradeship and stories of their very different lives.}} __NOTOC__

But much of the room remains untouched.}} Before unlocking, it is called the "Blackened Staff-Room" and requires {{Lore|Grail|11}} or {{Lore|Heart|11}} [[Assistance]] to access. The Smithy.title: The Smithy
The Smithy.text:
{{BoH Room |image1=[[File:The Smithy.png]] |required_aspects= *[[An Introduction]] or
[[An Old Friend's Address]] *{{Lore|Edge}}, {{Lore|Forge}} or {{Lore|Heart}} *Forbidden - [[Reluctant]]}} {{Location |location=[[Brancrug Village]] |inhabitants=[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]]}} {{Quote|Denzil Smith, strong as oak, blackened by smoke. He will never surpass his father, and he is no longer a soldier. But he still has his craft.

Denzil doesn't smile when he welcomes you in, but that's only because he's Denzil.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a location in [[Brancrug Village]], available after unlocking the village at the [[The Beginning|start of the game]]. It is home to [[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]]. Denzil can be [[Assistance|hired]] by using an [[Element of the Soul]] with {{Lore|Edge}}, {{Lore|Forge}} or {{Lore|Heart}}. If the location was unlocked with [[An Old Friend's Address]], he can be hired for free. Otherwise, his services will cost a [[Shilling]]. Denzil can also perform the Service of Division: if given a [[Tally|Spintria]] of value greater than Iron, he will split it into two Spintriae - one of which is Iron, and the other a level lower than what was given. As this is usually used for drawing [[Ductile|Wire]], the Librarian should manually collect the coins, as collecting them automatically will simply combine them once more. The action takes 10 seconds. ==The Smithy [Locked]== {{Quote|Denzil Smith has more work than he needs, and he rarely opens his door to strangers. [You need an Introduction, or a mutual acquaintance marked with Edge, Forge, or Heart - someone in a similar trade, or someone who can appeal to his secret passion for saffron cake.]}} Before unlocking, it has the same name and requires an {{Lore|Edge}}, {{Lore|Forge}} or {{Lore|Heart}} [[An Introduction|Introduction]] to access. If [[An Old Friend's Address]] is used, it must be a specific one. [[Category:Locations]]

The Rector.title: The Rector
The Rector.text:
{{PersonInfobox |title1=Reverend Timothy |image1=therector.png |aspects=[[Assistance]], [[An Introduction]] |fee=12p |principles={{Lore|Lantern|2}}, {{Lore|Knock|1}}}} {{quote|Reverend Timothy, Rector of Brancrug, ordained by the Church of the Unconquered Sun. A learned man, blessed in the Tally, the Gate, and the Light.}} __NOTOC__
'''Reverend Timothy''' is an inhabitant of [[Brancrug Village]], and the [[Librarians|Librarian's]] acquaintance if [[Phost]] is chosen in [[The Beginning]]. For a [[Pence#Denominations|Shilling]] (or free if he is your acquaintance), Reverend Timothy can be hired as an [[Assistants|Assistant]]. His [[Principles]] are {{Lore|Lantern|2}} and {{Lore|Knock|1}}. Unlike other Assistants, Reverend Timothy can make use of [[Candle]]s. In the ''[[House of Light]]'' DLC, he can be invited to a [[Salon]] once per [[Season]]. His card will remain in the Sundries tab until used for a Salon, but he can still be hired and used to unlock rooms as usual. ==Introduction== ===An Old Friend's Address=== {{quote|I first heard of Brancrug through its Rector, Reverend Timothy. For years now I've been exchanging letters with him. I can find shelter for tonight under his roof - once I've reached Brancrug Village. [The Rector can also introduce you to other villagers.]}}
If Reverend Timothy is the Librarian's acquaintance, he will provide shelter and warmth following the storm, and he will always offer his services for free. {{Quote|The door opens a few cautious inches. 'Who's there? I say, who's there?' [The storm-wind plucks at you, plucks at the door, shakes the trees around the house...]

The Reverend staggers back as if he'd received a blow, and then he's bombarding me with terrified, delighted questions before I'm even through the door.

''Timothy ushers me into the bright hall, casting about for his housekeeper, and asking questions the whole time. 'How did you come here? Was it the wreck? Terrence! Terrence, do fetch towels!'''

''Reverend Timothy flutters fussily while Terrence the Housekeeper busies herself with practicalities. She shows me to a warm room at the top of the house where a fire is already made up.''

''Reverend Timothy is touchingly excited to meet his correspondent in person. I am still too exhausted to hold up my end of the conversation, and Terrence is not a talkative woman, but the Reverend can talk for three. At last however he suddenly realises how exhausted I am, and lets me sleep.''}} ===The Rectory [Locked]=== {{quote|Reverend Timothy is a hospitable soul, but Terrence, his housekeeper, guards her employer fiercely. She doesn't want his innocent theological enthusiasms getting him in trouble with the New King's men.
[You need an Introduction, or a mutual acquaintance marked with Lantern, Knock, or Sky - perhaps someone who shares his interests in theology or poetry.]}} Unlocking [[The Rectory]] requires [[An Introduction]] with {{Lore|Lantern}}, {{Lore|Knock}}, or {{Lore|Sky}}. After unlocking the Rectory, the Librarian gains a [[Memory: Foresight]] and Reverend Timothy can be hired as an [[Assistants|Assistant]]. ==Conversation== {{quote|Reverend Timothy is always, always happy to chat.}} [[Talk]]ing with Reverend Timothy takes 45 seconds instead of the usual 30. Conversation will draw one of the following [[Memory|Memories]] at random: {{#lst:Decks|d.chat.scholar}} ==Salon== He can be invited to a Salon by using the [[Writing-Case]] in the ''Topic'' verb. He will gift the Librarian one of the following items: {{Quote|Reverend Timothy is almost speechless with excitement... almost. [Timothy has sent a gift ahead.]}} {{#lst:Decks|timothy.invite}} ==Trivia== *His last name is not mentioned in-game, but according to a pamphlet featured on the Weather Factory website, the Rector's full name is Reverend Timothy MacDonald.https://weatherfactory.biz/reverend-timothy-on-the-history-of-hush-house/ [[Category:People]] [[Category:Assistants]]

{{PersonInfobox|title1=The Miner |image1=The_Miner.png |aspects=[[Assistance]], [[An Introduction]] |fee=12p |principles={{Lore|Scale|2}}, {{Lore|Forge|1}}, {{Lore|Moon|1}}}} {{quote|‘Thus they more or less ruled themselves, with the help of their wild Celtic temperament, made wilder by the hardness of their lives and the truly ghastly conditions under which they worked [...] with all this it is not to be wondered that the tinners acquired the reputation of being scarcely human. But it must be remembered that among them at all times were those whose characters could stand comparison with the best of men.’|L. Russell Muirhead}}

Assistants.title: Assistants
Assistants.text:
[[File:Assistance icon.png|right]] {{Tocright}} {{Quote|The Librarian lives alone. But there's no shame in seeking assistance from others.
[Assistance can open new rooms or help with your studies. It disappears when used, or at dawn.]}}
'''Assistants''' are needed to help unlock most of the areas in [[Hush House]] and [[Brancrug Village]]. There are several different assistants that can be employed, each with different skills. There is no limit on how many can be hired at the same time. Assistants always leave at dawn and after being used to unlock a room - only one room can be unlocked at a time, but they can be rehired while the room is unlocking. ==Increasing Aspects== An Assistant's [[Principles]] can be increased by using [[Talk]] with an [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]], [[Beverage]], [[Memory]], [[Sustenance]], or a [[Tools|Tool]]. Some Assistants also have a unique collaboration material. An Assistant's principles can be increased multiple times but not by any card of the same category; for example, a Memory and a Beverage may both be used with the same Assistant, but not two Beverages. Principles cannot be increased after nightfall, but Assistants can still be used to unlock rooms until dawn, when they will automatically leave. ==Villagers== You can employ four of the local [[Villagers]]. Mrs and Mr Kille can be hired from their house, The Reverend from the Rectory, and The Smith from the Blacksmith, with the right [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]] and 12p, except for your starting friend. If your starting friend was either Mrs or Mr Kille, you can hire both of them free of charge - just make sure you add the right Principle to hire the Assistant you want. Because Mr Kille requires a card with {{Lore|Winter}} to hire him, he can only be hired with a [[Wist]] card. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Assistant !! To Hire !! Principles !! Unique Collaboration |- | [[The Blacksmith]] || {{Lore|Edge}}, {{Lore|Forge}}, or {{Lore|Heart}} || {{Lore|Forge|2}}, {{Lore|Edge|2}} || [[Metal]] |- | [[The Coffinmaker]] || {{Lore|Winter}} || {{Lore|Winter|2}}, {{Lore|Sky|1}} || [[Wood]] |- | [[The Midwife]] || {{Lore|Grail}} || {{Lore|Grail|2}}, {{Lore|Heart|1}} || [[Fabric]] |- | [[The Rector]] || {{Lore|Lantern}} or {{Lore|Knock}} || {{Lore|Lantern|2}}, {{Lore|Knock|1}} || [[Candle]] |} == Seasonal Workers == Can be sought by offering at least a [[Pence|Shilling]] (12p) in [[The Sweet Bones]]' "Mine" slot with ''no'' [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]] card. Seasonal Assistants do not have any unique collaborations. {| class="wikitable" !Season !Assistant !Principles |- |Spring |[[The Miner]] |{{Lore|Scale|2}}, {{Lore|Forge|1}}, {{Lore|Moon|1}} |- |Summer |[[The Barber]] |{{Lore|Moth|2}}, {{Lore|Rose|1}} |- |Autumn |[[The Orchard-Keeper]] |{{Lore|Nectar|2}}, {{Lore|Heart|1}} |- |Winter |[[The Fisherman]] |{{Lore|Moon|2}}, {{Lore|Sky|1}} |} == Unusual Helpers == Can be found by using an [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]] with any amount of pence at the [[The Sweet Bones|Sweet Bones]] (the initial currency offering is not consumed).
