Bee-Silk Journal.title: Bee-Silk Journal
Bee-Silk Journal.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1= Bee-Silk Journal.png|Bee-Silk Journal Journal.artist.unc.png|Silken Book |principles={{Lore|Grail}} |type=[[Journals|Journal]] |skill=[[Desires & Dissolutions]]
[[Rites of the Roots]]}} {{quote|'Picasso? I'll give you Picasso.' [The Artist came to Hush House to shape and share a History of primal, ultimate, unprecedented experience; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Bosk Wisdom.]}}
The '''Bee-Silk Journal''' is the [[The Artist|Artist's]] [[Journals|Journal]]. It is obtained by selecting [[Ereb]] in [[The Beginning]]. ==The Silken Book== {{quote|The binding is unusual - and half-familiar - some kind of silk? It's survived its soaking remarkably well.}} Once the Drowned Book has been dried out, it will turn into the Silken Book, which is [[Uncatalogued Book|uncatalogued]]. Cataloguing turns the Silken Book into the Bee-Silk Journal, and awards an [[Ereb]]. ==Mastery== The Bee-Silk Journal has Mystery: {{Lore|Grail|1}}. Upon mastery, it will provide 3 ''[[Desires & Dissolutions|Lesson: Desires & Dissolutions]]'' and 1 ''[[Rites of the Roots|Lesson: Rites of the Roots]]''. [[Category:Journal]] [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Grail]]

Amber-Flecked Journal.title: Amber-Flecked Journal
Amber-Flecked Journal.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1= Amber-Flecked Journal.png|Amber-Flecked Journal Journal.twiceborn.unc.png|Stone-Studded Book |principles={{Lore|Lantern}} |type=[[Journals|Journal]] |skill=[[Auroral Contemplations]]
[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]]}} {{quote|I am the Twice-Born Librarian of Hush House, and this is the journal in which I keep my remaining memories. [The Twiceborn's 'third choice' might be life as the Librarian, or it might be something more radical. But you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Illumination Wisdom.]}}
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the [[The Twice-Born|Twice-Born's]] [[Journals|Journal]]. It is obtained by selecting [[Shapt]] and [[Phost]] in [[The Beginning]]. ==The Stone-Studded Book== {{quote|Dull-gleaming yellowish stones. Amber? I feel that I should know...}}
Once the Drowned Book has been dried out, it will turn into the Stone-Studded Book, which is [[Uncatalogued Book|uncatalogued]]. Cataloguing turns the Stone-Studded Book into the Amber-Flecked Journal, and awards a [[Phost]]. ==Mastery== The {{PAGENAME}} has Mystery: {{Lore|Lantern|1}}. Upon mastery, it will provide 3 ''[[Auroral Contemplations|Lesson: Auroral Contemplations]]'' and 1 ''[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing|Lesson: Glaziery & Lightsmithing]]''. [[Category:Journal]] [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Lantern]]

Sand-Scarred Journal.title: Sand-Scarred Journal
Sand-Scarred Journal.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1= Sand-Scarred Journal.png|Sand-Scarred Journal Journal.archaeologist.unc.png|Scarred Book |principles={{Lore|Edge}} ([[Wist]]) or {{Lore|Winter}} ([[Mettle]]) |type=[[Journals|Journal]] |skill=[[Inks of Containment]] ([[Wist]]) or [[Ragged Crossroads]] ([[Mettle]])
[[Wolf Stories]]}} {{quote|I am the Librarian of Hush House, and this journal will record what arose from my Crime and my Curse.
[The Archaeologist's dearest wish, when they came to the House, was to record a History where their crime could be forgiven... or redefined. But you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Skolekosophy Wisdom.]}}
The '''Sand-Scarred Journal''' is the [[The Archaeologist|Archaeologist's]] [[Journals|Journal]]. It is obtained by selecting [[Shapt]] and [[Wist]] or [[Mettle]] in [[The Beginning]]. ==The Scarred Book== {{quote|Goatskin? Antelope? Some scarred leather that catches at my memory. I should know.}}
Once the Drowned Book has been dried out, it will turn into the Scarred Book, which is [[Uncatalogued Book|uncatalogued]]. Cataloguing turns the Scarred Book into the Sand-Scarred Journal, and awards a [[Shapt]]. ==Mastery== If Wist is chosen at the start, the Sand-Scarred Journal will have Mystery: {{Lore|Winter|1}}. Upon mastery, it will provide 3 ''[[Inks of Containment|Lesson: Inks of Containment]]'' and 1 ''[[Wolf Stories|Lesson: Wolf Stories]]. If Mettle is chosen at the start, the Sand-Scarred Journal will have Mystery: {{Lore|Edge|1}}. Upon mastery, it will will provide 3 ''[[Ragged Crossroads|Lesson: Ragged Crossroads]]'' and 1 ''[[Wolf Stories|Lesson: Wolf Stories]]''. [[Category:Journal]] [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Winter]] [[Category:Edge]]

Silver-Bound Journal.title: Silver-Bound Journal
Silver-Bound Journal.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1= Magnate Journal.png|Silver-Bound Journal Journal.magnate.unc.png|Silvery Book |principles={{Lore|Winter}} |type=[[Journals|Journal]] |skill=[[Quenchings & Quellings]]
[[Sacra Limiae]]}} {{quote|I was rich; but something was missing. I am no longer rich... and still, something is missing. Hush House is a place of conclusions, and here, as Librarian, I may find mine. [The Magnate came to the House to conclude a History where they will find peace; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Hushery Wisdom.]}}
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the [[The Magnate|Magnate's]] [[Journals|Journal]]. It is obtained by selecting [[Fet]] and [[Wist]] in [[The Beginning]]. ==The Silvery Book== {{quote|Is that real silver? I feel that it should be. I should remember.}}
Once the Drowned Book has been dried out, it will turn into the Silvery Book, which is [[Uncatalogued Book|uncatalogued]]. Cataloguing turns the Silvery Book into the Silver-Bound Journal, and awards a [[Wist]]. ==Mastery== The {{PAGENAME}} has Mystery: {{Lore|Winter|1}}. Upon mastery, it will provide 3 ''[[Quenchings & Quellings|Lesson: Quenchings & Quellings]]'' and 1 ''[[Sacra Limiae|Lesson: Sacra Limiae]]''. [[Category:Journal]] [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Winter]]

Ironclad Journal.title: Ironclad Journal
Ironclad Journal.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1= Ironclad Journal.png|Ironclad Journal Journal.revolutionary.unc.png|Gunmetal Book |principles={{Lore|Edge}} |type=[[Journals|Journal]] |skill=[[Edicts Martial]]
[[Sky Stories]]|mystery=|memory=}} {{quote|I have striven to be the last Librarian of Hush House. This journal records my strivings. [The Revolutionary's dearest wish, when they came to the House, was to carve out a new History where the most fundamental law would be overthrown; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Horomachistry Wisdom.]}}
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the [[The Revolutionary|Revolutionary's]] [[Journals|Journal]]. It is obtained by selecting [[Fet]] and [[Mettle]] in [[The Beginning]]. ==The Gunmetal Book== {{quote|The heavy metal cover nearly took me down with it. But I survived, and so will this.}}
Once the Drowned Book has been dried out, it will turn into the Gunmetal Book, which is [[Uncatalogued Book|uncatalogued]]. Cataloguing turns the Gunmetal Book into the Ironclad Journal, and awards a [[Mettle]]. ==Mastery== The {{PAGENAME}} has Mystery: {{Lore|Edge|1}}. Upon mastery, it will provide 3 ''[[Edicts Martial|Lesson: Edicts Martial]]'' and 1 ''[[Sky Stories|Lesson: Sky Stories]]''. [[Category:Journal]] [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Edge]]

Horned Journal.title: Horned Journal
Horned Journal.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1= Horned Journal.png|Horned Journal Journal.executioner.unc.png|Mottled Book |principles={{Lore|Edge}} |type=[[Journals|Journal]] |skill=[[Sickle & Eclipse]]
[[Surgeries & Exsanguinations]]}} {{quote|I laid so many of those uncanny things to rest. I thought it was right. I fear now it was not. I am the Librarian of Hush House, and here I will ensure they will be remembered. [The Executioner's dearest wish, when they came to the House, was to record a new History which will atone for their crimes; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Preservation Wisdom.]}}
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the [[The Executioner|Executioner's]] [[Journals|Journal]]. It is obtained by selecting [[Chor]] and [[Mettle]] in [[The Beginning]]. ==The Mottled Book== {{quote|The cover is unusual. Horn? Bakelite? Chitin? I should be able to remember.}} Once the Drowned Book has been dried out, it will turn into the Mottled Book, which is [[Uncatalogued Book|uncatalogued]]. Cataloguing turns the Mottled Book into the Horned Journal, and awards a [[Health]]. ==Mastery== The Horned Journal has Mystery: {{Lore|Edge}} 1. Upon mastery, it will provide three ''[[Sickle & Eclipse|Lessons: Sickle & Eclipse]]'' and one ''[[Surgeries & Exsanguinations|Lesson: Surgeries & Exsanguinations]]''. [[Category:Journal]] [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Edge]]

Feather-Decked Journal.title: Feather-Decked Journal
Feather-Decked Journal.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1= Feather-Decked Journal.png|Feather-Decked Journal Journal.symurgist.unc.png|Feathered Book |principles={{Lore|Winter}} |type=[[Journals|Journal]] |skill=[[Rhyme & Remembrance]]
[[Sky Stories]]}} {{quote|In Caer Adar I heard the secret gods speak one to another. I thought that would be the end of my journey, but the more I heard, the more I knew must be missing. I am the Librarian of Hush House, and I will find what has been lost. [The Symurgist came to Hush House to find a History with the songs that have fallen to silence; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Birdsong Wisdom.]}}
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the [[The Symurgist|Symurgist's]] [[Journals|Journal]]. It is obtained by selecting [[Chor]] and [[Wist]] in [[The Beginning]]. ==The Feathered Book== {{quote|The feathers that adorn its cover are bedraggled from its time in the sea.}}
Once the Drowned Book has been dried out, it will turn into the Feathered Book, which is [[Uncatalogued Book|uncatalogued]]. Cataloguing turns the Feathered Book into the Feather-Decked Journal, and awards a [[Chor]]. ==Mastery== The {{PAGENAME}} has Mystery: {{Lore|Winter|1}}. Upon mastery, it will provide 3 ''[[Rhyme & Remembrance|Lesson: Rhyme & Remembrance]]'' and 1 ''[[Sky Stories|Lesson: Sky Stories]]''. [[Category:Journal]] [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Winter]]

Hammered Copper Journal.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1= Hammered Copper Journal.png|Hammered Copper Journal Journal.prodigal.unc.png|Coppery Book |principles={{Lore|Lantern}} |type=[[Journals|Journal]] |skill=[[Pyroglyphics]]
[[Bells & Brazieries]]}} {{quote|I've crossed three oceans and almost drowned in one. Now I am the Librarian of Hush House. Perhaps here I will be safe from my parents; but I can't take that for granted. [The Prodigal's dearest wish is sanctuary - as Librarian, or in a History where things are different;but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Ithastry Wisdom.]}}
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the [[The Prodigal|Prodigal's]] [[Journals|Journal]]. It is obtained by selecting [[Chor]] and [[Phost]] in [[The Beginning]]. ==The Coppery Book== {{quote|The unusual metal binding is untouched by the sea.}}
Once the Drowned Book has been dried out, it will turn into the Coppery Book, which is [[Uncatalogued Book|uncatalogued]]. Cataloguing turns the Coppery Book into the Hammered Copper Journal, and awards a [[Phost]]. ==Mastery== The {{PAGENAME}} has Mystery: {{Lore|Lantern|1}}. Upon mastery, it will provide 3 ''[[Pyroglyphics|Lesson: Pyroglyphics]]'' and 1 ''[[Bells & Brazieries|Lesson: Bells & Brazieries]]''. [[Category:Journal]] [[Category:Book]] [[Category:Lantern]]

Serpentskin Journal.text:
{{Book (BoH) |image1= Serpentskin Journal.png|Serpentskin Journal Journal.cartographer.unc.png|Scaled Book |principles={{Lore|Lantern}} |type=[[Journals|Journal]] |skill=[[Inks of Revelation]]
[[Path & Pilgrim]]}} {{quote|I am the Librarian of Hush House, and this journal will be my Perpetual Map. [The Cartographer's dearest wish, when they came to the House, was to chart a new History in which their impossible map would be possible; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Nyctodromy Wisdom.]}}
The '''Serpentskin Journal''' is the [[The Cartographer|Cartographer's]] [[Journals|Journal]]. It is obtained by selecting [[Fet]] and [[Phost]] in [[The Beginning]]. ==The Scaled Book== {{quote|The scaled binding has survived the soaking well enough.}}
Once the Drowned Book has been dried out, it will turn into the Scaled Book, which is [[Uncatalogued Book|uncatalogued]]. Librarians.title: Librarians
Librarians.text:
In Book of Hours, you play as the Librarian of Hush House, but each Librarian has their own reason for being there. At [[The Beginning|the beginning of the game]], your choice of Soul Elements determines which Librarian you play as.

* [[The Archaeologist]]
* [[The Artist]]
* [[The Cartographer]]
* [[The Executioner]]
* [[The Magnate]]
* [[The Prodigal]]
* [[The Revolutionary]] 
* [[The Symurgist]]
* [[The Twice-Born]]

[[Category:The Librarian|*]]

The Revolutionary.title: The Revolutionary
The Revolutionary.text:
[[File:Memories.revolutionary.png|64px|right]] {{quote|'Knowledge is the terror of oppressors.' I have overthrown my share of earthly oppressions; but Calyptra is the tyranny of eternity. When at last we can speak its name and live - only then can we call ourselves free.|Memories: the Revolutionary}} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Librarians|Librarian]] that you can play as, if [[Fet]] and [[Mettle]] are chosen in the [[The Beginning|beginning]]. The Revolutionary is associated with [[Horomachistry]], one of the Bright Arts. Their [[Journals|journal]] is the [[Ironclad Journal]], which requires {{Lore|Edge}} for mastery. ==Unique Endings== {{Spoilers|caption=This section contains information about [[Endings|endings]].|content=
The Revolutionary can reach 9 unique endings using [[Numen: Back Into Balance]], [[Numen: the Bells of Ys]], and [[Numen: Three Rules]].
Each [[Numen]] can be used to achieve 3 different endings, depending on which principle is used to write a [[History]].}} [[Category:The Librarian|Revolutionary, The]]

The Magnate.title: The Magnate
The Magnate.text:
[[File:Memories.magnate.png|64px|right]] {{quote|‘I've lived too long, but I'm not ready to die. I've tasted everything, and it wasn't enough. Give me silence; give me peace; give me the peace of snow.’|Memories: the Magnate}} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Librarians|Librarian]] that you can play as if [[Fet]] and [[Wist]] are chosen in the [[The Beginning|beginning]]. The Magnate is associated with [[Hushery]], one of the Night Arts. Their [[Journals|journal]] is the [[Silver-Bound Journal]], which requires {{Lore|Winter}} for mastery. ==Unique Endings== {{Spoilers | caption = This section contains information about [[Endings|endings]]. | content =
The Magnate can reach 6 unique endings using [[Numen: a Final Understanding]] and [[Numen: That Old Lost Music]].
Each [[Numen]] can be used to achieve 3 different endings, depending on which principle is used to write a [[History]]. }} [[Category:The Librarian|Magnate, The]]

The Cartographer.title: The Cartographer
The Cartographer.text:
[[File:Memories.cartographer.png|64px|right]] {{quote|‘There is no map of the House of the Sun, where the invisible gods walk. How could there be, when every year it changes, and yet every year it remains the same? Tricky, certainly. Impossible? Let's see.’|Memories: the Cartographer}} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Librarians|Librarian]] that you can play as if [[Fet]] and [[Phost]] are chosen in the [[The Beginning|beginning]]. The Cartographer is associated with [[Nyctodromy]], one of the Night Arts. Their [[Journals|journal]] is the [[Serpentskin Journal]], which requires {{Lore|Lantern}} for mastery. ==Unique Endings== {{Spoilers|caption=This section contains information about [[Endings|endings]].|content=
The Cartographer can reach 6 unique endings using [[Numen: Weaving the World]] and [[Numen: the Paths of the Sun]].
Each [[Numen]] can be used to achieve 3 different endings, depending on which principle is used to write a [[History]].}} [[Category:The Librarian|Cartographer, The]]

The Artist.title: The Artist
The Artist.text:
[[File:Memories.artist.png|64px|right]] {{quote|‘Dada was a start. The Surrealist Manifesto? A step along the road, but only a step. The road goes nowhere, unless it goes into the Wood; and that's a road we can only walk in the dark. Wait, no, not ‘in the dark’. ‘In blood.’ ‘Hip-deep in blood.’ Oh shut up. Give it to me, I'll write it - ’|Memories: the Artist}} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Librarians|Librarian]] that you can play as if [[Ereb]] is chosen in the [[The Beginning|beginning]]. The Artist is associated with [[The Bosk]], one of the Arts Unregarded. Their [[Journals|journal]] is the [[Bee-Silk Journal]], which requires {{Lore|Grail}} for mastery. ==Unique Endings== {{Spoilers|caption=This section contains information about [[Endings|endings]].|content=
The Artist can reach 6 unique endings using [[Numen: Merciless Alteration]] and [[Numen: an Irresistible Feast]].
Each [[Numen]] can be used to achieve 3 different endings, depending on which principle is used to write a [[History]].}} [[Category:The Librarian|Artist, The]]

The Prodigal.title: The Prodigal
The Prodigal.text:
[[File:Memories.prodigal.png|64px|right]] {{quote|‘My parents were Long - which is to say immortal - and Long are not permitted to make children. Their punishment is this: now that they know I live, they cannot rest until they devour me. Here in Hush House, I will be safe. It is even possible that I might learn to shape a weapon to defend myself.’|Memories: the Prodigal}} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Librarians|Librarian]] that you can play as if [[Chor]] and [[Phost]] are chosen in the [[The Beginning|beginning]]. The Prodigal is associated with [[Ithastry]], one of the Bright Arts. Their [[Journals|journal]] is the [[Hammered Copper Journal]], which requires {{Lore|Lantern}} for mastery. ==Unique Endings== {{Spoilers|caption=This section contains information about [[Endings|endings]].|content=
The Prodigal can reach 6 unique endings using [[Numen: Inescapable Confinement]] and [[Numen: the Bells of Ys]].
Each [[Numen]] can be used to achieve 3 different endings, depending on which principle is used to write a [[History]].}} [[Category:The Librarian|Prodigal, The]]

The Symurgist.title: The Symurgist
The Symurgist.text:
[[File:Memories.symurgist.png|64px|right]] {{quote|‘I eavesdropped on the songs of the Aviform Hours. I'd heard the warnings; I'd lose my mind, my soul, my skin. All those things are true, but no-one ever warns you what happens if you get away with it... which is to say, after that, there just doesn't seem to be anything else worth hearing.’|Memories: the Symurgist}} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Librarians|Librarian]] that you can play as if [[Chor]] and [[Wist]] are chosen in the [[The Beginning|beginning]]. The Symurgist is associated with [[Birdsong]], one of the Arts Unregarded. Their [[Journals|journal]] is the [[Feather-Decked Journal]], which requires {{Lore|Winter}} for mastery. ==Unique Endings== {{Spoilers|caption=This section contains information about [[Endings|endings]].|content=
The Symurgist can reach 6 unique endings using [[Numen: Weaving the World]] and [[Numen: That Old Lost Music]].
Each [[Numen]] can be used to achieve 3 different endings, depending on which principle is used to write a [[History]].}} [[Category:The Librarian|Symurgist, The]]

The Archaeologist.title: The Archaeologist
The Archaeologist.text:
[[File:Memories.archaeologist.png|64px|right]] {{quote|‘I opened a tomb, and found - too late - that it was a prison. The plague that I released is now my shadow - or perhaps I am its reflection. It is too late to set matters right, but it is never too late to protect the future from the past. In Hush House I can do no harm. Perhaps I can even make amends.’|Memories: the Archaeologist}}
'''The Archaeologist''' is a [[Librarians|Librarian]] that you can play as if [[Shapt]] and [[Wist]] or [[Mettle]] are chosen in the [[The Beginning|beginning]]. The Archaeologist is associated with [[Skolekosophy]], one of the Night Arts. Their [[Journals|journal]] is the [[Sand-Scarred Journal]], which requires {{Lore|Edge}} or {{Lore|Winter}} for mastery, depending on which [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]] was chosen in the beginning, [[Mettle]] or [[Wist]] respectively. The Archaeologist is the only Librarian whose journal mastery [[Principles|principle]] can be different depending on their soul choices. ==Unique Endings== {{Spoilers|caption=This section contains information about [[Endings|endings]].|content=
The Archaeologist can reach 6 unique endings using [[Numen: Inescapable Confinement]] and [[Numen: Merciless Alteration]].
Each [[Numen]] can be used to achieve 3 different endings, depending on which principle is used to write a [[History]].}} [[Category:The Librarian|Archaeologist, The]]

The Executioner.title: The Executioner
The Executioner.text:
[[File:Memories.executioner.png|64px|right]] {{quote|‘I was employed by the Suppression Bureau to preserve the daylight world, by destroying those things that walk in the night. For years I was faithful to that duty... but sometimes the things I hunted wept when I slew them. And so at last I set aside my knives, and came here, where I can do no more harm. Perhaps I can even make amends.’|Memories: the Executioner}} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Librarians|Librarian]] that you can play as if [[Chor]] and [[Mettle]] are chosen in the [[The Beginning|beginning]]. The Executioner is associated with [[Preservation]], one of the Arts Unregarded. Their [[Journals|journal]] is the [[Horned Journal]], which requires {{Lore|Edge}} for mastery. ==Unique Endings== {{Spoilers|caption=This section contains information about [[Endings|endings]].|content=
The Executioner can reach 6 unique endings using [[Numen: Back Into Balance]] and [[Numen: the Sun's Weakness]].
Each [[Numen]] can be used to achieve 3 different endings, depending on which principle is used to write a [[History]].}} [[Category:The Librarian|Executioner, The]]

The Twice-Born.title: The Twice-Born
The Twice-Born.text:
[[File:Memories.twiceborn.png|64px|right]] {{quote|‘I remember that I once walked the House of the Sun as a bodiless immortal; but there was a matter that could only be resolved if I returned to flesh. Now, if I go back to the House of the Sun, I will be hunted and punished; if I stay in flesh, I will be hunted and devoured. I need a third choice. To remain at Hush House, as Librarian, would be one such choice. But there might be something more.’|Memories: the Twice-Born}} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Librarians|Librarian]] that you can play as if [[Shapt]] and [[Phost]] are chosen in the [[The Beginning|beginning]]. The Twice-Born is associated with [[Illumination]], one of the Bright Arts. Their [[Journals|journal]] is the [[Amber-Flecked Journal]], which requires {{Lore|Lantern}} for mastery. ==Unique Endings== {{Spoilers|caption=This section contains information about [[Endings|endings]].|content=
The Twice-Born can reach 9 unique endings using [[Numen: the Great Counterfeit]], [[Numen: Loopholes]], and [[Numen: the Paths of the Sun]].
Each [[Numen]] can be used to achieve 3 different endings, depending on which principle is used to write a [[History]].}} [[Category:The Librarian|Twice-Born, The]]

Dewulf Family.title: Dewulf Family
Dewulf Family.text:
{{Family infobox |title1=Dewulf Family |image1=Dewulf_Coa.png |family_members=*[[Hendrik Dewulf]] *[[Thomas Dewulf]] *[[Eva Dewulf]] |titles=[[Baron of Brancrug]]}} {{Quote|In the 16th Century, the Dewulf family became the Barons Brancrug, governing the Isle as their personal estate - until 1759, when their line ended in madness and death.}} __NOTOC__
The '''Dewulf Family''' was a noble family in Brancrug. Their time as Barons of Brancrug marked the [[Baronial Period]] of [[Hush House]]. ==Family Members== ===Barons of Brancrug === *[[Hendrik Dewulf]], 1st Baron Brancrug *[[Thomas Dewulf]], 2nd Baron Brancrug *[[Walter Dewulf]], 3rd Baron Brancrug *[[Musgrave Dewulf]], 4th Baron Brancrug *[[Gideon Dewulf]], 5th Baron Brancrug *[[Valentine Dewulf]], 6th Baron Brancrug *[[Eva Dewulf]], 7th Baroness Brancrug === Other Members=== *[[Bryan Dewulf]] *[[Sebastian Dewulf|Captain Sebastian Dewulf]] *Giles Dewulf *Abra Southey (supposedly) *Eales Dewulf *The Dewulf Twins ===Marriages=== *Hafren Waters ==Arms== [[File:Coat of Arms.png|thumb|right|Located in the
[[Westcott Room]]]] In ''[[A True History of Valentine Dewulf]]'', the Dewulf family coat of arms is described in blazon as: {{Quote|On a field or, a chevron enarched gules between two corby heads erased sable in chief and a wolf sejant sable in base.}} ==Curse == It was rumoured that the family was cursed, although the exact nature of the curse was debated. Despite it only being rumours, according to Father Theo, Eva believed in the curse enough to drown herself and her grandkids at the same time. ===The Curse of Red William=== This was a supposed curse placed on Henrik Dewulf by Red William ===The Pale Heritage of Hafren=== The Dewulf's pale complexion was the result of genetic descent from Hafren Waters, a woman of 'uncertain lineage' who married Giles. [[Category:People]] [[Category:Dewulf Family]]

Kitty Mazarine.title: Kitty Mazarine
Kitty Mazarine.text:
{{Individual infobox |image1=Kitty Mazarine.png |name=Kitty Mazarine
Second Librarian |family=Two sons |species=Mortal}} {{Quote|Kitty Mazarine, second Librarian - musician, composer, one-time placée. 'Almost French, almost Spanish, or almost American.'}}
'''Kitty Mazarine''' was the second [[Librarians|Librarian]] of the Curia of the Isle, "Who was born of three nations, and of none". She was a talented musician. Her [['Kitty Mazarine'|Bust]] is located in the [[Mazarine Room]]. ==Description== She was patient, but quite eccentric and never cared much for tradition. She hated the smell of pipe smoke, or possibly hated [[Ambrose Westcott]], her predecessor. Kitty Mazarine made jam from [[Honeyscar Jasmine]]. According to tradition, all amber pumpkins in Brancrug were grown from seeds she brought from her home across the sea. Amber Pumpkin Pie was a favourite of her second son. She had to leave both her sons behind when she left for Hush House, but she brought the recipe with her to Brancrug. Her quarters were in the [[Pale Chamber]]. The only piece of furniture she brought to Hush House was a cypress-wood table filled with memories of the times she was contracted to another. She established the [[Mazarine Room|music room]], which still contains her [['Kitty Mazarine'|Bust]], and was better known for her vocal compositions, but she was a versatile musician and on winter evenings would invite villagers and visitors alike to her recitals. She was possibly in a famous band called ''El Bretón''. She gifted the [[Instrument: Piano|piano]] in the [[Servants' Hall]] and would sometimes visit to sing there. There is a story told of her napping in an [[Kitty's Armchair|armchair]] and dreaming of mirrors. Then, upon waking, she hums an unknown melody, which becomes her fuging-tune 'Thirty Birds'. Dr Yvette Southey.title: Dr Yvette Southey
Dr Yvette Southey.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Dr_Yvette_Southey.png |principle1={{Lore|Moon}} |principle2={{Lore|Winter}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Ericapaean]], [[Greek]], [[Henavek]], [[Latin]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |relationships=[[Southey Family]] |address=St David's Hill, Exeter}} {{quote|Playwright, philologist, psychoanalyst: as happy with questions as with answers.}}
'''Dr. Yvette Southey''' is a [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] and a member of the [[Southey Family]]. She is a potential Secretary Enigmatic for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. Dr Southey can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Ericapaean]] or [[Henavek]]. ==Invitations and Salons== Dr Southey requires 3 {{Lore|Moon}} to be invited to Hush House. She has no food or drink preferences. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor ! First Conversation !1st Lesson !Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] |Yvette and Dagmar have both dreamt of conversations with half-faced Xenodice, ‘fair to strangers’, Name of the Horned-Axe. Dagmar is convinced they both met the real Xenodice. Yvette is equally convinced that both of them were conversing with an ambassador from the collective unconscious, but she struggles to answer when Dagmar asks what the difference would be between that and an ‘actual’ Name. |[[Rhyme & Remembrance]] |Dagmar talks to Yvette of her dreams of the Painted River. ‘Hard to tell if it’s a dream ''of'' the River, or ''in'' the River. River’s behind the Stag Door. Never passed the Stag Door; well, not formally speaking; well, let’s not talk about that, eh? But anyway the Vagabond painted the River, and her whole thing y’see, is she gets in where she’s not meant to. Actually shall we talk about something else?’ |[[Pearl & Tide]] |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Yvette speaks of her monograph on 'Lagiah's Turn' - the ascension of the Queen Unsated to sit at the Red Grail's left hand - in which she develops a consistent Jungian interpretation of the myth. Al-Adim reacts with sceptical amusement - he claims to have met Lagiah - but Yvette is undaunted. 'Things don't have to be real to be true,' she points out. |[[Hill & Hollow]] |Yvette asks al-Adim what he remembers of his parents. He replies that he recalls only their deaths. He speaks of those deaths with a dispassion that seems to surprise him more than it does her. |[[Wolf Stories]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] | | | | |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] |Arun and Yvette began with a serious philological discussion - the similarities between Henavek and Vak - but the conversation has devolved into something more like gossip, comparing the virtues and charms of Vak and Henavek as if they were individuals. Arun mentions the tradition that the two languages are brother and sister. 'It would be a shame, wouldn't it, if they were?' Yvette responds archly. 'If they were brother and sister, nothing unsuitable could occur between them, surely?' Arun's whole face creases in an unusually fervent smile. |[[Kernewek Henavek|Henavek]] |Yvette and Arun revisit an innuendo-laced conversation about a possible entanglement between Vak and Henavek. Each recites poetry in their language of preference. Before very long, they have drawn their chairs closer together so they can whisper the poetry in one another’s ears.
[Arun and Yvette will leave together tonight…] |[[Rhyme & Remembrance]] |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] |Yvette is considering keeping her notes in houndsgall, for safety. Serena advises her on some of the dangers of houndsgall use and storage. |[[Inks of Containment]] | | |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Yvette and Stanislav chat about the notorious erotic-occult novel, 'Ettery After', which Yvette considers 'flimsy' and Stanislav considers 'saucy'. |[[Inks of Containment]] | | |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] |Yvette questions Chaima about the motives and credibility of 'Little Sophia', the monster-hunting, and specifically Worm-hunting, author of 'Oblations in Iron'. Chaima is non-commital, but very clear that she herself tries not to hunt Worms. |[[Inks of Containment]] |Chaima asks Yvette to interpret a dream - of a white waste west of the world where pale mutes redden the snow with the blood of a bull... |[[Snow Stories]] |- |[[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Yvette is fascinated by the language-of-signs called Sabazine, in which Arthur is proficient. He teaches her a few signs, but she grows suddenly frightened and asks him to stop. |[[Sabazine]] |Yvette raises the subject of Sabazine again with Athur. She has been reading of the god Sabazos, who brings madness by deploying the weapons of speech-in-silence. Arthur has heard of these techniques, and very cautiously shares a very little… |[[Sharps]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Yvette asks Hokobald whether there are ways to determine who might be a child of two Long. He insists with apparent pride that it is very rare for the children of Long to survive - that one of their parents almost always devours them and 'ascends' to alukite status - but acknowledges that it has been known, under rare circumstances, and shares some of the signs... |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |Hokobald demands to know whether Yvette ever hears the bells of Ys when she’s near the sea. Yvette bridles at his tone, but answers carefully that she thinks perhaps that she might; they discuss what form the sounds might take, and Hokobald’s brusqueness softens a little. |[[Bells & Brazieries]] |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] |Connie and Yvette are discussing a patient of Yvette's who, it now appears, may have died before attending his first session. ('I had wondered,' Yvette says slowly, 'why my rooms were always so cold afterwards.') Connie is of the opinion that since the man is dead, no ethical considerations about confidentiality need apply. Yvette is not convinced. |[[Rhyme & Remembrance]] |‘The language of the Four Quarters.’ Connie shakes her head. ‘I learnt it out there, before I joined the Bureau. If I talk too much about it, it’ll spoil the mood. But here’s some pointers.’ |[[Killasimi]] |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] |Morgen seems taken with Yvette, and devotes more attention to her than Yvette seems comfortable with. When Yvette falls silent, Morgen raises her silvery voice in a silvery song. The tune is jaunty; but the words are Killasimi; and by the end of it, even Morgen seems distraught. 'I wish, sometimes, that I might still weep,' she confides.
[These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Killasimi]] |Emboldened by their last conversation, Yvette asks pointed questions about how Morgen came to be what she is. Morgen won’t talk about how she went alukite, but she does talk about growing Long – her tutoring in the Old Form by Sulochana, her fascination with the Thunderskin’s New Form, and the last dances which took her to the House of the Moon. |[[Tridesma Hiera]] |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Yvette wonders whether the gods-who-were-stone can be resolved to psychic or psychological factors – to what degree they were ever real Hours at all, rather than baser, part-sublimated impulses of the existing Hours. Olympe is intrigued. |[[Putrefactions & Calcinations]] | | |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Yvette and Ehsan speak wistfully of what they have read of the lost Hour called Tide. Yvette recalls that when the Sister withdraws, other Hours sometimes fill the space left by her withdrawal, and wonders whether the Tide is gentle enough to remain afterwards… but Ehsan politely insists that the gods-who-were-stone are never gentle. |[[Pearl & Tide]] |Ehsan and Yvette speak of Tentreto, the perhaps-human saint of the early church. Ehsan describes his pilgrimage to Tentreto’s shrine in Venice, but admits he was motivated only partly by religious curiosity – more by an enthusiasm for Venetian cuisine and a desire to catch up with an old (he coughs in embarrassment) friend… |[[Pearl & Tide]] |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Yvette is asking Fraser about his 'dreams of eyes'. He is eager to tell her - he interprets them as messages from the 'greater hybridity' of the Carapace Cross, though she is sceptical. |[[Hill & Hollow]] |Yvette and Fraser discuss his further 'dreams of eyes', and his theories about the entry of the Scīmafectra-kind and the Thritige-kind to human flesh. Yvette wonders aloud whether he has ever considered that most - perhaps all - of the dreams arise from his own frustrated desire for fatherhood. In a fit of temper, he snatches off the glove on his changed hand, and displays its glossy, altered angles to her. For a moment there is silence at the table. |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |‘It is cold,’ Zachary whispers to Yvette. He shivers. ‘I must stay cold, mustn’t I? If I thaw, I will come loose, won’t I?’ Yvette nods carefully. ‘I think it’s for the best that you don’t thaw – not yet – ’ she agrees. |[[Snow Stories]] | | |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |In one History, Alexander heard a secret from Darius that convinced him to abandon battle and return home, announcing, ‘the Sun has his course, and so do I.’ Yvette asks Azita what she knows about the secret, apparently under the impression that Azita and Alexander were contemporaries, which causes Azita some amusement (I’m not even a thousand years old’). In any case Azita is of the opinion that the secret is ‘a Lionsmith nonsense’ and Alexander was ‘much overestimated.’ |[[Sickle & Eclipse]] |Yvette asks Azita about the Edge-dyad Torgue and Dearday, with whom she has been known to go drinking every century or two. Yvette mentions (casually?) that she’s always had a bit of a pash on Dearday. Azita’s eyes glitter: ‘Have you now.’
[There’s something between Azita and Yvette, although exactly what remains to be seen.] |[[Edicts Martial]] |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Coquille asks Yvette what she knows of the line of Kelemdu, the 'Black Dove'. Yvette describes a Henavek folk-tale in which the Black Dove is assigned the wardenship of the Moon-marches by Henavek himself - a folk-tale associated with Brancrug. |[[Sea Stories]] |Coquille presses Yvette on her resemblance to Rowena Hengerst; she asks whether they have ever met. 'No,' says Yvette; 'she will never agree to an interview with me.' Coquille theorizes eagerly about why; Yvette nods and smiles. |[[Sea Stories]] |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Yvette and Corso discuss the reckoner mobs - the predatory merchants of years-of-life. Yvette tentatively suggests that she might like Corso to put her in touch with the reckoners, if he can… but he discourages her. 'Do you know what sanding is? Or dolling? Find out, Dr Southey, and then ask me again.' |[[Snow Stories]] | | |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Yvette listens as Agdistis grapples with his dislike of Solomon Husher's work: he cannot, will not, accept that everything must end - he is unwilling even to accept that anything must end. |[[Sights & Sensations]] |Agdistis listens as Yvette expounds her theories on the paintings of Nina Lagasse: how, Yvette believes, her choice of colours over the years shows that she knew when her time was coming to an end. |[[Sights & Sensations]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Yvette, unexpectedly, asks if she can paint Mrs Kille. Mrs Kille, no less surprisingly, agrees - 'been a while' - but asks Yvette detailed questions about her technique. Mr Kille pays close, albeit unobtrusive, attention. |[[Sights & Sensations]] |Yvette has heard from Corso of Mr Kille's tendency to poetry. She asks him about his inspirations, and he shares them, albeit cautiously. She asks him about his dreams, and he glances around, then puts a finger to his lips. 'Not in the House,' he says. |[[Sights & Sensations]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |Denzil's eyes widen at the sight of Yvette. He inclines his head respectfully, but barely responds to any of her questions. |[[Memory: Fear]] |Yvette does her best to put Denzil at his ease; he is plainly very wary of her. He remains polite, but taciturn even by his own taciturn standards. He does eventually admit that in Brancrug, there is a tradition that it is bad luck to insult, or to buy from, or to drink with a pale-haired woman… |[[Sea Stories]] |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Reverend Timothy is discussing historical heresies and heterodoxies with Yvette. She seems moderately engaged by the conversation, but Reverend Tim is fairly boiling with excitement. |[[Watchman's Paradoxes|Watchman’s Paradoxes]] |Yvette and Reverend Timothy are discussing differences between the Received and Sanctioned versions of the Book of Suns. Yvette, whose formal theological education ended with Sunday school, is clearly confused by the details, but this only makes Reverend Tim more eager to correct her, and his innocent enthusiasm is making her smile. |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |} ==Incidents== Dr Southey can visit for the following incidents: *[[The Affair of the Endless Guest]] *[[The Affair of the Forgivable Debt]] *[[The Affair of the Friar's Tapestry]] *[[The Affair of the Grunewald Provision]] *[[The Affair of the Messenger's Casket]] *[[The Affair of the Open Reverend]] *[[The Affair of the Particular Mystique]] *[[The Affair of the Rising While]] [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]]

Dr Ibn al-Adim.title: Dr Ibn al-Adim
Dr Ibn al-Adim.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Dr_Ibn_al-Adim.png |principle1={{Lore|Rose}} |principle2={{Lore|Scale}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Aramaic]], [[Greek]], [[Latin]], [[Phrygian]], [[Sabazine]], [[Sanskrit]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |address=Rue Bonaparte, Nice}} {{Quote|'The Aleppine': Historian, doctor, and above all, traveller. The good doctor has been associated with all but one of the libraries of the Watchman's Tree. He was even Secretary Nunciant of Hush House for a little while, but he has never been on good terms with the Suppression Bureau.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Rose}} and {{Lore|Scale}}. He is a potential Secretary Nunciant for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. He can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Sabazine]]. == Incidents == Dr al-Adim can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of the Absent Friend]] *[[The Affair of the Claw and the Clouds]] *[[The Affair of the Dappled Rose]] *[[The Affair of the Other Horizon]] *[[The Affair of the Rising While]] *[[The Affair of the Sandalwood Saint]] *[[The Affair of the Second Skin]] == Invitations and Salons == Dr al-Adim requires 7 {{Lore|Rose}} to be invited to Hush House. He prefers food with {{Lore|Scale}}, and cannot be given [[Intoxicating]] drinks. == Salon Conversations== {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor ! First Conversation !First Lesson !Second Conversation !Second Lesson |- | [[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Al-Adim and Agdistis are gossiping, quietly, about al-Adim's patroness. 'Not a hundred legs,' says al-Adim, 'but more than you'd think…' |[[Sky Stories]] |Agdistis and al-Adim have a lively chat about the uses of birdsong in the prediction of weather. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |- |[[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Arthur and al-Adim are discussing the dyes and dyers of the city of Tyre. | [[Inks of Power]] |Al-Adim asks Arthur if he ever thought to grow Long, but Arthur shakes his head. 'Too many sacrifices - too many more. I know your patroness is gentler. But I will not pay the price, nor have others pay it for me.' |[[Auroral Contemplations]] |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] |Al-Adim is chaffing Arun about the fading potency of 'your venoms'. Arun is clearly subsiding into a sulk. |[[Serpents & Venoms]] |Arun, complacently: 'The traveller is always returning. One who does not is no traveller.' Al-Adim, waspishly: 'Tell that to my patroness.' |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |Azita and al-Adim discuss the varieties of messenger-birds and courier-spirits that they have employed across the centuries of their acquaintance. |[[Sky Stories]] |Al-Adim and Azita are reminiscing about the time of their first acquaintance in the city of Damascus, in the days before the coming of Timur. 'Good fighting!' she sighs. 'I preferred the hawking,' he says; and they spend some time discussing desert falconry. | [[Furs & Feathers]] |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] |Chaima listens intently while al-Adim describes the rare occasions on which labhites have been successfully brought to ground. Neither of them look happy. | [[Horns & Ivories]] |Chaima and al-Adim are comparing navigation techniques. |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] |Connie and al-Adim are discussing the stories about Franklin Bancroft and Eva Dewulf - heads together - smiling. Evidently the location has inspired them. |[[Pearl & Tide]] |Once again, Connie and al-Adim are discussing Eva Dewulf and Bancroft. Connie sips from her glass, watching him as he leans in close to recite Bancroft's poetry. |[[Pearl & Tide]] |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Al-Adim politely interrogates Coquille about her family and nature. Yes, she is associated with the Tomb of Lies; no, she is no longer welcome there; yes, she is, she supposes, technically a pentiment… |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |Al-Adim and Coquille are fencing again. She asks him outright about the nature of his Longhood; he tells her he 'found his patron in the desert.' He asks her if she is 'Clogg-relevant'; she pretends outrage that he is asking about her age, and will say only that she is less than a century old. |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Al-Adim is reminiscing to Corso about Yarden of Nishapur, who knew the 'songs that came before the sun' … |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |Corso is eager to hear more about Yarden of Nishapur, who al-Adim may have known long ago… although al-Adim grows chillier when Corso's interest crystallises into interest into curiosity about the location of certain valuable texts. |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |- |[[Daymare]] |Dagmar and al-Adim chat happily about Medina's 'Queens of the Rivers: |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |Al-Adim and Dagmar are engrossed in a deeply technical discussion about the accuracy - and possible transience - of Westergren's accounts of the Mansus. (Dagmar keeps deferentially reminding al-Adim that she's never passed the Stag Door.) |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] |Al-Adim is spinning tales of his travels, in the mountains of Persia, the taiga of the farthest East, the snows of Antarctica ... Douglas listens, enraptured. 'Sometimes,' he says gruffly, I wish I'd done things different.' |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |Douglas and al-Adim are trying to work out whether the unusual nature of al-Adim's ascension to Longhood - under the Vagabond - actually means he hasn't actually broken any British laws. They decide that he probably has, but Douglas is very practical about the difficulties of arresting him, and offers to let him off with a caution if he doesn't ever ascend to immortality again. |[[Edicts Inviolable]] |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Ehsan and al-Adim are talking about goats. They both seem remarkably well-informed and exceptionally enthusiastic about goats. Neither of them will quite admit to ever having been a goatherd. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |Ehsan and al-Adim discuss the care and feeding of birds of prey. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Al-Adim and Fraser are debating – very cautiously, even here in Hush House – the nature of the Red Flower of the Calyptra – to what extent it makes use of the cleansing fire, and to what extent it relies on illusion and deception. |[[Inks of Power]] |Al-Adim, the historian, and Fraser, the collector, debate the longevity and the peril of their favourite Great Inks. |[[Inks of Power]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Hokobald speaks to al-Adim of the final Pilgrimage of Seven that the Vagabond supposedly intends - up the Mansus and beyond, into the Glory. He gloatingly explains why he believes her Pilgrimage will fail. Al-Adim disagrees; he thinks that, eventually, it will succeed; but the prospect clearly makes him unhappy. (It may be, in fact, that this was Hokobald's intention in raising the matter...) |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |Hokobald expounds on his belief that the Great Ink called Orpiment Exultant is - or will become - a Name of the Chandler. Al-Adim listens first with incredulity, but then with sceptical interest. |[[Inks of Power]] |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] |AI-Adim and Morgen discuss the meditations of Abbot Thomas of St Brandan's. Morgen asks if al-Adim ever met the Abbot. 'I acknowledge that I am rather older than you,' he replies, a little stiffly, 'but I am not that old.' |[[Applebright Euphonies]] |Morgen and al-Adim compare their experiences of the notorious blossoms of the City of Messenger Eagles, which they have both visited, although, it seems, their visits were almost two hundred years apart... |[[Orchids & Narcotics]] |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Al-Adim and Olympe exchange stories of meetings with the prehuman dead: gentle things that yearn for a redder sun, and hungrier things that seek human blood to satisfy that yearning. |[[Stone Stories]] |Olympe shows al-Adim sketches she's made based on signs she saw in a dream. 'Yes,' he says, 'this is almost Sabazine. Here. The Towers of the Little Hammer. The Wolf-Wife. The Black Dove. I think you dreamt that you were coming to Brancrug…' |[[Sabazine]] |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] |Al-Adim and Serena discuss the Great Inks of Power and their personalities. Serena is concerned that the use of a particular ink might alter the meaning of a text. Al-Adim considers this a benefit; or a way to add meaning to the text; or at least something fundamental. |[[Inks of Power]] |Serena quizzes al-Adim about the Damascene branch of the organisation now called the Obliviates. He shares what he remembers. |[[Sacra Limiae]] |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |AI-Adim describes his memories of Thirza Blake, and her work, in his time as Secretary Nunciant of the House. He is clearly caught between affection and annoyance. Stanislav shakes hjs head: 'I wish I had known her. I think we'd have got on.' |[[Herbs & Infusions]] |Towards the end of the meal, Father Stanislav demonstrates some of the signs that he used to communicate with 'singlefoots' in his travels 'east of Hsian', He draws the signs on his plate, and wipes them away afterwards. 'Safer not,' he says quietly, 'unless you wanted to stay east of Hsian.' |[[Cracktrack]] |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Yvette speaks of her monograph on 'Lagiah's Turn' - the ascension of the Queen Unsated to sit at the Red Grail's left hand - in which she develops a consistent Jungian interpretation of the myth. Al-Adim reacts with sceptical amusement - he claims to have met Lagiah - but Yvette is undaunted. 'Things don't have to be real to be true,' she points out. |[[Hill & Hollow]] |Yvette asks al-Adim what he remembers of his parents. He replies that he recalls only their deaths. He speaks of those deaths with a dispassion that seems to surprise him more than it does her. |[[Wolf Stories]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Zachary and al-Adim speak of how things end; al-Adim with a kind of eager nostalgia; Zachary with simple eagerness. |[[Putrefactions & Calcinations]] |Zachary, unselfconsciously, recites a poem-in-progress to al-Adim: a clashing fortress of a piece. He beats out the rhythm on the tabletop. Al-Adim tentatively suggests a refinement, which Zachary, judiciously, accepts. |[[Preliminal Meter]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] | | | | |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] | | | | |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Timothy and al-Adim discuss al-Jabal, 'the sun rising over the mountain' - the Syrian god with whom the notorious emperor Elagabalus notoriously identified himself. They speak, too, of the Emesan cult that honours god and emperor still - to Timothy's clear if furtive fascination. |[[Sand Stories]] | | |} ==Further Stories== *After completing [[The Affair of the Absent Friend]], Dr. al-Adim will ask for one of four Languages, which impact the outcome of the event. **If provided with [[Ramsund]] or [[Killasimi]], he will gain [[Inspired]], Agenda: Stone Consumed, and Fear: Devourers. This will conclude the Further Story. **If provided with [[Kernewek Henavek|Henavek]] or [[Cracktrack]], he will gain [[Inspired]] and Agenda: Stone Remembered. This will conclude the Further Story. *After completing [[The Affair of the Dappled Rose]], Dr. al-Adim will ask for any material the library has concerning Miah. **If provided with [[Book of Miah]], he will gain [[Inspired]], Agenda: Peace, and Fear: Carapace. This will conclude the Further Story. *After completing [[The Affair of the Other Horizon]] Dr. al-Adim will ask for a Sea Stories or Door and Wall 10 book or Manuscript. **If provided with a suitable book such as [[The Messenger Awaiting Her Destination]], he'll be able to send the delegate off, gaining [[Inspired]], [[Agenda|Agenda: Peace]] and [[Fear|Fear: Ys]], leaving you with a Bronze [[Tally|Spintria]] for the trouble. ==Trivia== *Dr al-Adim also appeared in ''[https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Cultist_Simulator_Wiki Cultist Simulator]'' as a Patron who could give commissions for {{Lore|Lantern}} or Secret Histories Lore. Secret Histories does not appear in ''Book of Hours'', but {{Lore|Rose}} and {{Lore|Moon}} encapsulate many of the same themes, which is likely why al-Adim has an interest in {{Lore|Rose}}. *In ''Cultist Simulator'', Dr al-Adim is notably missing the "Mortal" aspect, suggesting he is immortal. It has been speculated that he may be a member of the House of Lethe, which had an Aleppine branch, but this is contradictory with his willingness to interact with the outside world. *Dr Ibn al-Adim is probably the same person as [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibn_al-Adim Kamal al-Din ʻUmar ibn Aḥmad Ibn al-Adim], a 13th century Arab biographer and historian from Aleppo. *Per his conversation with [[Mlle Margot Matutine]], he was not old enough to have met [['Abbot Thomas'|Abbot Thomas]] during the [[Solar Gothic Period]]. That places his birth, at the earliest, in the 11th century. *According to the text after Dr. al-Adim acts on The Affair of the Dappled Rose, his pattron is The Vagabond. Her being ad-Adim's patron might also lend credence to Dr. al-Adim being associated with [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Obliviates The House of Lethe], as The Vagabond is likely at least partially responsible for the House of Lethe's founding. [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]]

Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.).title: Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)
Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.).text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Lt_Arthur_Thomas_Moore.png |principle1={{Lore|Edge}} |principle2={{Lore|Lantern}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Aramaic]], [[Latin]], [[Sabazine]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |relationships=[[DI Douglas Moore]] (nephew) |address=c/o the Endeavour Club, Park Place, London}} {{quote|Hero, pilgrim, traitor. He'll always be a soldier, but never again can he be only a soldier.}}
'''Lt Arthur Thomas Moore''' is a potential [[visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Edge}} and {{Lore|Lantern}}. He is a potential Secretary Vigilant for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. Moore can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Sabazine]]. ==Invitations and Salons== Moore requires 3 {{Lore|Lantern}} to be invited to Hush House. He preferes {{Lore|Edge}} food and drink. If attending a [[Salon]] alongside [[DI Douglas Moore]], there is a chance that they will interact and learn that their surnames matching is not a coincidence - Arthur is Douglas' uncle. This adds an aspect to each character denoting their connection. ==Salon Conversations== {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation !1st Lesson !Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Arthur and al-Adim are discussing the dyes and dyers of the city of Tyre. |[[Inks of Power]] |Al-Adim asks Arthur if he ever thought to grow Long, but Arthur shakes his head. 'Too many sacrifices - too many more. I know your patroness is gentler. But I will not pay the price, nor have others pay it for me.' |[[Auroral Contemplations]] |- |[[Daymare]] |Dagmar and Arthur discuss 'transinhabitation' - the means by which Lantern-long and similar Mansus entities may manifest in mirrors and lights. (Dagmar deprecates the term 'scrining', which she considers 'cheap'.) |[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]] |Dagmar and Arthur toast past glories, and count the wars where their shifting nationalities have put them on opposing sides. |[[Ragged Crossroads]] |- | [[DI Douglas Moore]] |Douglas and Arthur have a businesslike chat about the Edge dyad known as Dearday and Torgue, and the trouble they've caused over the years. ... which is abruptly derailed when Douglas, who is after all a detective, pierces the veil of discretion surrounding Arthur's family history and realises that the concidence of surnames is not a coincidence, and that he's Arthur's great-nephew. Douglas' emotions are manifest only in his repetition of the phrase 'Well, I'll be blowed', and an unusually long handshake at the evening's end.
[Douglas and Arthur realised that they were family. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Disciplines of the Scar]] |Douglas greets Arthur with a handshake and an 'Uncle'. Arthur addresses him smilingly as 'young Douggie.' Then both men hesitate, clearly grappling with the reminder that Douglas looks twenty years older than Arthur. When he next speaks, Douglas' voice cracks just for a moment. Then they spend the rest of the evening talking very practically about Edge-long. |[[Disciplines of the Scar]] |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] |Arun and Arthur are reminiscing about the city of Pune, though Arun has not visited it, he confides, since the time of the Maratha Empire. 'One exile after another; the pentiment's fate. Exile is addictive. You'll learn that too.' |[[Sickle & Eclipse]] |Arthur and Arun are discussing which forbidden weapons should be permitted, and which weapons have been permitted too long. Arthur is concerned by rumours of Dawnbreaker experiments in Britain; Arun is bragging, a little, about his experiences with the terrible feather called the Imhullune Tectrix. |[[Sharps]] |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] |Arthur speaks of the light that supposedly dwelt in the Wood before the coming of the Gods-from-Light: he suggests it might be the redder Sun of the gods-who-were-stone. Serena thinks it is simply fire - 'if we can ever say 'simply' of the Wood.' |[[Pyroglyphics]] |Serena and Arthur discuss the Red Flower of the Watchman's Tree in hushed voices. Serena recalls ways that the Serapeum has used the ithast's arts to preserve knowledge even in a book that is burnt... |[[Pyroglyphics]] |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Yvette is fascinated by the language-of-signs called Sabazine, in which Arthur is proficient. He teaches her a few signs, but she grows suddenly frightened and asks him to stop. |[[Sabazine]] |Yvette raises the subject of Sabazine again with Athur. She has been reading of the god Sabazos, who brings madness by deploying the weapons of speech-in-silence. Arthur has heard of these techniques, and very cautiously shares a very little… |[[Sharps]] |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Stanislav and Arthur argue happily about which herbal tisane tastes the most disgusting, and hence is most useful to speed lingering guests on their way. |[[Herbs & Infusions]] |Stanislav and Arthur discuss the herbs of Persia, and their uses in the infirmary of the Labyrinth of Lions. |[[Herbs & Infusions]] |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] |Chaima and Arthur are discussing the difficulties of desert campaigns, in Algeria and in Persia; the clarity of the stars; the ubiquity of sand; the tales told at the water's edge. |[[Sand Stories]] |Arthur and Chaima are talking guns. Chaima is disparaging about the reliability of the Berthier rifles once issued to her Goumier unit, but she and Arthur are both keenly interested in recent work of the Manufacture d'Armes de Saint-Étienne company… and both concerned about where to commission 'noble ammunition' for the new weapons. |[[Disciplines of the Hammer]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Hokobald is lecturing Arthur on the strategy and tactics of the War of the Roads - specifically, the ways in which the natures of the Sovereigns of the Leashed Flame became manifest through their choices in battle. Arthur listens politely.
[Hokobald lectured Arthur on the War of the Roads. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Meniscate Reflections]] |Hokobald picks up where he left off, lecturing Arthur on the strategies of the Leashed Flame in the War of the Roads in a knowledgeable but hectoring sort of way. Arthur, again, listens politely; but bridles when Hokobald speaks sneeringly of the Flame's remnant, the Endeavour Club, where Arthur has friends. Hokobald becomes scaldingly contemptuous; Arthur, bitterly polite; and the converation ends. |[[Meniscate Reflections]] |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] |Connie and Arthur are discussing Teresa Galmier's work on the enigmatic power known as 'Janus', with slightly strained professional courtesy. |[[Watchman's Paradoxes]] |Arthur and Connie are rather stiffly discussing the New King's projects. Both of them seem wary of each other. |[[Disciplines of the Hammer]] |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] |Morgen smilingly entreats Arthur to speak to her of the 'Flaw in the Glass' - the menace that [[Omar, the Blaze]] identified in the enclosure of a sacred flame at the Labyrinth of Lions. She is at her most charming, and even Arthur - not a man one might expect to be susceptible to Morgen's charms - unbends enough to drop a few hints. |[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]] |Morgen presses Arthur again on the 'Flaw in the Glass' identified in the enclosure of a sacred flame at the Labyrinth of Lions - and on its connection to the Chandler. He is on his guard this time, but he does allow that a connection might 'come alive' with sufficient Lantern and Knock - and that this is why the Labyrinth permits no Knock-adepts to enter the enclosure. |[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]] |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Arthur and Olympe debate the hypothetical City Unbuilt, the dwelling-place of perfect balance. Olympe suggests it might be achievable in the Moon-marches, or even the House of the Moon. Arthur believes it's better as an unachievable ideal - especially since the Meniscate, the Hour of perfect balance, is one of the trio of Chancel Hours, and the other two might prefer to limit her power by forbidding the City. |[[Meniscate Reflections]] |Olympe is interested in a Ramsund-inscribed altar to the Beach-Crow that Arthur found in a cliff-grotto near Trebizond. He sketches some of the signs for her. |[[Ramsund]] |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Arthur and Ehsan discuss Anaël Verdier's account of the ascent of the 'Unwise Mortal' to the heights of the Mansus - perhaps even to the Glory - and how he, perhaps, succeeded when so many others failed. 'I learnt in my time here' - Ehsan gestures to indicate the House - 'that it can be as important who witnesses a deed, as who performs it.' Arthur nods, slowly. |[[Watchman's Paradoxes]] |Arthur speaks of the lightsmithing arts practised at the Labyrinth of Lions; Ehsan offers to show Arthur the stained glass windows in the chapel of Hush House after the meal ('with your permission, Librarian'?). |[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]] |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Arthur and Fraser are discussing the Althiban Abyss near Baghdad. Fraser hopes the power that stirs there might be connected to the Carapace Cross, but Arthur firmly dissuades him: if once it was Cross, he says, it belongs to something else now.
[After a conversation with Arthur, Fraser was tempted to visit the Althiban Abyss. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Coil & Chasm]] |Fraser had, it seemed, ignored Arthur's warnings about the Althiban Abyss, and had travelled there hoping to find a great remnant of the Carapace Cross - perhaps even a lost dragon. Just as Arthur warned him, he found something hatched and grown in a decaying tendril of the Seven-Coils - something that had acquired the Worm-nature. 'I had known it was possible for the Cross to turn,' he laments, 'but I had hoped never to see it.' |[[Coil & Chasm]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Arthur and Zachary reminisce about London at night - how it has changed, and how they have changed. |[[Ragged Crossroads]] |Zachary and Arthur discuss a prophecy of the War of the Roads, in which the Imperishable Legions war with the Leashed Flame, to apocalyptic effect. Arthur fears that the prophecy is not yet complete - that it refers to a coming war in Europe. Zachary agrees, but finds it difficult to articulate his reasons - he says that the Imperishable Legions are not the Légion du Seuil, but (gesturing, ever gesturing) that they are 'yoked at the Heart.' |[[Ragged Crossroads]] |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |Arthur has been describing the mirror-mazes of the Labyrinth of Lions to a smiling Azita - but now he seems to grow suspicious of her motives in questioning him, and he withdraws. |[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]] |Azita is describing her experiences in the Mansus to Arthur - who, it seems, has never passed the Stag Door, though he speaks fondly of its watchman. |[[Watchman's Paradoxes]] |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Coquille and Arthur are discussing the perils of family; the Crime of the Sky; the tragedy of Matthias and the Amethyst Imago. Coquille is at her most charming, and Arthur is at his most watchful. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |Once again, Arthur and Coquille are discussing the perils of family, birth, and marriage. Coquille has begun to hint that she would enjoy an introduction to one of Arthur's younger and more eligible relatives. A coil of dark hair dangles artlessly across one flawless cheek. Her teeth and eyes are very bright. Arthur, unmoved as a fortress under fire, repeatedly steers the conversation back to the businesses of blood. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Arthur and Corso are discussing Ericapaean - a language that both of them are struggling to master. They agree to correspond in that language, although Corso points out that it'll probably get their post opened by the Suppression Bureau.
[Corso and Arthur agreed to correspond in Ericapaean. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Ericapaean]] |Corso and Arthur have, it seems, been corresponding clumsily in half-learnt Ericapaean. Arthur has made more progress: he explains, very quietly, that he has had help from Julian Coseley. 'Is he actually alive?' Corso asks sceptically. 'Alive? What's alive?' responds Arthur. 'Is the Empire alive?' |[[Ericapaean]] |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Arthur and Agdistis are talking, softly and seriously, about those absences which scar. 'I still miss him: Arthur says. Agdistis squeezes his hand and quotes in Greek: 'Roses by the head, jasmine at the feet …' |[[Disciplines of the Scar]] |Agdistis invites Arthur to visit him in Berlin, but Arthur shakes his head. 'I can do without the temptation. The old ties would be too much for me. The War, I mean. We both know what's coming.' |[[Auroral Contemplations]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] | | | | |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] | | | | |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Reverend Timothy is in possession of a manuscript on ink-mixing that he proudly believes originated in the Labyrinth of Lions. He and Arthur discuss the  content and provenance until at last it becomes apparent, to Timothy's obvious disappointment, that it's a  much more recent forgery.  |[[Inks of Revelation]] |Timothy and Arthur are discussing Isaac of Karth's History of the Shadowless Kings. Arthur is sceptical of Isaac of Karth's reliability; Timothy is a ferocious admirer. |[[Sand Stories]] |} ==Incidents== Moore can visit for the following [[incident]]s: *[[The Affair of the Absent Friend]] *[[The Affair of the Forgivable Debt]] *[[The Affair of the Particular Mystique]] *[[The Affair of the Royal Endeavour]] *[[The Affair of the Second Skin]] *[[The Affair of the Threshold Revolution]] *[[The Affair of the Unfettered Eye]] ==Further Stories== *After completing [[The Affair of the Second Skin]], Arthur can be spoken with. **After speaking with him, you gain Lesson: Echidna's Prowlings, which has the following text: I know that the Ligeian Echidna prowls the empty places. [Consider this with the strongest of your Coil & Chasm, Pentiments & Precursors, Serpents & Venoms or Wolf Stories skills. You'll learn how to invite Echidna to Brancrug. ] **You then have the choice of feeding him to Echidna, or giving him [[De Horis book 3|De Horis Book 3]] or the [[Manuscript]] on [[Coil & Chasm]] (12) (Note: there are no suitable [[Readable|Readables]] with that or higher Mystery level). ***If you choose to feed him to Echidna, he will be removed from the visitor deck, and no longer visit for [[Incident|Incidents]]. In return, you will be able to use Echidna as you Secretary Persistent, and she has relevant aspects Agenda: Corrivality, Agenda: Secrecy, Agenda: Stone Consumed, and [[Inspired]]. She also can teach [[Hyksos]] and [[Killasimi]]. She will not attend salons as she has the Unsociable aspect. ***If you choose to give him the book, Arthur will give Echidna the slip and become [[Inspired]] and receive Fear: Devourers. *After completing [[The Affair of the Absent Friend]], Arthur can be spoken with **When speaking with him, you will get three options to answer Medusa's Riddle, all asking you to input one of three languages that Arthur needs a word in to answer; ***If given Ericapaean, Arthur will gain Inspired and Agenda: Revelations ***If given Ramsund, Arthur will gain Inspired, Agenda: Stone Devoured and Fear: Devourers ***If given Killasami, Arthur will gain Inspired, Agenda: Stone Devoured and Fear: Devourers ==Hidden Interaction== {{Spoilers | caption = This section is about a hidden interaction. | content =
While visiting, the Librarian can present Moore with ''[[The Sun's Design]]'' to receive one ''[[Auroral Contemplations|Lesson: Auroral Contemplations]]'' and an [[Occult Scrap]]. This only works once, and he will not disappear after this interaction.
{{Quote|'A very great treasure, Librarian -'

'I cannot read this script, Librarian, but I have seen it before, and it was translated to me - by one I held very dear. Long ago, you see, I made my own pilgrimage to the sanctuary of Elagabalus... though in that country they still call him Ilah al-Gabal. May I examine the stone?' [Moore will examine the book and return it to you. He won't leave until his other business is concluded.]

'If Death's direction is down, and Eternity's is up, which directions do we assign to Life and to History? It is a frequent topic of discussion, at the Labyrinth. I wonder, sometimes, if my teachers have nothing better to do with all those years of learning... but in the Labyrinth, more than any other place I have been, even Emesa, Sun and Stone and Silence are the first constants.'}} }}
==Trivia== Arthur Thomas Moore is a fictive equivalent of a real life Irish [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Thomas_Moore Major General of the same name]. This is made explicit in a letter posted on the Weather Factory website.https://weatherfactory.biz/tabriz-january-1866/ [[Category:Visitor]] [[Category:People]] [[Category:Hidden Interactions]]

Magister Hokobald.title: Magister Hokobald
Magister Hokobald.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Magister Hokobald.png |principle1={{Lore|Forge}} |principle2={{Lore|Grail}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Aramaic]], [[Deep Mandaic]], [[Greek]], [[Latin]], [[Phrygian]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |address=A reluctantly disclosed PO box in Dover.}} {{Quote|Metallurgist, gourmet, corrupted immortal. And, supposedly, a long-ago king's by-blow.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Forge}} and {{Lore|Grail}}. He is a potential Treasurer for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. He can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Deep Mandaic]]. Hokobald of Pocsind is an Alukite and a {{Lore|Forge}} Long, who was formerly a member of the order of immortals called the [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/The_House_of_Lethe House of Lethe] (later known as the the Ordo Limiae, currently known as the Fraternity of Obliviates), before being expelled for committing the [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/Crime_of_the_Sky Crime of the Sky]. As a speaker of Deep Mandaic, he may have been born in the [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/The_Shadowless_Kings Shadowless Empire]. [[Ambrose Westcott]] named a [[Hokobald|hunting trophy of his]] after him. He has authored ''[[My Deeds, My Powers, My Achievements and the Injustices Perpetrated Against Me]]''. == Invitations & Salons == Hokobald requires an invitation written in [[Orpiment Exultant]] to be invited to Hush House. He will only consume food and drink with {{Lore|Forge}} aspect. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation !1st Lesson !Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] |Hokobald and Dagmar discuss the work of Willem Harries, with particular reference to lintels and thresholds. Hokobald’s habitual air of contempt thins – he listens with real interest to Dagmar’s answers – but Dagmar retains a careful distance, and, after he arranges her plate and tea-spoon to illustrate her point, she eyes them sidelong and does not touch them again. |[[Door & Wall]] |Hokobald has a proposal for a ‘nine-arched wind-door’ which he hopes to construct on Dagmar’s estate. Dagmar is clearly interested in the project, but firmly refuses to let Hokobald use her estate, or even visit it. Hokobald grinds his teeth, but keeps his temper. |[[Door & Wall]] |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Hokobald speaks to al-Adim of the final Pilgrimage of Seven that the Vagabond supposedly intends - up the Mansus and beyond, into the Glory. He gloatingly explains why he believes her Pilgrimage will fail. Al-Adim disagrees; he thinks that, eventually, it will succeed; but the prospect clearly makes him unhappy. (It may be, in fact, that this was Hokobald's intention in raising the matter...) |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |Hokobald expounds on his belief that the Great Ink called Orpiment Exultant is - or will become - a Name of the Chandler. Al-Adim listens first with incredulity, but then with sceptical interest. |[[Inks of Power]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] | | | | |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] |Arun strokes Hokobald’s arm and whispers about the ‘pleasures of the Princes’. Hokobald’s response can best be described as ‘angry curiosity’. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |Arun and Hokobald are debating the truth of a rumour about Winter-long: that they cannot sire or birth children, and so can safely lie together without fear of the Crime of the Sky. Hokobald insists that even were that true, the fruitfulness of Grail-long – or the vigour of Forge-long – would still allow conception. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] |Hokobald and Serena are speculating about the nature and possible identity of the still-nascent Hour referred to as the Chandler, who carries fire in darkness; who leaves a place without entering it; whose endeavours are profitable. Serena thinks it possible the Chandler may manifest through the New King. Hokobald shakes his great head. 'A name attends him, certainly. But no more than a Name.' |[[Transformations & Liberations]] | | |- | [[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Yvette asks Hokobald whether there are ways to determine who might be a child of two Long. He insists with apparent pride that it is very rare for the children of Long to survive - that one of their parents almost always devours them and 'ascends' to alukite status - but acknowledges that it has been known, under rare circumstances, and shares some of the signs... |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |Hokobald demands to know whether Yvette ever hears the bells of Ys when she’s near the sea. Yvette bridles at his tone, but answers carefully that she thinks perhaps that she might; they discuss what form the sounds might take, and Hokobald’s brusqueness softens a little. |[[Bells & Brazieries]] |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Stanislav asks Hokobald about the tradition that the Velvet makes immortals of those sufficiently savorous to be hunted by her pet, Kitling Ripe. Hokobald confidently confirms that it's so, but his explanations are derailed by rants about those immortals who ''should'' have become her victims - or who she devoured despite their blandness. (He sounds almost jealous of these last.) |[[Spices & Savours]] | | |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] |Hokobald has heard that Chaima had hunted and despatched an alukite in Tripoli a few months ago. He asks for details, which she provides. Her face is typically expressionless throughout. Hokobald asks, eyes glittering, if she has any trophies of the hunt. After a long pause, in which her face remains expressionless, she says that she does not. |[[Disciplines of the Hammer]] |Chaima speculates about the manner in which she might hunt and defeat Hokobald. Hokobald describes the manner in which he might ensnare and devour her. It is difficult to be sure how much each of them is really enjoying the conversation. |[[Disciplines of the Hammer]] |- | [[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Hokobald is lecturing Arthur on the strategy and tactics of the War of the Roads - specifically, the ways in which the natures of the Sovereigns of the Leashed Flame became manifest through their choices in battle. Arthur listens politely.
[Hokobald lectured Arthur on the War of the Roads. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Meniscate Reflections]] |Hokobald picks up where he left off, lecturing Arthur on the strategies of the Leashed Flame in the War of the Roads in a knowledgeable but hectoring sort of way. Arthur, again, listens politely; but bridles when Hokobald speaks sneeringly of the Flame's remnant, the Endeavour Club, where Arthur has friends. Hokobald becomes scaldingly contemptuous; Arthur, bitterly polite; and the converation ends. |[[Meniscate Reflections]] |- | [[MCO Constance Lee]] |Hokobald grandiosely condescends to share information about the depredations of a Grail-long and associated coven in Maremma. Connie listens carefully, her expression neutral. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |Connie questions Hokobald narrowly about recent mephitic manifestations on the Swiss-German border. Hokobald denies any involvement, and argues plausibly that these may be the first signs of the emergence of another Chandler-name... |[[Pyroglyphics]] |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] |Hokobald attends Morgen with a kind of surly, lascivious obsequiousness, and she permits him to talk to her about the jewels he has brought for her, occasionally offering different opinions to which Hokobald pays due attention. At the end of the conversation, to his evident perplexity, she gives him a cabochon sapphire ‘to hold on to.’ |[[Anbary & Lapidary]] |Last time, Morgen gave Hokobald a cabochon sapphire; he now returns it, sneering at the obviousness of her 'trap'. His manner towards her has changed from surly obsequiousness to surly menace, although the lascivious undertone remains. Morgen insists laughingly that it was 'only a little game,' and though Hokobald plainly doesn't believe her, he decides in the end to accept the excuse - perhaps for the sake of their tenuous alukite un-kinship. |[[Anbary & Lapidary]] |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Hokobald and Olympe share a series of peculiar meditations on chrysalides and crossroads. ‘It will never be as it was,’ she says, several times, softly. |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |Olympe and Hokobald exchange elliptical observations about lymph, wine, choroid, and chitin.
