She pats his hand and smiles; he shrugs his vast shoulders. |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Hokobald admits in a subterranean growl that even though – or perhaps – because of his Forge-long status, the sea airs of Brancrug cause his joints to stiffen. ‘To rust, perhaps?’ Ehsan enquires blandly. In response to Hokobald’s glare, he apologises, and prescribes a tisane. |[[Herbs & Infusions]] |Hokobald and Ehsan discuss the origin of the Amiranis Beteli, the inscribed stone of secrets which fell from the sky, perhaps before the departure of the Cross. Ehsan believes the inscriptions were the work of Ys, after the meteorite struck the sea; Hokobald insists they were a ‘Gleam-gift’ from a Star (and also insists that Ehsan is a ‘pug-faced lion-fewmet’ when Ehsan dissents). |[[Bells & Brazieries]] |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Hokobald negotiates the purchase, from Fraser, of certain exotic alloys. He presses Fraser on the availability of Ys-metal, but Fraser, glancing around nervously, insists that he can provide no such thing. |[[Bells & Brazieries]] |Fraser and Hokobald bicker about whether Henavek - the language-spirit sometimes called 'the Eldest' belongs to the Wood or to the Mansus. |[[Kernewek Henavek|Henavek]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Zachary and Hokobald discuss the Sun’s division, which Zachary suspects is an outcome of a ‘conspiracy of heaven’, and Hokobald insists was ‘the Great Work of Destiny’. |[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars]] |Hokobald insists impatiently to Zachary that it is a crime not to yield to his ‘burgeoning nature’, and that he should 'get on with the devouring.’ Zachary firmly but quietly dissents. |[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars]] |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |Hokobald challenges Azita to an arm-wrestling match. She accepts with enthusiasm. For the sake of decorum, they leave the room to conduct the match. When they return, It becomes apparent that Hokobald has won; but that his wrist is broken. ‘That shouldn’t happen! It should not be permitted!’ he keeps whining, through gritted teeth. Azita only shrugs.
[Hokobald and Azita arm-wrestled. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Disciplines of the Hammer]] |Last time, Azita and Hokobald arm-wrestled, and though he won, Hokobald’s wrist was broken. This time, he demands another match. Azita refuses; after some minutes of wheedling she tells him, with a flash of temper, that last time she let him win, and he won’t be so lucky another time. Hokobald, enraged, refuses to believe her; they spend the next half hour arguing the merits of the unstoppable force and the immovable object. |[[Disciplines of the Hammer]] |- | [[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Coquille is flirting outrageously with Hokobald. His head is tilted to one side and he is staring at her with a furnace gaze that might equally indicate lust or hunger. His mouth is stringed with saliva. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |Hokobald and Coquille continue their unnerving flirtation. She strokes his bald head and murmurs estimates of the measurements of the bones of her pelvis and rib-cage. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Corso has bought a Deep Mandaic cylinder seal as a gift for Hokobald – ‘because, Magister, there are so few who might appreciate it.’ While Hokobald is thus gratified, he brings out a collection of similar cylinder seals, and secures Hokobald’s opinion and advice on their authenticity… |[[Deep Mandaic]] |Corso adroitly flatters Hokobald into an impromptu lesson in the sigillography of Deep Mandaic. |[[Deep Mandaic]] |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Agdistis and Hokobald have a scrupulously polite conversation about acoustics, resonance, and bellringing in the churches of London. |[[Bells & Brazieries]] |Hokobald and Agdistis discuss the possibility of a ballet of bells. Agdistis becomes sufficiently engaged to smile at Hokobald, despite his clear suspicion of that corrupt immortal… |[[Bells & Brazieries]] |- | [[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Hokobald asks Mr Kille whether he works with other materials than wood. Mr Kille gets up, bows deeply, says that he regrets that he does not, and leaves the room for several minutes. When he returns, he is careful not to sit near Hokobald. |[[Memory: Fear]] |Mr and Mrs Kille sit as far away from Hokobald as possible. Neither of them will look at him. |[[Memory: Fear]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |Hokobald condescendingly shares some of his personal theories on the 'Great Debasement', and its metallurgical consequences. Denzil chews his food slowly and says nothing at all. |[[Bells & Brazieries]] |Hokobald presses Denzil on the coastal tales of the deep bells of Ys. Denzil grudgingly shares scraps gleaned from his father. |[[Bells & Brazieries]] |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Hokobald is pressing Reverend Timothy on the New King – particularly, on the claims by some prelates that he may be associated with the Second Dawn, even though that might seem to conflict with the Received Version of the Book of Suns. Hokobald’s aim is clearly malice. Timothy clearly realizes this, and he is also clearly quite frightened of Hokobald. He remains polite, although pale and unusually quiet. |[[Purifications & Exaltations]] |Hokobald has questions on the stained glass windows in the chapel of Hush House, and their depictions of the Hours. Reverend Timothy – who has long been passionately interested in the history and architecture of the House – is eager to share what he knows, but is clearly nervous that Hokobald may have some ulterior interest. Hokobald, however, evinces nothing but genuine (if condescending) curiosity. |[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]] |} ==Incidents== Hokobald can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of 'Apollo and Marsyas']] *[[The Affair of the Invisible Opera]] *[[The Affair of the Oriflamme Heist]] *[[The Affair of the Royal Endeavour]] *[[The Affair of the Threshold Revolution]] *[[The Affair of the Unfinished Lark]] ==Further Stories== * After completing [[The Affair of the Unfettered Eye]], Hokobald is an option to discuss the Incident despite not visiting during it. ** First discussing it with him opens a choice between himself, Serena, and Corso. ** Hokobald requests a [[Transformations & Liberations]] Manuscript with Mystery 14, or [[Each Flame His Fuel|"a work of Omar's which touched on relevant truths"]]. *** If given the latter, Hokobald gains [[Inspired]], Agenda: Better Gods, and Sympathy: Chandler. He rewards the Librarian with an [[Inkling]] and a [[Tally|Bronze Spintria]]. ==Hidden interactions== {{Spoilers|caption=This section contains information on hidden interactions.|content=
While visiting, the Librarian can present Hokobald with the book he has written to receive rewards. This only works once, and he will leave after this discussion and will not return for the current incident (if one is active).
Presenting Hokobald with ''[[My Deeds, My Powers, My Achievements and the Injustices Perpetrated Against Me]]'' rewards the Librarian with a [[Tally|Gold Spintria]] and the following dialogue: {{Quote|'Is that...?'

'I had feared no copies yet remained! There is so much despite in the world - so much needless contumely - so much contempt for hard-earned wisdom - forgive me. I will purchase this treasure from you - if you are prepared to give it up. A gold spintria?' [Hokobald will take the book and depart, forgetting about any current Incident.]

I have been so very greatly wronged. But I am capable of wreaking wrongs yet greater. My dear Librarian, bon appetit}}}} ==Trivia== *Hokobald's introduction will change according to the [[Season]]: {{Quote|And this is what you call summer?? Pathetic. Don't make me stand around out here.|In Summer}}{{Quote|What a grim and chilly little country. I hope you've prepared a suitable welcome.|In other seasons}} [[Category:Authors]] [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]] [[Category:Hidden Interactions]]

DI Douglas Moore.title: DI Douglas Moore
DI Douglas Moore.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=DI Douglas Moore.png| |principle1={{Lore|Heart}} |principle2={{Lore|Lantern}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Greek]] |address=Suppression Bureau, Hobbs End, London}} {{Quote|Detective-Illuminate of the Suppression Bureau. A stoic, but weary, fellow. His dearest wish is to move to Chingford and grow roses. But the buggers won't let him retire.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Heart}} and {{Lore|Lantern}}. He is a potential Secretary Vigilant for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation !1st Lesson !Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] |Dagmar is hectoring Douglas on Suppression Bureau overreach, but he just sits quietly smiling with his arms folded and every so often names another incident sinister enough to need Bureau intervention: 'Rheims', or 'Revek' or 'Treowen' or 'the Wildwood Club'. Each of these puts Dagmar on the back foot, but she rallies and explains why each in turn is different; this at least gives Douglas time to sip his drink or pack his pipe. |[[Edicts Inviolable]] |With the ghoulish camaraderie of two pensioners in a retirement home, Douglas and Dagmar discuss the details of their medical issues, and their subsequent surgeries. |[[Surgeries & Exsanguinations]] |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Al-Adim is spinning tales of his travels, in the mountains of Persia, the taiga of the farthest East, the snows of Antarctica ... Douglas listens, enraptured. 'Sometimes,' he says gruffly, 'I wish I'd done things different.' |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |Douglas and al-Adim are trying to work out whether the unusual nature of al-Adim's ascension to Longhood - under the Vagabond - actually means he hasn't actually broken any British laws. They decide that he probably has, but Douglas is very practical about the difficulties of arresting him, and offers to let him off with a caution if he doesn't ever ascend to immortality again. |[[Edicts Inviolable]] |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] |Arun is concerned about the progress of a recent candidate for Lantern-longhood: he shares names and details with Douglas. 'Knife, noose, flame, word, hm? I don't like it; but I don't like this aspirant either.' |[[Maggephene Mysteries]] |Douglas has tracked down the Long-in-the-making of whom Arun warned him last time. Arun congratulates him; Douglas describes, with distaste, the empty eyes of his target's victims… |[[Maggephene Mysteries]] |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] |Douglas and Serena discuss a shared, concealed, but evidently profound passion for knitting. Douglas: 'If you tell anyone outside this room, I'll have you locked up.' Serena: 'If ''you'' tell anyone outside this room, I'll give King Crucible your address.' |[[Weaving & Knotworking]] |Serena and Douglas have discovered a shared passion for knitting; they show each other examples of their works. Douglas says absent-mindedly, 'There's a prophecy among the weavers of one who unwisely seeks to find out the future...' Serena recoils in surprise, and Douglas grumbles: 'No-one ever thinks I've read a bleedin' book.' |[[Weaving & Knotworking]] |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] | | | | |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Douglas has been looking into the six-centuries-past death of Abbess Nonna. He’s questioned unspecified sources that he doesn’t share with Stanislav, and concludes that Nonna was possessed by a Name of the Blackbone and ‘put down’ by her sistren – ‘nasty business, but best thing for it.’ He and Stanislav discuss the herb-mixtures that might have laid her open to that possession. |[[Herbs & Infusions]] | | |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] |Chaima and Douglas are discussing Ilse Bischoff's experimental film ''The Open Head''. 'I saw it in Alexandria,' Chaima offers. 'I think perhaps she was moved by a dream of the Chandler - that when it emerges, it will emerge from war - and from knowledge unwisely shared.' Douglas sucks on his pipe. 'Mrs M wanted to see it,' he says morosely. 'She likes that Buñuel too.' He sucks on his pipe again. 'I don't like that Buñuel.' |[[Disciplines of the Scar]] |Douglas and Chaima are enjoying a very practical conversation about what to do when someone bites you, what to do when something bites you, and what to do when someone bites something else. |[[Stitching & Binding]] |- |[[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Douglas and Arthur have a businesslike chat about the Edge dyad known as Dearday and Torgue, and the trouble they've caused over the years. ... which is abruptly derailed when Douglas, who is after all a detective, pierces the veil of discretion surrounding Arthur's family history and realises that the concidence of surnames is not a coincidence, and that he's Arthur's great-nephew. Douglas' emotions are manifest only in his repetition of the phrase Well, I'll be blowed', and an unusually long handshake at the evening's end. [Douglas and Arthur realised that they were family. [These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.]] |[[Disciplines of the Scar]] |Douglas greets Arthur with a handshake and an 'Uncle'. Arthur addresses him smilingly as 'young Douggie.' Then both men hesitate, clearly grappling with the reminder that Douglas looks twenty years older than Arthur. When he next speaks, Douglas' voice cracks just for a moment. Then they spend the rest of the evening talking very practically about Edge-long. |[[Disciplines of the Scar]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] | | | | |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] |Douglas and Connie are talking shop; the kind of shop that requires them to spill salt on the table after naming certain entities, and not to name others at all, but rather to refer to them as 'the spiky royal one', 'the bluey one with the temper', and 'the glossy one'. |[[Maggephene Mysteries]] |Douglas and Connie reminisce about old cases, and cheerfully speculate about the final fate of adepts they’ve locked up. |[[Edicts Inviolable]] |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] | | | | |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Douglas warns Olympe darkly of the dangers of knitting before sleep, and the paths it can open in the Wood. ('Yes, I knit. Gentlemen can knit.') |[[Weaving & Knotworking]] | | |- | [[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] | | | | |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Fraser complains to Douglas about break-ins. Douglas unsympathetically suggests that Fraser might want to keep less contraband on the premises, then. |[[Wolf Stories]] |Fraser would like to know what Douglas proposes to 'do about Raw Prophets: Douglas doesn't plan to do anything about Raw Prophets. Fraser would like to know, then, what the Bureau intends to do about Raw Prophets. Douglas expresses his confusion. Fraser expresses his irritation. Douglas expresses his inability to do anything about Raw Prophets. Both men agree that Raw Prophets aren't the kind of thing you can really do anything about. |[[Stone Stories]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Douglas tries to reminisce with Zachary about their shared work at the Suppression Bureau - the time they had to suppress a Percussigiant troupe which was roaming the Forest of Dean. But Zachary only stares and shakes his head - 'I don't remember' - 'I don't remember' - 'I remember that it was cold' - 'I don't remember'. |[[Quenchings & Quellings]] | | |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] | | | | |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Coquille smilingly asks Douglas to remind her if there is an arrest warrant out for her just now. 'Not just now,' he replies, 'but I'm sure we can sort something out.' Coquille spends much of the rest of the meal quoting from Zahra's 'Time of Division', and asking which bits would get her arrested if she recited them at a cocktail party. [Coquille asked incautious questions of Douglas. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Surgeries & Exsanguinations]] | | |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Douglas and Corso discuss the nuances of the differences in the Received and Sanctioned versions of the Book of Suns… once Corso's got over his surprise at Douglas' interests. ('No-one ever bleeding believes I got a bleeding scholarship,' Douglas grumbles.) |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |Douglas and Corso chat affably about church. (Douglas used to be a chapel-goer, but Mrs Moore disapproves.) |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Douglas and Agdistis speak of the Ecdysis Club, where Agdistis once worked and which Douglas had a hand in closing down. Douglas is unrepentant, but also regretful. |[[Drums & Dances]] |Douglas has been to a performance of Keirle's Ceaseless - for assessment of oneiric hazard, not for pleasure, but he took Mrs Moore ('free tickets is free tickets;) and both enjoyed it - Douglas much more than they expected. Agdistis is more than happy to discuss Keirle's work. |[[Weaving & Knotworking]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Douglas is commissioning a very particular coffin from Mr Kille: lightning-struck wood, copper bands (which Mr Kille says doubtfully that he hopes Denzil can do), and the whole not to be allowed to touch the earth before Douglas takes delivery... |[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]] |Douglas asks Mr Kille whether any of the occupants of his coffins have ever caused 'difficulties' before, after or during burial. Mr Kille, clearly sceptical, answers that they never have. Douglas nevertheless suggests refinements which might prevent any such misbehaviour, if it were ever to occur. |[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |Denzil and Douglas are complaining amicably about the recent decline in the quality of their preferred pipe tobacco. |[[Door & Wall]] | | |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Douglas and Reverend Timothy happily discuss the raising of roses. |[[Leaves & Thorns]] |Douglas has difficult questions for Timothy about a fugitive who has been seen along the coast. Timothy is initially evasive but crumbles almost instantly and admits that he took pity on the man in a spirit of charity, and instructed his housekeeper Terrence to take meals to the coal-cellar where the man was hiding for almost a week... |[[Memory: Hindsight]] |} ==Incidents== Moore can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of the God in the Wood]] *[[The Affair of the Grunewald Provision]] *[[The Affair of the Open Reverend]] *[[The Affair of the Particular Mystique]] *[[The Affair of the Royal Endeavour]] *[[The Affair of the Unfettered Eye]] ==Further Stories== * After completing [[The Affair of the God in the Wood]], Douglas will request [[Insects & Nectars]] 6 - [[Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1927]] suffices, and in cleaning it up, he will gain Agenda: Secrecy and Fear: Carapace, leaving you a [[Tally|Bronze Spintria]] for the trouble. * After Douglas tells what happened with the cult of Ivory Dawn, it's possible to discuss the Incident again with him or other Visitors. Douglas requests more information on Black Elie. **Giving him [[A Journey to the Grove]] will give him Inspired and [[Fear|Fear: Nowhere]] but will not conclude the Incident. **Giving him [[The Secret Colours]] will give him Inspired and [[Fear|Fear: Ys]]. This will conclude the Incident and reward the Librarian with a Bronze Spintria and an [[Inkling]]. *After completing [[The Affair of the Open Reverend|The Affair of the Open Reverend,]] Douglas will request [[Sharps]] [8] or [[Sand Stories]] [8]. Speak with him a second time and he will request anything on [[OGHKOR OGHKOR TISSILAK OGHKOR|Gnathobasis]], or [[Quenchings & Quellings|Quenchings and Quellings]] [16] or [[Wolf Stories]] [16]. **Giving him [[OGHKOR OGHKOR TISSILAK OGHKOR]] or an appropiate Quenching and Quellings text will give him Inspired, [[Fear|Fear: Nowhere]] and [[Agenda|Agenda: Secrecy.]] == Food Preferences == Douglas requires 3 [[Lantern]] to be invited to Hush House . He prefers food and drink with {{Lore|Lantern}}. [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]] == Trivia == * In ''[[Book of Hours]]''' sister work, [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Cultist_Simulator ''Cultist Simulator''], Douglas is the [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Weary_Detective Weary Detective], a Hunter working for the [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Suppression_Bureau Suppression Bureau] and a potential disciple. It is almost certain this is the same character, although the Detective - as a disciple - is associated with {{Lore|Forge}} rather than {{Lore|Lantern}} or {{Lore|Heart}}. (He retains the latter associations as a Prisoner.)

Lalla Chaima.title: Lalla Chaima
Lalla Chaima.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Lalla Chaima.png |principle1={{Lore|Edge}} |principle2={{Lore|Rose}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Aramaic]], [[Cracktrack]], [[Greek]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |address=Rue des Jardins, Hydra, Algiers}} {{quote|Huntress, goumier, occasional Bureau consultant. When it can't be killed, and it really needs killing, Chaima's the one they turn to.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[People|Visitor]] interested in {{Lore|Edge}} and {{Lore|Rose}}. She is a potential Secretary Vigilant for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. She can be paid one [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Cracktrack]]. ==Invitations and Salons== Chaima requires 3 {{Lore|Edge}} to be invited to Hush House. She prefers {{Lore|Edge}} food and drink. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation ! 1st Lesson !Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] |Dagmar is planning a visit to the Mozabite Pentapolis in Algeria 'to catch up with a wretched troublemaker.' She earnestly solicits advice on the region from Chaima (who she keeps addressing unselfconsciously as 'Charlie').
[Dagmar asked Chaima for advice on a visit to the Mazabite Pentapolis. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Sand Stories]] |Dagmar has returned from the Mazabite Pentapolis ('no sign of my friend, probably been et, but charming place, makes a gel wish she could paint.') She's full of news about the region, and Chaima is keen to hear it. Although Dagmar still seems to think she's called 'Charlie'. |[[Sand Stories]] |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Chaima listens intently while al-Adim describes the rare occasions on which labhites have been successfully brought to ground. Neither of them look happy. |[[Horns & Ivories]] |Chaima and al-Adim are comparing navigation techniques. |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] |Chaima and Douglas are discussing Ilse Bischoff's experimental film ''The Open Head''. 'I saw it in Alexandria,' Chaima offers. 'I think perhaps she was moved by a dream of the Chandler - that when it emerges, it will emerge from war - and from knowledge unwisely shared.' Douglas sucks on his pipe. 'Mrs M wanted to see it,' he says morosely. 'She likes that Buñuel too.' He sucks on his pipe again. 'I don't like that Buñuel.' |[[Disciplines of the Scar]] |Douglas and Chaima are enjoying a very practical conversation about what to do when someone bites you, what to do when something bites you, and what to do when someone bites something else. |[[Stitching & Binding]] |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] | | | | |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] |Chaima describes her defeat in the Bounds at the hands of a 'door-watcher' she names Forculus. Serena, fascinated, tries to draw her out: is Forculus truly a Name of Janus? Is Janus, then, real? Chaima denies interest in either of these questions - and adds quietly that it is unwise of Serena to ask them. |[[Auroral Contemplations]] |Serena and Chaima have both undergone the process known as Torgue's Cleansing. Serena describes it as 'horrible'. Chaima suggests instead that it is 'bracing.' |[[Disciplines of the Scar]] |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Yvette questions Chaima about the motives and credibility of 'Little Sophia', the monster-hunting, and specifically Worm-hunting, author of 'Oblations in Iron'. Chaima is non-commital, but very clear that she herself tries not to hunt Worms. |[[Inks of Containment]] |Chaima asks Yvette to interpret a dream - of a white waste west of the world where pale mutes redden the snow with the blood of a bull... |[[Snow Stories]] |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Stanislav and Chaima are discussing the treatment of wounds caused by great beasts: labhites and skaptodons; tarrasques and raveleurs; and the great serpents called Younger Sisters for their kinship with the Mother of Ants. |[[Stitching & Binding]] |Stanislav and Chaima speak of the Seven-Coiled, the 'Father of the Mother', who has passed from the world; of the seven unhuman acolytes she has inspired; of their prophecies. Chaima reflects wistfully on what a great hunt the end of the Seven-Coiled might have been... |[[Sand Stories]] |- |[[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Chaima and Arthur are discussing the difficulties of desert campaigns, in Algeria and in Persia; the clarity of the stars; the ubiquity of sand; the tales told at the water's edge. |[[Sand Stories]] |Arthur and Chaima are talking guns. Chaima is disparaging about the reliability of the Berthier rifles once issued to her Goumier unit, but she and Arthur are both keenly interested in recent work of the Manufacture d'Armes de Saint-Étienne company… and both concerned about where to commission 'noble ammunition' for the new weapons. |[[Disciplines of the Hammer]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Hokobald has heard that Chaima had hunted and despatched an alukite in Tripoli a few months ago. He asks for details, which she provides. Her face is typically expressionless throughout. Hokobald asks, eyes glittering, if she has any trophies of the hunt. After a long pause, in which her face remains expressionless, she says that she does not. |[[Disciplines of the Hammer]] |Chaima speculates about the manner in which she might hunt and defeat Hokobald. Hokobald describes the manner in which he might ensnare and devour her. It is difficult to be sure how much each of them is really enjoying the conversation. |[[Disciplines of the Hammer]] |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] |Chaima and Connie are discussing - with sorrow - the 'khalvites', those labhites who have chosen to drink what Echidna offers... |[[Wolf Stories]] | | |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] | | | | |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] | | | | |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] | | | | |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Chaima is commissioning 'noble ammunition' from Fraser, for prey which isn't so very bothered by the usual sort of bullet. |[[Disciplines of the Hammer]] |Fraser is quizzing Chaima about routes across the Algerian desert. |[[Sand Stories]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Chaima and Zachary discuss regrets, one hunter to another. |[[Ragged Crossroads]] |Zachary and Chaima talk about how it is when the hunt ends - the uneasy space before the next begins. |[[Ragged Crossroads]] |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] | | | | |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] | | | | |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Corso listens intently as Chaima describes a nasty tangle with the Reckoner Mobs - the loan-sharks of lifetime - back in the 20s… |[[Ragged Crossroads]] | | |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Chaima is describing for Agdistis one of the dances of the Rif Mountains, her home. Her shoulders twitch as if she might wish to show him, but her dignity keeps her in her seat. From his gentle smile, Agdistis has noticed. |[[Drums & Dances]] | | |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Mrs Kille and Chaima commiserate about the near-impossibility of finding decent coffee in England. |[[Spices & Savours]] |Chaima and Mr Kille discuss funerary customs across Europe and beyond. |[[Rhyme & Remembrance]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |Denzil and Chaima are engaged in some sort of contest where each of them hold the palm of a hand over candle-flame for increasingly long periods of time. Chaima provides occasional philosophical interjections. |[[Sharps]] |Denzil and Chaima sit companionably together as she demonstrates alarming tricks with her knife. |[[Sharps]] |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Timothy clearly has no idea what to say to Chaima, at least for the first few minutes. At this point he arbitrarily picks aquatic snails as a topic (he is, it seems, a keen amateur naturalist) and for so time he talks to Chaima about aquatic snails. And for some, Chaima listen to him talks about them. |[[Pearl & Tide]] |Reverend Timothy, having determined to his own satisfaction that Chaima is someone with an interest in aquatic snails, continues to talk to Chaima about aquatic snails. Chaima listens with a huntress' patience. |[[Pearl & Tide]] |} ==Incidents== {{PAGENAME}} can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of the Absent Friend]] *[[The Affair of the Dappled Rose]] *[[The Affair of the Forgivable Debt]] *[[The Affair of the Other Horizon]] *[[The Affair of the Second Skin]] *[[The Affair of the Threshold Revolution]] ==Further Stories== *After completing [[The Affair of the Threshold Revolution]] , and speaking with [[Ms Azita Bukhara]], Lalla can be spoken with. **She can either be given a manuscript of [[Sharps]] 10+ or [[An Almanac of Entrances]] ***Giving her the latter results gives you an [[Inkling]], a Bronze Spintria, and gives Lalla [[Inspired]], Fear: Chandler, and Agenda: Corrivality [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]]

Dr Serena Blackwood.title: Dr Serena Blackwood
Dr Serena Blackwood.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Serena.png |principle1={{Lore|Forge}} |principle2={{Lore|Lantern}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Aramaic]], [[Fucine]], [[Greek]], [[Latin]], [[Phrygian]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |address=Cecil Hotel, Alexandria}} {{Quote|One-time Librarian of Hush House, one-time Librarian of the Invisible Serapeum in Alexandria, and currently... what, exactly? Serena is close-mouthed, but I know that she has worked with the St Rhonwen Trust.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Forge}} and {{Lore|Lantern}}. She is a potential Secretary Nunciant for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. She can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Fucine]]. [[File:'Serena Blackwood'.png|left|64px]] She was also the tenth [[Previous Librarians|Librarian]] of the Curia of the Isle, "Who departed, but did not forget". Her [[Busts|Bust]] is carved from alabaster. Serena Blackwood may not be her real name; [[The Serenity of the Black Wood]] states that "Sereno Blackwood" is a common occult alias, and Serena is the feminine form of the same name. {{Clear|left}} ==Time as Librarian== While Librarian, she arranged rooms for [[Christopher Illopoly]] in the [[Motley Tower: Illopoly's Nook|Motley Tower]], perhaps because she saw a potential ally against the Governor of the Cucurbit, [[George Collers]], as relations between the Cucurbit and the House were badly strained at that time. She reluctantly assisted George Collers with his clock project in the early twentieth century.[https://book-of-hours.fandom.com/wiki/Tower_Clock Tower Clock] In return, in 1915, the Suppression Bureau paid for two bells which had previously cracked to be recast.[https://book-of-hours.fandom.com/wiki/Bells Bells] She was known to spend time reading in the [[Church Tower]] to avoid Collers.[https://book-of-hours.fandom.com/wiki/Bell-Tower_Chair Bell-Tower Chair] Right under Governor Collers' nose, Blackwood, [[Brian Levinsen]] and [[Gervinus van Lauren]] all continued their careful investigations of the Brancrug [[Sea-Caves|sea-caves]]. The painting ''[['Dr Serena Blackwood']]'' has no-one in the picture - only an empty garden. She spent time in Greece, bringing back the [[Cyprian's Lamp]] from her travels. She forged the [[Hush House Key]], because she was "tired of losing it". She never finished her term as Librarian at Hush House. It is rumoured she took a specimen of [[Lenten Rose]] when she left for the Invisible Serapeum in Alexandria. == Invitation and Salon == Unlike other Visitors, Serena Blackwood can be invited to Hush House before she visits on her own, because her address is already recorded in the [[Writing-Case]]. Blackwood can be invited using {{Lore|Forge|3}}, and prefers {{Lore|Forge}} food and drink. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" ! Visitor !First Conversation ! 1st Lesson !Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] |Serena and Dagmar discuss the relationship between the Bounds, the Moon-Marches, and Nowhere. Serena considers Nowhere and the space beyond the Moon-Marches to be contiguous, but Dagmar shakes her head firmly. 'Ys never could find a way into Nowhere. And no Star ever found a way back.' |[[Door & Wall]] |Dagmar is quoting risqué jokes from Savage's 'A Seventh Voice' to Serena. Serena is pointing out oneirogenic correspondences in the rhyme schemes; Dagmar keeps chortling and quoting more jokes. |[[Preliminal Meter]] |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Al-Adim and Serena discuss the Great Inks of Power and their personalities. Serena is concerned that the use of a particular ink might alter the meaning of a text. Al-Adim considers this a benefit; or a way to add meaning to the text; or at least something fundamental. |[[Inks of Power]] |Serena quizzes al-Adim about the Damascene branch of the organisation now called the Obliviates. He shares what he remembers. |[[Sacra Limiae]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] |Douglas and Serena discuss a shared, concealed, but evidently profound passion for knitting. Douglas: 'If you tell anyone outside this room, I'll have you locked up.' Serena: 'If ''you'' tell anyone outside this room, I'll give King Crucible your address.' |[[Weaving & Knotworking]] |Serena and Douglas have discovered a shared passion for knitting; they show each other examples of their works. Douglas says absent-mindedly, 'There's a prophecy among the weavers of one who unwisely seeks to find out the future...' Serena recoils in surprise, and Douglas grumbles: 'No-one ever thinks I've read a bleedin' book.' |[[Weaving & Knotworking]] |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] | | | | |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Yvette is considering keeping her notes in houndsgall, for safety. Serena advises her on some of the dangers of houndsgall use and storage. |[[Inks of Containment]] | | |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] | | | | |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] |Chaima describes her defeat in the Bounds at the hands of a 'door-watcher' she names Forculus. Serena, fascinated, tries to draw her out: is Forculus truly a Name of Janus? Is Janus, then, real? Chaima denies interest in either of these questions - and adds quietly that it is unwise of Serena to ask them. |[[Auroral Contemplations]] |Serena and Chaima have both undergone the process known as Torgue's Cleansing. Serena describes it as 'horrible'. Chaima suggests instead that it is 'bracing.' |[[Disciplines of the Scar]] |- |[[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Arthur speaks of the light that supposedly dwelt in the Wood before the coming of the Gods-from-Light: he suggests it might be the redder Sun of the gods-who-were-stone. Serena thinks it is simply fire - 'if we can ever say 'simply' of the Wood.' |[[Pyroglyphics]] |Serena and Arthur discuss the Red Flower of the Watchman's Tree in hushed voices. Serena recalls ways that the Serapeum has used the ithast's arts to preserve knowledge even in a book that is burnt... |[[Pyroglyphics]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Hokobald and Serena are speculating about the nature and possible identity of the still-nascent Hour referred to as the Chandler, who carries fire in darkness; who leaves a place without entering it; whose endeavours are profitable. Serena thinks it possible the Chandler may manifest through the New King. Hokobald shakes his great head. 'A name attends him, certainly. But no more than a Name.' |[[Transformations & Liberations]] | | |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] | | | | |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] | | | | |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] | | | | |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Ehsan and Serena reminisce about their time at Hush House in the days of its power, when the winds were leashed to keep the seas safe, when the Fine-Takers still responded to the words of the Covenant… |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |Serena and Ehsan speak of the ‘shrouded rites’ of the Church Solar – the ones forbidden to the public, who still largely think of the Hours as fables or god-masks. |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Serena and Fraser speculate about bisclavrets, the werewolves of Broceliande. Serena proposes connections both to Ys and to families like the Ravelines who labour under a beast-curse. She cuts Fraser's response off impatiently: 'Not everything has to be about the Carapace Cross, you know.' |[[Coil & Chasm]] |Fraser and Serena speak of Antaios, who might have been a child of Name-emanations of the Flint and Wheel. Fraser wonders why, if Antaios' forebears were immortal, they did not suffer the urge to devour him. Serena provokingly asks when he thinks the Crime of the Sky first became a Crime... |[[Stone Stories]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Zachary asks Serena about the Wheelocks of Treowen and in particular poor doomed Gregory, the 'demi-dyad'; but they conclude that nothing in that sad story will help Zachary. |[[Door & Wall]] |Serena offers to shape a prison for Zachary and his passenger if things become too dire. He will consider it; he wryly shares his thoughts on what might contain him. |[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]] |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] | | | | |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Coquille and Serena discuss the fabled ‘Paths of the Sun’ through the Mansus which were reserved for the undivided Sun speculating whether the Sun’s fission-selves – like the Wolf and the Madrugad – now walk them. Coquille speculates that if the Meniscate walks them, that may account for some of the stories about the shadow-Mansus sometimes called the House of the Moon… |[[Door & Wall]] | | |- | [[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Serena and Corso gloomily dispute the poet Kalle's menacing aphorism: 'A star is a pin-prick, but the Sun is a wound.' Corso believes it presages the later division of the Sun; Serena suggests it anticipates a horrific ending to the Vagabond's prophesied pilgrimage up to the Glory... |[[Pyroglyphics]] | | |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Agdistis and Serena discuss a masked play - a sort of degenerate Sufic hybrid - that he saw in Alexandria some years ago. 'They would only perform it,' he says, 'in the hours before dawn.' Serena nods: 'I think that was wise.' |[[Watchman's Paradoxes]] |Serena and Agdistis discuss the rites of the Damascene branch of the House of Lethe. She wonders - she is tactful, but the implication is clear - whether Agdistis participated in any similar rites to preserve his wonderful voice. He says that he did not, and he is smiling, but it is a smiling mask. |[[Sacra Limiae]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Serena knew Mr Kille when he was an 'untidy youth'. They reminisce about Brancrug just after the War; then she reminds him of the time he got caught scrumping in the Practic Garden, and though he laughs with her, the tone turns awkward, and the conversation ends shortly afterwards. |[[Memory: Gossip]] |Serena knew Mr Kille as an ‘untidy youth’ in Brancrug just after the Great War. She shares some of her memories with Mrs Kille, who listens closely and smiles fondly, though she does not laugh. (It is not easy to make Mrs Kille laugh.) Serena asks if Mr Kille ever speaks of her, but Mrs Kille says no; she says that she thinks Mr Kille is still a little frightened of her. ‘Silence after lightning; silence before thunder,’ she observes, and Serena looks at her sidelong. |[[Memory: Gossip]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |Denzil and Serena reminisce about her time as Librarian, and the weeks the younger Denzil spent up at Hush House, helping repair the foundry, after he quarrelled with his father… and before he went off to war. |[[Memory: Hindsight]] |Serena asks Denzil about the work that his father did for Governor Coller of the Cucurbit. Denzil replies briefly, but politely. It is plain that neither of them much liked Collers. |[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]] |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Timothy barrages Serena with questions about the architecture of Hush House, and the changes she notices since her time here. She answers the more innocuous questions and steers him away from the more difficult ones. |[[Door & Wall]] |Timothy has questions for Serena about the Church in Alexandria, the cult of St Lucia, and various instances of syncretism with pre-Solar beliefs. She does her best to answer him. |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |} ==Incidents== Blackwood can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of the Oriflamme Heist]] *[[The Affair of the Particular Mystique]] *[[The Affair of the Royal Endeavour]] *[[The Affair of the Unfettered Eye]] *[[The Affair of the Unfinished Lark]] ==References== [[Category:Past Librarians]] [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]]

Daymare.title: Daymare
Daymare.text:
{{BoH Character |name='Daymare' |image=File:Daymare.png |principle1={{Lore|Knock}} |principle2={{Lore|Rose}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Greek]], [[Latin]], [[Ramsund]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |address=Schloss Nagelsburg, Ruritania}} {{Quote|Grāfin Friederike Dagmar Sophia Theresia Helena Benigna von Nagelsburg, if you prefer. She doesn't.}}
''''Daymare'''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Knock}} and {{Lore|Rose}}. She is a potential Treasurer for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. She can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Ramsund]]. ==Incidents== 'Daymare' can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of the Absent Friend]] *[[The Affair of the Dappled Rose]] *[[The Affair of the Endless Guest]] *[[The Affair of the Messenger's Casket]] *[[The Affair of the Oriflamme Heist]] *[[The Affair of the Other Horizon]] == Invitations and Salons == 'Daymare' requires 3 {{Lore|Knock}} to be invited to Hush House. She prefers food and drink with {{Lore|Knock}}. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation !1st Lesson ! Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Dagmar and al-Adim chat happily about Medina's 'Queens of the Rivers: |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |Al-Adim and Dagmar are engrossed in a deeply technical discussion about the accuracy - and possible transience - of Westergren's accounts of the Mansus. (Dagmar keeps deferentially reminding al-Adim that she's never passed the Stag Door.) |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |- | [[DI Douglas Moore]] |Dagmar is hectoring Douglas on Suppression Bureau overreach, but he just sits quietly smiling with his arms folded and every so often names another incident sinister enough to need Bureau intervention: 'Rheims', or 'Revek' or 'Treowen' or 'the Wildwood Club'. Each of these puts Dagmar on the back foot, but she rallies and explains why each in turn is different; this at least gives Douglas time to sip his drink or pack his pipe. |[[Edicts Inviolable]] |With the ghoulish camaraderie of two pensioners in a retirement home, Douglas and Dagmar discuss the details of their medical issues, and their subsequent surgeries. |[[Surgeries & Exsanguinations]] |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] |Arun and Dagmar greet each other with delight and are soon engaged in another round of their perennial riddle-game. ‘What is the difference,’ Arun asks ‘between a Twin?’ Dagmar roars happily, ‘One of its Names is both the same!’ |[[Edicts Liminal]] |Arun and Dagmar greet each other with delight and are soon engaged in another round of their perennial riddle-game; but Arun becomes haughty when he realises that Dagmar has asked him about 'Sorrow's Solvent' just to see if she can make the ex-Hooded Prince's 'teeth stick out hissing.' |[[Solutions & Separations]] |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] |Serena and Dagmar discuss the relationship between the Bounds, the Moon-Marches, and Nowhere. Serena considers Nowhere and the space beyond the Moon-Marches to be contiguous, but Dagmar shakes her head firmly. 'Ys never could find a way into Nowhere. And no Star ever found a way back.' |[[Door & Wall]] |Dagmar is quoting risqué jokes from Savage's 'A Seventh Voice' to Serena. Serena is pointing out oneirogenic correspondences in the rhyme schemes; Dagmar keeps chortling and quoting more jokes. |[[Preliminal Meter]] |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Yvette and Dagmar have both dreamt of conversations with half-faced Xenodice, ‘fair to strangers’, Name of the Horned-Axe. Dagmar is convinced they both met the real Xenodice. Yvette is equally convinced that both of them were conversing with an ambassador from the collective unconscious, but she struggles to answer when Dagmar asks what the difference would be between that and an ‘actual’ Name. |[[Rhyme & Remembrance]] |Dagmar talks to Yvette of her dreams of the Painted River. ‘Hard to tell if it’s a dream ''of'' the River, or ''in'' the River. River’s behind the Stag Door. Never passed the Stag Door; well, not formally speaking; well, let’s not talk about that, eh? But anyway the Vagabond painted the River, and her whole thing y’see, is she gets in where she’s not meant to. Actually shall we talk about something else?’ |[[Pearl & Tide]] |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Stanislav gives bee-keeping advice to Dagmar. The hives on her estate, she informs him, have been 'slacking off'. |[[Insects & Nectars]] |Dagmar describes matter-of-factly to Stanislav some of those routes through the Bounds which are available only to one who sheds her own blood. She even shows him the scars. |[[Surgeries & Exsanguinations]] |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] |Dagmar is planning a visit to the Mozabite Pentapolis in Algeria 'to catch up with a wretched troublemaker.' She earnestly solicits advice on the region from Chaima (who she keeps addressing unselfconsciously as 'Charlie').
[Dagmar asked Chaima for advice on a visit to the Mazabite Pentapolis. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Sand Stories]] |Dagmar has returned from the Mazabite Pentapolis ('no sign of my friend, probably been et, but charming place, makes a gel wish she could paint.') She's full of news about the region, and Chaima is keen to hear it. Although Dagmar still seems to think she's called 'Charlie'. |[[Sand Stories]] |- |[[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Dagmar and Arthur discuss 'transinhabitation' - the means by which Lantern-long and similar Mansus entities may manifest in mirrors and lights. (Dagmar deprecates the term 'scrining', which she considers 'cheap'.) |[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]] |Dagmar and Arthur toast past glories, and count the wars where their shifting nationalities have put them on opposing sides. |[[Ragged Crossroads]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Hokobald and Dagmar discuss the work of Willem Harries, with particular reference to lintels and thresholds. Hokobald’s habitual air of contempt thins – he listens with real interest to Dagmar’s answers – but Dagmar retains a careful distance, and, after he arranges her plate and tea-spoon to illustrate her point, she eyes them sidelong and does not touch them again. |[[Door & Wall]] |Hokobald has a proposal for a ‘nine-arched wind-door’ which he hopes to construct on Dagmar’s estate. Dagmar is clearly interested in the project, but firmly refuses to let Hokobald use her estate, or even visit it. Hokobald grinds his teeth, but keeps his temper. |[[Door & Wall]] |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] | | | | |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] | | | | |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Olympe is writing a novel where one of the characters is a criminal chemist specializing in acids and poisons; she’s hoping Dagmar can help with her research. Dagmar is immediately wary, and keeps insisting that she only knows about ‘lemon juice and things’; but once Olympe explains that the protagonist is based on Coquille, she relaxes enough to discuss the properties of Glassfinger Toxin. |[[Solutions & Separations]] |Olympe and Dagmar compare their experiences of getting drunk on Skinshuck Mead. Both wonder whether they really changed shape, or whether their spirits walked in the beast-shape; both agree that they’ll only drink the stuff again in trustworthy company. |[[Solutions & Separations]] |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Dagmar’s warning Ehsan darkly about ‘goings-on’ in Vienna: ‘That bloody little man. The roofs are stiff with ''striges'', you know. They like war even more than gossip.’ |[[Sky Stories]] | | |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Fraser wishes to commission Dagmar to inspect his security arrangement. He is particularly concerned about intruders using the key-weapons known as [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Frangiclave frangiclaves], and about the Ligeians with their Keys, though Dagmar scoffs: 'Ligeians won't care about your collection one way or another.'
[Fraser commissioned Dagmar to inspect his security arrangements. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Lockworks & Clockworks]] |Fraser wants Dagmar's help again, this time to open a nine-locked box he has received from the Evening Isles, which he hopes might contain 'a certain map'. He flatly refuses, however, to show the box to Dagmar, who expresses indignation that he won't trust her; and the conversation founders. |[[Lockworks & Clockworks]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Zachary shows Dagmar a Tanglebrag he's made. He tries to explain how it 'portrays and betrays' the paths of his future. She tries to understand. |[[Edicts Liminal]] |Dagmar is trying to explain the more risqué jokes in Savage's 'A Seventh Voice' to Zachary. Zachary is courteously taking notes. |[[Preliminal Meter]] |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |Dagmar and Azita are discussing means to contain the wild wood-things called Hügelkinder, who apparently have been causing trouble for a business of Azita’s that apparently needs quantities of guns moved through wild European regions by dead of night. |[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]] | | |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Dagmar and Coquille’s conversation about the Great Signs and the Great Scars is repeatedly disrupted by Dagmar’s attempts to introduce Coquille to a ‘very nice Margrave.’
[Dagmar wanted to introduce Coquille to a friend. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars]] |Dagmar and Coquille are talking again about the Great Signs and the Great Scars; again their conversation is punctuated by discussion of the ‘very nice Margrave’ to whom Dagmar did, in fact, introduce Coquille – a fact Dagmar seems now to be regretting. |[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars]] |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Dagmar and Corso are arguing good-naturedly about whether Abbot Geffrey's dialogues on Forculus, Limentinus and Cardea qualify as 'proper nyctodromy.'  |[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars]] |Corso and Dagmar are enjoying an ''entirely theoretical'' discussion of how locks might be subverted through vulgar nyctodromy. And whether Teresa Galmier was a nyctodromist (Dagmar) or a horomachist (Corso). |[[Lockworks & Clockworks]] |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Agdistis recites - with caution - some of the lake-songs of the witches of the Fucine marshes. 'I am more comfortable with the Phrygian tongue,' he says, 'but it is wise to pay the Sister her due.' |[[Fucine]] |Dagmar rambles merrily at a sceptical Agdistis about the possibilities - nyctodromic and musical - of the new Hammond organs. 'Having one shipped over, put up in my organ loft,' she says happily. 'Course we'll need electricity in the organ loft first. And the castle. And put the roof back on the castle. Any chance you're rich, Aggers? Help a gel out?' |[[Lockworks & Clockworks]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Dagmar, chatting amiably to Mr Kille, disparagingly mentions the 1848 'Springtime of Nations' in a way that suggests she might have been present for it - which would make her something like ninety years old. Mr Kille expresses shock, then surprise, then begins to stammer. Dagmar waves the whole thing away: 'First, I was ''very'' young. Second, age is not a number. I'll tell you what's a number, though: nine. Nine's an utter number.' |[[Occult Scrap]] |Dagmar greets Mrs Kille as ‘Mlle Raveline’, corrects herself, thumps her on the shoulder, asks about various French relatives of Mrs Kille’s that Mrs Kille hasn’t seen in years, enthuses about various other French relatives of Mrs Kille’s that Mrs Kille hasn’t seen in years, and eventually asks if she’s had any trouble with ''‘la malaise raveline’''. Mrs Kille answers politely that she has not… but that she has chosen not to have children, just in case. Across the table, Mr Kille catches her eye with the familiarity of long marriage and reaches for her hand. |[[Memory: Gossip]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |Dagmar is explaining to Denzil how he’s going to move out to become her resident smith and help with ‘lots of little projects’. Denzil intermittently affirms that he’s not going to do anything of the kind. Dagmar doesn’t seem to notice, or at least doesn’t seem to mind. |[[Door & Wall]] | | |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Timothy has become aware, somehow, that Dagmar has a ruinous castle somewhere in Mitteleuropa, and that this quite naturally features a chapel. He has many questions about the construction and decoration of this chapel. Dagmar is initially delighted to talk about it, but her knowledge shows its weaknesses under the relentless cannonade of Reverend Timothy's questions. When he unfolds a ''list'' of further questions that he has prepared in advance, her courage fails her, she makes her excuses and heads outside for a smoke. Timothy, however, follows. |[[Door & Wall]] |Dagmar, complaining about her aching back, launches into a blistering assault on Timothy: she seems to hold him personally responsible, through the Church and ultimately the Madrugad, for the Tally of Years which the Madrugad maintains and which determines mortal lifespans. Timothy bows before the assault like a willow in a storm but nevertheless rehearses the usual moral and theological arguments in the Tally’s favour. Dagmar eventually lets slip that she has engaged in ‘nectaring and reckoning’, apparently adjusting her entry in the Tally, and rather shiftily retires from the argument. |[[Edicts Liminal]] |} == Further Stories == * After completing [[The Affair of the Endless Guest]] and asking what happened, [[Daymare|'Daymare']] will tell the Librarian that Spencer is no longer inhabited by Worms and roams Poland with the sword Ebrehel attacking Carabees. She gets [[Inspired]], Fear: Nowhere, and Agenda: Revelation. Spencer himself will also arrive in the next Numa. * After completing [[The Affair of the Oriflamme Heist]], various Visitors may be spoken to, including Daymare: ** If asked, Daymare will first respond with 'Can't promise anything, but old Daymare knows who's who, can put word around, ask what's which, apply the old lemon? Least I can do.' The Librarian must then wait a day. ** Upon returning the next day, Daymare will say; "Well I've had a damned good think and a dashed good snout around and all I can say is that's all I can say. One of the eternal ineffabilities, what? Meantersay I can't tell you who did it. If anyone did it. Sorry, Libsy." This will appear to end her part in the further story. ** After speaking to either [[Mr Zachary Wakefield]], [[Mme Olympe Bechet]], [[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]], or [[Magister Hokobald]] and learning from them that she orchestrated the Heist, you may either: *** Confront and expose Daymare. Her theft is revealed, and Oriflamme's will send you a reward a full day after this choice, three [[Uncatalogued Book|Uncatalogued Books]]. *** You can promise silence, choosing to mention one of three possible dangers: Ys, Nowhere, or the Chandler. This will give her [[Inspired]] and [[Fear]] of the danger you chose. If she already has [[Sympathy]]: Ys, choosing Ys will '''replace''' that Sympathy with Fear. *After completing [[The Affair of the Other Horizon]], Daymare will request a book (either Door & Wall [10] or Sea Stories [10] to help the Bureau deal with the interlopers…or a book on Ys to sate her curiosity. **Upon giving her a book with Door & Wall [10] or Sea Stories [10], she will see off the Ysien emissary, and confide to the Librarian how distressing their appearance was. She will gain [[Inspired]], [[Agenda]]: Peace and [[Fear]]: Ys, and reward the librarian with an [[Inkling]] and a bronze spintria. **Upon giving her [[The Kerisham Portolan]], Daymare will decide to meet the Ysien emissary instead of deporting them. She will gain [[Inspired]], [[Agenda]]: Autarchy and [[Sympathy]]: Ys, and reward the Librarian with an [[Inkling]] and a bronze spintria. *After completing [[The Affair of the Dappled Rose|The Affair of the Dapple Rose,]] Daymare will ask to "''gen up a bit on Miah first".'' **Upon giving her [[The Book of Masks]] or [[The Book of the Centipede|The Book of The Centipede]], the Librarian must wait a day. When Daymare returns she will gain [[Sympathy|Sympathy: Carapace]] and [[Agenda|Agenda: Revelation]]. [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]]

Dr Arun Peel.title: Dr Arun Peel
Dr Arun Peel.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Dr Arun Peel.png |principle1={{Lore|Moon}} |principle2={{Lore|Moth}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Aramaic]], [[Greek]], [[Latin]], [[Phrygian]], [[Sanskrit]], [[Vak]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |relationships=[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] (distant relative)|address=Kardia House, Chania, Crete}} {{Quote|Exile, riddlemonger, Thunderskin devotee. ('I'd rather say confidant.'). Impeccably dressed, but always in dark clothing so the stains don't show. Dark the dressings too at his ankles and his wrists. ('I won't take a seat. It's kind of you to offer. It would be unkind of me to accept.')}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Moon}} and {{Lore|Moth}}. He can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Vak]]. He is a potential Secretary Enigmatic for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. A Great Hooded Prince who broke from its brethren and became a follower of the Thunderskin, Dr Arun Peel is known for his humorous poetry and lectures. He has authored the following [[Books]]: *''[[Collected Hush House Lectures]]'' *''[[The Flayed Tantra]]'' *''[[The Radical Measure]]'' *''[[The Victory of Crowns]]'' ==Invitations and Salons== Dr Arun Peel requires 7 {{Lore|Moon}} to be invited to Hush House. He prefers food and drink with {{Lore|Moon}}. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor ! First Conversation !1st Lesson !Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] |Arun and Dagmar greet each other with delight and are soon engaged in another round of their perennial riddle-game. ‘What is the difference,’ Arun asks ‘between a Twin?’ Dagmar roars happily, ‘One of its Names is both the same!’ |[[Edicts Liminal]] |Arun and Dagmar greet each other with delight and are soon engaged in another round of their perennial riddle-game; but Arun becomes haughty when he realises that Dagmar has asked him about 'Sorrow's Solvent' just to see if she can make the ex-Hooded Prince's 'teeth stick out hissing.' |[[Solutions & Separations]] |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Al-Adim is chaffing Arun about the fading potency of 'your venoms'. Arun is clearly subsiding into a sulk. |[[Serpents & Venoms]] |Arun, complacently: 'The traveller is always returning. One who does not is no traveller.' Al-Adim, waspishly: 'Tell that to my patroness.' |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] |Arun is concerned about the progress of a recent candidate for Lantern-longhood: he shares names and details with Douglas. 'Knife, noose, flame, word, hm? I don't like it; but I don't like this aspirant either.' |[[Maggephene Mysteries]] |Douglas has tracked down the Long-in-the-making of whom Arun warned him last time. Arun congratulates him; Douglas describes, with distaste, the empty eyes of his target's victims… |[[Maggephene Mysteries]] |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] | | | | |- | [[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Arun and Yvette began with a serious philological discussion - the similarities between Henavek and Vak - but the conversation has devolved into something more like gossip, comparing the virtues and charms of Vak and Henavek as if they were individuals. Arun mentions the tradition that the two languages are brother and sister. 'It would be a shame, wouldn't it, if they were?' Yvette responds archly. 'If they were brother and sister, nothing unsuitable could occur between them, surely?' Arun's whole face creases in an unusually fervent smile. |[[Kernewek Henavek|Henavek]] |Yvette and Arun revisit an innuendo-laced conversation about a possible entanglement between Vak and Henavek. Each recites poetry in their language of preference. Before very long, they have drawn their chairs closer together so they can whisper the poetry in one another’s ears.
[Arun and Yvette will leave together tonight…] |[[Rhyme & Remembrance]] |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Arun and Stanislav compare the sacred places where it is fitting to spill blood; those where the spilling of blood is welcome; and those where one may only spill one's own. |[[Rites of the Roots]] |Stanislav speaks of a provoking line on the White Jade Tablet -  'our skins were yet soft, and fell easily from us…' He wonders how Peel's own 'shedding' might be related, but Peel is typically evasive. |[[Rites of the Roots]] |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] |Arun and Chaima are speaking of the 'Younger Sisters' of the Mother of Ants, whom Chaima has hunted in the past. 'There are not so many of them left in serpent-form,' Arun tells her. 'The world changes, and they take human form. As the dragons did.' |[[Hill & Hollow|Lesson: Hill & Hollow]] |Arun is telling stories of the times when he was still numbered among the Great Hooded Princes - stories of the indirect wars they waged against the invaders of their adoptive country - the rivers they roused, the lions they made… |[[Edicts Martial|Lesson: Edicts Martial]] |- | [[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Arun and Arthur are reminiscing about the city of Pune, though Arun has not visited it, he confides, since the time of the Maratha Empire. 'One exile after another; the pentiment's fate. Exile is addictive. You'll learn that too.' |[[Sickle & Eclipse]] |Arthur and Arun are discussing which forbidden weapons should be permitted, and which weapons have been permitted too long. Arthur is concerned by rumours of Dawnbreaker experiments in Britain; Arun is bragging, a little, about his experiences with the terrible feather called the Imhullune Tectrix. |[[Sharps]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Arun strokes Hokobald’s arm and whispers about the ‘pleasures of the Princes’. Hokobald’s response can best be described as ‘angry curiosity’. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |Arun and Hokobald are debating the truth of a rumour about Winter-long: that they cannot sire or birth children, and so can safely lie together without fear of the Crime of the Sky. Hokobald insists that even were that true, the fruitfulness of Grail-long – or the vigour of Forge-long – would still allow conception. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] | | | | |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] | | | | |- | [[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Olympe and Arun chuckle over a Roost-rumour that’s recently resurfaced, of ancient trysts between the Malachite and the Mare-in-the-Tree; they speak of the tradition that the Mare-in-the-Tree can sometimes be the Witch’s Sister, what that might mean, and especially what that might mean for Rowena and Aunt Mopsy. |[[Transformations & Liberations]] | | |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Arun and Ehsan - the ex-skaptodon, the perhaps-ex-Knock-long - talk about how it is to have been something that one no longer is. Ehsan complains that he needs to employ both hammers and nutcrackers, also that his joints have begun to ache when the weather turns. Arun rubs at the bandages on his wrists, and says ruefully: 'But we endure; we endure.' |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |Ehsan gives Arun practical advice on the preservation and protection of those parts of Arun that are no longer protected and preserved by skin. |[[Stitching & Binding]] |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Fraser is speaking to Arun of the changes he's been undergoing as his inner nature becomes more manifest. He speaks with obvious pride; but he's concerned that his body might have begun to produce a venom, and he's not sure what to do about it…
[Fraser asked Arun for help with the changes he's undergoing. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Serpents & Venoms]] |Fraser thanks Arun warmly for the advice that Arun gave him last time about the development of one's venom glands. They chat wryly about the difficulties of expressing venom, and the effects of diet on its potency. |[[Serpents & Venoms]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Zachary asks Arun about the fabled war between the Great Hooded Princes and the Obliviates. Arun favours Zachary with his triangular smile. 'It wasn't really a war. Mother Many-Armed just took offence at some of their rites. Well, their habits. And we were all still her children...' |[[Edicts Liminal]] |‘Remember,’ Arun tells Zachary, ‘that it’s always too late, eventually; but it never is until then.’ Zachary lets out a long sigh. ‘You always say that. It’s less helpful than you think it is.’ |[[Putrefactions & Calcinations]] |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |Arun and Azita speak of the Tragulari, the 'Dartsmen' who once used exotic poisons to hunt immortals. Arun expresses distaste for the Colonel's part in the Tragulari's creation, but Azita is unabashed: 'Good exercise. Honestly, I miss them.' Arun flatly refuses to believe her. |[[Sharps]] | | |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Coquille and Arun have discovered that they share family in the subcontinent from which they have both been exiled. They gossip eagerly about their cousins’ expression of familial traits; their alterations and development; their new-hatched kin. |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |‘We all loved Vak, back home,’ Arun sighs. Coquille nods, her eyes glowing. ‘You remember the poems we wrote for her? In other languages, of course. Except me; I got in a great deal of trouble for that. Again.’ He recites a few verses, and Coquille claps her hands in delight. |[[Vak]] |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Corso and Arun are chuckling together about Musgrave Dewulf's theories on the Great Ink porphyrine. |[[Inks of Revelation]] |Arun and Corso are discussing a scheme to track down valuable books by observing the effects of their ink on the dreams of those nearby, but Corso subsides into a sulk when it becomes apparent that Arun is not taking the idea seriously. |[[Inks of Revelation]] |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Arun and Agdistis are discussing the technical details of flensing, without any particular regard for the effect it might have on anyone's appetite. |[[Stitching & Binding]] |Agdistis and Arun are discussing the Thunderskin's rites in Phrygia, India, and Cyprus… |[[Drums & Dances]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Arun exercises his charm to overcome Mr Kille's wariness of foreigners. He describes his 'skin condition' in elliptical terms, and invites advice from Mr Kille on how it might be better concealed. Mr Kille insists that he is a coffinmaker, not an embalmer, but has a suggestion or two nevertheless... |[[Surgeries & Exsanguinations]] | | |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |Arun begins an animated, if one-sided conversation with Denzil, treating him to an impromptu translation of the Incandescent Tantra: ‘a great change requires a melting dissolution.’ Arun’s tone becomes more sibilant, and he sits very close to Denzil, who begins, cautiously, to smile.
[Denzil and Arun enjoyed an unusually heated conversation. These two might have more to say if you invite them both back for another Salon.]
[Arun and Denzil have discreetly established an affinity.] |[[Transformations & Liberations]] |Denzil and Arun are enjoying an unexpectedly cordial conversation, though Arun is doing most of the talking. Arun asks, evidently not for the first time, when Denzil is going to visit him in London, but Denzil only shakes his head stolidly; and the conversation cools a little, after. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |- | [[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Reverend Timothy has realised that Arun is the author of ‘The Radical Measure’, the notorious nineteenth-century manifesto for experimental poetry, and is hanging on Arun’s every word: he has almost stopped talking.
[Reverend Timothy was excited to find himself at a Salon with the author of ‘The Radical Measure’. Timothy and Arun might have more to say if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Preliminal Meter]] |Since their last meeting, Reverend Timothy has actually ''read'' Arun’s ‘The Radical Measure’, and is boiling with detailed questions about it. Arun’s memory of the book is obviously a little hazier than Timothy, and he tries to retreat into the habitual conversational thicket of riddles; but the ingenuity of Timothy’s enthusiasm is merciless. |[[Preliminal Meter]] |} ==Incidents== Peel can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of the Dappled Rose]] *[[The Affair of the Forgivable Debt]] *[[The Affair of the Friar's Tapestry]] *[[The Affair of the Invisible Opera]] *[[The Affair of the Messenger's Casket]] *[[The Affair of the Rising While]] == Further Stories == * After completing [[The Affair of the Forgivable Debt]], Peel requests a book on the [[Disciplines of the Scar]] (Mystery:10) or something on Hush House's Winter Tower to democratise the 'Wangle', a way to win years of life out of the Madrugad's tally. ** Providing him [[Against Vitruvius]] will get him [[Inspired]], Agenda: Better Gods and Sympathy: Reckoner and reward the Librarian with an [[Inkling]] and a [[Edicts Inviolable|Lesson:Edicts Inviolable]]. * After completing [[The Affair of the Invisible Opera]], Peel can request a book on Hush House's Winter Tower. ** Providing [[Against Vitruvius]] or [[Annals of St Brandan's]] will give him [[Inspired]] and Sympathy: Reckoners and reward the Librarian with an [[Inkling]] and a [[Forbidden Epic]]. *After completing [[The Affair of the Dappled Rose]], Peel will request a book on Miah. ** ''Providing The [[Book of Miah]]'', ''[[The Book of the Centipede]]'' or ''[[The Book of Masks]]'' will give him [[Inspired]], Sympathy: Carapace and Agenda: Revelation and reward the Librarian with an [[Inkling]] and a [[Forbidden Epic]]. == Trivia == * "Arun" is a Hindi name, derived from the Sanskrit ''Aruna'', meaning either "reddish-brown" or "dawn", who was the charioteer of Surya, personified deity of the Sun in Hinduism. As Dr Peel is (or was) a Great Hooded Prince, it may be a macabre reference to the "stains" that his dark clothing conceals. "Peel" is a modern English surname, but may refer to Arun shedding his skin as snakes do. ==Hidden interactions== {{Spoilers | caption = This section contains information on hidden interactions. | content =
While visiting, the Librarian can present Peel with the books he has written to receive rewards. This only works once, and he will not disappear after this interaction.

*Presenting Dr Arun Peel with ''[[Collected Hush House Lectures]]'' rewards the Librarian with a [[Wormwood Dream]] and the following dialogue: {{Quote|
'Something, as it were, coming through.'

'I forgot I'd written in the Third History. Well well. Can I take a look? I'll keep my gloves on.' [Peel will examine the book and return it to you. He won't leave until his other business is concluded.]

'You know that Oriflamme's was established in the same year as the Masque of Masques? But not the same history. So it's probably a concidence. Come closer, though, and I'll whisper you a footnote.'}}
*Presenting Dr Arun Peel with ''[[The Flayed Tantra]]'' "rewards" the Librarian the following dialogue: {{Quote|
'Undiplomatic, Librarian -'

'Every one of us still living - we all shed histories as a snake casts its skin. And I cast this history off long ago. I have no wish - no wish at all - to revisit it.'}}
*Presenting Dr Arun Peel with ''[[The Radical Measure]]'' rewards the Librarian with a [[Preliminal Meter|Lesson: Preliminal Meter]], a [[Horizon-Sight]] and the following dialogue: {{Quote|
'Not to everyone's taste, I know -'

'A prophet is without honour in his own country, as the saying has it; and I'm pretty much from everywhere these days, so I suppose no one will ever really take me seriously again. Mind if I take a look? I can point out a couple of the better bits. And I'll keep my gloves on.' [Peel will examine the book and return it to you. He won't leave until his other business is concluded.]

'Here. And here. And the editor tried to take that bit out. So I arranged a motivational sort of dream. Worth it.'}}
*Presenting Dr Arun Peel with ''[[The Radical Measure (Glossed)]]'' rewards the Librarian with a [[Tally|Silver Spintria]] and the following dialogue (Note - he won't return the book): {{Quote|
'The glossed version?'

'I've been trying to get my hands on this edition for quite some time. Once I have it, I can decide if I need to get my hands on young Illopoly. I'll give you a silver spintria for it?' [Peel will take the book, but won't leave until his other business is concluded.]

'I see. I see. I see. Christopher. Christopher Christopher Christopher...'}}
*Presenting Dr Arun Peel with ''[[The Victory of Crowns]]'' rewards the Librarian with two random [[Uncatalogued Book]]s and the following dialogue (Note - he won't return the book): {{Quote|
'The Victory of Crowns?'

'You know, I can never quite remember if that's actually one of mine. Or one of, um, another mine. Do you mind if I take it away with me? I'll swap you the other books I happen to be carrying. No, I won't tell you what those might be. Rocks are no sharper in the dark.' [Peel will take 'Crowns' and give you two books of unpredictable nature and origin. He won't leave until his other business is concluded.]

'Here you go. And here I go.'}} }}
