Fr. Stanislav John Schaller.title: Fr. Stanislav John Schaller
Fr. Stanislav John Schaller.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Fr. Stanislav John Schaller.png |principle1={{Lore|Heart}} |principle2={{Lore|Nectar}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Cracktrack]], [[Fucine]], [[Greek]], [[Latin]], [[Phrygian]], [[Sanskrit]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |address=Prieuré des Capitaines, Morbihan}} {{Quote|Priest, diplomat, gardener: a soft-voiced man with a very steady gaze.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Visitors|Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Heart}} and {{Lore|Nectar}}. He is a potential Secretary Salvant for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. He can be paid one [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Cracktrack]] or [[Fucine]]. He has authored the following [[Books]]: *''[[Deaths and their Evasions]]'' *''[[Singlefoot Songs]]'' *''[[The Devoured Tantra]]'' - Transcribed from a Red Long. ==Invitations and Salons== Schaller requires 3 {{Lore|Nectar}} to be invited to Hush House. He prefers {{Lore|Heart}} food and drink. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation !1st Lesson ! Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] |Stanislav gives bee-keeping advice to Dagmar. The hives on her estate, she informs him, have been 'slacking off'. |[[Insects & Nectars]] |Dagmar describes matter-of-factly to Stanislav some of those routes through the Bounds which are available only to one who sheds her own blood. She even shows him the scars. |[[Surgeries & Exsanguinations]] |- | [[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |AI-Adim describes his memories of Thirza Blake, and her work, in his time as Secretary Nunciant of the House. He is clearly caught between affection and annoyance. Stanislav shakes his head: 'I wish I had known her. I think we'd have got on.' |[[Herbs & Infusions]] |Towards the end of the meal, Father Stanislav demonstrates some of the signs that he used to communicate with 'singlefoots' in his travels 'east of Hsian', He draws the signs on his plate, and wipes them away afterwards. 'Safer not,' he says quietly, 'unless you wanted to stay east of Hsian.' |[[Cracktrack]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] |Douglas has been looking into the six-centuries-past death of Abbess Nonna. He’s questioned unspecified sources that he doesn’t share with Stanislav, and concludes that Nonna was possessed by a Name of the Blackbone and ‘put down’ by her sistren – ‘nasty business, but best thing for it.’ He and Stanislav discuss the herb-mixtures that might have laid her open to that possession. |[[Herbs & Infusions]] | | |- | [[Dr Arun Peel]] |Arun and Stanislav compare the sacred places where it is fitting to spill blood; those where the spilling of blood is welcome; and those where one may only spill one's own. |[[Rites of the Roots]] |Stanislav speaks of a provoking line on the White Jade Tablet -  'our skins were yet soft, and fell easily from us…' He wonders how Peel's own 'shedding' might be related, but Peel is typically evasive. |[[Rites of the Roots]] |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] | | | | |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Yvette and Stanislav chat about the notorious erotic-occult novel, 'Ettery After', which Yvette considers 'flimsy' and Stanislav considers 'saucy'. |[[Inks of Containment]] | | |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] |Stanislav and Chaima are discussing the treatment of wounds caused by great beasts: labhites and skaptodons; tarrasques and raveleurs; and the great serpents called Younger Sisters for their kinship with the Mother of Ants. |[[Stitching & Binding]] |Stanislav and Chaima speak of the Seven-Coiled, the 'Father of the Mother', who has passed from the world; of the seven unhuman acolytes she has inspired; of their prophecies. Chaima reflects wistfully on what a great hunt the end of the Seven-Coiled might have been... |[[Sand Stories]] |- |[[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Stanislav and Arthur argue happily about which herbal tisane tastes the most disgusting, and hence is most useful to speed lingering guests on their way. |[[Herbs & Infusions]] |Stanislav and Arthur discuss the herbs of Persia, and their uses in the infirmary of the Labyrinth of Lions. |[[Herbs & Infusions]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Stanislav asks Hokobald about the tradition that the Velvet makes immortals of those sufficiently savorous to be hunted by her pet, Kitling Ripe. Hokobald confidently confirms that it's so, but his explanations are derailed by rants about those immortals who ''should'' have become her victims - or who she devoured despite their blandness. (He sounds almost jealous of these last.) |[[Spices & Savours]] | | |- | [[MCO Constance Lee]] |Connie is investigating stories of something described as ‘Spinnennebel’ – a kind of spider-vapor – which has begun to manifest in Germany and the Low Countries. Stanislav has heard nothing, but agrees it sounds nothing like Hive, nor Nest, nor Chrysalis…
[Connie aroused Stanislav’s interest in the ‘Spinnennebel’. The two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Insects & Nectars]] |Stanislav confirms to Connie that he, too, has now heard something of the ‘Spinnennebel’ which first appeared in Austria but has afflicted remote parts of the countryside across Europe – even as far west as his sanctuary in Brittany. He agrees that it has many of the hallmarks of a Nowhere irruption – but adds thoughtfully that one informant claims it’s been manufactured… |[[Insects & Nectars]] |- | [[Mlle Margot Matutine]] |Morgen asks Stanislav, gaily and lightly, about 'Three Faces', the guardian of the Grove of Green Immortals, where Stanislav is reputed to have spent time. Stanislav replies respectfully, urbanely, and elliptically. |[[Orchids & Narcotics]] | | |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Olympe asks Stanislav about the ‘Pontine Yew’ of legend; and then about the honey of its flowers, which opens a door to another place. He has tasted the honey, but he will say of that place only that it is not the Mansus. |[[Rites of the Roots]] |Stanislav and Olympe discuss the Hours of the Wood. Stanislav points out that monks cut their hair; he suggests, perhaps mischievously, that as a class they belong to the Moth… |[[Rites of the Roots]] |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Stanislav and Ehsan debate which rivers and weathers may still qualify - metaphorically or prophetically - at which times and seasons - as the 'blood of the Seven-Coils'. |[[Coil & Chasm]] | | |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Stanislav and Fraser discuss the work of the entomologist Juliana Zawistowski. Fraser is firmly of the belief that she bore within her the nature of the Thritige-kind of the Carapace Cross. |[[Stone Stories]] |Fraser and Stanislav discuss the Unnumbered Stones of Brittany, not far from Stanislav's current digs. Fraser insists they were placed by the Carapace Cross. Stanislav humours him. |[[Stone Stories]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Stanislav and Zachary discuss the 'merciful measures' of the witch Nyn. Zachary agrees that her techniques are potent against Devourers, but he has become unwilling to use them since he began to fear that he himself might qualify as a Devourer... |[[Quenchings & Quellings]] |Stanislav advises Zachary on ‘words of mercy’, which might quell the urgencies that trouble Zachary’s skin. ‘I know that one!’ Zachary says suddenly. ‘It descends from Chione.’ |[[Quenchings & Quellings]] |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |Azita and Stanislav discuss the Names of the Thunderskin - the seven Instruments whose musics support his rhythm. Azita repeats the tradition that a duendrazon which has known seven caesurae becomes eligible to replace an Instrument. Stanislav shakes his head. 'Duendrazones. An odd choice, I've always thought, to become eternally conscious, and then to pursue the caesura so...' |[[Strings & Songs]] | | |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Stanislav and Coquille swap stories of Aunt Mopsy. He met her when she made a pilgrimage to the Grove of Green Immortals, in the days he dwelt in its penumbra; she introduced him to her adoptive brother in Tiflis when his tastes had become jaded and he sought more dangerous diversions... |[[Leaves & Thorns]] | | |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Stanislav and Corso speak of Zulfiya Zakirova, to whom Corso was once very nearly married – by Stanislav, in fact. Corso tugs miserably at his moustache as he describes her struggles with deliria and her obsession with the whimsies of the Wood. ‘Then one day she started wearing wigs and ran off with a piano-tuner. Last I heard she was giving piano lessons in Leipzig.’ |[[Orchids & Narcotics]] | | |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Stanislav and Agdistis discuss pruning techniques used when a plant is wounded by winter; how to ensure no ragged bark remains; of how not to be distracted by timidity or tenderness. |[[Leaves & Thorns]] |Agdistis and Stanislav talk about gardening under glass in winter. Their tone is fatherly. |[[Leaves & Thorns]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Stanislav and Mr Kille discuss Mr Kille’s marrows. Stanislav appears to be in honest awe of Mr Kille’s marrows. |[[Herbs & Infusions]] | | |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |Denzil gives Stanislav what advice he can muster on warding off rust. |[[Putrefactions & Calcinations]] |Stanislav solicitously advises Denzil on a poultice for his lumbago. |[[Herbs & Infusions]] |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Timothy is a doctor of theology: a qualification which has apparently been a source of confusion in Brancrug, where a number of villagers have taken ‘doctor’ to mean they should ask him for help with their aches and sprains. He dislikes turning them away, and prevails on Stanislav for some practical advice. |[[Herbs & Infusions]] |Stanislav and Timothy share gossip about doctrinal and political differences between the Church establishment on the Continent, and its sister denomination in Britain. Stanislav leans back in his chair, eyes half-closed, chuckling now and then; Timothy is so delighted and clearly feels so guilty that his teeth are chattering a little. |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |} ==Incidents == Schaller can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of the Friar's Tapestry]] *[[The Affair of the God in the Wood]] *[[The Affair of the Grunewald Provision]] *[[The Affair of the Open Reverend]] *[[The Affair of the Sandalwood Saint]] == Further Stories == * After completing [[The Affair of the God in the Wood]] and discussing the incident with [[DI Douglas Moore]], Schaller will offer several potential conclusions. (The following occurs if Schaller is given a {{lore|Nectar}} book during the Incident, and may differ if he is instead given a {{lore|Heart}} book.) ** His first option requests [[Horns & Ivories]] 10 or [[Kitling Ripe's Tasty Treats]]. Schaller will gain [[Inspired]], Agenda: Stone Consumed, and Fear: Carapace, and reward the Librarian with a [[Tally|Bronze Spintria]] and an [[Inkling]]. ** He alternately can be given [[Honey: the Comprehensive Guide]] or [[The Bee-Keeper's Ends]]. Schaller will gain [[Inspired]], Agenda: Stone Remembered, and Sympathy: Carapace. It aslo gives you Liselotte's Lore, which has the following text: Lyterion director; dietician; ally of the Blomberende-kind. Liselotte wishes to bring a case of sleeping Blomberende noble larvae, so they can find a refuge here at Hush House. [Use this card in the Hush House beehive to give them refuge - or if you decide to refuse her, return this card to Stanislav in the God in the Wood node.]. *** You can either let Liselotte access your beehives, letting the Blomberende larvae shelter there or not. **** Allowing her access gives you [[Bittersweet Certainty]], an [[Inkling]], a lesson, and your beehives now have a chance to produce [[Cuckoo-Honey]] even while not in [[Numa]] ==Hidden interactions== {{Spoilers|caption=This section contains information on hidden interactions.|content=
While visiting, the Librarian can present Schaller with a book he has written to receive rewards. This only works once, and he will not disappear after this interaction.
Presenting Schaller with ''[[Deaths and their Evasions]]'' rewards the Librarian with a [[Edicts Liminal|Lesson: Edicts Liminal]] and the following dialogue: {{Quote|'I remember this - '

'I'm surprised that it's found its way here... but that's Hush House, I suppose. May I refresh my memory? I remember that I wrote about the Galmier business - not as cautiously as I might have...' [Stanislav will examine the book and return it to you. He won't leave until his other business is concluded.]

'That law I will not name aloud - the law of the three - it can be defied. It is rarely wise to attempt that defiance. The penalty of failure is paid by one - but the penalty of success, by many. I would ask you, Librarian, to remember that, when you decide how to address yourself to Eternity. But I already have faith in your judgement. Thank you for the loan of the book.'}}}}

Aunt Mopsy.title: Aunt Mopsy
Aunt Mopsy.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Aunt Mopsy.png |principle1={{Lore|Moon}} |principle2={{Lore|Nectar}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Hyksos]], [[Phrygian]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]]}} {{Quote|Collector of proverbs, connoisseur of wines, herald of the Hour called Mare-in-the-Tree.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Moon}} and {{Lore|Nectar}}. She can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Hyksos]]. Aunt Mopsy has authored ''[[Snare of the Tree: Collected Proverbs of Aunt Mopsy]]''. ==Incidents== Aunt Mopsy can visit for the following [[Incident]]s during [[Numa]]: *[[A Matter of Counterfeit Memory]] *[[A Matter of Knot and Tangle]] *[[A Matter of the Midnight Twin]] ==Hidden interactions== {{Spoilers|caption=This section contains information on hidden interactions.|content=
While visiting, the Librarian can present Aunt Mopsy with the book she has written to receive rewards. This only works once, and she will not disappear after this interaction.
Presenting her with ''[[Snare of the Tree: Collected Proverbs of Aunt Mopsy]]'' rewards the Librarian with a [[Applebright Euphonies|Lesson: Applebright Euphonies]] and the following dialogue (Note - the book will be [[Contamination|Contaminated]] with [[Keeperskin]]): {{Quote|'Ooh!'

'That publisher in Kerisham. I promised her if she did right by me, she'd never see me again. Well, dear, a promise is a promise, but a story is a story. If you let me touch that book, I promise I'll give it back.' [Aunt Mopsy will examine the book and return it to you. She won't leave until her other business is concluded.]'

'There you are, dear. A little lesson for you. And another little lesson for you later.'}}}}

Julian Coseley.title: Julian Coseley
Julian Coseley.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Julian Coseley.png |principle1={{Lore|Moon}} |principle2={{Lore|Winter}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Aramaic]], [[Ericapaean]], [[Greek]], [[Latin]], [[Phrygian]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]]}} {{Quote|Magus, Winter-long, controversial philosopher. For an immortal exalted by an Hour of Silence, especially one who might be dead, he has had a great deal to say for himself over the years.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Moon}} and {{Lore|Winter}}. He can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Ericapaean]]. Julian Coseley has authored many [[Books]]. However, no unique dialogue will be given when he is provided with those books. *''[[The Fallen Cross]]'' *''[[Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic]]'' *''[[Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic: Second Edition]]'' *''[[The Five Letters On Memory]]'' *''[[The Six Letters on Necessity]]'' *''[[The Twelve Letters On Consequence]]'' ==Description== Julian Coseley is a former teacher to the occult historian [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Claude_Hersault Claude Hersault]. In ''[[An Introduction to Histories]]'', Coseley is described as [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/Birds_of_a_Feather_and_Worms_of_a_Scale 'a Worm of Worms']. It is also described that he finds the order of the Hours oppressive. ''[[The Twelve Letters On Consequence]]'' The painting ''[['Julian Coseley']]'' in [[Cell: Long]] reveals that "at a prescribed date, his Hour-patron will ensure him a beautiful ending, but until then, he is even harder than most Long to dispose of finally". Additionally, it is revealed that he was defeated by an ascendant Long in the 1920's and his current status is a subject of debate. His views on [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/Janus Janus] are mentioned in ''[[The Locksmith's Dream: Stolen Reflections]]''. ==Incidents== Julian can visit for the following [[Incident]]s during [[Numa]]: *[[A Matter of Counterfeit Memory]] *[[A Matter of the Midnight Twin]] *[[A Matter of the Softer Frost]] ==References== [[Category:Authors]] [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]]

Ambrose Westcott.title: Ambrose Westcott
Ambrose Westcott.text:
{{BoH Librarian |image1=[[File:Bust.ambrose.png]] |time_as_librarian=1785 - 1797 |birth=1734 |death=1797}} {{quote|Ambrose Westcott, first Librarian of Hush House: metallurgist, alchemist, pyrographer.}}
'''Ambrose Westcott''' was the first [[Previous Librarians|Librarian]] of the Curia of the Isle, 'Who often purified, but was not often pure'. He was known to be a voracious cigar smoker, and liked to try flavouring his pipe tobacco with things like [[Honeyscar Jasmine]] and [[Westcott's Compounds]]. His [['Ambrose Westcott'|Bust]] is cast in brass and located in the [[Westcott Room]]. == Early life == He was born in 1734. Before becoming Librarian, Ambrose was a member of the Oblivates, although he was a Know rather than Long. When the order began to schism over whether or not to remain neutral in the struggle between Birds and Worms, he proposed a third way, based on [[Numen: the Sun's Weakness|a secret]] he found in [[The Sun Disfigured|'a volume of transcendent heresy']]. He convinced a handful of Oblivates to follow him to [[Hush House]], where they founded the library, with the rest departing for Port Noon. ==Time as Librarian== After the Curia of the Isle acquired the deed for the abandoned Dewulf estate in 1785, Ambrose Westcott became its first Librarian. He had the [[Librarian's Quarters]] built. He was an antiquarian and had an enthusiasm for roccoco, as evidenced by the [[Librarian's Timepiece]] and the [[Daybreak Clock]], though most of his successors thought them hideous. Another one of his possessions is a [[Pigeon Statuette]] - 'a watcher of the skies'. He also refurbished the [[Foundry]] to be suitable for his metallurgical experiments. Villagers recall the Turbot Crisis of 1786, when Dr Westcott caught a prodigious turbot, and required the kitchen to poach it for him 'without division'. No vessel of sufficient size could be found to poach it entire, so they had to resort to 'alchemical assistance'. He developed the 'Westcott Method' of dispelling [[Actinic Theoplasma]], originally requiring tobacco-smoke. He probably did not develop all of 'Westcott's Compounds', but knew how to make a name stick. Westcott ordered the destruction of [[Valentine Dewulf]]'s bed in Gullscry Tower, 'for reasons he did not choose to articulate'. The [[Westcott Room]] is named after him, as he used it as the smoking room while he was Librarian. He spent time sat at [[Desk: Ambrose|his desk]] writing long cross letters to the Times about the flaws of the British constitution. There are several of Westcott's hunting trophies in the house that are named after his rivals and adversaries, which he said the trophies resembled. From these, we can see that Westcott's adversaries included Finnian Boole (a tobacconist whose bills he inexplicably refused to pay); [[Magister Hokobald]]; Philemon, a poet who called Westcott 'the Magus of the Silver'd Smoke', which seemed to enrage him; and Tavish, a gamekeeper who 'once derided Westcott's ability to shoot straight'. He was once lost on the moors and would not suffer it to be spoken of. Westcott wrote several books on the subjects of {{Lore|Forge}}, [[Nyctodromy]], and tobacco, including ''[[Ambrosial!]]'', ''[[A Shape in Smoke]]'', ''[[The Carbonek Schism]]'', and ''[[The Temptations of Architecture]]''. He mocked ''[[Opus Magnum Caeruleum]]'' by referring to it as 'the Big Blue Business', as it was written at least two centuries prior to his birth, and either anticipated or undermined many of his preferred conclusions. He was a man of considerable girth. Scrutiny of the [[Delightful Repose]] reveals, 'House folklore claims that Ambrose Westcott suffered his final apoplexy on this sofa, after a particularly hasty trample up and down the stairs to argue with visiting priests.' He died in 1797. Quotes associated with him: *'''A true adept is never troubled by fire, nor by fever, nor by restless spirit.''' - Ambrose Westcott *'''By God, Sir, we shall have no Cigars in the Library, and we shall have no House without a Smoking-Room.''' - Dr Ambrose Westcott *'''Ambrose used to say that Music minus Time was Ink. But Ambrose liked brandy as much as he liked ink.''' - Kitty Mazarine [[Category:Authors]] [[Category:Past Librarians]] [[Category:People]]

Brian Levinsen.title: Brian Levinsen
Brian Levinsen.text:
{{BoH Librarian |image1=[[File:'Brian Levinsen'.png]] |time_as_librarian=? - 1914}} {{Quote|Brian Levinsen, ninth Librarian, painter and doctor, who never returned from the Western Front.}}
'''Brian Levinsen''' was the ninth [[Previous Librarians|Librarian]] of the Curia of the Isle, "Who saw his fate, and did not shirk it". His [['Brian Levinsen'|Bust]] is cast from aluminium - oxidised to grey. ==Time as Librarian== He was a painter and doctor. The [[Infirmary]] flourished under his tenure. Levinsen often painted 'prefigures' - copies of paintings that would be painted over twenty years in the future. He painted this copy of Max Ernst's work[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Ernst Max Ernst], a German surrealist painter., titled after a small city in Arizona[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedona,_Arizona Sedona, Arizona.], signing it with an [[Illumination]] mark and dating it '1958': *[['Sedona, Not Yet']] He painted the following copies of paintings by Picasso,[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Picasso Pablo Ruiz Picasso], a Spanish cubist and surrealist painter. signed them, but added a question mark after his signature: *''[['Red, Blue']]'' *''[['To Be Fruitful']]'' He also painted prefigures of Kirchner's painting,[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_Ludwig_Kirchner Ernst Ludwig Kirchner], a German expressionist painter. one of his favourite pre-subjects, whose work Levinsen often anticipated in his mirror-dreams: *''[['Again, at Night']]'' *''[['Love in a Quiet Place']]'' *''[['To Hear Those Voices']]'' Right under [[George Collers|Governor Collers]]' nose, Brian Levinsen, [[Serena Blackwood]] and [[Gervinus van Lauren]] all continued their careful investigations of the Brancrug [[Sea-Caves|sea-caves]]. Brian Levinsen had the [[Soft Blue Sofa]] installed so he could nap in [[Gullscry Tower: Valentine's Room|Valentine’s room]]. He often spoke of his sympathy for [[Valentine Dewulf]] and commissioned a [[Valentine's Memorial|memorial stone]] in 1914, but by the time it arrived, he had volunteered as a medical officer in the Great War and served for a time on the Western Front. He never returned; he never saw the memorial; and it became his own. His body was never found. Kirchner and Levinsen fought in the Great War on opposite sides, but there is no reason to believe Kirchner had anything at all to do with Levinsen's death. Quotes associated with him: *'''On a clear autumn day, the story goes, you can see Ys from the Watchman's Tower. I don't know whether that's true. But on a clear day in Numa… you would see the City Unbuilt.''' - Dr Brian Levinsen[[Horizon-Sight]]. ==References== [[Category:Past Librarians]] [[Category:People]]

Lord Franklin Bancroft.title: Lord Franklin Bancroft
Lord Franklin Bancroft.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Lord Franklin Bancroft.png |principle1={{Lore|Grail}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Aramaic]], [[Deep Mandaic]], [[Greek]], [[Latin]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]]}} {{Quote|Rakehell, dilettante, infuriating prodigy. Possibly dead, possibly real.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Grail}}. He can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Deep Mandaic]]. Brian of Brittany.title: Brian of Brittany
Brian of Brittany.text:
{{BoH Character
|name=Brian of Brittany
|knownfor=Building the Watchman's Tower
|born=c. 1042
|died=c. 1086}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a Breton nobleman born around 1042, and was Earl of Cornwall during the [[Solar Gothic Period]], from 1068 until his death. 

Following the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Conquest Norman Conquest] in 1066, King William I named Brian the Earl of Cornwall. In 1068, Brian funded the construction of the Watchman's Tower and a fortified gate for St Brandan's Abbey, the church that would become [[Hush House]]. 

Brian brought the Yew Tree that grows in [[Earl Brian's Field]] from Brittany, which the monks agreed to "shelter" in return for constructing the gate and tower.

At some point during his Earlhood, Brian gifted (and may have written) the three Books of Brittany ([[The Black Book of Brittany|Black]], [[The Red Book of Brittany|Red]] and [[The White Book of Brittany|White]]).

[[Category:People]]

Gervinus van Lauren.title: Gervinus van Lauren
Gervinus van Lauren.text:
{{BoH Librarian |image1=[[File:Bust.gervinus.png]] |time_as_librarian= ? - 1929 |birth= |death=}} {{quote|Gervinus van Lauren, eleventh Librarian of Hush House: an enigmatic recluse and reluctant ally of the Suppression Bureau, as skilled at closing ways as his predecessor Harries was at opening them.}}
'''Gervinus van Lauren''' was the eleventh Librarian of [[Hush House]], and was librarian at the time of the alleged fire that led to the House being abandoned. His bust is made of highly polished bronze. ==Time as Librarian== He had several [[Wine-Dark Chair]]s destroyed within a week of his arrival at the house, only saying, 'bad memories.' Like [[Willem Harries]], van Lauren preferred the [[Violet Chamber]] to the [[Librarian's Quarters]], and he had Harries' shrine to St Agnes removed from the room. The description for [[Grand Ascent - Second Floor]] before unlocking states that van Lauren was skilled at 'the forbidding of ways'. It is said that van Lauren found a way to use [[Flower|Honeyscar Jasmine]] to create [[Azoth]]. Gervinus was fond of riddles, as mentioned in the description of [[Nameday Riddle]]. In [[Letters To My Successor]], it is revealed that van Lauren made a wager with the Hooded Princes to solve seven riddles, and he believes he will not solve the seventh, which, he says, Collers has confined in the cellar of the gaol. With previous librarians [[Dr Serena Blackwood]] and [[Brian Levinsen]], he secretly explored the [[Sea-Caves]] beneath the house without the knowledge of [[George Collers|Governor Collers]]. The Nocturnal Branch gifted him the [[Desk: Reading Room|Reading Room Desk]] in 1928. He was regularly at odds with Governor Collers, as evidenced by [[Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1928]], in which Collers' secretary writes that Collers was irritated by van Lauren's refusal to assist in containing a 'Singlefoot' in the Gaol. He developed the method for removing [[Sthenic Taint]] from books during his final years as Librarian. [[Category:People]] [[Category:Past Librarians]]

An Old Friend's Address.title: An Old Friend's Address
An Old Friend's Address.text: '''An Old Friend's Address''' will be added to your Sundries after choosing the starting two [[Elements of the Soul]] cards. The exact address is determined by the second soul card chosen. Your initial acquaintance can always be hired as an [[Assistants|Assistant]] free of charge. Once you have rested at your acquaintance's, your [[Health]] will be restored. ==The Blacksmith== [[File:Introduction.blacksmith.start.png|128px|thumb|right]] {{quote|Denzil is the blacksmith of Brancrug Village. I remember him from the War. If he remembers me, I can find shelter beneath his roof - once I've reached Brancrug Village.|An Old Friend's Address}} If [[Mettle]] was chosen, your acquaintance will be Denzil, [[The Blacksmith]]. Denzil can be hired with {{Lore|Edge}}, {{Lore|Forge}}, or {{Lore|Heart}}. As an assistant, he has {{Lore|Forge|2}} and {{Lore|Edge|2}}, making him the only villager with both principles at 2. ===A Firelit Doorway=== ''Denzil looms in the fire-bright doorway. 'You? Here? How?''' ''I stagger into the smithy, out of the cold at last. Without another word, Denzil hands me a blanket and sets about stoking the fire: the warmest welcome of which he is capable.'' ''Denzil only has the one bed, but he can offer me a straw mattress in the smithy. It's smoky, but the warmth is very welcome.'' ''Denzil pauses at the door as I wish him goodnight. 'Sun'll be back,' he observes. 'Always do. Used to say that in the War, dint we?' The words linger as he clumps up the passage. The lamp-flame flickers red, gold, red.'' ==The Coffinmaker== [[File:Introduction.coffinmaker.start.png|128px|thumb|right]] {{quote|Mr Kille is the coffinmaker of Brancrug Village. I once wrote kindly of his poetry. His home is always open to me (though he's asked me never to mention poetry in front of Mrs Kille). I can find shelter for tonight under their roof - once I've reached Brancrug Village.}} If [[Wist]] was chosen, your acquaintance will be Mr Kille, [[The Coffinmaker]]. Mr Kille can be hired with {{Lore|Winter}}. As an assistant, he has {{Lore|Winter|2}} and {{Lore|Sky|1}}. If Mr Kille is your starting acquaintance, you can also hire his wife, Mrs Kille, free of charge. ===Shelter!=== ''Mr Kille struggles with the door. The wind almost snatches it from his hands. His eyes widen as he sees me.'' ''Mr Kille is grinning like the happiest of skulls. 'Come in, come in! Less 'ee wants fitted for a box?' And he leads me into the warmth of the parlour, calling for Mrs Kille to come see, come see the rescue.'' ''Mr Kille constructed the bed himself - I rather fear with the same tools he uses to shape coffins. It is not a comfortable bed. But it's dry, clean, and warm.'' ''I sit up talking with Mr and Mrs K, as the wind rattles the shutters and the fire shrugs its way emberward. I'm very hungry, and Mrs K's galettes are impossibly good. Mr K pretends to grumble about foreign cooking. No-one is convinced.'' ==Mrs Kille== [[File:Introduction.midwife.start.png|128px|thumb|right]] {{quote|Mrs Kille is the handywoman - the midwife - of Brancrug village. I knew her long ago in Paris, when her surname was not 'Kille' but 'Raveline', and her sister was a viscountess. Her home is always open to me (though she's asked me not to bring up the title thing when Mr Kille's around). I can find shelter for tonight under their roof - once I've reached Brancrug Village.}} If [[Ereb]] was chosen, your acquaintance will be Mrs Kille, [[The Midwife]]. Mrs Kille can be hired with {{Lore|Grail}}. As an assistant, she has {{Lore|Grail|2}} and {{Lore|Heart|1}}. If Mrs Kille is your starting acquaintance, you can also hire her husband, Mr Kille, free of charge. ===Shelter=== ''Mrs Kille opens the door with caution, but flings it wide, letting the wind bang it, when she sees me.'' '''Mrs Kille drags me into her broad embrace, releases me when she realises how damp I am, and then she's calling for Mr Kille and dragging me into the warmth of the parlour. 'Sit 'ee down and get a drop of warm in!', she enjoins sternly.'' ''Mr K constructed the bed himself - I rather fear with the same tools he uses to shape coffins. It is not a comfortable bed. But it's dry, clean, and warm.'' ''Mrs K and I sit up late talking over old times in the Latin Quarter, when the world and we were very different. Mr K listens as he cleans his pipe. 'Wine and roses,' he observes. 'Spose the wine is all spilt now, but the roses'll come up again, won't them?''' ==The Rector== [[File:Introduction.rector.start.png|128px|thumb|right]] {{quote|I first heard of Brancrug through its Rector, Reverend Timothy. For years now I've been exchanging letters with him. I can find shelter for tonight under his roof - once I've reached Brancrug Village. [The Rector can also introduce you to other villagers.]}} If [[Phost]] was chosen, your acquaintance will be Reverend Timothy, [[The Rector]]. Reverend Timothy can be hired with {{Lore|Lantern}} or {{Lore|Knock}}. As an assistant, he has {{Lore|Lantern|2}} and {{Lore|Knock|1}}. ===A Clergyman Distrait=== ''The Reverend staggers back as if he'd received a blow, and then he's bombarding me with terrified, delighted questions before I'm even through the door.'' ''Timothy ushers me into the bright hall, casting about for his housekeeper, and asking questions the whole time. 'How did you come here? Was it the wreck? Terrence! Terrence, do fetch towels!''' ''Reverend Timothy flutters fussily while Terrence the Housekeeper busies herself with practicalities. She shows me to a warm room at the top of the house where a fire is already made up.'' ''Reverend Timothy is touchingly excited to meet his correspondent in person. I am still too exhausted to hold up my end of the conversation, and Terrence is not a talkative woman, but the Reverend can talk for three. At last however he suddenly realises how exhausted I am, and lets me sleep.'' [[Category:People]]

Abbot Geffrey.title: Abbot Geffrey
Abbot Geffrey.text:
{{BoH Character
|name=Abbot Geffrey
|image=[[File:Geffrey.png]]
}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was an abbot, author, a prophet-dreamer, and possibly a nyctodromist. 

He is associated with the [[Principles|Principle]] of {{Lore|Knock}}

== Life ==

{{PAGENAME}} was an abbot of [[Hush House#Solar_Gothic_Period|St Brandan's Abbey]] in the fifteenth century of the [[Solar Gothic Period]].<ref>[['Abbot Geffrey']]</ref> 

All three of his written works are in [[Latin]], so he knew that language.

All three of his written works discuss [[w:c:secret-histories:Janus|Janus]], and their potential names if Janus were an [[w:c:secret-histories:Hour|Hour]]. All of these works have information about [[The Great Signs and the Great Scars]], so it can be presumed he knew some of that skill.

He permitted [[Natan of Regensburg]] to live at [[Hush House#Solar_Gothic_Period|St Brandan's Abbey]]. 

According to the descriptions of [['The Sister-and-Witch']] and [['The Witch-and-Sister']], he has had prophetic dreams involving both of these Hours.

He ordered the that the [[w:c:secret-histories:Chancel|Chancel]] be venerated in the [[Chancel of the Abbey Church]], but not actually be named to avoid heresy. 

[[The Carbonek Schism]] references the [[Workstations|workstation]] [[Shrine: the Chancel]] as 'Abbot Geffrey's Secret', and is connected to a [[The Sun Disfigured|secret of the house]]

He has a bust in the [[Hush House]] - [['Abbot Geffrey']]

== Works ==
He has written three [[Readable|books]]:
* ''[[The Raptures of Forculus]]''
* ''[[The Elations of Limentinus]]''
* ''[[Cardea's Delights]]''

== Speculation ==
* As is it known that he had dreams of the [[w:c:secret-histories:The_Twins|Sister-and-Witch]], and that hour (but notable '''not''' the twin hour of [[w:c:secret-histories:The_Twins|The Witch-and-Sister]])<ref>[[The Three and the Three (Vatican Manuscript)]]</ref> is a member of the Chancel, is is possible the Sister-and-Witch either inspired or influenced him to revere the Chancel at the [[Chancel of the Abbey Church]]

Ernestine Peterhans.title: Ernestine Peterhans
Ernestine Peterhans.text: '''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the Seneschale of [[Hush House|Brancrug]] for over five decades. ==Biography== Ernestine Peterhans was [[Hendrik Dewulf]]'s quartermaster while he was a mercenary, until he appointed her as head of his new household. She was known as the 'Iron Seneschale' and served for three generations of [[Dewulf Family|Dewulfs]]. She served during Hendrik's son, [[Thomas Dewulf]], and great-grandson, [[Walter Dewulf]]'s reigns. Ernestine was soft-spoken and steely-willed. There were persistent rumours of inappropriate activities between her and Hendrik, as well as Thomas, as they were both often seen descending the back stairs and visiting her [[Servants' Quarters - North|private chambers]] in person. Credence is given to this due to the fact that the contents of ''[[An Impertinent Vitulation]]'', a book she wrote, concern the brewing of aphrodisiacs and her casual mention of the rousing liquor [[Rubywise Ruin]] being a favourite of the severe Hendrik Dewulf. She recorded her conversations with the 'little darkness' in the [[Stair Tenebrous]] in ''[[The Shadow in the Stair]]'', which she called 'Donkerling'. After failing to consume her, it demanded sacrifices of her; she brought it mice instead. She was very interested in what it could tell her about the circumstances of shipwrecks, hinting that she may have been planning a salvage expedition. Ernestine attempted to use the growths of [[The Earl's Yew|the yew tree]] in [[Earl Brian's Field]] to advantage in her business affairs, but it failed. Fearing that she misinterpreted all the omens, she was very worried when the heir and grandson of Thomas Dewulf, Giles, ran off with 'the Pale Trollop Hafren' in a year when the tree flowered white, deeply concerned for the continuation of the Dewulf line. She was over eighty years old when she reconciled Thomas and his disgraced son Giles on his death bed. She was the author of: *''[[An Impertinent Vitulation]]'' *''[[The Shadow in the Stair]]'' *''[[Three Flowers Hath the Tree]]'' ==Trivia== *She may be related to [[Alexander Peterhans]]. Christopher Illopoly.title: Christopher Illopoly
Christopher Illopoly.text:
{{BoH Character |name=Christopher Illopoly |image=[[File:Christopher Illopoly.png]] |knownfor=Writing the ''Travelling at Night'' series |born=1888-1889 |relationships=[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] (adoptive father)
[[Teresa Galmier]]
(romantic relationship)}} __NOTOC__'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an author best known for his ''Travelling at Night'' series. ==Life== Illopoly was born around 1888-89. Very little is known about his upbringing prior to 1903, when [[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] adopted him from a Bristol orphanage. For four years, he served as Fraser's protégé, although the two had a complicated relationship.''[[Perugian Diaries]]'' In 1907, at the age of 18, the two parted ways 'almost amicably', according to Illopoly's diaries, when he moved to Italy to study theology at the University of Perugia, enrolling under the name 'Christopher Strathcoyne'. He changed his surname to 'Illopoly' at some point after this.[[Motley Tower: Dispensary]] Illopoly did not complete his degree, leaving Perugia in 1909 to study Umbrian folk-songs. During this time, he may have visited the site of Lake Fucino,''[[Perugian Diaries]]'' near where the [[Fucine]] language originated. In 1912, he published ''[[Just Verse]]'', a volume of experimental poetry that did not perform well. At some point, he had a romantic relationship with [[Teresa Galmier]], author of the ''Locksmith's Dream'' novels and {{Lore|Lantern}}-long. It is implied that their relationship ended because Galmier wanted to ascend to Longhood.[https://uadaf.theevilroot.xyz/frangiclave/deck/mansus_whitedoor1 ''Cultist Simulator'': Lodge of the Sage Knight] He recuperated in the [[Infirmary]] at some point after the Great War and stayed at [[Hush House]] for some time, after [[Dr Serena Blackwood]] arranged rooms for him at the [[Motley Tower: Illopoly's Nook]], ostensibly to help with the collection, but possibly because she saw a potential ally against [[George Collers]], the Governor of the Cucurbit Prison. ==Works== Illopoly has written five books including the ''Travelling at Night'' series. He has also edited one text. *''[[Just Verse]]'' *''[[Perugian Diaries]]'' *''[[The Radical Measure (Glossed)]]'' - Illopoly's 'well regarded' edited version of ''[[The Radical Measure]]'' *''[[Travelling at Night, vol 1]]'' *''[[Travelling at Night, vol 2]]'' *''[[Travelling at Night, vol 3]]'' ==Trivia== *The [['Fraser Strathcoyne'|bust of his adoptive father]] can be found in the room he was staying in. ==References== [[Category:Authors]] [[Category:People]]

George Collers.title: George Collers
George Collers.text:
'''George Collers''' was the governor of Brancrug Gaol, also known as [[The Cucurbit]]. 

==Life==
He oversaw the construction, operation, and records for the prison between 1896 and 1929. The prison was established on Brancrug Isle in the period immediately following [[Thirza Blake|Thirza Blake's]] disappearance, as her profligate spending had caused [[Hush House]] to fall deep into debt. Collers, an employee of Nocturnal Branch, which subsequently became the Suppression Bureau, had an extremely tense relationship with the Librarians of this period. He was highly dedicated to his mission, but appreciated a certain degree of luxury, at least as far as prison governor's offices go.

Although the Prison's original intent was to [[Cell: ?|isolate]], [[Cell: Long|pacify]], and in some cases [[Cell: Worm-Inhabited|decontaminate]] (formerly-)human prisoners, Collers also used it and its prisoners for various experiments. Among these experiments, he attempted to identify those who had Carapace Cross lineage, and even caused two prisoners to transform into 'sickle-formed pseudocrustacea' and lose the ability to breathe air.<ref>[[Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1927]]</ref> He designed the [[Condignator]] allegedly to treat the most recalcitrant prisoners, though few survived his ministrations. Despite his ruthlessness, however, he did occasionally release prisoners who had completed their rehabilitation.

Collers perished in the fire that both destroyed the prison and caused Brancrug to be abandoned in the first place. He had taken the prisoner in the [[Oubliette]], an unidentified 'Name of greed and time', and successfully 'confined a flame in human flesh'. This Name eventually escaped its imprisonment, and sought vengeance against Collers for what he had done to it; however, by the time it got Collers to the Condignator, there wasn't enough left of him to interrogate.

==Works==

Although there are no known works written by him, there records of experiments directed by him

* ''[[Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1927]]
* ''[[Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1928]]
* ''[[The Admonitory Automata Project]]

Burzghash.title: Burzghash
Burzghash.text:
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an author of several books, and was formerly in service to the [[w:c:secret-histories:The_Elegiast|Ivory Dove]] <ref>[[The Silver Book]]</ref> also known as The Elegiast

== Life ==

The books he wrote all are classified in the [[Dawn Period]], so he was active during that time.

He at one point was in service to the [[The Hours|Hour]] called [[w:c:secret-histories:The_Elegiast|The Elegiast]], but later joined the [[w:c:secret-histories:House_of_Lethe|Ordo Limiae]].

He at some point made prophecies regarding the [[Hush House]] and the City Unbuilt, and two of his books (''[[The Messenger Awaiting Her Destination]]'' and ''[[The Road to Janus]]'') concern these.

As he has written books both in [[Vak]] and [[Fucine]], he knows both these languages.

== Works ==
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is known to have written four books.

* ''[[The Grand Passage of the Hours]]''
* ''[[The Road to Janus]]''
* ''[[The Messenger Awaiting Her Destination]]''
* ''[[The Silver Book]]''

== Trivia ==

As members of the [[w:c:secret-histories:House_of_Lethe|Ordo Limiae]] are known for taking pseudonyms, it is likely this is not the original name of this author.

== Speculation ==

The other two books associated with the other oaths the members of the Ordo Limiae take ([[The Iron Book]] and [[The Ivory Book]]) are written by authors that have names that appear to be named after characters from other fictional universes. [[Melerai Yivni]] is likely associated with Fallen London<ref>https://x.com/failbettergames/status/1483739576799842308</ref> and [[Kurenai]] possibly being associated with Naruto, and highly likely to be associated with Japan as a whole given they 'fled the tyranny of the Chrysanthemum Throne' <ref>[[The Ivory Book]]</ref>. As such, the name Burzghash may also reference a character from a fictional universe - possible a character from the Lord of the Rings<ref>https://lotro-wiki.com/wiki/Warchief_B%C3%BArzgh%C3%A2sh</ref>. If the name is rendered as Búrz Ghâsh - these could be the words for Dark (from Black Speech)<ref>https://tolkiengateway.net/wiki/B%C3%BArz</ref> and Fire (from Orkish)<ref>https://tolkiengateway.net/wiki/Gh%C3%A2sh</ref>, making the English translation to this name "Dark Fire"

Ilse Bischoff.title: Ilse Bischoff
Ilse Bischoff.text:
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the creator of several films, and is Mansus-aware, perhaps among the Know, but likely not a Long.

== Life ==

Likely born 1901 (See Trivia) and is dead as of March 7th, 1936 - when the Twelfth Librarian arrives at [[Brancrug Village]].

At some point during her life, created three films (see Works), and as [[EXPERIMENT BEYOND SIGHT]] mentions her untimely death, and is available for the Librarian to watch, she is dead when we are able to access this film. 

She displays knowledge of Edge-Hours and likely knew some [[Hyksos]]<ref>[[THE OPEN HEAD]]</ref>

She appeared to have predicted or forseen the fire that lead to the [[Hush House]] being abandoned per the mastery text of [[EXPERIMENT BEYOND SIGHT]]

== Works ==
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is known to have produced three films.

* ''[[EXPERIMENT BEYOND SIGHT]]''
* ''[[THE OPEN HEAD]]''
* ''[[COLOURS IN THE LIVER]]''

== Trivia ==

This Book of Hours character is likely a reference to the real-life person Ilse Bischoff<ref>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilse_Bischoff</ref>, though her interest in film and difference in known death in Book of Hours versus when the real-life person died suggests her life may be only loosely based on the real-life person.

Lars Westergren.title: Lars Westergren
Lars Westergren.text:
{{BoH Character
|name=Lars Westergren
|image=[[File:Lars_Westergren_Diarist.png]]
|aka=The Diarist
}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a {{Lore|Lantern}}-Long, an author, an explorer, and a murder.

==Life==

He was active during the [[Dawn Period]] as one of his known works [[The Concursum Diaries]] is from that period, so he can be stated to be born during or before that time period.

He may have employed some life-extending methods, as the collected letters of his time as a fugitive [[Letters from a Fugitive]] are dated to the [[Baronial Period]].

He at some point had a daughter, as that was who he was writing his letters to. 

During his time as a fugitive, he claims he spent a year with the Légion de Seuil, patrolling the Bounds, a month in the Priory of Captains in Morbihan, and seven days, in Ys behind the wave.

After this, his pursuers caught up with him, and he then 'attempted the Paths of the Sun'. This may have succeeded, as he was reportedly spotted at the 'Christmas Market' in Vienna in 1929. 

According to a [[Salon]] conversation between [[Dr Serena Blackwood]] and [[Ms Azita Bukhara]], he ascended to a {{Lore|Lantern}}-Long that went by the name [[w:c:cultistsimulator:The_Diarist|The Diarist]], possibly as a result of attempting the Paths of the Sun.

==Works==

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is known to have written one book

* [[The Concursum Diaries]]

He also wrote letters to his daughter which were collected into another book 

* [[Letters from a Fugitive]]

==Trivia==
* It is possible to face him as an ascended {{Lore|Lantern}}-Long in [[w:c:cultistsimulator:Cultist_Simulator|Cultist Simulator]] in the [[w:c:cultistsimulator:Legacies#Apostle_Entheate|Apostle Entheate Legacy]]

Little Sophia.title: Little Sophia
Little Sophia.text:
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an author, a monster-hunter, and an initiate of [[w:c:secret-histories:The_Colonel|The Colonel]] 

== Life ==

At some point in her life, Sophia began monster-hunting, one prominent example of monsters being hunted is [[w:c:secret-histories:Worms|Worms]]. She would render some of these for display in the Worm Museum by making and ink of the remains, recording the hunt, then burning the record at an altar to The Colonel<ref>[[Oblations in Iron]]</ref>.

She has never visited the [[w:c:secret-histories:Mansus|Mansus]] in person.

She is familiar with [[w:c:secret-histories:Long|Long]], and has likely come into conflict with them<ref>[[By Their Marks Shall Ye Know them]]</ref>.

All of the books she is known to have written are in English, so she knows that language.

All of the books she is known to have written are from the [[Curia Period]], so she was active around that time.

== Works ==
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is known to have written two books.

* ''[[By Their Marks Shall Ye Know them]]''
* ''[[Oblations in Iron]]''

== Speculation ==
* There is a [[Salon#Salon_Stories|Salon]] story where [[Dr Yvette Southey]] questions [[Lalla Chaima]] about {{PAGENAME}}'s motives and credibility, and Lalla is non-committal. As Lalla is known to be associated with The Colonel, as {{PAGENAME}} is, this may indicate that there is some context about her that Lalla knows, but is unclear to us.
* Her name may be a reference to the Gnostic Sophia<ref>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophia_(Gnosticism)</ref>, as there are other Gnostic references in the Secret Histories universe

Hagar.title: Hagar
Hagar.text:
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' has other titles including
*Queen of Shur<ref name="shuritic">[[Shuritic Book of Suns]]</ref>
*Mother of Wolves<ref name="shuritic">[[Shuritic Book of Suns]]</ref>

== Life ==

Not much is known about the life of {{PAGENAME}} though some might mirror that of the biblical Hagar<ref name="biblical_hagar">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hagar</ref>

As the only known work by her dates to the [[Dawn Period]], she may have been active then, though that might conflict with the life of the biblical Hagar.

She knows [[Deep Mandaic]], as her only known work is written in that language.

==Works==
She has written one [[Readable|scroll]]:

* [[Shuritic Book of Suns]]

This scroll contains a [[Numen]] related to the romance between [[w:c:secret-histories:The_Sun-in-Splendour|The Sun-in-Splendor]] and [[w:c:secret-histories:The_Forge_of_Days|The Forge of Days]]

== Trivia ==
*This author is likely a reference to the biblical figure Hagar<ref name="biblical_hagar">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hagar</ref>
*The place Shur likely refers to the location mentioned in the bible<ref>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shur_(Bible)</ref>, which would also explain why this scroll is in [[Deep Mandaic]] as that language is associated with the "deep desert"<ref>[[Deep Mandaic]]</ref>, as the biblical Shur is supposed to be.

C.R.O.D.title: C.R.O.D
C.R.O.D.text:
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an author best known for his work [[Those Indignities Perpetrated By the Deceitful Fraternity of Obliviates]], known for its scathing tone for the apparent disregard of [[w:c:secret-histories:Obliviates|The Obliviates]]' disregard for the predecessor society [[w:c:secret-histories:House_of_Lethe|House of Lethe]]'s traditions

== Life ==

Not much is known about his origins, but at some point he became familiar with both the House of Lethe and The Obliviates, and their occult traditions, so it can be assumed he knew of, and likely associated with some of the members of the order in one or both of its forms.

His one known book is dated to the [[Baronial Period]], and the Obliviates were active in that period under that name, so he was likely active during that time period.

His one known book is in [[Latin]] so he likely knew that language.
== Works ==

He has written one [[Readable|book]]:

* [[Those Indignities Perpetrated By the Deceitful Fraternity of Obliviates]]

== Trivia ==
* The one known book by this author exists in both ''[[Book of Hours]]'' and ''[[w:c:cultistsimulator:Cultist_Simulator|Cultist Simulator]]'', however the reading completion text for both of these mention different 'offenses' by the Obliviates in the eyes of {{PAGENAME}}
* The cover of [[Those Indignities Perpetrated By the Deceitful Fraternity of Obliviates]] has the same icon as [[Sceptical]] from ''Book of Hours'' and [[w:c:cultistsimulator:Resentment|Resentment]] from ''Cultist Simulator'', which seem to correlate with how {{PAGENAME}} feels about the Obliviates.

Abbess Melancthe.title: Abbess Melancthe
Abbess Melancthe.text:
{{BoH Character
|name=Abbess Melancthe
|image=[[File:'St Melancthe'.png]]
}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was an abbess, author, alchemist, a painter, an illustrator, and visionary. 

She has also gone by the name '''St Melancthe'''

She is associated with the [[Principles]] of {{Lore|Forge}}, {{Lore|Lantern}}, and {{Lore|Sky}}

== Life ==

{{PAGENAME}} was an abbess of [[Hush House#Solar_Gothic_Period|St Brandan's Abbey]] in the early years of the [[Solar Gothic Period]]. 

She was known for her visions, and was highly interested in the sun, both of which are strongly associated with {{Lore|Lantern}}-lore, and makes sense as an abbess for the [[w:c:secret-histories:Church_of_the_Unconquered_Sun|Church of the Unconquered Sun]].

She corresponded with Gunhild of Wesse<ref>[[Salon]]</ref>. It is considered likely that she sent [[A Descent of the Shell]] to Gunhild, which resulted in Gunhild's blindness and provoked in her 'a dream of eyes'.

Given her connection to Gunhild, daughter of King Harold, and the timeline of the [[Solar Gothic Period]] is is possible she is one of the first, if not the first abbesses for the [[Solar Gothic Period]]. 

Some of her works are known to dazzle or otherwise strain eyes.

She was almost burned for heresy for her comments on how to create [[Iotic Essence]].

She is the most revered and heterodox of the Isle's abbesses.

Her skull is inside a bust of her - [['St Melancthe']].

== Works ==
She has written two [[Readable|books]]:
* ''[[A Descent of the Shell]]''
* ''[[The Mirror of Melancthe]]''

She also created [[Wall Art]] in the form of illustrated vellum pages
* ''[['As Above, So Below']]

== Quotes ==
{{Quote|In the later operations of the Forge, the Madrugad yields to the true Forge of Days, and the essence begins to redden.}}
From the description of [[Iotic Essence]]

== Trivia ==
* It is possible that the name was inspired by character Melancthe from the Lyonesse Trilogy<ref>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyonesse_Trilogy</ref>. Notably, there are connection to Ys and Arthurian legend in the trilogy, making the connection besides the exact name more plausible.
* She is connected to Gunhild, and the historical Gunhild<ref>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunhild_of_Wessex</ref> married Alan the Red, then later Alan the Black. This is highly suggestive of a connection to [[Earl Brian's Field]], becoming even more notable when in-universe the sons of King Harold (who would be Gunhild's brothers) raided Cornwall.

== Speculation ==

The other two books associated with the other oaths the members of the Ordo Limiae take ([[The Iron Book]] and [[The Silver Book]]) are written by authors that have names that appear to be named after characters from other fictional universes. Garcia Sauri.title: Garcia Sauri
Garcia Sauri.text:
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an author, ectastic, and mystic.

He goes by Garcia Sauri in [[The Crossing to Noon]], but if the text for [[The Known-Unknown Tantra]] is correct, his full name is ''Carlos {{PAGENAME}}''

== Life ==

He knew and wrote of the relationship between [[Lord Franklin Bancroft]] and [[Eva Dewulf]] in [[The Crossing to Noon]], where he shows awareness of secret histories concepts like the [[w:c:secret-histories:Mansus|Mansus]]. 

The books he wrote is classified in the [[Curia Period]], so he was active during that time.

He has written a book in [[Latin]], and as noted in the [[The Known-Unknown Tantra]], he was known to recite that tantra in three languages, perhaps Latin, [[Sanskrit]] (which that book is in) and Spanish, given his name and that is noted to be in the Pyrenees.<ref>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrenees</ref>

== Works ==
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is known to have written one book.

* ''[[The Crossing to Noon]]''

He is mentioned to have recited the [[The Known-Unknown Tantra]], but the tantra was likely not created by him.

Mr Zachary Wakefield.text:
{{BoH Character |name=Mr Zachary Wakefield |image=Zachary_Wakefield.png |principle1={{Lore|Knock}} |principle2={{Lore|Winter}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Fucine]], [[Greek]], [[Killasimi]], [[Latin]], [[Phrygian]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |address=One is instructed to address the letter literally 'HOUSE, STREET, TOWN, SHIRE, COUNTRY'}} {{Quote|Marksman, detective, renegade. He has always been a quiet man, but since he left the Suppression Bureau, he has grown even quieter, and terribly still - except for his fingers and for his eyes, always in restless motion.}}
'''Mr Zachary Wakefield''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]], interested in {{Lore|Knock}} and {{Lore|Winter}}. He is a potential Secretary Enigmatic for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. He can be paid one [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Fucine]] or [[Killasimi]]. During [[Brian Levinsen]]'s time as Librarian, Wakefield spent time recuperating in the [[Infirmary]] of Hush House from injuries sustained during the Great War. ==Invitations and Salons== Wakefield requires 3 {{Lore|Winter}} to be invited to Hush House. He prefers food and drink with {{Lore|Winter}}. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation !1st Lesson !Second Conversation ! 2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] |Zachary shows Dagmar a Tanglebrag he's made. He tries to explain how it 'portrays and betrays' the paths of his future. She tries to understand. |[[Edicts Liminal]] |Dagmar is trying to explain the more risqué jokes in Savage's 'A Seventh Voice' to Zachary. Zachary is courteously taking notes. |[[Preliminal Meter]] |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Zachary and al-Adim speak of how things end; al-Adim with a kind of eager nostalgia; Zachary with simple eagerness. |[[Putrefactions & Calcinations]] |Zachary, unselfconsciously, recites a poem-in-progress to al-Adim: a clashing fortress of a piece. He beats out the rhythm on the tabletop. Al-Adim tentatively suggests a refinement, which Zachary, judiciously, accepts. |[[Preliminal Meter]] |- | [[DI Douglas Moore]] |Douglas tries to reminisce with Zachary about their shared work at the Suppression Bureau - the time they had to suppress a Percussigiant troupe which was roaming the Forest of Dean. But Zachary only stares and shakes his head - 'I don't remember' - 'I don't remember' - 'I remember that it was cold' - 'I don't remember'. |[[Quenchings & Quellings]] |Zachary and Douglas reminisce about a case they both worked on, years ago, when they had to find a way to bind a thriceros which had somehow found its way into the Thames. Douglas recalls how the binding-process first awakened his enthusiasm for knitting, and Zachary makes the necessary effort to fold his face into a smile. |[[Quenchings & Quellings]] |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] |Zachary asks Arun about the fabled war between the Great Hooded Princes and the Obliviates. Arun favours Zachary with his triangular smile. 'It wasn't really a war. Mother Many-Armed just took offence at some of their rites. Well, their habits. And we were all still her children...' |[[Edicts Liminal]] |‘Remember,’ Arun tells Zachary, ‘that it’s always too late, eventually; but it never is until then.’ Zachary lets out a long sigh. ‘You always say that. It’s less helpful than you think it is.’ |[[Putrefactions & Calcinations]] |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] |Zachary asks Serena about the Wheelocks of Treowen and in particular poor doomed Gregory, the 'demi-dyad'; but they conclude that nothing in that sad story will help Zachary. |[[Door & Wall]] |Serena offers to shape a prison for Zachary and his passenger if things become too dire. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Stanislav and Zachary discuss the 'merciful measures' of the witch Nyn. These two might say more if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]] |After their conversation on containment-in-glass last time, Morgen and Zachary have brought each other exhibits – or gifts. For her, a blued glass mirror that’s always cold to the touch; for him, a glass key that she suggests he crush if things become ‘too much what they are.’
[Morgen seems almost protective of Zachary.] |[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]] |- | [[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |‘I have a name’, Zachary says dispassionately, ‘and another name. One of them is written only in Killasimi. I will speak of it, because you have invited me. But I will not speak it, because I am a guest.’ |[[Killasimi]] |Zachary is having a bad day. His eyes are wide and staring; his teeth chatter. Olympe lays a hand on his arm to comfort him, and quotes from the Debate of Seven Cups: ‘Sorrow then is Sense’s final Solvent…’ |[[Solutions & Separations]] |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Zachary speaks to Ehsan of the stairway to Nowhere which haunts his paintings, of the lamps of black nephrite, the star-twinkle of the flowers in Miss Naenia's hair. There is more than one temptation to Nowhere, he says... |[[Sights & Sensations]] |Ehsan and Zachary discuss Illopoly’s line – after Husher: ‘the White is West of the World, and Winter does not wait forever.’ Zachary says suddenly that he would like to paint the White; Ehsan gently encourages him; they discuss the palest pigments. |[[Sights & Sensations]] |- | [[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Fraser inquires - sometimes tactfully - about Zachary's condition, what exactly he bears within him, what dangers it might present, and what it might become. Zachary answers - always cautiously and elliptically. |[[Serpents & Venoms]] |Fraser suggests ways in which Zachary might advance or evolve his limbless passengers so that they might both become something more - in safety. Zachary is not convinced. |[[Serpents & Venoms]] |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |Azita and Zachary discuss how to maintain a delicate balance, in the occult or the personal; and also how to dispose of corpses. |[[Sickle & Eclipse]] |Zachary and Azita compare exorcism techniques. She asks jokingly what techniques might be used to exorcise him, and immediately regrets it when he doesn't realise she's joking and answers as seriously as he can. |[[Sickle & Eclipse]] |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Zachary and Coquille discuss the ways in which the Hours ‘restrain and constrict’ their rivalries, to prevent war in the Mansus. Zachary feels the ‘restraints and constrictions’ are growing weak. Coquille seems titillated by the prospect, but Zachary moves his head from side to side in negation. ‘The Worms,’ he whispers. |[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars]] |Zachary and Coquille swap parables of the 'Great Scar' - the goddess-language Vak, who is the Peacock Door - and of how she might be healed. Coquille points out that would be the end of Vak. 'Yes,' Zachary agrees, 'the end of her pain.' |[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars]] |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Zachary asks Corso to teach him a prayer in Hyksos - 'in case I should die when I wake.'...
[These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Hyksos]] |Zachary wants more help from Corso with his Hyksos studies. He’s heard that the ceremonies of the Légion du Seuil sometimes employ that language. He’s considering joining the Légion, but he wants to understand it better first. |[[Hyksos]] |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Zachary describes his understanding of the 'Angel of Storms', the beauty of her underclouds, the accesses of her lightning, how he yearns to cage her in glass. Agdistis listens patiently; now and then his eyes flicker as if he understands. |[[Quenchings & Quellings]] |Zachary speaks with staccato enthusiasm of the poetic sabotage efforts of someone he calls 'Hammerbreaker'. His voice remains flat but his hands twitch wildly: his fingers beat a complex rhythm on the tabletop. Agdistis listens sympathetically. |[[Putrefactions & Calcinations]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Zachary confides to Mrs Kille that he thinks he will eventually be delivered of 'a kind of child'. He asks if she can help. She scrutinizes him; and says quietly that she cannot. He asks if she thinks he will live through the birth; she considers for a long time, and then says more quietly that she thinks that he will. He asks, last, when she thinks the child might be born: she leans in close and whispers, 'I think on a midsummer's day.' |[[Snow Stories]] |Zachary asks if Mr Kille might make a coffin for him. ‘I don’t need it yet,’ he says, ‘but we all might be grateful.’ Mr Kille shakes his head slowly: not his kind of work. But he suggests that Zachary speak of his troubles, and Zachary does so, albeit elliptically, in terms of mirrors; snow; wings; and the ‘twist in the heart’. |[[Snow Stories]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |It seems that Denzil and Zachary know each other from the time that Zachary spent recuperating in Brancrug after the Great War. They speak of the paths they have not taken. Denzil has never married, nor been further south than Ypres. Zachary has not touched a gun since the War, nor ever returned to the place of his birth. |[[Ragged Crossroads]] |Denzil and Zachary speak more of their old acquaintance from the time when Zachary was recovering in Brancrug after the Great War. They recall those they both knew at Hush House: Hattington (‘in a New York madhouse, I think’), Illopoly (‘in Marseilles, I think’), and Collers (‘dead, I hope’)… |[[Ragged Crossroads]] |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Reverend Timothy talks excitedly to Zachary about eggs, clocks, the local badger population and his housekeeper's black pudding. Eventually, he notices that Zachary isn't really paying attention, and that Zachary's expression is not cheerful. In a softer tone, he begins to explicate St Lewen's discourses on endings and beginnings. |[[Auroral Contemplations]] |Reverend Timothy, who perhaps has gleaned something of the nature of Zachary's condition - or perhaps only thought he has gleaned it - offers Zachary prayers and meditative exercises that he believes might help. Zachary repeats them back to him without any change in expression. |[[Quenchings & Quellings]] |- |Hidden Conversation |''[Requires [[Onion Gratin]]]''
Zachary sits suddenly upright, staring at the dish of onion au gratin before him. 'We used to get this in the infirmary,' he says to no one in particular. 'When I came back from the War. I used to call it ''trojan cheese''.' He takes a cautious bite; then another. 'I still don't like it,' he confides. His face is typically expressionless, but tears trickle down his cheeks. He begins to talk about the War... |[[Disciplines of the Scar]] | | |} ==Incidents== Wakefield can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of the Endless Guest]] *[[The Affair of the Grunewald Provision]] *[[The Affair of the Messenger's Casket]] *[[The Affair of the Open Reverend]] *[[The Affair of the Oriflamme Heist]] *[[The Affair of the Particular Mystique]] ==Further Stories== *After completing [[The Affair of the Oriflamme Heist]], Zachary can be spoken with. **You can speak with him by giving him one of any [[Memory]]. He will inform you that [[Daymare]] is behind the Heist. * After completing [[The Affair of the Messenger's Casket]], Zachary can be spoken with. ** If you also assisted [[Daymare]] during the incident, you will need to speak with him twice. He can be provided with a book of [[Sights & Sensations|Sights and Sensations]] 10, or a something on 'a Hooded Prince, Jekadu, who knew a way of escape we might find useful'. Doing so gives Zachary [[Inspired]] and Sympathy: Chandler. He will reward the Librarian with an [[Inkling]] and the [[Wall Art]] 'Mihail in Glory' which has aspects of [[Forge]] 2 and [[Lantern]] 2. It can be placed in the Chancel to allow it to accept Forge and Lantern. *After completing The Affair of the Endless Guest, Zachary will tell the Librarian that Spencer "wants to go out" if offered the {{Lore|Knock}} Readable or "down" if offered the {{Lore|Winter}} Readable. He always warns that Spencer is on his way and asks the Librarian to help him. He gets [[Inspired]], Fear: Nowhere, and Agenda: Revelation if Spencer goes "out" or Agenda: Peace if Spencer goes "down". Spencer himself will also arrive in the next Numa. ==Trivia== *Wakefield also appeared in [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Cultist_Simulator_Wiki Cultist Simulator] as a Hunter who, if made into a Rival and recruited, would have the {{Lore|Winter}} primary aspect and the {{Lore|Lantern}} secondary aspect.
