Southey Family.title: Southey Family
Southey Family.text:
{{Family infobox
|title1=Southey Family
|family_members=*[[Abra Southey]]
*[[Dr. Yvette Southey]]}}

'''The Southey Family''' were a family with ties to the [[Dewulf Family|Dewulfs]]. Although they never directly married into the family, rumours persist that some of the Southeys alive today are related to the Dewulfs. 

=Notable Family Members=
*[[Abra Southey]]
*[[Dr. Yvette Southey]]
*[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Southey Robert Southey]

[[Category:People]]

Mr Peter Agdistis.title: Mr Peter Agdistis
Mr Peter Agdistis.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Mr_Peter_Agdistis.png |principle1={{Lore|Heart}} |principle2={{Lore|Sky}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Aramaic]], [[Fucine]], [[Greek]], [[Phrygian]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |address=Deutsche Tanzbühne, Berlin}} {{quote|Musician, mystic, impresario. Agdistis was a dancer once. One cannot see him without knowing it. The wound in his thigh keeps him from the stage; but his every movement still has the cadence of a prayer.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]]. He is a potential Secretary Salvant for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. He can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Fucine]]. ==Invitations and Salons== Agdistis reqiures 3 {{Lore|Sky}} to be invited to Hush House. He prefers food and drink with {{Lore|Heart}}. == Incidents== Agdistis can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of 'Apollo and Marsyas']] *[[The Affair of the Claw and the Clouds]] *[[The Affair of the God in the Wood]] *[[The Affair of the Grunewald Provision]] *[[The Affair of the Open Reverend]] *[[The Affair of the Unfinished Lark]] ==Further Stories== *After completing [[The Affair of 'Apollo and Marsyas']] you have the option to give Peter a manuscript on [[Tridesma Hiera]] of level 10, or something on duendrazones to help the Soprano ascend via a Heart path. **Giving him [[The Instruments of the Heart]] satisfies the latter requirement, and results in [[Inkling]], a Bronze Spintria, and Peter gets [[Inspired]], and Fear: Carapace **Giving him the former is the same result as the latter. *Consulting with Peter on [[The Affair of the God in the Wood|The Affair of The God in the Wood]] will provide additional context as to what's going on, but he is not an option to close out the event. *After completing [[The Affair of the Claw and the Clouds]], you have the option to make an offering at the shrine of St Tentreto for him or refuse to do so. Speak to Agdistis with the remnant of the offering to accept, or speak with the original offering to refuse, **The former grants the shrine a {{Lore|Heart}} aspect, grants Agdistis [[Inspired]] and Fear: Carapace, and rewards you with [[Inkling]] and [[Insects & Nectars|Lesson: Insects & Nectars]]. *After completing [[The Affair of the Grunewald Provision]], you have the option to ask Peter what happened after he helped his friend dispose of something he bought from the Grunewald circus. Peter will give you a memory named Agdistis's Wisp which you can offer to the [[Chrysalis]]. Doing so allows the [[Chrysalis]] to accept {{Lore|Winter}} offerings and also provide 1 Winter. Offering the wisp to the [[Chrysalis]] will also drop a shell that you can give to Peter to give him the Agenda: Stone Remembered quality, he also gives you one lesson of [[Resurgences & Emergences]]. ==Salon Conversations== {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation !First Lesson !Second Conversation !Second Lesson |- | [[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Al-Adim and Agdistis are gossiping, quietly, about al-Adim's patroness. 'Not a hundred legs,' says al-Adim, 'but more than you'd think…' |[[Sky Stories]] |Agdistis and al-Adim have a lively chat about the uses of birdsong in the prediction of weather. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |- |[[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Arthur and Agdistis are talking, softly and seriously, about those absences which scar. 'I still miss him: Arthur says. Agdistis squeezes his hand and quotes in Greek: 'Roses by the head, jasmine at the feet …' |[[Disciplines of the Scar]] |Agdistis invites Arthur to visit him in Berlin, but Arthur shakes his head. 'I can do without the temptation. The old ties would be too much for me. The War, I mean. We both know what's coming.' |[[Auroral Contemplations]] |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] |Arun and Agdistis are discussing the technical details of flensing, without any particular regard for the effect it might have on anyone's appetite. |[[Stitching & Binding]] |Agdistis and Arun are discussing the Thunderskin's rites in Phrygia, India, and Cyprus… |[[Drums & Dances]] |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |Azita and Agdistis are discussing the roles played in the world's sustention by the Thunderskin ('who does not permit conclusion') and the Corrivality (the eternal contest of the Edge-powers). They agree it's a business that could only be entrusted to Hours familiar with suffering... |[[Edicts Martial]] |'You are Sogdian, are you not?' Agdistis asks Azita. 'I was born,' she agrees, 'in the Sogdian twilight, after the coming of ibn Asad, when our language was already passing from the world… but I still recall a few of our songs, if that is what you were going to ask me.' |[[Strings & Songs]] |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] |Chaima is describing for Agdistis one of the dances of the Rif Mountains, her home. Her shoulders twitch as if she might wish to show him, but her dignity keeps her in her seat. From his gentle smile, Agdistis has noticed. |[[Drums & Dances]] |Agdistis is plainly delighted to see Chaima again, and she favours him with a rare smile, bright as mica in moonlight. Again they fall to discussing the dances of the Rif mountains - since they last met, he has travelled there himself to learn of them… |[[Drums & Dances]] |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] |Connie and Agdistis, unexpectedly, are discussing ouranoscopy: she's intrigued by the ways in which the 'dance' of the Hours and of the heavenly bodies might serve as a source of horomachic information. Agdistis is nonplussed, but does his best to keep up. |[[Ouranoscopy]] |Once again, Connie and Agdistis are discussing ouranoscopy. She's had some of her people looking into some of Agdistis' ideas, and her face is serious. 'Much more than an eclipse,' she says somberly. 'Perhaps even a War in the Sun.' |[[Ouranoscopy]] |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Coquille and Agdistis are talking contemporary dance. |[[Drums & Dances]] |Agdistis and Coquille are chatting about opera. He prefers German; she, Italian. |[[Strings & Songs]] |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Agdistis and Corso chat about Solar doctrine. Both of them, it seems, were raised in the Sun: both of them admit to an absurd degree of guilt about their absence from church on the Sun's Day. |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |Agdistis and Corso are chatting amicably about growing up in the ways of the Sun. Apparently they were both choirboys. ('I know, I know,' says Corso. 'Then I started smoking.) |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |- |[[Daymare|'Daymare']] |Agdistis recites - with caution - some of the lake-songs of the witches of the Fucine marshes. 'I am more comfortable with the Phrygian tongue,' he says, 'but it is wise to pay the Sister her due.' |[[Fucine]] |Dagmar rambles merrily at a sceptical Agdistis about the possibilities - nyctodromic and musical - of the new Hammond organs. 'Having one shipped over, put up in my organ loft,' she says happily. 'Course we'll need electricity in the organ loft first. And the castle. And put the roof back on the castle. Any chance you're rich, Aggers? Help a gel out?' |[[Lockworks & Clockworks]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] |Douglas and Agdistis speak of the Ecdysis Club, where Agdistis once worked and which Douglas had a hand in closing down. Douglas is unrepentant, but also regretful. |[[Drums & Dances]] |Douglas has been to a performance of Keirle's Ceaseless - for assessment of oneiric hazard, not for pleasure, but he took Mrs Moore ('free tickets is free tickets;) and both enjoyed it - Douglas much more than they expected. Agdistis is more than happy to discuss Keirle's work. |[[Weaving & Knotworking]] |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Ehsan and Agdistis discuss duendrazones, the Heart-long who are eternally active, and possess mortals so they can sometimes know peace. 'I had hoped to be something like that, once,' Agdistis said, 'but I learn from my friend Sulochana what it means to he a Long, and I set my face against it.' |[[Purifications & Exaltations]] |Ehsan and Agdistis are discussing needlework techniques for stitching sigils of healing into closing wounds - or of guidance into costumes. |[[Stitching & Binding]] |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Fraser hopes to fund a ballet, to help accelerate the development of the Cross-nature in his 'kin under the Cross'; he hopes to employ Agdistis as a choreographer. Agdistis is clearly wary, but clearly tempted. |[[Purifications & Exaltations]] |Agdistis and Fraser have returned to their discussion of the prospective ballet for which Fraser wishes to act as impresario. Agdistis has finally agreed to act as choreographer, but only on condition that he can veto Fraser's initial choice of name, which he strongly dislikes: 'The Buzzing in the Skull.' |[[Purifications & Exaltations]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Agdistis and Hokobald have a scrupulously polite conversation about acoustics, resonance, and bellringing in the churches of London. |[[Bells & Brazieries]] |Hokobald and Agdistis discuss the possibility of a ballet of bells. Agdistis becomes sufficiently engaged to smile at Hokobald, despite his clear suspicion of that corrupt immortal… |[[Bells & Brazieries]] |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] |Agdistis and Morgen share news of his friend, and her un-sister, the Ligeian Sulochana (who, it seems, was at one point Morgen's dance-instructor). She is in Georgia now: Agdistis wonders why. 'Medea,' Morgen says, but she teasingly refuses to be drawn on what that might mean. |[[Serpents & Venoms]] |Morgen and Agdistis discuss the folk-songs of Umbria and their connection to the Twins. It transpires that they both met Christopher Illopoly during his year in Italy as a young man. Morgen wonders where he might be, and Agdistis blurts out impulsively: 'Stay away from him!' He immediately blanches at his own boldness, but Morgen seems entertained. |[[Strings & Songs]] |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Agdistis and Olympe speak of the kind of wounds that words as weapons may cause - the big ones and the little ones. They speak also of the creation of stars - the big ones, and the little ones ... |[[Pyroglyphics]] |Olympe has become interested in an 'demi-dyad' - a supposed partway Edge-long who attempted to ascend under the Horned-Axe, a habitué of the now-defunct Ecdysis Club where Agdistis once worked. Agdistis suggests she cease her investigations: that it is not wise to pursue any implication that the Horned-Axe may still possess any trace of Edge... |[[Edicts Liminal]] |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] |Agdistis and Serena discuss a masked play - a sort of degenerate Sufic hybrid - that he saw in Alexandria some years ago. 'They would only perform it,' he says, 'in the hours before dawn.' Serena nods: 'I think that was wise.' |[[Watchman's Paradoxes]] |Serena and Agdistis discuss the rites of the Damascene branch of the House of Lethe. She wonders - she is tactful, but the implication is clear - whether Agdistis participated in any similar rites to preserve his wonderful voice. He says that he did not, and he is smiling, but it is a smiling mask. |[[Sacra Limiae]] |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller|Fr Stanislav John Schaller]] |Stanislav and Agdistis discuss pruning techniques used when a plant is wounded by winter; how to ensure no ragged bark remains; of how not to be distracted by timidity or tenderness. |[[Leaves & Thorns]] |Agdistis and Stanislav talk about gardening under glass in winter. Their tone is fatherly. |[[Leaves & Thorns]] |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Yvette listens as Agdistis grapples with his dislike of Solomon Husher's work: he cannot, will not, accept that everything must end - he is unwilling even to accept that anything must end. |[[Sights & Sensations]] |Agdistis listens as Yvette expounds her theories on the paintings of Nina Lagasse: how, Yvette believes, her choice of colours over the years shows that she knew when her time was coming to an end. |[[Sights & Sensations]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Zachary describes his understanding of the 'Angel of Storms', the beauty of her underclouds, the accesses of her lightning, how he yearns to cage her in glass. Agdistis listens patiently; now and then his eyes flicker as if he understands. |[[Quenchings & Quellings]] |Zachary speaks with staccato enthusiasm of the poetic sabotage efforts of someone he calls 'Hammerbreaker'. His voice remains flat but his hands twitch wildly: his fingers beat a complex rhythm on the tabletop. Agdistis listens sympathetically. |[[Putrefactions & Calcinations]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Mrs Kille and Agdistis greet each other warmly. It seems they knew each other in Paris, in the days before they married. She asks about his dance school… |[[Drums & Dances]] |Mrs Kille and Agdistis revisit the memories of their time of acquaintance in Paris. He asks if she is still in touch with 'Aunt Adeline', and she emphatically shakes her head. 'When I married Mr Kille,' she says firmly, 'I told him I'd put all that behind me. He's a good man.' |[[Rhyme & Remembrance]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |Agdistis enumerates a number of 'smithing songs', tapping on the table as he does so. Denzil nods politely, but is clearly paying no attention. |[[Drums & Dances]] |Agdistis wants to hear about Cornish traditional songs. Denzil hums one, and Agdistis listens with care, repeating it back to him. Denzil is a little out of key, but Agdistis hums it back into shape. | [[Strings & Songs]] |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Timothy and Agdistis are discussing historical accounts of the mountain rites of the Phrygians. Both of them noticeably lower their voices whenever they mention the word 'Grail'. |[[Tridesma Hiera]] |Agdistis expresses an interest in Ericapaean. Reverend Timothy, who has not been initiated into the higher mysteries of the Church, professes himself 'very far from fluent' in it, but is happy to share a few pointers. |[[Ericapaean]] |} ==Trivia== *Agdistis also appeared in ''[https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Cultist_Simulator_Wiki Cultist Simulator]'' as an employee at the esoteric Ecdysis Club. *His homonym is a phrygian deityhttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agdistis who is linked to Cybele and Attis, two phrygian deities mentioned in stories related to the Thunderskin. The phrygian deity is a castrated hermaphrodite: two salon discussions allude to the fact, as in one with Dagmar Agdistis mentions he is 'more comfortable with the Phrygian tongue', and in another denies to Serena that his 'wonderful voice' comes from similar 'rites of the Damascene branch of the House of Lethe' (castration). Furthermore, in Medieval stories, a 'wound in the thigh' was a common euphemism for genital injury. [[Category:Visitor]] [[Category:People]]

Mr Ehsan Fekri.title: Mr Ehsan Fekri
Mr Ehsan Fekri.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Mr_Ehsan_Fekri.png |principle1={{Lore|Heart}} |principle2={{Lore|Sky}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Aramaic]], [[Deep Mandaic]], [[Greek]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |address=Water Lane, Steeple Aston}} {{quote|Formerly; Ehsan was a healer; he was not human; he was Secretary Salvant of Hush House. But not all at the same time. Fussy, kind, famously foul to look upon.}} __NOTOC__
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Heart}} and {{Lore|Sky}}. He is a potential Secretary Salvant for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. Ehsan can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Deep Mandaic]]. He was formerly a skaptodon, and has authored ''[[Fekri's Herbary]]'' and ''[[The Sea Does Not Regret]]''. The latter details his experiences in Brancrug during his time as Secretary Salvant for the Curia of the Isle. ==Invitations and Salons== Ehsan requires 3 {{Lore|Heart}} to be invited to Hush House. He prefers {{Lore|Moon}} food, but {{Lore|Sky}} drink. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation !1st Lesson ! Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] |Dagmar’s warning Ehsan darkly about ‘goings-on’ in Vienna: ‘That bloody little man. The roofs are stiff with ''striges'', you know. They like war even more than gossip.’ |[[Sky Stories]] | | |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Ehsan and al-Adim are talking about goats. They both seem remarkably well-informed and exceptionally enthusiastic about goats. Neither of them will quite admit to ever having been a goatherd. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |Ehsan and al-Adim discuss the care and feeding of birds of prey. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] | | | | |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] |Arun and Ehsan - the ex-skaptodon, the perhaps-ex-Knock-long - talk about how it is to have been something that one no longer is. Ehsan complains that he needs to employ both hammers and nutcrackers, also that his joints have begun to ache when the weather turns. Arun rubs at the bandages on his wrists, and says ruefully: 'But we endure; we endure.' |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |Ehsan gives Arun practical advice on the preservation and protection of those parts of Arun that are no longer protected and preserved by skin. |[[Stitching & Binding]] |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] |Ehsan and Serena reminisce about their time at Hush House in the days of its power, when the winds were leashed to keep the seas safe, when the Fine-Takers still responded to the words of the Covenant… |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |Serena and Ehsan speak of the ‘shrouded rites’ of the Church Solar – the ones forbidden to the public, who still largely think of the Hours as fables or god-masks. |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Yvette and Ehsan speak wistfully of what they have read of the lost Hour called Tide. Yvette recalls that when the Sister withdraws, other Hours sometimes fill the space left by her withdrawal, and wonders whether the Tide is gentle enough to remain afterwards… but Ehsan politely insists that the gods-who-were-stone are never gentle. |[[Pearl & Tide]] |Ehsan and Yvette speak of Tentreto, the perhaps-human saint of the early church. Ehsan describes his pilgrimage to Tentreto’s shrine in Venice, but admits he was motivated only partly by religious curiosity – more by an enthusiasm for Venetian cuisine and a desire to catch up with an old (he coughs in embarrassment) friend… |[[Pearl & Tide]] |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Stanislav and Ehsan debate which rivers and weathers may still qualify - metaphorically or prophetically - at which times and seasons - as the 'blood of the Seven-Coils'. |[[Coil & Chasm]] | | |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] | | | | |- |[[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Arthur and Ehsan discuss Anaël Verdier's account of the ascent of the 'Unwise Mortal' to the heights of the Mansus - perhaps even to the Glory - and how he, perhaps, succeeded when so many others failed. 'I learnt in my time here' - Ehsan gestures to indicate the House - 'that it can be as important who witnesses a deed, as who performs it.' Arthur nods, slowly. |[[Watchman's Paradoxes]] |Arthur speaks of the lightsmithing arts practised at the Labyrinth of Lions; Ehsan offers to show Arthur the stained glass windows in the chapel of Hush House after the meal ('with your permission, Librarian'?). |[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Hokobald admits in a subterranean growl that even though – or perhaps – because of his Forge-long status, the sea airs of Brancrug cause his joints to stiffen. ‘To rust, perhaps?’ Ehsan enquires blandly. In response to Hokobald’s glare, he apologises, and prescribes a tisane. |[[Herbs & Infusions]] |Hokobald and Ehsan discuss the origin of the Amiranis Beteli, the inscribed stone of secrets which fell from the sky, perhaps before the departure of the Cross. Ehsan believes the inscriptions were the work of Ys, after the meteorite struck the sea; Hokobald insists they were a ‘Gleam-gift’ from a Star (and also insists that Ehsan is a ‘pug-faced lion-fewmet’ when Ehsan dissents). |[[Bells & Brazieries]] |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] |Ehsan wants to know if Connie ever gets tired of enforcing laws. ‘I might ask you,’ she responds. ‘if you ever get tired of healing bodies.’ |[[Edicts Inviolable]] | | |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] |Morgen and Ehsan discuss the motives of the aviform Hours. Ehsan is firm in his belief that they are fundamentally benevolent to mortals; Morgen says smilingly: ‘Perhaps then you know the Twins better than do I.’ |[[Strings & Songs]] | | |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Ehsan longingly, regretfully describes the jewels he knew in the earth, in his skaptodon years, as he perceived them through slower, stronger senses. (Olympe: ‘How long were you in the earth?’ Ehsan: ‘That’s the Lionsmith’s secret.’) |[[Anbary & Lapidary]] |Ehsan and Olympe discuss the lunatic theories of the heresiarch Cygnifer. Olympe mentions the connection Cygnifer draws between amber and the city Ys – the city beyond the wave – and admits that this connection has always made intuitive sense to her, though she can’t explain why… |[[Anbary & Lapidary]] |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Fraser and Ehsan are discussing tarascisation and 'la malaise raveline' - the horrible changes that occur in certain families that have conducted 'traffic with beasts'. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |Fraser is experiencing pain in the altered joints of the hand that he prefers to keep gloved; Ehsan has some advice. |[[Herbs & Infusions]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Zachary speaks to Ehsan of the stairway to Nowhere which haunts his paintings, of the lamps of black nephrite, the star-twinkle of the flowers in Miss Naenia's hair. There is more than one temptation to Nowhere, he says... |[[Sights & Sensations]] |Ehsan and Zachary discuss Illopoly’s line – after Husher: ‘the White is West of the World, and Winter does not wait forever.’ Zachary says suddenly that he would like to paint the White; Ehsan gently encourages him; they discuss the palest pigments. |[[Sights & Sensations]] |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |Ehsan and Azita are discussing Ehsan's time as a skaptodon, a warrior-creation of the Lionsmith. There was more than one reason that Ehsan allowed himself to be debased into human shape. His enthusiasm for seafood was one; but he was never comfortable as a warrior. (Azita shakes her head and smiles.) |[[Furs & Feathers]] |Azita, the Colonel-devotee, listens to Ehsan, who once served the Lionsmith, explain his conception of the Corrivality. 'The Histories are I think not braided, but woven. The Corrivality, back and forth between our masters' - he gestures - 'like a shuttle on a loom...' |[[Stitching & Binding]] |- | [[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Ehsan and Coquille speak of Tryphon, the Grail-long. Ehsan says: 'She was adored; and so she was happy.' An expression passes like cloud-shadow over Coquille's face, and for a moment she looks older. 'No,' she says, 'she was adored, and so she was not happy.' |[[Applebright Euphonies]] |Coquille is teasing Ehsan about the medical possibilities offered by the influence of the Applebright. He doesn't find it funny. |[[Applebright Euphonies]] |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Corso insists to Ehsan that Teresa Galmier visited his bookshop in Oxford, in person. ‘She used a different name. So I didn’t want to embarrass her. She’s changed. But it’s her. But she’s changed. Taller. Well, something like taller, not taller exactly. Stop laughing, Ehsan – ’ |[[Purifications & Exaltations]] | | |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Ehsan and Agdistis discuss duendrazones, the Heart-long who are eternally active, and possess mortals so they can sometimes know peace. 'I had hoped to be something like that, once,' Agdistis said, 'but I learn from my friend Sulochana what it means to be a Long, and I set my face against it.' |[[Purifications & Exaltations]] |Ehsan and Agdistis are discussing needlework techniques for stitching sigils of healing into closing wounds - or of guidance into costumes. |[[Stitching & Binding]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Ehsan and Mr Kille discuss freshwater fishing. (Mr Kille admits that he has never gone out on a fishing boat: too many stories about the seas near Brancrug Isle.) |[[Sea Stories]] |Mrs Kille and Ehsan discuss the binding and suturing of wounds. |[[Stitching & Binding]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] | | | | |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Timothy has come to understand that Ehsan was once something else, although he is not clear exactly what that was, and Ehsan is not particularly eager to enlighten him. He asks what it is like, the change in life. Ehsan leans back, and declares – or perhaps quotes – a little melodramatically: ‘The sea does not regret the tide, and after the tide withdraws, something always remains, which we call memory.’ That is the last thing he has to say on the matter, and against his silence, Timothy’s questions fall like rain. |[[Memory: Salt]] | | |} ==Incidents== Ehsan can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of 'Apollo and Marsyas']] *[[The Affair of the Claw and the Clouds]] *[[The Affair of the God in the Wood]] *[[The Affair of the Grunewald Provision]] *[[The Affair of the Open Reverend]] *[[The Affair of the Unfinished Lark]] ==Further Stories== * After completing [[The Affair of the Claw and the Clouds]]: **If the Librarian provided Ehsan an appropriate text, then interacting further will give him [[Inspired]], [[Fear: Carapace]], and [[Agenda: Secrecy]], and reward the Librarian with an [[Inkling]] and one ''[[Quenchings & Quellings|Lesson: Quenchings & Quellings]]''. **Otherwise, he will give the Librarian [[An Offering to St Tentreto]], which can either be returned unused, or poured out at the [[Altar: St Tentreto]]. ***Returning the Offering gives Ehsan Inspired, [[Sympathy: Carapace]] and [[Agenda: Stone Remembered]], giving the Librarian an Inkling and one ''[[Insects & Nectars|Lesson: Insects & Nectars]]''. ***Making the Offering gives him Inspired, Fear: Carapace, and Agenda: Secrecy, giving the Librarian an Inkling and one ''Lesson: Quenchings & Quellings''. Further, Altar: St Tentreto will accept {{Lore|Heart}}, and provide {{Lore|Heart|2}} innately. * After completing [[The Affair of the Grunewald Provision]], the Librarian can speak with Ehsan to get [[Ehsan's Wisp]], which has the following text:
A 'poor wisp' preserved by Ehsan from the Grunewald disaster. Cooing, mewing, warm to the touch.  Notionally harmless. [Ehsan has asked you to place this in the Chrysalis that you can find in the Cucurbit, but you could destroy it in the furnace if you were suspicious.]
** Once placed in the [[Chrysalis]], the latter will accept {{Lore|Winter}} and provide {{Lore|Winter}} 1 innately. The Librarian will also receive a unique Memory, [[Ehsan's Wisp: Shed Skin]]. ** Discussing the Wisp with Ehsan provides an Inkling and a Lesson: [[Resurgences & Emergences]]. Ehsan gains Inspired, [[Sympathy: Carapace]], and [[Agenda: Stone Remembered]]. *Consulting Ehsan about [[The Affair of the God in the Wood]] provides additional context as to what's going on, but he is not a visitor that can complete this particular story. *Consulting Ehsan about [[The Affair of the Open Reverend]] causes him to request a text on [[Ragged Crossroads]] or [[Solutions & Separations]] (mystery 8+). He determines the Reverend is beyond his help, and directs the Librarian to [[MCO Constance Lee]] or [[DI Douglas Moore]]. ==Hidden Interactions== {{Spoilers|caption=This section contains information on hidden interactions.|content=
While visiting, the Librarian can present Fekri with the books he has written to receive rewards. This only works once, and he will not disappear after this interaction.
Presenting Fekri with ''[[Fekri's Herbary]]'' awards the Librarian with a [[Herbs & Infusions|Lesson: Herbs and Infusions]] and the following dialogue: {{Quote|'Not a bad effort, that one -'

'I've learnt a little more lore since then, but I hope you still find it useful. May I take a look?' [Ehsan will examine the book and return it to you. He won't leave until his other business is concluded.]'

'If there's one thing I wish I'd known back then, it's this...'}}
Showing him ''[[The Sea Does Not Regret]]'' awards a [[Spices & Savours|Lesson: Spices and Savours]] and the following dialogue: {{Quote|'Oh my -'

'Old memories, Librarian! Some of them - well, some of those memories are better than others. Can I take a look?' [Ehsan will examine the book and return it to you. He won't leave until his other business is concluded.]

'Does the Sweet Bones still do that starygazy pie...? Perhaps I'll drop in on my way home. Come to think of it, that reminds me of a recipe. You have to hear this -'}}}} == Trivia == *The word '''Ehsan''' means '''to do good''' in Arabic, Persian, and other regional languages. The name '''Fekri''' in Arabic, Persian, etc. means '''thoughtful''' or '''meditative''', but could also mean something like '''spiritual''' or '''intellectual'''. [[Category:Authors]] [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]] [[Category:Hidden Interactions]]

Ms Azita Bukhara.title: Ms Azita Bukhara
Ms Azita Bukhara.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Ms Azita Bukhara.png |principle1={{Lore|Sky}} |principle2={{Lore|Edge}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Aramaic]], [[Deep Mandaic]], [[Latin]], [[Phrygian]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |address=Bukhara Exports, Samarkand}} {{quote|Businesswoman, chess-master, initiate of the scarred Hour sometimes called the Colonel.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Visitors|Visitor]] interested in {{Lore|Sky}} and {{Lore|Edge}}. She is a potential Secretary Vigilant for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. She can be paid one [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Deep Mandaic]]. She is also an Edge-long in the service of the Colonel forming an Edge-dyad with her enemy-twin Mehrad, servant of the Lionsmith. Whether they are actually siblings by blood is unclear. == Invitations and Salons == Azita requires 7 {{Lore|Edge}} to be invited to Hush House. She prefers {{Lore|Edge}} food and drink. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation !1st Lesson !Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] |Dagmar and Azita are discussing means to contain the wild wood-things called Hügelkinder, who apparently have been causing trouble for a business of Azita’s that apparently needs quantities of guns moved through wild European regions by dead of night. |[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]] | | |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Azita and al-Adim discuss the varieties of messenger-birds and courier-spirits that they have employed across the centuries of their acquaintance. |[[Sky Stories]] |Al-Adim and Azita are reminiscing about the time of their first acquaintance in the city of Damascus, in the days before the coming of Timur. 'Good fighting!' she sighs. 'I preferred the hawking,' he says; and they spend some time discussing desert falconry. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] | | | | |- | [[Dr Arun Peel]] |Arun and Azita speak of the Tragulari, the 'Dartsmen' who once used exotic poisons to hunt immortals. Arun expresses distaste for the Colonel's part in the Tragulari's creation, but Azita is unabashed: 'Good exercise. Honestly, I miss them.' Arun flatly refuses to believe her. |[[Sharps]] | | |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] | | | | |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] |In one History, Alexander heard a secret from Darius that convinced him to abandon battle and return home, announcing, ‘the Sun has his course, and so do I.’ Yvette asks Azita what she knows about the secret, apparently under the impression that Azita and Alexander were contemporaries, which causes Azita some amusement (I’m not even a thousand years old’). In any case Azita is of the opinion that the secret is ‘a Lionsmith nonsense’ and Alexander was ‘much overestimated.’ |[[Sickle & Eclipse]] |Yvette asks Azita about the Edge-dyad Torgue and Dearday, with whom she has been known to go drinking every century or two. Yvette mentions (casually?) that she’s always had a bit of a pash on Dearday. Azita’s eyes glitter: ‘Have you now.’
[There’s something between Azita and Yvette, although exactly what remains to be seen.] |[[Edicts Martial]] |- | [[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Azita and Stanislav discuss the Names of the Thunderskin - the seven Instruments whose musics support his rhythm. Azita repeats the tradition that a duendrazon which has known seven caesurae becomes eligible to replace an Instrument. Stanislav shakes his head. 'Duendrazones. An odd choice, I've always thought, to become eternally conscious, and then to pursue the caesura so...' |[[Strings & Songs]] | | |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] | | | | |- |[[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Arthur has been describing the mirror-mazes of the Labyrinth of Lions to a smiling Azita - but now he seems to grow suspicious of her motives in questioning him, and he withdraws. |[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]] |Azita is describing her experiences in the Mansus to Arthur - who, it seems, has never passed the Stag Door, though he speaks fondly of its watchman. |[[Watchman's Paradoxes]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Hokobald challenges Azita to an arm-wrestling match. She accepts with enthusiasm. For the sake of decorum, they leave the room to conduct the match. When they return, It becomes apparent that Hokobald has won; but that his wrist is broken. ‘That shouldn’t happen! It should not be permitted!’ he keeps whining, through gritted teeth. Azita only shrugs.
[Hokobald and Azita arm-wrestled. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Disciplines of the Hammer]] |Last time, Azita and Hokobald arm-wrestled, and though he won, Hokobald’s wrist was broken. This time, he demands another match. Azita refuses; after some minutes of wheedling she tells him, with a flash of temper, that last time she let him win, and he won’t be so lucky another time. Hokobald, enraged, refuses to believe her; they spend the next half hour arguing the merits of the unstoppable force and the immovable object. |[[Disciplines of the Hammer]] |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] | | | | |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] |Morgen teases Azita with references to 'Medusa's Lament', which purports to describe the death of the god-from-stone Seven-Coils at the hands of the Colonel, Azita's patron. |[[Horns & Ivories]] |Azita and Morgen compare their hunts of ‘upright prey.’ Morgen observes disapprovingly that unlike Azita, she never hunts for pleasure. Azita raises her eyebrows and leaves them there until Morgen dissolves into silvery giggles. |[[Horns & Ivories]] |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Olympe is writing a novel where one of the characters is a jewel-smuggler, and she’s hoping Azita can help with her research. Azita is understandably suspicious, despite Olympe’s repeated assurances that none of this is on the record, but she unbends enough to ‘talk rubies’ once Olympe explains that the protagonist is based on Dagmar. |[[Anbary & Lapidary]] |Olympe tries to interrogate Azita on her alleged provision of weapons to various rebel and partisan groups east of the Black Sea. Azita insists that her dyad-twin Mehrad is the one responsible. |[[Edicts Martial]] |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Ehsan and Azita are discussing Ehsan's time as a skaptodon, a warrior-creation of the Lionsmith. There was more than one reason that Ehsan allowed himself to be debased into human shape. His enthusiasm for seafood was one; but he was never comfortable as a warrior. (Azita shakes her head and smiles.) |[[Furs & Feathers]] |Azita, the Colonel-devotee, listens to Ehsan, who once served the Lionsmith, explain his conception of the Corrivality. 'The Histories are I think not braided, but woven. The Corrivality, back and forth between our masters' - he gestures - 'like a shuttle on a loom...' |[[Stitching & Binding]] |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Fraser and Azita are agreeing a complex deal involving a sheep farming operation of Azita's in the Middle East. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |Fraser and Azita are negotiating something shady-sounding about mammoth ivory and dreams of ice… |[[Horns & Ivories]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Azita and Zachary discuss how to maintain a delicate balance, in the occult or the personal; and also how to dispose of corpses. |[[Sickle & Eclipse]] | | |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |'Breath is the temptation of the soul.' Azita and Coquille are discussing the ways in which beauty can be absorbed through the lungs; and Azita is angling for a connection to Coquille's friend Giorgiou, the cigarette smuggler…
[Azita wanted an introduction to Coquille’s friend Giorgiou. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Applebright Euphonies]] |Once again, Coquille and Azita are discussing the ‘temptations of the soul’ enabled by the inhalation of aromatic essences. Coquille is piqued that her friend and supplier Giorgiou has disappeared; she wonders if Azita found him to be a troublesome competitor. Azita blandly disclaims any responsibility. |[[Applebright Euphonies]] |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Corso and Azita are both intrigued by recent government interest in the alchemies of the Sunset Road (and in what that might mean for those who could, say, lay their hands on lost Sunset Road works, even works of uncertain provenance.) |[[Purifications & Exaltations]] |Corso and Azita are discussing recently discovered letters supposedly sent by the Abbess Melancthe to Gunnhild, daughter of Harold. Their musings on its contents are punctuated with bald estimates of their possible value. |[[Purifications & Exaltations]] |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Azita and Agdistis are discussing the roles played in the world's sustention by the Thunderskin ('who does not permit conclusion') and the Corrivality (the eternal contest of the Edge-powers). They agree it's a business that could only be entrusted to Hours familiar with suffering... |[[Edicts Martial]] |'You are Sogdian, are you not?' Agdistis asks Azita. 'I was born,' she agrees, 'in the Sogdian twilight, after the coming of ibn Asad, when our language was already passing from the world… but I still recall a few of our songs, if that is what you were going to ask me.' |[[Strings & Songs]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Azita and Mr Kille discuss the qualities of the timber of the great cedars of Lebanon. Azita offers to provide a quantity of cypress-wood at a very cheap price; Mr Kille, smiling as usual, refuses. Azita offers a free sample, and Mr Kille’s smile vanishes. He apologizes, he says, but in Brancrug they have been taught not to accept gifts from visitors to Hush House. |[[Leaves & Thorns]] |Azita and Mrs Kille exchange weather-lore. (‘Plenty of babies shy of birth, can’t wait to stick their heads out in a storm’ opines Mrs Kille gloomily.) |[[Sky Stories]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] | | | | |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Azita and Reverend Timothy are discussing the churches of the East - variations on the Solar faith with other hours acknowledged, and hold-outs of the Crucian heresy. (Azita objects mildly to Timothy describing it as the 'Crucian heresy'.) |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] | | |} ==Incidents == {{PAGENAME}} can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of 'Apollo and Marsyas']] *[[The Affair of the Absent Friend]] *[[The Affair of the Claw and the Clouds]] *[[The Affair of the Forgivable Debt]] *[[The Affair of the Second Skin]] *[[The Affair of the Threshold Revolution]] *[[The Affair of the Unfinished Lark]] == Further Stories == * After completing [[The Affair of the Forgivable Debt]], Azita can be spoken with. ** She can either be given a [[readable]] with [[Disciplines of the Scar]] 10+ or on the topic of 'the Madrugad's presence in the bones of the living and the dead'. *** Offering the former will gain Azita [[Inspired]], Sympathy: Reckoners, and Agenda: Autarchy. *After completing [[The Affair of the Unfinished Lark]], Azita can be spoken with. **She can either be given a [[readable]] with [[Sky Stories]] 10+ or ''[[On the Winding Stair]]'' to reveal the Roost-secrets, or ''[[The Book of the White Cat]]'' to return the Roost-secrets. ***Offering the former will gain Azita [[Inspired]] and Agenda: Corrivality; offering the latter will gain Azita [[Inspired]] and Agenda: Peace [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]]

Princess Coquille Amirejibi.title: Princess Coquille Amirejibi
Princess Coquille Amirejibi.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Princess Coquille Amirejibi.png |principle1={{Lore|Grail}} |principle2={{Lore|Knock}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Greek]], [[Sanskrit]], [[Vak]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |relationships=[[Dr Arun Peel]] (distant relative)|address=Sachino Palace, Tiflis}} {{Quote|Artist, socialite... burglar? An unspeakably charming woman with a particular knack for getting adopted.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Grail}} and {{Lore|Knock}}. She is a potential Treasurer for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. She can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Vak]]. ==Invitations and Salons== Coquille requires 5 {{Lore|Grail}} to be invited to Hush House. She prefers {{Lore|Grail}} food and drink. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation ! 1st Lesson !Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] |Dagmar and Coquille’s conversation about the Great Signs and the Great Scars is repeatedly disrupted by Dagmar’s attempts to introduce Coquille to a ‘very nice Margrave.’
[Dagmar wanted to introduce Coquille to a friend. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars]] |Dagmar and Coquille are talking again about the Great Signs and the Great Scars; again their conversation is punctuated by discussion of the ‘very nice Margrave’ to whom Dagmar did, in fact, introduce Coquille – a fact Dagmar seems now to be regretting. |[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars]] |- | [[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Al-Adim politely interrogates Coquille about her family and nature. Yes, she is associated with the Tomb of Lies; no, she is no longer welcome there; yes, she is, she supposes, technically a pentiment… |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |Al-Adim and Coquille are fencing again. She asks him outright about the nature of his Longhood; he tells her he 'found his patron in the desert.' He asks her if she is 'Clogg-relevant'; she pretends outrage that he is asking about her age, and will say only that she is less than a century old. |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] |Coquille smilingly asks Douglas to remind her if there is an arrest warrant out for her just now. 'Not just now,' he replies, 'but I'm sure we can sort something out.' Coquille spends much of the rest of the meal quoting from Zahra's 'Time of Division', and asking which bits would get her arrested if she recited them at a cocktail party.
[Coquille asked incautious questions of Douglas. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Surgeries & Exsanguinations]] | | |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] |Coquille and Arun have discovered that they share family in the subcontinent from which they have both been exiled. They gossip eagerly about their cousins’ expression of familial traits; their alterations and development; their new-hatched kin. |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |‘We all loved Vak, back home,’ Arun sighs. Coquille nods, her eyes glowing. ‘You remember the poems we wrote for her? In other languages, of course. Except me; I got in a great deal of trouble for that. Again.’ He recites a few verses, and Coquille claps her hands in delight. |[[Vak]] |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] |Coquille and Serena discuss the fabled ‘Paths of the Sun’ through the Mansus which were reserved for the undivided Sun speculating whether the Sun’s fission-selves – like the Wolf and the Madrugad – now walk them. Coquille speculates that if the Meniscate walks them, that may account for some of the stories about the shadow-Mansus sometimes called the House of the Moon… |[[Door & Wall]] | | |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Coquille asks Yvette what she knows of the line of Kelemdu, the 'Black Dove'. Yvette describes a Henavek folk-tale in which the Black Dove is assigned the wardenship of the Moon-marches by Henavek himself - a folk-tale associated with Brancrug. |[[Sea Stories]] |Coquille presses Yvette on her resemblance to Rowena Hengerst; she asks whether they have ever met. 'No,' says Yvette; 'she will never agree to an interview with me.' Coquille theorizes eagerly about why; Yvette nods and smiles. |[[Sea Stories]] |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Stanislav and Coquille swap stories of Aunt Mopsy. He met her when she made a pilgrimage to the Grove of Green Immortals, in the days he dwelt in its penumbra; she introduced him to her adoptive brother in Tiflis when his tastes had become jaded and he sought more dangerous diversions... |[[Leaves & Thorns]] | | |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] | | | | |- | [[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Coquille and Arthur are discussing the perils of family; the Crime of the Sky; the tragedy of Matthias and the Amethyst Imago. Coquille is at her most charming, and Arthur is at his most watchful. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |Once again, Arthur and Coquille are discussing the perils of family, birth, and marriage. Coquille has begun to hint that she would enjoy an introduction to one of Arthur's younger and more eligible relatives. A coil of dark hair dangles artlessly across one flawless cheek. Her teeth and eyes are very bright. Arthur, unmoved as a fortress under fire, repeatedly steers the conversation back to the businesses of blood. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Coquille is flirting outrageously with Hokobald. His head is tilted to one side and he is staring at her with a furnace gaze that might equally indicate lust or hunger. His mouth is stringed with saliva. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |Hokobald and Coquille continue their unnerving flirtation. She strokes his bald head and murmurs estimates of the measurements of the bones of her pelvis and rib-cage. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] |Connie and Coquille are discussing recent shipwrecks, and a possible connection to Ys... |[[Sea Stories]] |Coquille and Connie are discussing the rumors about the liaison between Franklin Bancroft and Eva Dewulf, more than two hundred years ago; about Bancroft’s departure and the child they might have had. ‘It is good to be adopted into a loving family,’ Coquille says smilingly, but she will not be drawn on what that means. |[[Sea Stories]] |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] |Coquille and Morgen are locked in an icy war of compliments. |[[Sights & Sensations]] | | |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Olympe is writing a novel where one of the characters is an architect specialising in secret passages and concealed entrances. She’s hoping Coquille can help with her research. Coquille is understandably suspicious, although Olympe promises up and down that any difficult details will be in strict confidence. Eventually Olympe explains that the protagonist is based on Fraser, and Coquille relaxes enough to share her secrets. |[[Door & Wall]] |Coquille and Olympe are comparing restaurants in Tiflis. Coquille insists that the place has gone downhill since the establishment of the Socialist Republic; Olympe counters that you just need to know where to look. |[[Spices & Savours]] |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Ehsan and Coquille speak of Tryphon, the Grail-long. Ehsan says: 'She was adored; and so she was happy.' An expression passes like cloud-shadow over Coquille's face, and for a moment she looks older. 'No,' she says, 'she was adored, and so she was not happy.' |[[Applebright Euphonies]] |Coquille is teasing Ehsan about the medical possibilities offered by the influence of the Applebright. He doesn't find it funny. |[[Applebright Euphonies]] |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Fraser asks Coquille to advise him on some Eastern pieces he has recently purchased, which he hopes may be pentiments of the Sixth History… |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |Coquille and Fraser discuss the Great Hooded Princes' (and Princesses') transition between Histories. He asks whether there were Carapace Cross still active in the Fifth History, but she will not answer him. |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Zachary and Coquille discuss the ways in which the Hours ‘restrain and constrict’ their rivalries, to prevent war in the Mansus. Zachary feels the ‘restraints and constrictions’ are growing weak. Coquille seems titillated by the prospect, but Zachary moves his head from side to side in negation. ‘The Worms,’ he whispers. |[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars]] | | |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |'Breath is the temptation of the soul.' Azita and Coquille are discussing the ways in which beauty can be absorbed through the lungs; and Azita is angling for a connection to Coquille's friend Giorgiou, the cigarette smuggler…
[Azita wanted an introduction to Coquille’s friend Giorgiou. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Applebright Euphonies]] |Once again, Coquille and Azita are discussing the ‘temptations of the soul’ enabled by the inhalation of aromatic essences. Coquille is piqued that her friend and supplier Giorgiou has disappeared; she wonders if Azita found him to be a troublesome competitor. Azita blandly disclaims any responsibility. |[[Applebright Euphonies]] |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] | | | | |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Coquille and Agdistis are talking contemporary dance. |[[Drums & Dances]] |Agdistis and Coquille are chatting about opera. He prefers German; she, Italian. |[[Strings & Songs]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Coquille, it transpires, grows orchids. Mr Kille, a keen gardener, is very interested. Mrs Kille keeps a proprietary eye on them both to ensure that his interest is not unnecessarily inflamed. |[[Orchids & Narcotics]] |Coquille and Mrs Kille discuss means to ease childbirth, and to prevent it. |[[Orchids & Narcotics]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |Coquille is asking Denzil to describe the storms of the coast to her. She leans close and smiles at him from beneath her lashes. Denzil does not engage, except to complain about a recent storm that closed that Sweet Bones. Eventually he does speak of an incident of ‘St Piran’s candles’ – a light that sometimes plays around the rectory weathercock in storms – but his detached, practical description plainly fails to satisfy Coquille. |[[Anbary & Lapidary]] |Coquille tugs at Denzil’s hair and asks him playfully when he will be shorn. He says only ‘When it be needful’, and moves irritably away from her. They do not speak again. |[[Memory: Gossip]] |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] | | | | |- |Hidden Conversation |''[Requires [[Honey-Haunted Pumpkin Pie]]]''
Coquille smilingly samples the cuckoo-honey-dosed pumpkin pie. ‘Coucou,’ she coos, eyes half-closed. ‘I have always enjoyed the work of the Blomberende-kind.’ Sleepily, she tells the startling story of her seduction of a scion of the House of Scudamore – ‘one toothsome enough that I enjoyed his company, but not so tempting that I might regret it when the time came to press him out of their lovely nest…’ |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] | | |} ==Incidents== Coquille can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of 'Apollo and Marsyas']] *[[The Affair of the Endless Guest]] *[[The Affair of the Invisible Opera]] *[[The Affair of the Messenger's Casket]] *[[The Affair of the Oriflamme Heist]] *[[The Affair of the Threshold Revolution]] == Further Stories == * After completing [[The Affair of the Messenger's Casket]], Coquille can be spoken with. ** If [[Daymare]] was also assisted during the incident, Coquille can be provided with a [[Manuscript]] on [[Sights & Sensations]] 10, or the [[Book]] ''[[Ettery After]]''. Doing so gives Coquille [[Inspired]] and [[Sympathy: Chandler]]. She will reward the Librarian with an [[Inkling]] and ''[[Mihail in Glory]]'', which has aspects of {{Lore|Forge|2}} and {{Lore|Lantern|2}} and can be placed in [[Shrine: the Chancel]] to allow it to accept {{Lore|Forge}} and {{Lore|Lantern}}. *After completing [[The Affair of the Endless Guest]], Coquille can be spoken with. **Upon doing so, Spencer Hobson will be summoned to the House during the next [[Numa]]. Coquille will gain [[Inspired]], [[Fear|Fear: Nowhere]], and [[Agenda|Agenda: Corrivality]]. [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]]

Mme Olympe Bechet.title: Mme Olympe Bechet
Mme Olympe Bechet.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Mme Olympe Bechet.png |principle1={{Lore|Forge}} |principle2={{Lore|Moth}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Latin]], [[Greek]], [[Phrygian]], [[Ramsund]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |address=Kerisham Review,
Plover Street, Kerisham}} {{Quote|Essayist, illustrator, critic. Editor of the Kerisham Review.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Forge}} and {{Lore|Moth}}. She is a potential Secretary Nunciant for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. She can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Ramsund]]. == Invitations and Salons == Olympe requires 3 {{Lore|Moth}} to be invited to Hush House. She prefers food and drink with {{Lore|Forge}}. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation !1st Lesson !Second Conversation ! 2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] |Olympe is writing a novel where one of the characters is a criminal chemist specializing in acids and poisons; she’s hoping Dagmar can help with her research. Dagmar is immediately wary, and keeps insisting that she only knows about ‘lemon juice and things’; but once Olympe explains that the protagonist is based on Coquille, she relaxes enough to discuss the properties of Glassfinger Toxin. |[[Solutions & Separations]] |Olympe and Dagmar compare their experiences of getting drunk on Skinshuck Mead. Both wonder whether they really changed shape, or whether their spirits walked in the beast-shape; both agree that they’ll only drink the stuff again in trustworthy company. |[[Solutions & Separations]] |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Al-Adim and Olympe exchange stories of meetings with the prehuman dead: gentle things that yearn for a redder sun, and hungrier things that seek human blood to satisfy that yearning. |[[Stone Stories]] |Olympe shows al-Adim sketches she's made based on signs she saw in a dream. 'Yes,' he says, 'this is almost Sabazine. Here. The Towers of the Little Hammer. The Wolf-Wife. The Black Dove. I think you dreamt that you were coming to Brancrug…' |[[Sabazine]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] |Douglas warns Olympe darkly of the dangers of knitting before sleep, and the paths it can open in the Wood. ('Yes, I knit. Gentlemen can knit.') |[[Weaving & Knotworking]] | | |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] |Olympe and Arun chuckle over a Roost-rumour that’s recently resurfaced, of ancient trysts between the Malachite and the Mare-in-the-Tree; they speak of the tradition that the Mare-in-the-Tree can sometimes be the Witch’s Sister, what that might mean, and especially what that might mean for Rowena and Aunt Mopsy. |[[Transformations & Liberations]] | | |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] | | | | |- | [[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Yvette wonders whether the gods-who-were-stone can be resolved to psychic or psychological factors – to what degree they were ever real Hours at all, rather than baser, part-sublimated impulses of the existing Hours. Olympe is intrigued. |[[Putrefactions & Calcinations]] | | |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Olympe asks Stanislav about the ‘Pontine Yew’ of legend; and then about the honey of its flowers, which opens a door to another place. He has tasted the honey, but he will say of that place only that it is not the Mansus. |[[Rites of the Roots]] |Stanislav and Olympe discuss the Hours of the Wood. Stanislav points out that monks cut their hair; he suggests, perhaps mischievously, that as a class they belong to the Moth… |[[Rites of the Roots]] |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] | | | | |- |[[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Arthur and Olympe debate the hypothetical City Unbuilt, the dwelling-place of perfect balance. Olympe suggests it might be achievable in the Moon-marches, or even the House of the Moon. Arthur believes it's better as an unachievable ideal - especially since the Meniscate, the Hour of perfect balance, is one of the trio of Chancel Hours, and the other two might prefer to limit her power by forbidding the City. |[[Meniscate Reflections]] |Olympe is interested in a Ramsund-inscribed altar to the Beach-Crow that Arthur found in a cliff-grotto near Trebizond. He sketches some of the signs for her. |[[Ramsund]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Hokobald and Olympe share a series of peculiar meditations on chrysalides and crossroads. ‘It will never be as it was,’ she says, several times, softly. |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |Olympe and Hokobald exchange elliptical observations about lymph, wine, choroid, and chitin. She pats his hand and smiles; he shrugs his vast shoulders. |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |- | [[MCO Constance Lee]] |Olympe insists to Connie that she has never breached oneiric law in her use of exotic pigments in her work. Connie is certain that Olympe has used refulgin; Olympe admits she has, but assures Connie that it was diluted beyond the hazard-point… |[[Inks of Revelation]] |Olympe is pressing Connie on the suppression by the Bureau of recordings of Verro’s ‘Opening the Sky’. Connie evidently enjoys fencing with her: there were good reasons; is this an interview, Olympe; lot of questions for not-an-interview; and so on. Although when Olympe mentions the word ‘Chandler’, she becomes a little testier. |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] |Morgen repeats half-remembered fragments of Ramund that the wind brought her when she was sailing. Olympe translates them for her. |[[Ramsund]] |Olympe asks frankly if Morgen wished to become alukite, and if not, whether there are any steps she might have taken to avoid conception. Morgen shivers with amusement – is it only amusement? – and observes that Olympe never did understand the Grail; that it’s no wonder Olympe ‘chose another path.’ |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Ehsan longingly, regretfully describes the jewels he knew in the earth, in his skaptodon years, as he perceived them through slower, stronger senses. (Olympe: ‘How long were you in the earth?’ Ehsan: ‘That’s the Lionsmith’s secret.’) |[[Anbary & Lapidary]] |Ehsan and Olympe discuss the lunatic theories of the heresiarch Cygnifer. Olympe mentions the connection Cygnifer draws between amber and the city Ys – the city beyond the wave – and admits that this connection has always made intuitive sense to her, though she can’t explain why… |[[Anbary & Lapidary]] |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Olympe is writing a novel where one of the characters owns a mining firm, and she's hoping Fraser can help with her research. Fraser is desperately concerned about unnecessary publicity, although Olympe promises him that the character will not share his name, his appearance, or any of his biographical details. He does grudgingly agree to help out when Olympe confides that the protagonist is based on Azita. |[[Coil & Chasm]] |Olympe and Fraser discuss asimel and ashartine. Olympe confesses in a rush that she can never remember which is which; after an agonising moment, Fraser shakes his head and admits 'No more can I.' They grin at each other. |[[Inks of Revelation]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |‘I have a name’, Zachary says dispassionately, ‘and another name. One of them is written only in Killasimi. I will speak of it, because you have invited me. But I will not speak it, because I am a guest.’ |[[Killasimi]] |Zachary is having a bad day. His eyes are wide and staring; his teeth chatter. Olympe lays a hand on his arm to comfort him, and quotes from the Debate of Seven Cups: ‘Sorrow then is Sense’s final Solvent…’ |[[Solutions & Separations]] |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |Olympe is writing a novel where one of the characters is a jewel-smuggler, and she’s hoping Azita can help with her research. Azita is understandably suspicious, despite Olympe’s repeated assurances that none of this is on the record, but she unbends enough to ‘talk rubies’ once Olympe explains that the protagonist is based on Dagmar. |[[Anbary & Lapidary]] |Olympe tries to interrogate Azita on her alleged provision of weapons to various rebel and partisan groups east of the Black Sea. Azita insists that her dyad-twin Mehrad is the one responsible. |[[Edicts Martial]] |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Olympe is writing a novel where one of the characters is an architect specialising in secret passages and concealed entrances. She’s hoping Coquille can help with her research. Coquille is understandably suspicious, although Olympe promises up and down that any difficult details will be in strict confidence. Eventually Olympe explains that the protagonist is based on Fraser, and Coquille relaxes enough to share her secrets. |[[Door & Wall]] |Coquille and Olympe are comparing restaurants in Tiflis. Coquille insists that the place has gone downhill since the establishment of the Socialist Republic; Olympe counters that you just need to know where to look. |[[Spices & Savours]] |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Corso chaffs Olympe about her recent review of a performance of Menander’s ‘The Burning Woman’, which she considers an outright manifesto for the creation of new Hours – ‘Gods-from-Steel’. She acknowledges that it’s an absurd idea… but disagrees that the director thought it was absurd. |[[Transformations & Liberations]] |Olympe and Corso commiserate about the difficulty of getting the ink asimel out of one’s dreams, grumbling that one’s sleep stays silver for months… |[[Inks of Revelation]] |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Agdistis and Olympe speak of the kind of wounds that words as weapons may cause - the big ones and the little ones. They speak also of the creation of stars - the big ones, and the little ones ... |[[Pyroglyphics]] |Olympe has become interested in an 'demi-dyad' - a supposed partway Edge-long who attempted to ascend under the Horned-Axe, a habitué of the now-defunct Ecdysis Club where Agdistis once worked. Agdistis suggests she cease her investigations: that it is not wise to pursue any implication that the Horned-Axe may still possess any trace of Edge... |[[Edicts Liminal]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Mr Kille and Olympe are enthusing about Noël Coward, of whom, it seems, they are both enthusiastic admirers. Olympe mentions that she has, packed carefully away inside her luggage, a 78 disc with Coward’s most recent work, ‘Don’t Put Your Daughter On the Stage, Mrs Worthington’, and offers to lend it to Mr Kille, who is so excited that he almost kicks over his chair.
[Mr Kille and Olympe have discovered a shared interest in the works of Noël Coward. These two might have more to say if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Strings & Songs]] |Last time, Olympe lent Mr Kille her copy of Coward’s ‘Mrs Worthington’. He now returns it with thanks. They enthuse over the piece for some minutes, after which she smilingly presents him with two tickets for a Coward performance in London next month. Suddenly serious, he declines, with thanks. She insists that they’re comps, and cost her nothing; he says very quietly that he has learnt that it can be unwise to accept gifts from visitors to Hush House. Olympe’s smile flickers; she withdraws the tickets; the conversation is at an end. |[[Strings & Songs]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |Olympe chats to Denzil about her travels in Europe. From time to time Denzil says something. Usually what he says is ‘Be that so?’, but once he observes, gnomically, ‘Wonder.’ |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |Olympe chats to Denzil about village life. It is mostly Olympe who does the chatting. |[[Memory: Gossip]] |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Timothy is delighted to hear that Olympe knows Georgia. He has literally hundreds of questions, he assures her, about the wine, the heterodoxies, the Panther’s Skin, the Fifth Cup, the myth of the Amiranis Beteli… Olympe massages her temples and tells him that he’s allowed ten questions. She does, however, answer each of them in detail. |[[Sand Stories]] | | |} ==Incidents== Olympe can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of the Dappled Rose]] *[[The Affair of the Invisible Opera]] *[[The Affair of the Oriflamme Heist]] *[[The Affair of the Royal Endeavour]] *[[The Affair of the Unfinished Lark]] ==Further Stories== *After completing [[The Affair of the Invisible Opera]], Olympe can request a book on Hush House's Winter Tower. **Providing ''[[Against Vitruvius]]'' or ''[[Annals of St Brandan's]]'' will give her [[Inspired]], [[Sympathy: Reckoners]], and [[Agenda: Revelation]] and reward the Librarian with an [[Inkling]] and a [[Forbidden Epic]]. *After completing [[The Affair of the Dappled Rose]], Olympe can request a book on Miah. **Providing ''[[Book of Miah]]'', ''[[The Book of the Centipede]]'' or ''[[The Book of Masks]]'' will give her [[Inspired]], [[Agenda: Peace]] and [[Fear: Carapace]], along with an [[Inkling]].
