Mr Fraser Strathcoyne.title: Mr Fraser Strathcoyne
Mr Fraser Strathcoyne.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Mr Fraser Strathcoyne.png |principle1={{Lore|Lantern}} |principle2={{Lore|Scale}} |aspects=[[Visitor]], [[Inspired]], [[Sympathy]]: Carapace |languages=[[Ramsund]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]]|address=Strathcoyne House, Midsomer Norton}} {{Quote|Philanthropist, collector, former Librarian. A complicated man, but not a cruel one.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Lantern}} and {{Lore|Scale}}. He is a potential Treasurer for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. He can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Ramsund]]. Strathcoyne was the fourth Librarian of Hush House from 1838 until [[Natalia Brulleau]] took over. ==Description== Fraser Strathcoyne is a collector and philanthropist, who briefly served as fourth Librarian of the Curia of the Isle; 'Who died not but passed within', in the absence of other candidates and to his annoyance, after [[Solomon Husher]] vanished in 1838. He often held the office of Treasurer of the Curia and much preferred it. His [['Fraser Strathcoyne'|Bust]] is located in [[Motley Tower: Illopoly's Nook]]. He is pedantic, austere, and secretive and has long been haunted by a certain dream of eyes. He is sympathetic to any who undertake a pilgrimage of flesh. He has his own distillery, which produces [[Strathcoyne Whisky]]. He once gifted Solomon Husher a nice set of silver candlesticks. His [[Fraser's Practice Sword|practice sword]] is made of dark ash. It has seen considerable use, and is notched, battered and more than fifty years old. Strathcoyne adopted [[Christopher Illopoly]] in 1903 from an orphanage in Bristol, who served as his pupil and protégé, but their relationship was troubled. Illopoly severed ties with him in 1909, at the age of 20. He is certain that he is descended from the Scimafectra-kind of the Carapace Cross; the 'Glory-Winged' ones - 'the most noble lineage' and that 'A great day is coming.' Quotes attributed to Strathcoyne: *''History is hybrid; Eternity pure.'' ==Invitations and Salons== Strathcoyne requires 5 {{Lore|Scale}} to be invited to Hush House. He prefers {{Lore|Scale}} food and drink. ==Salon Conversations== {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation !1st Lesson !Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Fraser hopes to fund a ballet, to help accelerate the development of the Cross-nature in his 'kin under the Cross'; he hopes to employ Agdistis as a choreographer. Agdistis is clearly wary, but clearly tempted.
[Fraser hoped to commission Agdistis as a choreographer. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Purifications & Exaltations]] |Agdistis and Fraser have returned to their discussion of the prospective ballet for which Fraser wishes to act as impresario. Agdistis has finally agreed to act as choreographer, but only on condition that he can veto Fraser's initial choice of name, which he strongly dislikes: 'The Buzzing in the Skull.' |[[Purifications & Exaltations]] |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Al-Adim and Fraser are debating – very cautiously, even here in Hush House – the nature of the Red Flower of the Calyptra – to what extent it makes use of the cleansing fire, and to what extent it relies on illusion and deception. |[[Inks of Power]] |Al-Adim, the historian, and Fraser, the collector, debate the longevity and the peril of their favourite Great Inks. |[[Inks of Power]] |- |[[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Arthur and Fraser are discussing the Althiban Abyss near Baghdad. Fraser hopes the power that stirs there might be connected to the Carapace Cross, but Arthur firmly dissuades him: if once it was Cross, he says, it belongs to something else now.
[After a conversation with Arthur, Fraser was tempted to visit the Althiban Abyss. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Coil & Chasm]] |Fraser had, it seemed, ignored Arthur's warnings about the Althiban Abyss, and had travelled there hoping to find a great remnant of the Carapace Cross - perhaps even a lost dragon. Just as Arthur warned him, he found something hatched and grown in a decaying tendril of the Seven-Coils - something that had acquired the Worm-nature. 'I had known it was possible for the Cross to turn,' he laments, 'but I had hoped never to see it.' |[[Coil & Chasm]] |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] |Fraser is speaking to Arun of the changes he's been undergoing as his inner nature becomes more manifest. He speaks with obvious pride; but he's concerned that his body might have begun to produce a venom, and he's not sure what to do about it…
[Fraser asked Arun for help with the changes he's undergoing. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Serpents & Venoms]] |Fraser thanks Arun warmly for the advice that Arun gave him last time about the development of one's venom glands. They chat wryly about the difficulties of expressing venom, and the effects of diet on its potency. |[[Serpents & Venoms]] |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |Fraser and Azita are agreeing a complex deal involving a sheep farming operation of Azita's in the Middle East. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |Fraser and Azita are negotiating something shady-sounding about mammoth ivory and dreams of ice… |[[Horns & Ivories]] |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] |Chaima is commissioning 'noble ammunition' from Fraser, for prey which isn't so very bothered by the usual sort of bullet. |[[Disciplines of the Hammer]] |Fraser is quizzing Chaima about routes across the Algerian desert. |[[Sand Stories]] |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] |Fraser wants to view exhibits from the Bureau's White Museum: the remains of animals who've undergone a Cross-change. He is arguing persuasively that he might be of assistance, but Connie is sceptical. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |Connie and Fraser are arguing about the potential return of the Carapace Cross. Connie, of course, views it as a threat; Fraser, inevitably, sees it as an opportunity. |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Fraser asks Coquille to advise him on some Eastern pieces he has recently purchased, which he hopes may be pentiments of the Sixth History… |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |Coquille and Fraser discuss the Great Hooded Princes' (and Princesses') transition between Histories. He asks whether there were Carapace Cross still active in the Fifth History, but she will not answer him. |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Corso has an unusual Book of Suns for sale, 'collated' by a mysterious pilgrim of Antaian heritage. Fraser is interested, but wants to speak to its collator. Corso shakes his head: 'My clients pay for my discretion.' |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |Fraser and Corso debate Medusa's Riddle: 'What Is Not Seen?' Corso gestures nonchalantly with his cigarette: 'If if's not seen, the Hours don't know where it happened. In the end,'it's all about provenance.' |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |- |[[Daymare|'Daymare']] |Fraser wishes to commission Dagmar to inspect his security arrangement. He is particularly concerned about intruders using the key-weapons known as [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Frangiclave frangiclaves], and about the Ligeians with their Keys, though Dagmar scoffs: 'Ligeians won't care about your collection one way or another.'
[Fraser commissioned Dagmar to inspect his security arrangements. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Lockworks & Clockworks]] |Fraser wants Dagmar's help again, this time to open a nine-locked box he has received from the Evening Isles, which he hopes might contain 'a certain map'. He flatly refuses, however, to show the box to Dagmar, who expresses indignation that he won't trust her; and the conversation founders. |[[Lockworks & Clockworks]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] |Fraser complains to Douglas about break-ins. Douglas unsympathetically suggests that Fraser might want to keep less contraband on the premises, then. |[[Wolf Stories]] |Fraser would like to know what Douglas proposes to 'do about Raw Prophets: Douglas doesn't plan to do anything about Raw Prophets. Fraser would like to know, then, what the Bureau intends to do about Raw Prophets. Douglas expresses his confusion. Fraser expresses his irritalion. Douglas expresses his inability to do anything about Raw Prophets. Both men agree that Raw Prophets aren't the kind of thing you can really do anything about. |[[Stone Stories]] |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Fraser and Ehsan are discussing tarascisation and 'la malaise raveline' - the horrible changes that occur in certain families that have conducted 'traffic with beasts'. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |Fraser is experiencing pain in the altered joints of the hand that he prefers to keep gloved; Ehsan has some advice. |[[Herbs & Infusions]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Hokobald negotiates the purchase, from Fraser, of certain exotic alloys. He presses Fraser on the availability of Ys-metal, but Fraser, glancing around nervously, insists that he can provide no such thing. |[[Bells & Brazieries]] |Fraser and Hokobald bicker about whether Henavek - the language-spirit sometimes called 'the Eldest' belongs to the Wood or to the Mansus. |[[Kernewek Henavek|Henavek]] |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] |Fraser expounds his theories on the naming of earthquakes - the origin of the limited roster of names that (he believes) all new earthquakes draw from. Morgen insists that there are no new earthquakes, except, now and then, under the sea when another of the Blackbone's limbs is further fractured. |[[Hill & Hollow]] |Morgen insists on the superiority of cats to dogs. Fraser insists on the inferiority of cats to bees. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Olympe is writing a novel where one of the characters owns a mining firm, and she's hoping Fraser can help with her research. Fraser is desperately concerned about unnecessary publicity, although Olympe promises him that the character will not share his name, his appearance, or any of his biographical details. He does grudgingly agree to help out when Olympe confides that the protagonist is based on Azita. |[[Coil & Chasm]] |Olympe and Fraser discuss asimel and ashartine. Olympe confesses in a rush that she can never remember which is which; after an agonising moment, Fraser shakes his head and admits 'No more can I.' They grin at each other. |[[Inks of Revelation]] |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] |Serena and Fraser speculate about bisclavrets, the werewolves of Broceliande. Serena proposes connections both to Ys and to families like the Ravelines who labour under a beast-curse. She cuts Fraser's response off impatiently: 'Not everything has to be about the Carapace Cross, you know.' |[[Coil & Chasm]] |Fraser and Serena speak of Antaios, who might have been a child of Name-emanations of the Flint and Wheel. Fraser wonders why, if Antaios' forebears were immortal, they did not suffer the urge to devour him. Serena provokingly asks when he thinks the Crime of the Sky first became a Crime... |[[Stone Stories]] |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller|Fr Stanislav John Schaller]] |Stanislav and Fraser discuss the work of the entomologist Juliana Zawistowski. Fraser is firmly of the belief that she bore within her the nature of the Thritige-kind of the Carapace Cross. |[[Stone Stories]] |Fraser and Stanislav discuss the Unnumbered Stones of Brittany, not far from Stanislav's current digs. Fraser insists they were placed by the Carapace Cross. Stanislav humours him. |[[Stone Stories]] |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Yvette is asking Fraser about his 'dreams of eyes'. He is eager to tell her - he interprets them as messages from the 'greater hybridity' of the Carapace Cross, though she is sceptical. |[[Hill & Hollow]] |Yvette and Fraser discuss his further 'dreams of eyes', and his theories about the entry of the Scīmafectra-kind and the Thritige-kind to human flesh. Yvette wonders aloud whether he has ever considered that most - perhaps all - of the dreams arise from his own frustrated desire for fatherhood. In a fit of temper, he snatches off the glove on his changed hand, and displays its glossy, altered angles to her. For a moment there is silence at the table. |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Fraser inquires - sometimes tactfully - about Zachary's condition, what exactly he bears within him, what dangers it might present, and what it might become. Zachary answers - always cautiously and elliptically. |[[Serpents & Venoms]] |Fraser suggests ways in which Zachary might advance or evolve his limbless passengers so that they might both become something more - in safety. Zachary is not convinced. |[[Serpents & Venoms]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Fraser asks Mrs Kille whether there have been any unusual births in the countryside hereabouts of late - animals, or humans? She admits that yes, there have. He asks if any of them have featured wings, or unusual eyes? After a longer pause, she says that yes, some have, but she knows of none that have survived. |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |Fraser quizzes Mrs Kille about her dreams; particularly any dreams she can remember from her childhood; and in particular whether she can recall any 'dreams of eyes'. Mrs Kille answers in detail, but without friendliness. |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |Fraser quizzes Denzil on his recollections of Cornish tin-mining. Denzil's family, it seems, included a number of tinners. 'Not many as do die old,' Denzil allows. |[[Coil & Chasm]] |Fraser returns to the subject of mining, and of Denzil's family connections with tinners. Evidently he has commercial ambitions in this part of the world... Denzil answers him, albeit reluctantly. |[[Coil & Chasm]] |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Timothy - an admirer of Christopher Illopoly's work - has learnt that Illopoly was adopted by Fraser Strathcoyne, and has many, many questions for Fraser about Illopoly's education and career. Fraser answers them in reasonably good temper until Timothy guilelessly asks why Illopoly now uses a different surname. |[[Auroral Contemplations]] |Timothy (a keen amateur naturalist) shares his wasp-related insights with Fraser. Fraser's interest waxes and wanes. |[[Insects & Nectars]] |} ==Incidents== Fraser can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of the Claw and the Clouds]] *[[The Affair of the Particular Mystique]] *[[The Affair of the Rising While]] *[[The Affair of the Royal Endeavour]] *[[The Affair of the Sandalwood Saint]] *[[The Affair of the Second Skin]] *[[The Affair of the Unfettered Eye]] [[Category:Past Librarians]] [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]]

Sr. Corso Reverte.title: Sr. Corso Reverte
Sr. Corso Reverte.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Sr. Corso Reverte.png |principle1={{Lore|Grail}} |principle2={{Lore|Lantern}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Greek]], [[Hyksos]], [[Phrygian]], [[Sanskrit]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |address=Mansard Books, Oxford}} {{Quote|Manuscript-hunter, legacy-scavenger... mercenary? Many would question his ethics; few would deny his acuteness.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Grail}} and {{Lore|Lantern}}. He is a potential Secretary Enigmatic for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. He can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Hyksos]]. == Invitations and Salons == Corso requires 3 {{Lore|Lantern}} to be invited to Hush House. He prefers {{Lore|Grail}} food and drink. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" ! Visitor !First Conversation !1st Lesson !Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] |Dagmar and Corso are arguing good-naturedly about whether Abbot Geffrey's dialogues on Forculus, Limentinus and Cardea qualify as 'proper nyctodromy.' |[[The Great Signs and the Great Scars]] |Corso and Dagmar are enjoying an ''entirely theoretical'' discussion of how locks might be subverted through vulgar nyctodromy. And whether Teresa Galmier was a nyctodromist (Dagmar) or a horomachist (Corso). |[[Lockworks & Clockworks]] |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Al-Adim is reminiscing to Corso about Yarden of Nishapur, who knew the 'songs that came before the sun' … |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |Corso is eager to hear more about Yarden of Nishapur, who al-Adim may have known long ago… although al-Adim grows chillier when Corso's interest crystallises into interest into curiosity about the location of certain valuable texts. |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |- | [[DI Douglas Moore]] |Douglas and Corso discuss the nuances of the differences in the Received and Sanctioned versions of the Book of Suns… once Corso's got over his surprise at Douglas' interests. ('No-one ever bleeding believes I got a bleeding scholarship,' Douglas grumbles.) |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |Douglas and Corso chat affably about church. (Douglas used to be a chapel-goer, but Mrs Moore disapproves.) |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] |Corso and Arun are chuckling together about Musgrave Dewulf's theories on the Great Ink porphyrine. |[[Inks of Revelation]] |Arun and Corso are discussing a scheme to track down valuable books by observing the effects of their ink on the dreams of those nearby, but Corso subsides into a sulk when it becomes apparent that Arun is not taking the idea seriously. |[[Inks of Revelation]] |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] |Serena and Corso gloomily dispute the poet Kalle's menacing aphorism: 'A star is a pin-prick, but the Sun is a wound.' Corso believes it presages the later division of the Sun; Serena suggests it anticipates a horrific ending to the Vagabond's prophesied pilgrimage up to the Glory... |[[Pyroglyphics]] | | |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Yvette and Corso discuss the reckoner mobs - the predatory merchants of years-of-life. Yvette tentatively suggests that she might like Corso to put her in touch with the reckoners, if he can… but he discourages her. 'Do you know what sanding is? Or dolling? Find out, Dr Southey, and then ask me again.' |[[Snow Stories]] | | |- | [[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Stanislav and Corso speak of Zulfiya Zakirova, to whom Corso was once very nearly married – by Stanislav, in fact. Corso tugs miserably at his moustache as he describes her struggles with deliria and her obsession with the whimsies of the Wood. ‘Then one day she started wearing wigs and ran off with a piano-tuner. Last I heard she was giving piano lessons in Leipzig.’ |[[Orchids & Narcotics]] | | |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] |Corso listens intently as Chaima describes a nasty tangle with the Reckoner Mobs - the loan-sharks of lifetime - back in the 20s… |[[Ragged Crossroads]] | | |- |[[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Arthur and Corso are discussing Ericapaean - a language that both of them are struggling to master. They agree to correspond in that language, although Corso points out that it'll probably get their post opened by the Suppression Bureau.
[These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Ericapaean]] |Corso and Arthur have, it seems, been corresponding clumsily in half-learnt Ericapaean. Arthur has made more progress: he explains, very quietly, that he has had help from Julian Coseley. 'Is he actually alive?' Corso asks sceptically. 'Alive? What's alive?' responds Arthur. 'Is the Empire alive?' | [[Ericapaean]] |- | [[Magister Hokobald]] |Corso has bought a Deep Mandaic cylinder seal as a gift for Hokobald – ‘because, Magister, there are so few who might appreciate it.’ While Hokobald is thus gratified, he brings out a collection of similar cylinder seals, and secures Hokobald’s opinion and advice on their authenticity… |[[Deep Mandaic]] |Corso adroitly flatters Hokobald into an impromptu lesson in the sigillography of Deep Mandaic. |[[Deep Mandaic]] |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] |Connie is quizzing a clearly nervous Corso about the contents and history of the book known as the 'Calicite Supplications'… and the recent disappearance of the Bureau's copy.
[These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Tridesma Hiera]] | | |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] |Corso has read conflicting accounts of traditional means of mixing the sacrament Calicite. He asks Morgen, as an ‘ambassadress of the Grail’, for her opinions. She objects to the characterization – ‘ambassadress of the Witch, perhaps, on a clear night at least’ – but does share her clearly informed opinions. |[[Applebright Euphonies]] |Corso banters with Morgen about the actual composition of her fabled ‘key of black sapphire’, which she insists is metaphorically glass, and which he suggests is a stained glass window ‘somewhere quiet’… |[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]] |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Corso chaffs Olympe about her recent review of a performance of Menander’s ‘The Burning Woman’, which she considers an outright manifesto for the creation of new Hours – ‘Gods-from-Steel’. She acknowledges that it’s an absurd idea… but disagrees that the director thought it was absurd. |[[Transformations & Liberations]] |Olympe and Corso commiserate about the difficulty of getting the ink asimel out of one’s dreams, grumbling that one’s sleep stays silver for months… |[[Inks of Revelation]] |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Corso insists to Ehsan that Teresa Galmier visited his bookshop in Oxford, in person. ‘She used a different name. So I didn’t want to embarrass her. She’s changed. But it’s her. But she’s changed. Taller. Well, something like taller, not taller exactly. Stop laughing, Ehsan – ’ |[[Purifications & Exaltations]] | | |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Corso has an unusual Book of Suns for sale, 'collated' by a mysterious pilgrim of Antaian heritage. Fraser is interested, but wants to speak to its collator. Corso shakes his head: 'My clients pay for my discretion.' |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |Fraser and Corso debate Medusa's Riddle: 'What Is Not Seen?' Corso gestures nonchalantly with his cigarette: 'If if's not seen, the Hours don't know where it happened. In the end, 'it's all about provenance.' |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Zachary asks Corso to teach him a prayer in Hyksos - 'in case I should die when I wake.'...
[These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Hyksos]] |Zachary wants more help from Corso with his Hyksos studies. He’s heard that the ceremonies of the Légion du Seuil sometimes employ that language. He’s considering joining the Légion, but he wants to understand it better first. |[[Hyksos]] |- | [[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |Corso and Azita are both intrigued by recent government interest in the alchemies of the Sunset Road (and in what that might mean for those who could, say, lay their hands on lost Sunset Road works, even works of uncertain provenance.) |[[Purifications & Exaltations]] |Corso and Azita are discussing recently discovered letters supposedly sent by the Abbess Melancthe to Gunnhild, daughter of Harold. Their musings on its contents are punctuated with bald estimates of their possible value. |[[Purifications & Exaltations]] |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] | | | | |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Agdistis and Corso chat about Solar doctrine. Both of them, it seems, were raised in the Sun: both of them admit to an absurd degree of guilt about their absence from church on the Sun's Day. |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |Agdistis and Corso are chatting amicably about growing up in the ways of the Sun. Apparently they were both choirboys. ('I know, I know,' says Corso. 'Then I started smoking.) |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |- | [[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Corso hauls his notebook from his pocket and displays a magazine clipping: 'Subtle Earth', a poem he enjoyed, written by none other than Mr Kille. Mr Kille, embarrassed, leans in close to discuss it. He admits that conversations in the Sweet Bones with the more memorable visitors to Hush House provided inspiration...
[These two might say more if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Applebright Euphonies]] |Corso has brought a volume of Franklin Bancroft's poetry for Mr Kille to read - he claims to see parallels with Kille's own work. Kille is grateful, but clearly cautious. He agrees at last to borrow it overnight on the promise that it is not a gift, and Corso will drop by to reclaim it before he leaves. (Mr Kille indicates that in Brancrug, they are wary of accepting gifts from visitors to the House.) |[[Applebright Euphonies]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |Denzil teaches Corso a few words of Kernewek Henavek, the ancient tongue still used in some of Brancrug Village’s winter ceremonies. He refers to it as ‘Tavas Mytern’ – perhaps ‘the King Tongue’ – and speaks not of ‘it’ but of ‘him’, as if the language were a living king indeed. |[[Kernewek Henavek|Henavek]] |Corso asks Denzil about the coastal paths, and those he’s seen walking them. Smugglers? Pilgrims? Ghosts? Denzil shakes his head to all of those, but he does describe an encounter his great-grandfather supposedly had with a ‘woman from behind the wave’… |[[Path & Pilgrim]] |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Timothy is relentlessly regaling Corso with his favourite moorland walks. |[[Stone Stories]] |Corso has learnt that Reverend Timothy has a tiny library of theological texts inherited from a Welsh maiden aunt, and is manoeuvring to identify whether Timothy has anything of value while also trying to avoid coming across as overly predatory. Fortunately for Corso, Timothy remains oblivious; unfortunately for Timothy and Corso both, the library consists largely of Victorian reprints. |[[Sacra Solis Invicti]] |} ==Incidents== Corso can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of 'Apollo and Marsyas']] *[[The Affair of the Invisible Opera]] *[[The Affair of the Particular Mystique]] *[[The Affair of the Royal Endeavour|The Affair of the Royal Endeavor]] *[[The Affair of the Threshold Revolution]] *[[The Affair of the Unfettered Eye]] == Further Stories == * After completing [[The Affair of 'Apollo and Marsyas']], Corso will ask for a book on 'Coseley on the Carapace' or on Resurgences & Emergences 10+ to help the soprano ascend via a Moth path. **After offering either [[The Fallen Cross]] or the latter above, Corso gains [[Sympathy: Carapace]] and [[Agenda: Stone Remembered]]. The Librarian is rewarded with an [[Inkling]] and a Bronze Spintria. * After completing [[The Affair of the Royal Endeavour|The Affair of the Royal Endeavor]], Corso will ask for a book on 'Cygnifer's thing on the dividing serpent' or on Pyroglyphics 10+ to sabotage the effort. **After offering the latter, Corso gains [[Fear: Chandler]] and rewards the Librarian with an [[Inkling]] and a Bronze Spintria. * After completing [[The Affair of the Unfettered Eye]] Corso will ask for "a book on Lucia's deeper traditions" (''[[Unhatched Hymns]])'' or a manuscript of [[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]] with Mystery: Lantern of 12 or higher. ** Giving him either book will result in Corso gaining [[Inspired]], Fear: Chandler, and Agenda: Revelation. It will also reward the Librarian with a Bronze Spintria and an [[Inkling]]. [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]]

MCO Constance Lee.title: MCO Constance Lee
MCO Constance Lee.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Connie Lee.png |principle1={{Lore|Moon}} |principle2={{Lore|Sky}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Aramaic]], [[Greek]], [[Killasimi]], [[Latin]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |address=Hotel Storchen, Zürich}} {{Quote|Connie has risen swiftly in the Suppression Bureau, to the exalted rank of Constable-Oculate Minor. Don't get in her way.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Moon}} and {{Lore|Sky}}. She is a potential Secretary Nunciant for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. She can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Killasimi]]. == Invitations and Salons == Connie requires 3 {{Lore|Moon}} to be invited to Hush House. She prefers food and drink with {{Lore|Sky}}. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation !1st Lesson !Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] | | | | |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |Connie and al-Adim are discussing the stories about Franklin Bancroft and Eva Dewulf - heads together - smiling. Evidently the location has inspired them. |[[Pearl & Tide]] |Once again, Connie and al-Adim are discussing Eva Dewulf and Bancroft. Connie sips from her glass, watching him as he leans in close to recite Bancroft's poetry. |[[Pearl & Tide]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] |Douglas and Connie are talking shop; the kind of shop that requires them to spill salt on the table after naming certain entities, and not to name others at all, but rather to refer to them as 'the spiky royal one', 'the bluey one with the temper', and 'the glossy one'. |[[Maggephene Mysteries]] |Douglas and Connie reminisce about old cases, and cheerfully speculate about the final fate of adepts they’ve locked up. |[[Edicts Inviolable]] |- |[[Dr Arun Peel]] | | | | |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] | | | | |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Connie and Yvette are discussing a patient of Yvette's who, it now appears, may have died before attending his first session. ('I had wondered,' Yvette says slowly, 'why my rooms were always so cold afterwards.') Connie is of the opinion that since the man is dead, no ethical considerations about confidentiality need apply. Yvette is not convinced. |[[Rhyme & Remembrance]] |‘The language of the Four Quarters.’ Connie shakes her head. ‘I learnt it out there, before I joined the Bureau. If I talk too much about it, it’ll spoil the mood. But here’s some pointers.’ |[[Killasimi]] |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Connie is investigating stories of something described as ‘Spinnennebel’ – a kind of spider-vapor – which has begun to manifest in Germany and the Low Countries. Stanislav has heard nothing, but agrees it sounds nothing like Hive, nor Nest, nor Chrysalis…
[Connie aroused Stanislav’s interest in the ‘Spinnennebel’. The two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Insects & Nectars]] |Stanislav confirms to Connie that he, too, has now heard something of the ‘Spinnennebel’ which first appeared in Austria but has afflicted remote parts of the countryside across Europe – even as far west as his sanctuary in Brittany. He agrees that it has many of the hallmarks of a Nowhere irruption – but adds thoughtfully that one informant claims it’s been manufactured… |[[Insects & Nectars]] |- |[[Lalla Chaima]] |Chaima and Connie are discussing - with sorrow - the 'khalvites', those labhites who have chosen to drink what Echidna offers... |[[Wolf Stories]] | | |- | [[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Connie and Arthur are discussing Teresa Galmier's work on the enigmatic power known as 'Janus', with slightly strained professional courtesy. |[[Watchman's Paradoxes]] |Arthur and Connie are rather stiffly discussing the New King's projects. Both of them seem wary of each other. |[[Disciplines of the Hammer]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Hokobald grandiosely condescends to share information about the depredations of a Grail-long and associated coven in Maremma. Connie listens carefully, her expression neutral. |[[Desires & Dissolutions]] |Connie questions Hokobald narrowly about recent mephitic manifestations on the Swiss-German border. Hokobald denies any involvement, and argues plausibly that these may be the first signs of the emergence of another Chandler-name... |[[Pyroglyphics]] |- |[[Mlle Margot Matutine]] |Connie asks Morgen careful, neutral questions about her connection to the Red Grail, the Hour of Birth and appetite. Morgen carelessly shares her reminiscences, but she insists that of all her un-sisters, she is the 'least grailsome'. |[[Tridesma Hiera]] |Connie asks business-like questions about a didumos – the twin or reflection of a star – that she fears may have been employed to commit crimes-of-dream. She suspects it has taken refuge in the Mansus-shadow called the House of the Moon. Morgen, answering with surprising frankness, nevertheless makes it clear to Connie that the Suppression Bureau will never be able to follow it into the House of the Moon – and that she will under no circumstances help them try. |[[Ouranoscopy]] |- | [[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Olympe insists to Connie that she has never breached oneiric law in her use of exotic pigments in her work. Connie is certain that Olympe has used refulgin; Olympe admits she has, but assures Connie that it was diluted beyond the hazard-point… |[[Inks of Revelation]] |Olympe is pressing Connie on the suppression by the Bureau of recordings of Verro’s ‘Opening the Sky’. Connie evidently enjoys fencing with her: there were good reasons; is this an interview, Olympe; lot of questions for not-an-interview; and so on. Although when Olympe mentions the word ‘Chandler’, she becomes a little testier. |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Ehsan wants to know if Connie ever gets tired of enforcing laws. ‘I might ask you,’ she responds. ‘if you ever get tired of healing bodies.’ |[[Edicts Inviolable]] | | |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Fraser wants to view exhibits from the Bureau's White Museum: the remains of animals who've undergone a Cross-change. He is arguing persuasively that he might be of assistance, but Connie is sceptical. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |Connie and Fraser are arguing about the potential return of the Carapace Cross. Connie, of course, views it as a threat; Fraser, inevitably, sees it as an opportunity. |[[Pentiments & Precursors]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Zachary asks Connie for advice on a plan to manage the development of his condition with tattoos-of-containment, 'I wish you'd come to me sooner,' she breathes. But of course she gives him what help she can.
[Zachary asked Connie for help. These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Inks of Containment]] | | |- |[[Ms Azita Bukhara]] | | | | |- |[[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Connie and Coquille are discussing recent shipwrecks, and a possible connection to Ys... |[[Sea Stories]] |Coquille and Connie are discussing the rumors about the liaison between Franklin Bancroft and Eva Dewulf, more than two hundred years ago; about Bancroft’s departure and the child they might have had. ‘It is good to be adopted into a loving family,’ Coquille says smilingly, but she will not be drawn on what that means. |[[Sea Stories]] |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Connie is quizzing a clearly nervous Corso about the contents and history of the book known as the 'Calicite Supplications'… and the recent disappearance of the Bureau's copy.
[These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Tridesma Hiera]] | | |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Connie and Agdistis, unexpectedly, are discussing ouranoscopy: she's intrigued by the ways in which the 'dance' of the Hours and of the heavenly bodies might serve as a source of horomachic information. Agdistis is nonplussed, but does his best to keep up. |[[Ouranoscopy]] |Once again, Connie and Agdistis are discussing ouranoscopy. She's had some of her people looking into some of Agdistis' ideas, and her face is serious. 'Much more than an eclipse,' she says somberly. 'Perhaps even a War in the Sun.' |[[Ouranoscopy]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Connie, recalling that Mrs Kille's maiden name was 'Raveline', questions her closely about whether she has had any dreams of wolves, or experienced any cravings for meat or for loam. Mrs Kille patiently, if wearily, answers no to each question. |[[Stone Stories]] |Connie questions Mrs Kille about stories of changelings in the remoter parts of the county. Mrs Kille insists that these are only stories… but admits she has been known to string windowsills with red thread, and place rowan twigs beneath the cradle, just in case. |[[Quenchings & Quellings]] |- | [[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] | | | | |- |[[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Timothy asks Connie detailed questions about the construction of the Cucurbit, which she answers very guardedly until she realises Timothy's interest is fundamentally architectural and that in fact he mostly seems to have forgotten that it's a prison. |[[Door & Wall]] |Timothy is excited to find himself within conversational range of a senior Suppression Bureau official, and asks Connie a great many questions about the Bureau's activities and its recently increased co-operation with the Church. She answers a number of them and politely bats down others, until he asks innocently 'where exactly is Calyptra?' - at which point she shakes her head, tells him quietly never to ask about Calyptra again, and changes the subject. |[[Edicts Inviolable]] |} ==Incidents== Connie can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of 'Apollo and Marsyas']] *[[The Affair of the Claw and the Clouds]] *[[The Affair of the Forgivable Debt]] *[[The Affair of the Friar's Tapestry]] *[[The Affair of the Messenger's Casket]] *[[The Affair of the Rising While]] *[[The Affair of the Unfinished Lark]] == Further Stories == After the completion of [[The Affair of the Friar's Tapestry]], Constance Lee will ask for a book about the Bureau activities. She will stay or leave the Bureau (and the game as a Visitor, becoming '''Constance Lee''' who may still be appointed Secretary Nunciant). * Offering ''[[Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1928]]'' will make her stay and gain [[Inspired]] and Agenda: Stone Consumed aspects. This will conclude the Incident. (please add more info which books influence the outcome of the Incident) * Offering [[Velletri Interviews]] will make her stay and gain [[Inspired]], Agenda : secrecy and Fear : Nowhere aspects. This will conclude the Incident. * Offering [[An Exorcist's Field Manual]] will make her stay and gain [[Inspired]], Agenda: Secrecy and Fear: Devourers. This will conclude the Incident. * Offering [[Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1927]], [[The Admonitory Automata Project]] or [[Journal of Sir David Greene, 1903]] will make her resign and no longer appear as a Visitor, but still available for recruitment in the Lighthouse Institute. She will gain the [[Unsociable]], [[Inspired]] and [[Agenda: Revelation]] aspects. After the completion of [[The Affair of the Open Reverend]] and talking with [[DI Douglas Moore]], you can discuss this event with Connie. She will request a manual with [[Quenchings & Quellings]] 12+ , [[Wolf Stories]] 12+ or a book about Gnathobasis. * Giving her the book [[OGHKOR OGHKOR TISSILAK OGHKOR]] fulfills the final requirement, giving you an [[Inkling]] and a Bronze Spintria. This will also give Connie [[Inspired]], Fear: Nowhere, and Agenda: Secrecy After the completion of the [[The Affair of the Rising While]], Connie will ask for a book to help interpret an oracle. * Giving her the book [[Eva's Treasury]] fulfills the requirement, giving you another choice to make: Give up Yvette Southey to Mrs. E for safekeeping or convince Connie that the prophecy is not so certain as it seemed. ** Giving her a manuscript of [[Ouranoscopy]] [14] will convince Connie to leave Yvette be. She will gain [[Inspired]], [[Agenda: Autarchy]], and [[Fear: Devourers]]. ** Handing over [[Dr Yvette Southey]] permanently removed her from the game. Connie gains Agenda: Secrecy, Fear: Ys, and rewards the Librarian with an [[Inkling]] and a Bronze Spintria. == Trivia == * In ''[[Book of Hours]]''' sister work, [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Cultist_Simulator ''Cultist Simulator''], Constance Lee appears as [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Connie_Lee Connie Lee], a Hunter working for the [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Suppression_Bureau Suppression Bureau] and a potential disciple. And tellingly, considered among the most difficult to deal with. * Interestingly, neither of her principles, {{Lore|Moon}} or {{Lore|Sky}}, existed in ''Cultist Simulator'', where she was instead associated with {{Lore|Edge}} and {{Lore|Grail}}. * According to the [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Sunset_Diaries ''Sunset Diaries''], Constance Lee will go on to buy the Suppression Bureau in 1974. Mlle Margot Matutine.title: Mlle Margot Matutine
Mlle Margot Matutine.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=Mlle Margot Matutine.png |principle1={{Lore|Grail}} |principle2={{Lore|Sky}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Greek]], [[Killasimi]], [[Latin]], [[Phrygian]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]] |address='Saphir', Marseilles}} {{Quote|Socialite, yachtswoman... and, under the name 'Morgen', an alukite, a Ligeian. The former means, among other things, that she eats people. The latter means, among other things, that she is not to be taken lightly.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Grail}} and {{Lore|Sky}}. She is a potential Secretary Persistent for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. She can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Killasimi]]. Morgen is a member of the [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Ligeia_Club Ligeia Club], a group of seven Alukites who hold the Keys to the Doors of the Mansus, required for a Long to ascend to a Name. She is the holder of the Key of Black Sapphire, called sea-born, tide-drawn[https://book-of-hours.fandom.com/wiki/Sea_Stories#Wisdom_Attunement Sea Stories]. [['Mlle Matutine'|A painting of her]] can be found in the [[Violet Chamber]]. ==Invitations & Salons== Mlle Matutine requires 7 {{Lore|Grail}} to be invited to Hush House. She prefers {{Lore|Sky}} food and drink...at least in polite company. == Salon Conversations == {| class="sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table" !Visitor !First Conversation !1st Lesson !Second Conversation !2nd Lesson |- |[[Daymare]] | | | | |- |[[Dr Ibn al-Adim]] |AI-Adim and Morgen discuss the meditations of Abbot Thomas of St Brandan's. Morgen asks if al-Adim ever met the Abbot. 'I acknowledge that I am rather older than you,' he replies, a little stiffly, 'but I am not that old.' |[[Applebright Euphonies]] |Morgen and al-Adim compare their experiences of the notorious blossoms of the City of Messenger Eagles, which they have both visited, although, it seems, their visits were almost two hundred years apart... |[[Orchids & Narcotics]] |- |[[DI Douglas Moore]] | | | | |- | [[Dr Arun Peel]] | | | | |- |[[Dr Serena Blackwood]] | | | | |- |[[Dr Yvette Southey]] |Morgen seems taken with Yvette, and devotes more attention to her than Yvette seems comfortable with. When Yvette falls silent, Morgen raises her silvery voice in a silvery song. The tune is jaunty; but the words are Killasimi; and by the end of it, even Morgen seems distraught. 'I wish, sometimes, that I might still weep,' she confides.
[These two might say something else on the matter if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Killasimi]] |Emboldened by their last conversation, Yvette asks pointed questions about how Morgen came to be what she is. Morgen won’t talk about how she went alukite, but she does talk about growing Long – her tutoring in the Old Form by Sulochana, her fascination with the Thunderskin’s New Form, and the last dances which took her to the House of the Moon. |[[Tridesma Hiera]] |- |[[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] |Morgen asks Stanislav, gaily and lightly, about 'Three Faces', the guardian of the Grove of Green Immortals, where Stanislav is reputed to have spent time. Stanislav replies respectfully, urbanely, and elliptically. |[[Orchids & Narcotics]] | | |- | [[Lalla Chaima]] | | | | |- | [[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]] |Morgen smilingly entreats Arthur to speak to her of the 'Flaw in the Glass' - the menace that [[Omar, the Blaze]] identified in the enclosure of a sacred flame at the Labyrinth of Lions. She is at her most charming, and even Arthur - not a man one might expect to be susceptible to Morgen's charms - unbends enough to drop a few hints. |[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]] |Morgen presses Arthur again on the 'Flaw in the Glass' identified in the enclosure of a sacred flame at the Labyrinth of Lions - and on its connection to the Chandler. He is on his guard this time, but he does allow that a connection might 'come alive' with sufficient Lantern and Knock - and that this is why the Labyrinth permits no Knock-adepts to enter the enclosure. |[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]] |- |[[Magister Hokobald]] |Hokobald attends Morgen with a kind of surly, lascivious obsequiousness, and she permits him to talk to her about the jewels he has brought for her, occasionally offering different opinions to which Hokobald pays due attention. At the end of the conversation, to his evident perplexity, she gives him a cabochon sapphire ‘to hold on to.’ |[[Anbary & Lapidary]] |Last time, Morgen gave Hokobald a cabochon sapphire; he now returns it, sneering at the obviousness of her 'trap'. His manner towards her has changed from surly obsequiousness to surly menace, although the lascivious undertone remains. Morgen insists laughingly that it was 'only a little game,' and though Hokobald plainly doesn't believe her, he decides in the end to accept the excuse - perhaps for the sake of their tenuous alukite un-kinship. |[[Anbary & Lapidary]] |- |[[MCO Constance Lee]] |Connie asks Morgen careful, neutral questions about her connection to the Red Grail, the Hour of Birth and appetite. Morgen carelessly shares her reminiscences, but she insists that of all her un-sisters, she is the 'least grailsome'. |[[Tridesma Hiera]] |Connie asks business-like questions about a didumos – the twin or reflection of a star – that she fears may have been employed to commit crimes-of-dream. She suspects it has taken refuge in the Mansus-shadow called the House of the Moon. Morgen, answering with surprising frankness, nevertheless makes it clear to Connie that the Suppression Bureau will never be able to follow it into the House of the Moon – and that she will under no circumstances help them try. |[[Ouranoscopy]] |- |[[Mme Olympe Bechet]] |Morgen repeats half-remembered fragments of Ramund that the wind brought her when she was sailing. Olympe translates them for her. |[[Ramsund]] |Olympe asks frankly if Morgen wished to become alukite, and if not, whether there are any steps she might have taken to avoid conception. Morgen shivers with amusement – is it only amusement? – and observes that Olympe never did understand the Grail; that it’s no wonder Olympe ‘chose another path.’ |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |- |[[Mr Ehsan Fekri]] |Morgen and Ehsan discuss the motives of the aviform Hours. Ehsan is firm in his belief that they are fundamentally benevolent to mortals; Morgen says smilingly: ‘Perhaps then you know the Twins better than do I.’ |[[Strings & Songs]] | | |- |[[Mr Fraser Strathcoyne]] |Fraser expounds his theories on the naming of earthquakes - the origin of the limited roster of names that (be believes) all new earthquakes draw from. Morgen insists that there are no new earthquakes, except, now and then, under the sea when another of the Blackbone's limbs is further fractured. |[[Hill & Hollow]] |Morgen insists on the superiority of cats to dogs. Fraser insists on the inferiority of cats to bees. |[[Furs & Feathers]] |- |[[Mr Zachary Wakefield]] |Zachary asks Morgen frankly about esoteric techniques to contain appetite in an external vessel. Morgen retorts haughtily that she’s never felt any need to contain her appetites, externally or otherwise – but over the course of her conversation, she clearly develops a degree of sympathy for the pale, twitching once-detective.
[Zachary sought help from Morgen. These two might say more if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]] |After their conversation on containment-in-glass last time, Morgen and Zachary have brought each other exhibits – or gifts. For her, a blued glass mirror that’s always cold to the touch; for him, a glass key that she suggests he crush if things become ‘too much what they are.’
[Morgen seems almost protective of Zachary] |[[Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]] |- | [[Ms Azita Bukhara]] |Morgen teases Azita with references to 'Medusa's Lament', which purports to describe the death of the god-from-stone Seven-Coils at the hands of the Colonel, Azita's patron. |[[Horns & Ivories]] |Azita and Morgen compare their hunts of ‘upright prey.’ Morgen observes disapprovingly that unlike Azita, she never hunts for pleasure. Azita raises her eyebrows and leaves them there until Morgen dissolves into silvery giggles. |[[Horns & Ivories]] |- | [[Princess Coquille Amirejibi]] |Coquille and Morgen are locked in an icy war of compliments. |[[Sights & Sensations]] | | |- |[[Sr. Corso Reverte]] |Corso has read conflicting accounts of traditional means of mixing the sacrament Calicite. He asks Morgen, as an ‘ambassadress of the Grail’, for her opinions. She objects to the characterization – ‘ambassadress of the Witch, perhaps, on a clear night at least’ – but does share her clearly informed opinions. |[[Applebright Euphonies]] |Corso banters with Morgen about the actual composition of her fabled ‘key of black sapphire’, which she insists is metaphorically glass, and which he suggests is a stained glass window ‘somewhere quiet’… |[[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]] |- |[[Mr Peter Agdistis]] |Agdistis and Morgen share news of his friend, and her un-sister, the Ligeian Sulochana (who, it seems, was at one point Morgen's dance-instructor). She is in Georgia now: Agdistis wonders why. 'Medea,' Morgen says, but she teasingly refuses to be drawn on what that might mean. |[[Serpents & Venoms]] |Morgen and Agdistis discuss the folk-songs of Umbria and their connection to the Twins. It transpires that they both met Christopher Illopoly during his year in Italy as a young man. Morgen wonders where he might be, and Agdistis blurts out impulsively: 'Stay away from him!' He immediately blanches at his own boldness, but Morgen seems entertained. |[[Strings & Songs]] |- |[[The Coffinmaker|Mr.]] & [[The Midwife|Mrs. Kille]] |Mrs Kille respectfully addresses Morgen as Chaculette – a title that Morgen seems to recognize – and bows her head. Morgen touches a finger to her lips, and then to Mrs Kille’s forehead – perhaps a blessing, perhaps something else. There is a pause, after which Morgen begins a casual account of a recent sea voyage.
[Mrs Kille addressed Morgen as ‘Chaculette’; Morgen responded as if she understood the term. These two might say more if you invite them both back for another Salon.] |[[Sea Stories]] |Once again, Mrs Kille addresses Morgen as ‘Chaculette’, and once again, Morgen kisses her finger and touches Mrs Kille’s forehead. (Mr Kille watches from a careful distance.) They both make small talk for some minutes, until Mrs Kille asks Morgen if she has ever considered ‘Medea’s Path’. A silvery sadness glints in Morgen’s eyes; she says that it is barred to her, and unexpectedly quotes a passage from the ''[https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Rarity:_The_Book_of_Suns,_Reassembled Book of Suns]'' about the commission of sins in twilight… |[[Resurgences & Emergences]] |- |[[The Blacksmith|Denzil Smith]] |Morgen disdains Denzil. He, in his turn, keeps a respectful distance, and can be observed to scratch a sun-cross covertly into the table when she's not looking. |[[Memory: Fear]] |Morgen continues to ignore Denzil, who maintains a safe distance, casting occasional sullen, wary glances in her direction. |[[Memory: Fear]] |- | [[The Rector|Reverend Timothy]] |Reverend Timothy sits next to Morgen and, initially, clearly finds her quite charming. He chatters happily away about his time in Brancrug and at theological college and eventually asks her about her background. He grows increasingly puzzled and when she mentions her 'un-sisters' the penny clearly drops. He moves his chair as far away from her as is politely possible and avoids conversation for the rest of the meal. She smiles and offers to cut up his food for him.
[Reverend Timothy hopes never to find himself in the same room as Mlle Matutine, ever again.] |[[Wolf Stories]] |From the moment Morgen saunters into the room, Timothy stares at her like an arachnophobe confronted with a moseying tarantula. She is clearly aware of it, and ignores him for the first half hour. At this point she turns to fix her gaze on him and abruptly claps her hands: he kicks over his chair, stumbles apologizing in the direction of the toilet, and does not return for some time. |[[Memory: Fear]] |} ==Incidents== Morgen can visit for the following [[Incident]]s: *[[The Affair of 'Apollo and Marsyas']] *[[The Affair of the Claw and the Clouds]] *[[The Affair of the Invisible Opera]] *[[The Affair of the Threshold Revolution]] *[[The Affair of the Unfinished Lark]] == Further Stories == ===== The Affair of the Unfinished Lark ===== After completing [[The Affair of the Unfinished Lark]], Morgen can be spoken with. She reveals that Zuthi has been dealing with someone eavesdropping on Hour-meetings at The Roost. Morgen thinks that it would be a 'lark' to share these rumours in the [['The Mansus'|Mansus]] and will ask for a [[manuscript]] on [[Sky Stories]] [10] for guidance on how to distribute these. Or upon offering her a more suitable book she might be dissuaded... * Offering her [[In The Mountains As Upon The Plain There May Not Be A Path Where None Has Passed]] will have her decide to reveal the secrets and give her the aspects [[Inspired]] and [[Agenda|Agenda: Corrivality]]. * Offering her [[The Book of the White Cat]] will have her decide to hang on to these rumours for a rainy day and give her the aspects [[Inspired]] and [[Agenda: Autarchy]]. ==References== [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]]

Sir David Greene.title: Sir David Greene
Sir David Greene.text:
{{BoH Librarian |image1=[[File:Sir David Greene.png]] |time_as_librarian=1903 - ?}} {{Quote|Sir David Greene, eighth Librarian - a former Nocturnal Branch superintendent, better known for rooting out mysteries than illuminating them.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the eighth [[Previous Librarians|Librarian]] of the Curia of the Isle, "Who served two masters as best he could". Prior to that, he was the superintendent of Nocturnal Branch. His [['Sir David Greene'|Bust]] is cast from reddish granite and located in [[Crucible Tower: Governor's Office]]. ==Time as Librarian== Being a believer of the Second Dawn variety, he financed the magnificent stained windows of the [[Nave of the Abbey Church|Abbey Church]], the original stained glass having been lost after the Abbey's dissolution. He had the [[Map Room]] refurbished at the turn of the 20th century, to plan his explorations and manage the operations of his many agents. He ruporposed the [[Desk: Vagabond]], an elegant relic, for his "small and secret war". Symbols are absent-mindedly carved down one leg of his [[Greene's Red Chair|wobbly red chair]] - from top to bottom: a cup; a winged insect; an axe; a candle. His [[Greene's Practice Sword|practice sword]] is made of varnished wood. Its hilt is charred, as if Greene had held it over a candle-flame. His favourite drink was [[Roscraggan Whisky]]. A [[Typewriter]] is monogrammed "D.G.". He sent a [[Inscribed Clock|gift]] to a favoured retainer, "A.M.F.", apologising "for the mirrors". He wrote a [[Journal of Sir David Greene, 1903|confidential journal in 1903]], in which he details his private disillusionment with Nocturnal Branch, which he increasingly regards as irresponsible, being especially concerned about the construction of a [[Oubliette Containment|'suppressive mechanism']] beneath Brancrug Gaol, and its likely occupant, whom he called 'the Sun's bastard grandchild'. He also details expressions of fevered longings for "A.F", along with financial calculations implying he had been embezzling funds in order to run away with them. Entries cease abruptly before the year's end. [[Category:Authors]] [[Category:Past Librarians]] [[Category:People]]

Nathaniel Darcy-Evers.title: Nathaniel Darcy-Evers
Nathaniel Darcy-Evers.text:
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an author and a book printer, notable for reprinting [[De Horis book 2|De Horis Book II]] and [[De Horis book 3|III]], and writing [[De Ratio Quercuum]].

De Horis discusses the topic of the [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Hours Hours]. [[De Horis book 1|De Horis Book I]] deals with the Hours of the Wood; it is unclear whether or not he reprinted this volume. [[De Horis book 2|De Horis Book II]] and [[De Horis book 3|Book III]] deal with the {{Lore|Edge}} Hours: [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/The_Lionsmith the Lionsmith] and [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/The_Colonel the Colonel] respectively.

De Ratio Quercuum touches on the subject of trees - specifically, their occult properties as used by the Great King of Pontus. 

All three of his books are in Latin, meaning he can understand the language. As the De Horis reprints are from the 19th century, it is reasonable to assume he was active during that period. Additionally, he must also have been familiar with the Hours discussed in De Horis.
[[Category:People]]
[[Category:Authors]]

Robert Fludd.title: Robert Fludd

Professor Rowena Hengerst.text:
{{BoH Character |name=Professor
Rowena Hengerst |image=Professor Rowena Hengerst.png |principle1={{Lore|Grail}} |principle2={{Lore|Winter}} |aspects=[[Visitor]] |languages=[[Greek]], [[Henavek]], [[Phrygian]] |fee=[[Tally|Iron Spintria]]}} {{Quote|For many years, under many names, Rowena has done, learnt, or eaten many things she really shouldn't have. But for many years, under many names, she's served as the protectress of Hush House.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a potential [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]] with interests in {{Lore|Grail}} and {{Lore|Winter}}. She can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Henavek]]. She is an Alukite[https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/Crime_of_the_Sky#Alukites Secret Histories Wiki, Alukites] and a Ligeian[https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/The_Ligeia_Club Secret Histories Wiki, The Ligeia Club], wolf-wife, and holder of the Mare's Key of worm-stone, called sea-opener[https://book-of-hours.fandom.com/wiki/Sea_Stories#Wisdom_Attunement Sea Stories], which opens the door to Nowhere[https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/Nowhere Secret Histories Wiki, Nowhere]. ==Incidents== Rowena can visit for the following [[Incident]]s during [[Numa]]: *[[A Matter of the Feasting Few]] *[[A Matter of Knot and Tangle]] *[[A Matter of the Sanctuary Draught]] *[[A Matter of the Softer Frost]] ==Rowena's Burden== {{BoH Character |name=Rowena's Burden |aspects=[[Lighthouse Institute#Positions|Secretary Persistent]], [[Agenda: Secrecy]], [[Inspired]], [[Fear: Ys]]}} {{Quote|Rowena, caught between moon and tide, blood and gold, Ys and the Marches, has long embraced her punishment. She will serve as protectress still, even while her appetites fade and the sea takes what's left of her, wave by lapping wave. Until she is gone, the Mare's Key remains her burden, hers alone.}}
In the ''[[House of Light]]'' DLC, '''Rowena's Burden''' is a default [[Lighthouse Institute#Positions|Secretary Persistent]], as she was during the [[Curia Period|Curia]], but it's possible to choose [[Echidna]] or [[Mlle Margot Matutine|Morgen]] instead. ==References== [[Category:People]] [[Category:Visitor]]

Solomon Husher.title: Solomon Husher
Solomon Husher.text:
{{BoH Librarian |image1=[[File:'Solomon Husher'.png]] |title1=Solomon Husher
Third Librarian |time_as_librarian=1818-1838 |death=Disappeared in 1838}} {{Quote|The Very Reverend Solomon Husher, third Librarian of Hush House. 'Nothing is a place. Everything ends.'}}
'''Solomon Husher''' was the third [[Previous Librarians|Librarian]] of [[Hush House]], "Whereof we cannot speak, thereof we must remain silent". His [['Solomon Husher'|Bust]] can be found in the [[Long Tower: Solomon's Study]]. ==Description== In 1818, the Very Reverend Solomon Husher became third Librarian of the Curia of the Isle. He brought ''[['The Foundation of the Sun']]'' with him and took a room in the [[Long Tower: Solomon's Quarters|Long Tower as his quarters]], widely regarded as the chilliest in the House. His tastes were spartan. He often used [[Blue Crown]] in his [[Solomon’s Preparation|Preparation]] and would take a dose of it before going to sleep every night, to close his ears to the sound of the waves. He commissioned [[Desk: Pale|the desk in his quarters]] from Lockwood Fen bog-yew, blackened and half-fossilised by centuries underwater, on which he wrote his doomy allegory of Winter and its romance with the sun, called ''[[On the White]]''. He wrote, perhaps allegorically, "of Winter, and its long slow doomed romance with the Sun". The epigraph is “Sunset at Noon”. It seems to be a theory of aesthetics, or perhaps a set of warnings about the dangers of painting. Husher writes distractedly about his suspicion of colours and his yearning for death. He hints at a Great Work he has envisaged, or begun, where the 'palest of paintings' will enthral the world. He returns again and again to certain compelling phrases which he claims are the 'secret words of Winter'. It is said that when he blotted the last word on his manuscript and rose from his work, the timber of his desk had turned pale as fresh-cut maple. [[Fraser Strathcoyne]] gifted him a nice set of silver candlesticks. Husher was never one for music and disliked the way the notes of the [[Instrument: Piano|piano]] in the [[Servants' Hall]] would drift up the stairs to the [[Reading Room]], and forbade the staff to play it before sunset. Some time in the mid 1830s, he spilt his tea on his [[Moon Footstool|footstool]] when he heard that [[Julian Coseley]] had apologised. Solomon Husher believed in the 'paradox of the eternal ending', a means in which perfection might be reconciled with freedom. Julian Coseley regarded him as a charlatan, but three paintings in 1895 by Nina Lagasse (or Ninegala of Lagash) before her death convinced him to change his mind. He disappeared on January 9th, 1838, after a heavy snow fell on Hush House. A resignation letter was discovered in his room. Husher was never seen again, but every year on the same day, his footprints can be found beneath the [[The Earl's Yew|Yew Tree]]. Quotes attributed to him: *"The White is west of the world, and winter does not wait forever." *"Nothing is a place. Everything ends." *"Death alters; Snow endures." *"Speech is a wound." *"Winter does not wait forever; though Janus might." [[Category:People]] [[Category:Past Librarians]]

Natalia Brulleau.title: Natalia Brulleau
Natalia Brulleau.text:
{{BoH Librarian |title1=Natalia Brulleau
Fifth Librarian |image1=[[File:'Natalia Brulleau'.png]] |time_as_librarian=? - 1861}} {{Quote|'Natalia Brulleau, fifth Librarian- duellist, mystic, traveller.'}}
'''Natalia Brulleau''' was the fifth [[Previous Librarians|Librarian]] of the Curia of the Isle, "Who was denied victory, though never defeated". She came from a family of painters. Her [['Natalia Brulleau'|Bust]] is cast in iron. ==Time as Librarian== A dyad of eternally duelling Edge-long agreed to stay at [[Hush House]] for a year and a day to allow Natalia to study them, if she satisfied certain conditions. A [[Duelling Hall|properly equipped space]] was one of those conditions. Ultimately, that turned out to be a trap or trick played by one or both of the dyad, and they left after only a single battle. Their names are recorded as "Mistress Dearday" and "Father Torgue". Brulleau hoped to lure them to Hush House, either to learn from them or to imprison them. Her practice sword is made of dark ash. It has seen considerable use, and is notched, battered and more than fifty years old. Inspired by Mistress Dearday - one half of the notorious Edge dyad, she developed the [[Dearday Lens]], a simple device, which is useful for starting fires and inciting headaches, among other things. She learnt the powerful, if unpleasant, technique [[Torgue's Cleansing]] from the priest and Edge-long, Reverend Torgue. Natalia Brulleau established a tradition that the [[Inscribed Stone]] should always remain in the [[Librarian's Quarters]], to inspire her, and her successors, with humility and to illustrate the limits of knowledge. She wrote ''[[Seven Shards]]'', which is a [[Readable|Book]] about The Lionsmith breaking his sword into seven shards, describing the nature of each of those shards, allegorically and otherwise. In the 1850s, and in deep secrecy, she built the [[Night Gallery]] into the foundations of the Gullscry Tower. Natalia Brulleau retired in 1861. Painting under her family name include: *''[[The Chiliarch's Victory]]'' - A blurred, menacing depiction of a vast, flabby carcass the colour of dirty sulphur, patched with brighter yellow. The environment is a chilly desert beneath a low red sun. On closer inspection, the brighter patches seem to be golden blood, seeping from vast wounds. It's signed "Brulleau, 1861". *''[['Raveline Summer']]'' - A dry spell in a still place. It's signed "Brulleau", but dated 1902. Quotes attributed to her: *"Break a window. What have you made? A way? A new light? A weapon?" *"A general says: when I make the right choice, I win. [[Illumination|An Illuminate]] says: when I win, I determine which choice was the right one." == Notes == * Her occult studies imply that she was an Illuminate. * Her name and the origin from the family of painters may indicate her as a relative of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Bryullov Karl Bryullov], Russian Romantic painter. [[Category:Authors]] [[Category:People]] [[Category:Past Librarians]]

Mrs E.title: Mrs E
Mrs E.text:
{{BoH Character |name={{PAGENAME}} |image=[[File:Echidna.png]] |aspects=[[Visitor]], [[Unsociable]] |languages=[[Greek]], [[Hyksos]]}} {{quote|The self-styled Mother of Monsters. A cheery, tubby woman in a green-grey garment like a baggy dirndl.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''', also known as '''Echidna''', is a summonable [[Visitor]] to [[Hush House]]. She is a Ligeian and a potential Secretary Persistent for the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. She can be paid an [[Tally|Iron Spintria]] to teach the Librarian [[Hyksos]]. If the Librarian feeds Moore, Chaima, or Bukhara to Echidna during the Further Story for [[The Affair of the Second Skin]], she will gain the [[Agenda]]s: Corrivality, Secrecy, and Stone Consumed. If she is not fed, she will not gain these aspects and cannot be appointed to the [[Lighthouse Institute]]. ==Summoning Echidna== {{quote|I pour the milk in a wide circle, and watch as it sinks into the scabbed earth. Serpent-eyes glint from the gorse. The wind rises to a hissing shriek. Rain rattles from the sky. I have attracted someone's attention.|Invite Echidna, Mother of Monsters, to Brancrug}} Echidna can be summoned after learning about her "prowlings" with a unique lesson in the further story for [[The Affair of the Second Skin]], if the Librarian consults [[Lt Arthur Thomas Moore (Ret.)]], [[Lalla Chaima]] or [[Ms Azita Bukhara]]. The lesson can be applied to any existing [[Skills|skill]] (it is recommended to use a {{Lore|Scale}} skill), and the skill can then be used along with [[Serpent-Milk]] and 7 {{Lore|Scale}} to summon Mrs E on [[A Walk on the Moor|the Moor]]. == Notes == * Mrs E will work with the Lighthouse Institute which has Foe: Devourers although she is the Devourer herself. It will provide certain texts to the founder's tabs of the Institute [[Endings|Ending]] including Mrs E's tab. Teresa Galmier.title: Teresa Galmier
Teresa Galmier.text:
{{BoH Character |name=Teresa Galmier |image=[[File:Teresa Galmier.png]] |aka=The Baldomerian |knownfor=Writing the ''Locksmith's Dream'' series |relationships=[[Christopher Illopoly]]
(romantic relationship)}} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a {{Lore|Lantern}}-Long and author best known for her ''Locksmith's Dream'' series. ==Life== Little is known of Galmier's personal life. At least ten years prior to [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Cultist_Simulator_Wiki ''Cultist Simulator''], which takes place in the 1920s, she and [[Christopher Illopoly]] met and (presumably) bonded over their shared interest in occultism and the Mansus; their works both focus heavily on reaching different parts of the Mansus. Illopoly refers to Galmier as 'Baldomera' in [[Travelling at Night, vol 3]], a reference to Saint Baldomerus, patron saint of locksmiths[https://twitter.com/alexiskennedy/status/1027514233783808001 Alexis Kennedy, Tweet, August 9 2018.]. It is implied that the romance between the two ended because Galmier wished to ascend to Longhood[https://uadaf.theevilroot.xyz/frangiclave/deck/mansus_whitedoor1 ''Cultist Simulator'': Lodge of the Sage Knight]. In [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Cultist_Simulator_Wiki ''Cultist Simulator''], Galmier is often encountered at [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Way:_The_White_Door#Lodge_of_the_Sage_Knight the Lodge of the Sage Knight] through the White Door. It is never explicitly stated which Hour she serves, but it is most likely the Watchman, given her status as a {{Lore|Lantern}}-Long and lack of shadow[https://uadaf.theevilroot.xyz/frangiclave/recipe/summon_spirit_lanterne_secret/ ''Cultist Simulator'': Summon the mysterious Name known as the Baldomerian]. Galmier plays a role in the [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Legacies#Apostle_Entheate Apostle Entheate] ascension in ''Cultist Simulator'', introducing the player character to Kleidouchos, a member of the Ligeia Club and holder of the Key of Days[https://uadaf.theevilroot.xyz/frangiclave/recipe/apostlelantern.recruitkleidouchos.teresa/ ''Cultist Simulator'': Ask Teresa about the Dream of the Key]. At some point, [[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller]] 'managed Galmier's reincorporation'[https://uadaf.theevilroot.xyz/rowenarium/recipe/talk.visitor.incident.success.stanislav.rite.renewal.nectar ''Book of Hours'': On the Friar's Tapestry], meaning that she may have a physical form at the time of ''Book of Hours'', although she does not make an appearance. ==Works== Galmier has written five novels, although the description for the fifth ''Locksmith's Dream'' insists that the volume was 'never published nor, apparently, even written'. *[[The Locksmith's Dream: a Light through the Keyhole]] *[[The Locksmith's Dream: Portions and Proportions]] *[[The Locksmith's Dream: Trespasses]] *[[The Locksmith's Dream: Stolen Reflections]] *[[The Locksmith's Dream: Incursus]] ==References== [[Category:Authors]] [[Category:People]]

Nyn.title: Nyn
Nyn.text:
{{BoH Character
|name=Nyn
|image=[[File:Travelling_At_Night_Promo_Art.png]]}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an actress, author, a painter, and a witch. 

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' has gone by other names including 
* Nina Lagasse<ref name="a-comedy-of-the-sun">https://weatherfactory.biz/a-comedy-of-the-sun/</ref> 
* Ninegala of Lagash - confirmed by the text for the The Lights Along The Way [[Endings|Ending]]

== Life ==

It is uncertain when she was born and how old she is, but given one of the names she went by was Ninegala of Lagash, she is likely quite old, being associated with the city-state of Lagash<ref name="lagash">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagash</ref>.

Given that that the oldest known work dated to her is from the [[Dawn Period]], we know she is contemporaneous with that period.

This is also the oldest known name she is associated with, and may be her first given name.

At some point she became a [[w:c:secret-histories:Long|Long]], possibly under the [[w:c:secret-histories:The_Sun-in-Splendor|The Sun-in-Splendor]], though she ended up under the auspices of [[w:c:secret-histories:The_Sun-in-Rags|The Sun-in-Rags]] <ref name="a-comedy-of-the-sun">https://weatherfactory.biz/a-comedy-of-the-sun/</ref>.

During the [[Solar Gothic Period]], she had a pupil, Mabelie of Bruges, and wrote [[Nyn's Cages (Avignon Text)]].

According to her, she was present at the [[w:c:secret-histories:Intercalate|Sun’s Division]].

She at some point became friends with [[Julian Coseley]], and knew [[Solomon Husher]], and as of 1894 all were [[w:c:secret-histories:Long|Long]] under the [[w:c:secret-histories:The_Sun-in-Rags|The Sun-in-Rags]].<ref name="a-comedy-of-the-sun">https://weatherfactory.biz/a-comedy-of-the-sun/</ref> 

Her appointed death as a {{Lore|Winter}}-Long was on February 9th, 1895, but as she will still be around in Travelling at Night, she may have found a way to evade it.<ref name="a-comedy-of-the-sun">https://weatherfactory.biz/a-comedy-of-the-sun/</ref>

==Works==
She has written four [[Readable|books]]:
* ''[[In The Mountains As Upon The Plain There May Not Be A Path Where None Has Passed]]''
* Nyn's Cages
** ''[[Nyn's Cages (Avignon Text)]]''
** ''[[Nyn's Cages (Bruges Text, Illuminated)]]''
* ''[[Observations on the Peacock Door]]''
* ''[[The Scar in the Sky]]''

She has also painted numerous [[Wall Art|paintings]]:
*''[['A Bargain']]''
*''[[Caer Ys]]''
*''[['Glory's Gift']]''
*''[['Gods Return']]''
*''[['Self-Born']]''
*''[['The Foundlings']]''
*''[['The First Answer']]''
*''[['The First Birth']]''
*''[['The First End']]''
*''[['The First Threshold']]''
*''[['The Hatching']]''
*''[['The Wheel Still Turns']]''
The following paintings only exist within the game's files:
*''[['Supplication']]''
*''[['The Bridge at Ortucchio']]''

According to the [[Consider]] description of [[Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic: Second Edition]], she painted three more paintings before her death to convince [[Julian Coseley]] to believe in the 'paradox of the eternal ending'.

Thanks to a letter she wrote to [[Julian Coseley]], we know the intended names of these paintings<ref name="a-comedy-of-the-sun">https://weatherfactory.biz/a-comedy-of-the-sun/</ref>

* 'Abydos Uncrowned'
* 'Nix Abolix'
* 'Sunset Celia and the Unleashed Flame'

== Trivia ==
*''[[The Scar in the Sky]]'' can be found in ''Cultist Simulator'' with the exact same descriptions.
*Lagash was an ancient city-state in Mesopotamia, and Nina was an ancient site marking its southern limits.<ref name="lagash">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagash</ref>

Twrog of Meirionnydd.title: Twrog of Meirionnydd
Twrog of Meirionnydd.text:
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' authored at least one book, is known to be an {{Lore|Edge}}-Long dyad with Dyddgu<ref>https://book-of-hours.fandom.com/wiki/Cudgels:_Dyddgu_and_St_Twrog</ref>, has visited the [[Hush House]], and is speculated to have killed [[Musgrave Dewulf]] in a pistol duel.

== Life ==

Twrog was known to be active during the [[Baronial Period]] due to the one known work he wrote - [[Sunrise Awakenings]] - being dated to that period.

He is known to have visited the [[Hush House]] multiple times.

Due to [[Sunrise Awakenings]] being in English, we know he is fluent in that language. 

== Works ==
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is known to have written one book.

* ''[[Sunrise Awakenings]]''

== Speculation ==

===Duel with Musgrave Dewulf===

Due to the consider description of [[Matched Flintlock Pistols]], we know there is a story that [[Musgrave Dewulf]] died in a pistol duel with a 'Welsh visitor'. Twrog is known to have be active during the [[Baronial Period]] and to have visited the [[Hush House]] in 'search of some sort of fight.' <ref>https://book-of-hours.fandom.com/wiki/Sunrise_Awakenings</ref>. Meirionnydd is region in Wales <ref>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meirionnydd</ref>, so presumably at least at this time {{PAGENAME}} was associated with that area.

===Possible Hour-Patron===

The one known book that Twrog has written - [[Sunrise Awakenings]] - is associated with the {{Lore|Lantern}} principle, so it possible that Twrog ascended under the one known {{Lore|Edge}} Hour associated with that aspect - [[w:c:secret-histories:The_Colonel|The Colonel]] 

===Out of Game Connections===

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' may be associated with the 6th-century Welsh saint Twrog<ref>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twrog</ref>. 

There are legends of '''{{PAGENAME}}''' under that exact name that are notably {{Lore|Edge}}-dyad like in nature <ref>https://heavyangloorthodox.blogspot.com/2019/06/venerable-twrog-of-merioneth.html</ref>

Omar, the Blaze.title: Omar, the Blaze
Omar, the Blaze.text:
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an author of several books, and was a member of the Labyrinth of Lions, which, like the [[Hush House]], is a library of the [[w:c:secret-histories:Watchman's_Tree#Labyrinth_of_Lions|Watchman's Tree]]

== Life ==

The books he wrote all are classified in the [[Dawn Period]], so he was active during that time.

He joined the Labyrinth of Lions before writing any of his books. 

Early in his work there, he wrote [[The Lion and the Glass]] while mastering the "Illumination techniques that rely on the 'Truths of Glass'" - which may refer to the same lessons we get from mastering the book - [[Glaziery & Lightsmithing]]

Later on, while he was working on constructing mirrors for the enclosure of a sacred flame, he realised a "Flaw in the Glass" - described in [[Each Flame His Fuel]]. In this same book, he expresses concern over [[w:c:secret-histories:The_Chandler|the Chandler]].

At some point, he was at fault for the "extinguishing of a sacred flame", possibly related to the "Flaw in the Glass" he previously realised.

He then spent seven years in Tyre manning a lighthouse to atone for this, and also wrote [[The Focus of Amber]]. 

During his time manning the lighthouse, he became so terrified of fire "he could not stand to share a room with a candle", possibly due to it's connection to [[w:c:secret-histories:The_Chandler|the Chandler]].

As all the known books he has written are in [[Deep Mandaic]], he knows that language.

== Works ==
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is known to have written three books.

* ''[[The Lion and the Glass]]''
* ''[[Each Flame His Fuel]]''
* ''[[The Focus of Amber]]''

Penelope of Gordion.title: Penelope of Gordion
Penelope of Gordion.text:
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' authored at least one book, and is purported to have listened to the aviform-[[w:c:secret-histories:Hour|Hours]] meeting at [[w:c:secret-histories:Roost|The Roost]] via a proxy of her blind white cat.

== Life ==

Given the epithet - ''of Gordion'' - in her name presumably she is from the historical city Gordion<ref name="gordion">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordion</ref>, which was the capital city of Phygria<ref>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phrygia</ref>. Notably, her one known book is written in [[Phrygian]], so it is known she both spoke that language, and it is possible the name of that language was inspired by the name of that real-life kingdom.

In [[The Dream of the Conspiracy of the Lower Skies]], it mentions that [[Damaon Azenaten]] sifted through 'the tall tales of {{PAGENAME}}', so it is possible that {{PAGENAME}} exaggerated in her writings.

Both the period of [[The Book of the White Cat]] - the [[Dawn Period]], and the suspected use dates of Gordion<ref name="gordion">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordion</ref> imply she was active during the [[Dawn Period]]

== Works ==

* ''[[The Book of the White Cat]]''
