Natan of Regensburg.title: Natan of Regensburg
Natan of Regensburg.text:
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was an author, a physician, and was Jewish.

His sons and grandsons were also named Natan, but this page refers to the Natan who originally moved that line to shelter in the [[Hush House]] after his exile.

== Life ==

Given his title, he is from Regensburg, which is located in modern day Germany. 

According to the description of the [[Motley Tower: Regensburg Room]], he was alive during the fifteenth century.

At some point during his life he learned about the healing arts, one application of that learning how to create the [[Regensburg Balm]]. 

According to the description of the [[Regensburg Balm]], he was at some point exiled from Regensburg. 

He eventually traveled to England, and the [[Hush House]], where [[Abbot Geffrey]] convinced the brothers to give {{PAGENAME}} and his family shelter. 

The Motley Tower (then called the Barber's Tower) was constructed for {{PAGENAME}} and his family, though it later housed others including [[Christopher Illopoly]].

He made expansions to the [[Physic Garden]], and eventually was trusted enough to visit [[Earl Brian's Field]], where he healed a bird's wing and was given 'treasures of history and music'

Some items in the [[Hush House]] related to him are the [[Regensburg Menorah]] and [[Desk: Natan]] - though it seems likely that the Natan in this case may be one of his offspring.

== Works ==
He has written one [[Readable|book]]:
* ''[[Warming Draughts to Uplift the Heart]]

== Trivia ==
* Regensburg is a real location in modern-day Germany<ref>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regensburg</ref>. It has changed hands multiple times, possibly resulting in the exile of Natan.

Soham.title: Soham
Soham.text:
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an author, ecstatic, and a sage.

== Life ==

He is purported to have discoursed with [[w:c:cultistsimulator:The_Beachcomber|the Beachcrow]] in person. It is possible that some of his knowledge including the topics discussed in [[The Origins of Hours]] was shared with him by that [[w:c:cultistsimulator:Hour|Hour]], who is a notorious hoarder of secrets.

His work shares some similarities with that of [[Shohei]], in particular [[Five Creations]] discusses the possible origins of humanity with a figure later claimed to be the Beachcrow, while [[The Origins of Hours]] discusses where the Hours might have come from. These authors seem to both be discussing [[Determination]]s

His one known work is in [[Vak]], so he knew that language.

His one known work is from the [[Dawn Period]], so he was likely active during that period.

* ''[[The Origins of Hours]]''

Valentine Dewulf.title: Valentine Dewulf
Valentine Dewulf.text:
{{Individual infobox |name=Valentine Dewulf,
6th Baron Brancrug |image1=[[File:'Valentine Dewulf'.png]] |family=*[[Dewulf Family]] **[[Gideon Dewulf]] (father) **[[Eales Dewulf]] (son) **[[Eva Dewulf]] (daughter) }} {{quote|Long have the two birds pursued my blood, yet one is no Crow, yet it is darker. Long has the Wolf rolled itself in gold like a clovered cow, until its slobberings stain our thoughts…|Valentine Dewulf}} __NOTOC__
'''Valentine Dewulf''' was the sixth [[Baron of Brancrug]], "Who knew cages". During his time as Baron he was known to have lead an eccentric life. ==Biography== ===Early Life=== Valentine was born to the Dewulf family some time in the 17th Century. He was the son and heir apparent of [[Gideon Dewulf]], and when Gideon died he inherited the Barony. ===Life as Baron=== Valentine was known to live an eccentric yet melancholic life as Baron, at various times engaging in matters of falconry, veterinary, heraldry, painting, and politics. He had an interest in the religions of the New World. He also wrote several dream-journals about the nowhere-hours and invisible arts. Towards the end of his life he began to increasingly take meals in the [[Gullscry Loggia]], where he could be surrounded by his beloved birds. ===Death, Succession, and Legacy=== [[Eva Dewulf]] was born to Valentine Dewulf and an unknown mother in 1702. At some point a son, [[Eales Dewulf|Eales]], was born to Valentine. In 1721 Valentine fell from the top of Gullscry Tower, possibly a suicide as a result of his melancholia. There were no witnesses to his death and his body wasn't found for three days. As his son was incapable of taking up the responsibilities of Baron, his daughter instead inherited the Barony. As was tradition for the Barons of Brancrug, there was a [['Valentine Dewulf'|Bust]] in his likeness set in a niche along the [[Grand Ascent - Ground Floor|Grand Ascent staircase]]. ==Works== ===Written Works=== *''[[A True History of Valentine Dewulf]]'' - An autobiographical account of his life. *''[[Black Nephrite]]'' - One of Valentine's Dream Journals. *''[[The Republic of Teeth]]'' - An extensive political treatise. ===Paintings=== * ''[['Chac']]'' - A painting of a Valentine's [[Magnificent Green Cockatoo]]. Found in the [[Night Gallery]] and [[Gullscry Tower: Valentine's Room]]. * ''[['Departure']]'' - A painting of gulls migrating, found in the [[Fludd Gallery]] and Gullscry Tower: Valentine's Room. * ''[['The Watcher']]'' - A painting of a barn owl Valentine nursed back to health, found in [[Gullscry Tower: Eales' Room]]. [[Category:Authors]] [[Category:Barons Brancrug]] [[Category:Dewulf Family]] [[Category:People]]

Willem Harries.title: Willem Harries
Willem Harries.text:
{{BoH Librarian |title1=Willem Harries
Sixth Librarian |image1=[[File:'Willem Harries'.png]] |time_as_librarian= ~1861 - ?}} {{quote|Willem Harries, sixth Librarian, priest and nyctodromist, whose end has always remained obscure.}}
'''Willem Harries''', sixth [[Previous Librarians|Librarian]] of the Curia of the Isle, "Who brought a key long lost". He was a priest and [[Nyctodromy|nyctodromist]]. His [['Willem Harries'|Bust]] can be found in the [[Solarium]]. ==Description== After Brulleau's retirement in 1861, the Curia found itself short of promising candidates, until the arrival of Willem Harries, a former Dutch Lutheran priest and a sometime correspondent of [[Fr. Stanislav John Schaller|Stanislav Schaller]]. He had been a missionary in the Dutch East Indies until his faith was lost or transmuted into a devotion to St Agnes of the Gate, and he was drawn to [[Hush House]]. He won his position by presenting the Curia with a "key long lost", sometime in the 1860s. That was the key to the [[Hidden Stair]], but only the naive would assume the key was a tangible object. Willem Harries took residence in the [[Violet Chamber]] and established a little shrine to St Agnes in the far corner, where it remained for many years until [[Gervinus van Lauren]] ordered it to be removed. Harries was skilled at opening ways, as much as his successor, van Lauren, was at closing them. There are two Serpent-Styled Glasses, belonging to each of them, “in earnest of their wager”. Harries wrote a book, called ''[[An Almanac of Entrances]]'', which is a handbook of sealed and unsealed byways and shortcuts through the Bounds, which was compiled in the 1860s. His end remains obscure. Quotes attributed to him: *"The lock seeks its key, the wall seeks its door, and we who would pass learn at last that they are not our servants." *"Who will see the Second Dawn?" [[Category:People]] [[Category:Past Librarians]]

Villagers.title: Villagers
Villagers.text: Some of the '''Villagers''' in [[Brancrug Village]] can be interacted with. [[The Beginning|In the Beginning]], the Librarian will recieve [[An Old Friend's Address]], which will lead them to one of the villagers; which one depends on the second [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]] chosen: *Selecting {{Soul|Ereb}} will provide the address of [[The Midwife]], Mrs Kille. *Selecting {{Soul|Mettle}} will provide the address of [[The Blacksmith]], Denzil Smith. *Selecting {{Soul|Phost}} will provide the address of [[The Rector]], Reverend Timothy MacDonald. *Selecting {{Soul|Wist}} will provide the address of [[The Coffinmaker]], Mr Kille. It is worth noting that having the Address for either Mr or Mrs Kille will allow the Librarian to hire either of them for free. Each villager can be hired as [[Assistance]] for the day, if a [[Elements of the Soul|Soul Card]] with the right [[Principles|Principle]] is used: *The Midwife requires {{Lore|Grail}}, meaning that {{Soul|Chor}} or {{Soul|Ereb}} can be used. *The Blacksmith requires {{Lore|Edge}}, {{Lore|Forge}} or {{Lore|Heart}}, meaning that {{Soul|Chor}}, {{Soul|Ereb}}, {{Soul|Health}}, {{Soul|Mettle}} or {{Soul|Shapt}} can be used. *The Rector requires {{Lore|Knock}} or {{Lore|Lantern}}, meaning that {{Soul|Phost}}, {{Soul|Shapt}} or {{Soul|Wist}} can be used. *The Coffinmaker requires {{Lore|Winter}}, meaning that only {{Soul|Wist}} can be used. [[Category:People]] [[Category:People]]

Visitors.title: Visitors
Visitors.text:
[[File:Visitor icon.png|right]] {{Tocright}} {{Quote|The primary route by which books enter and leave the library. The arrival of a visitor may be cause for a variety of emotions.}}
'''Visitors''' will arrive at [[Hush House]] periodically, either regarding [[Incident]]s, or for a general consultation. If Visitors arrive during a regular [[Season]], they will stay for a full day (six minutes). Their stay can be further extended by three minutes, by placing them in a [[Workstations#Beds|Bed]] which matches their interest. This can be done multiple times. Visitors who arrive during [[Numa]] will stay for only two minutes and their stay cannot be extended. Visitors will be interested in one or two [[Principles]]. Their interest starts at three (or seven for Numatic Visitors), which can be satisfied by presenting a [[Readable]] with an equal or greater amount of mystery. It will increase by one with each successful consultation, and each Readable can only be consulted once by each Visitor. If the item presented fits these requirements, The Librarian receives an [[Tally#Denominations|Iron Spintria]] for a general consultation, a Bronze Spintria if it's related to an ongoing Incident, or a Silver Spintria for a Numatic Incident. Visitors will only accept a Readable written in a Language which they can understand. If the Librarian is interested in learning a [[Skills#Languages|Language]] that the current Visitor can speak, they can offer the visitor monetary incentive to share that knowledge in the form of an Iron Spintria. If this option is chosen, the Visitor cannot be given a consultation and will depart. With ''[[House of Light]]'', when the Librarian completes their first consultation for any non-Numatic Visitor, that Visitor will leave their card. This can be used at a [[Desks|Desk]] with the [[Writing-Case]] to note the Visitor's address, allowing the Librarian to summon them back to Hush House at any time (other than Numa, when the [[Post Office]] is closed) for [[Salon]]s, further general consultations, or to learn Languages. Noting a Visitor's address using their card provides an [[Occult Scrap]]. There is no limit to the number of addresses that can be noted. In order to summon a Visitor, the Librarian must write [[An Invitation]] at a Desk, using the Writing-Case in the 'Papers' slot and an [[Ink]] (except for [[Perinculate]], which cannot be used for Invitations, most likely because it is deadly poisonous) in the 'With' slot. Each Visitor has specific requirements for their invitation, which can be viewed by examining the Aspects on the Writing-Case. Note that unlike general crafting, while [[Elements of the Soul]] can help with providing sufficient Aspects to pen an invitation, they are not required. Once written, an invitation will persist in the Librarian's 'Sundries' inventory until mailed at the Post Office for one [[Pence|penny]]. Once the invitation has been sent, the Visitor will arrive at Hush House after sixty-five seconds. ==List of Visitors== ===Regular=== Language key:

Elements of the Soul.text:
[[File:Element of the Soul.png|right]] {{Tocright}} {{Quote|The human soul is composed of nine elements, and this is one. Most other things have simpler souls. [Each Soul card can be used once a day, for the kind of things you do with your soul. That usually means 'talking to people' or 'crafting'.]}}
There are nine '''Elements of the Soul''': {| class="sortable article-table" !Element !Principles !Description |- |{{ES|Chor}} |{{Lore|Heart|2}}, {{Lore|Grail|1}} |Exuberance, instinct, rhythm. |- |{{ES|Ereb}} |{{Lore|Grail|2}}, {{Lore|Edge|1}} |Pride, compassion, hatred and fear. |- |{{ES|Fet}} |{{Lore|Rose|2}}, {{Lore|Moth|1}} |That part of us which walks in dreams. |- |{{ES|Health}} |{{Lore|Heart|1}}, {{Lore|Nectar|1}}, {{Lore|Scale|1}} |The dwelling-place of the soul. |- |{{ES|Mettle}} |{{Lore|Forge|2}}, {{Lore|Edge|1}} |Will; self-discipline; that part of us which makes the right choice. |- |{{ES|Phost}} |{{Lore|Lantern|2}}, {{Lore|Sky|1}} |Sight, perception, inspiration, all of the glory's gifts. |- |{{ES|Shapt}} |{{Lore|Knock|2}}, {{Lore|Forge|1}} |Eloquence and understanding; the door opens both ways. |- |{{ES|Trist}} |{{Lore|Moth|2}}, {{Lore|Moon|1}} |The change and the longing. |- |{{ES|Wist}} |{{Lore|Winter|2}}, {{Lore|Lantern|1}} |Name, memory, that part which remains. |}
At [[The Beginning|the Beginning]], the player starts with one [[Health]] and makes a choice between [[Chor]], [[Shapt]], or [[Fet]], and [[Mettle]], [[Phost]], [[Ereb]], or [[Wist]] ([[Trist]] needs to be acquired later). The elements chosen will determine which [[Librarians|Librarian]] you are and [[Journals|Journal]] you have. The latter decision also decides who your starting [[People|acquaintance]] is. They can also be used as an [[Opportunity]] - there's a 38% chance to be selected as an Opportunity when failing to meet the requirement for mastering a [[Readable]]. == Tree of Wisdom == To gain new Elements of the Soul, the Librarian must commit a skill to the [[The Tree of Wisdoms|Tree of Wisdom]]. The element gained depends on the [[Skills|Skill]] and the [[Wisdoms|Wisdom]]. See the [[Skills]] page for more info. == Evolution == Elements of the Soul can be upgraded to stronger variants. To do this you need to have two of the same Element, a [[Skill]] card attuned to that element through [[The Tree of Wisdoms]], and a [[Workstations|workstation]] that has the same [[Wisdoms|Wisdom]] as the [[Skill]] was attuned to. If all of those conditions are met, you can combine two Elements of the Soul into one higher Element (as denoted by a "+" sign in front of its name). Each [[Skill]] can only be used once for evolving an Element. Evolved Elements can be evolved further by combining two of the same evolved Elements with a different [[Skill]]. The resulting Element will have a number of plus signs ("+") in front of its name. For example: with 2 [[Phost]] cards and a skill card with the aspects: [[Attuned|Attuned:Phost]] and [[Horomachistry]], you are able to obtain a [[Phost]]+ card. Repeating this process, you can obtain a [[Phost]]++ card with 2 [[Phost]]+ cards. Additionally, there are certain memories, such as [[Curious Hunch]] or [[Wormwood Dream]] that have [[Wisdoms]] Aspects - with these you can evolve an element at any workstation, so long as it takes the relevant principles. [[Memories that can evolve Elements of the Soul|Here]] is a list of all memories that can evolve elements of the soul. The [[Principles]] per level of evolution are as follows: * Starting Element = 2 for primary principle & 1 secondary principle. e.g. [[Phost]] = {{Lore|Lantern|2}}, {{Lore|Sky|1}} * + level Element = 3 for primary principle & 2 secondary principle. * ++ level Element = 4 for primary principle & 3 secondary principle. * +++ level Element = 5 for primary principle & 4 secondary principle. The exception to this rule is [[Health]] which upgrades as follows: * Starting element = {{Lore|Heart|1}}, {{Lore|Nectar|1}}, {{Lore|Scale|1}} * + level Element = {{Lore|Heart|2}}, {{Lore|Nectar|2}}, {{Lore|Scale|1}} * ++ level Element = {{Lore|Heart|3}}, {{Lore|Nectar|3}}, {{Lore|Scale|2}} * +++ level Element = {{Lore|Heart|4}}, {{Lore|Nectar|4}}, {{Lore|Scale|3}} Fourth level (aka the +++ version) is the highest level an element can go up to. To reach fourth level takes 8 base elements and seven evolution oppurtunities, meaning that it is possible, with good planning, to bring all nine elements to fourth level. While it is theoretically possible to heavily overspecialise and gather 16 base elements of one type and 15 evolution opportunities for the same element, neither the 5th level of the element, nor the [Fatigued abilities always recover at dawn, unless you find a faster means of recovery.]}} '''Fatigued''' is an aspect that is applied to Elements of the Soul after use in most verbs - almost anything that uses an element will fatigue it. Elements recover from fatigue every morning at dawn, but they can also be recovered by paying [[Pence|Tuppence]] at [[The Sweet Bones]] with the fatigued card in the "Me" slot, which takes one minute, or by resting in an occupied [[Workstations#Beds|bed]] with a [[Beverage]] or a [[Basket of Clean Linen]], which takes one and a half minutes. To occupy a bed you need a non-fatigued soul card of the right principle for the bed. Be sure to take note of the time when deciding to recover a fatigued element this way; it would be wasteful to start recovery close to or after dusk, as you would likely reach morning before being able to use the recovered Element, at which point it would have recovered on its own. == Maladies == [[File:Malady.png|right|100px]] {{Quote|Something has snared or sickened my soul. [Soul cards can be Malady-tainted when you're exposed to dangerous influences - sometimes when you fail in a task. Maladies cannot be exhausted, but your soul is altered and weakened, and there can be serious consequences if they go untreated.]}} '''Malady''' is an aspect that is inflicted on Elements of the Soul cards in some circumstances. When a Malady that can affect this type of a soul card is with it in a process, the soul card becomes a distorted version of itself - it becomes Maladied. Unlike in [https://cultistsimulator.fandom.com/wiki/Cultist_Simulator_Wiki Cultist Simulator], Maladies do not decay and instead are static until the Malady is cured. There are a few ways a soul card can become maladied. [[Contamination|Contaminated]] books can cause maladies - each type of contamination can target two different elements. A soul card is also guaranteed to become maladied when failing to achieve mastery over the book if it's a not-upgraded soul card, and there is an element of the corresponding malady when all soul cards in the verb are exhausted. This will happen if the first soul card used and the Principle of its corresponding malady (see Types of Maladies, below) are both added in the attempt; e.g., Wist will be maladied if a Scale-bearing skill was used. This means that Chor, Fet, Phost and Shapt will always be maladied on failed reading attempt, while Ereb, Health, Trist and Wist can be preserved choosing the starting aspects accordingly. Keep in mind that a soul card does not become Maladied and Contaminated in one pass. It first needs to be come Maladied, and then it gets contaminated. Here is an example of when the soul element gets maladied. Imagine you try to master a Forge 12 book with Shapt and [[Chronsichord]]. In this case, Shapt doesn't get maladied because it got exhausted, and the Chronsichord got broken after the use - there was no Knock left in the verb at the time of malady-check. Shapt would get maladied if you added anything that has Knock and that does not get exhausted, like an item or a skill. Memories don't count since they are used up and are not present after the verb is done. Keep in mind that a random buff during the [[Opportunity|Opportunities]] can add Knock, and your Shapt could get maladied because of that. Elements of the Soul will also become maladied if a fatigued card is recovered or used for working in [[The Sweet Bones]] during [[Numa]] (except for [[Mettle]], which is immune and will be recovered normally). Swimming in [[Winter (Season)|Winter]] or Numa will cause a malady as well. Maladied soul cards do not fatigue. This can be utilised in some cases, such as when breaking down and re-learning skills in Numa, upgrading skills, [[Cooking]], cataloguing and reading books. === Curing Malady === Maladies can be cured by first occupying one of the many [[Workstations|beds]] found around the Hush House. Every bed has a specific [[Principles|Principle]] required before you can occupy it. You may only occupy one bed at a time and need to decamp from your current bed before moving to a different one, which takes 30 seconds. Occupying a bed takes 1 minute and 30 seconds. It is recommended that you occupy a bed that accepts the Principle required to cure your Malady. After occupying a bed, it will accept 5 new cards. An Element of the Soul, a [[Skills|Skill]], a [[Memory]], a Malady, and a [[Beverage]]. Put your Malady into the bed and fill the rest of the slots as required to meet the threshold to cure your Malady (starting at 5 of a specific Principle and increasing by 2 for each levelup for the maladied Element, up to 9). Every Malady will require a different Principle to be cured. A [[Restorative]] item must be supplied as well, such as a [[Beverage]] or [[Basket of Clean Linen]], or the game will try to initiate crafting instead of recovery. Curing a malady takes three minutes. You can cure two maladies at the time if your bed allows to fit two maladies and you satisfy the requirement to fix at least one of the maladies. === Types of Maladies === {| class="sortable mw-collapsible article-table" |+ style=text-align:left| !Malady !width=5%|Principle !Cured With !class=unsortable|Viable Beds !class=unsortable|Source !class=unsortable|Usable Desks !class=unsortable width=30%|Description |- |{{ES|Chor}}:

Aspects.text:
{{Stub}} {{Tocright}}
Almost everything in ''[[Book of Hours]]'' has '''Aspects'''. These are markers in the description box that can tell you more about the selected thing, such as its [[Principles]], what it is made of, what it can do, or how it works. Below are lists of Aspects, grouped by category. Toggle All {{Clear}} ==Principles== Principles are a type of Aspect applied to most items. For more information on Principles, [[Principles|see the dedicated page]]. ==Food and Drink== {| class="article-table mw-collapsible mw-collapsed sortable" style="width: 100%" id="mw-customcollapsible-principles" |+ style=text-align:left|Food and Drink Toggle |- ! [Use this at a fireplace or kitchen range.] |- | [[Cooking Ingredient]] |This will be part of something greater. [When you have HOUSE OF LIGHT, Cooking Ingredients can be used for cooking and making food in the kitchen.] |- | [[Egg]] || 'When an egg is not dead, something may emerge. When an egg is dead, something may be placed within.' - Thirza Blake, seventh Librarian of Hush House |- | [[First Course]] || Generally eaten as a light snack, or before a Main Course. |- | [[Fruit]] || The womb of a plant? |- | [[Main Course]] || The heart and mainstay of a good meal. |- | [[Pudding]] || 'If you don't eat yer meat, you can't have any pudding. [The most likely ingredients are beeswax and herbs; but to confound villagers and visitors, leave a meaningful pause before the word 'suitable.'] |- | [[Languages|Language]] || A skill that can be used to read particular books, among other much less important things. |- | [[Birdsong]] || Music, riddles, miscellanea. 'Less a wisdom, more a body of gossip hallowed by accretion,' a sniffy scholar once remarked. |- | [[The Bosk]] || The Wisdom of the primaeval wood; rarely written, often felt. |- | [[Horomachistry]] || This Wisdom is concerned with the laws (and disagreements) of the Hours (and their emanations). |- | [[Hushery]] || The Great Art of Hushery understands the beauty of silence, and of its sundering. |- | [[Illumination]] || Illuminates purify the self and its surroundings. Eventually, they often cease to see any difference between the two. |- | [[Ithastry]] || Alchemy, metallurgy, pyrotechnics: Ithastry is sometimes called the Art that Alters. |- | [[Nyctodromy]] || 'Travelling at night is neither faster nor safer. That's why we do it.' Knowledge of the ways and byways of the transmundane. |- | [[Preservation]] || Healing and restoration. An unglamorous Wisdom, at least to those who never wonder how the world still exists. |- | [[Skolekosophy]] || The study of things that should not be studied. Some call this a Wisdom. |- | Committed || You've determined where this skill should belong, in the wide kingdoms of understanding. [This skill is now committed to the Wisdom marked on the card.] |} [[Category:Aspect]]

Crafting.title: Crafting
Crafting.text:
{{Tocright}} == Summary == '''Crafting''' can be done at any [[Workstations|Workstation]] in [[Hush House]] and allows you to create [[Ink|Inks]], [[Tool|Tools]], [[Beverage|Beverages]], and many other useful [[Thing|Things]] to assist in Mastering [[Readable]]s - [[Codex|Codices]], [[Reels of Film]], [[Scroll]]s, [[Tablet]]s and [[Phonograph Records]], and restoring [[Hush House]] to its former glory. With the ''[[House of Light]]'' DLC, you can also craft [[Manuscript]]s which you can use to provide the knowledge sought by [[Visitors]] instead of Readables. Crafting can be a little confusing at times, as the type of Workstation ([[Workstations#Desks|Desks]], [[Workstations#Shrines|Shrines]], [[Instrumental Workstations|Instruments]], etc.) does not matter. What Crafting comes down to is the [[Skills|Skill]] being used and the level of the Challenge which is determined by the Power of the respective [[Principles|Principle]] you are attempting to Craft with. So, you can Craft a [[Memory]] in a [[Workstations#Kitchen Ranges|Kitchen Range]], or a Beverage at the [[Telescope]], as long as you can meet all the requirements for that recipe. ==Challenges== Challenge thresholds are every five levels of the respective power and divides all recipes into three types: Prentice, Scholar, and Keeper-level recipes. An example: if you use [[Putrefactions & Calcinations]] and obtain a {{Lore|Moon}} Power-level of 5-9, you will create the Ink [[Catwink]]. If you are able to get your power to 10 and add a [[Liquid]], you will instead create the more powerful Ink, [[Asimel]]. {| class="article-table" !Name !Description |- |style="white-space:nowrap|[[File:Prentice.png|frameless|64px|Prentice|link=]] Prentice-level |''The simpler techniques require skill alone. [For basic recipes, provide five degrees of the relevant Aspect]'' |- |style="white-space:nowrap|[[File:Scholar.png|frameless|64px|Scholar|link=]] Scholar-level |''More advanced techniques require power as well as significant skill. [For more challenging recipes, provide ten degrees of the relevant Aspect. Every Scholar-level recipe also needs an ingredient with a specific Aspect.]'' |- |style="white-space:nowrap|[[File:Keeper.png|frameless|64px|Keeper|link=]] Keeper-level |''Available only to the wise, the great, or the most fortunate of idiots. [For the most challenging recipes, provide fifteen degrees of the relevant Aspect. The Tree of Wisdoms.title: The Tree of Wisdoms
The Tree of Wisdoms.text: {{Tocright}} {{quote|Scholars and Adepts recognise nine wisdoms...though they disagree where one wisdom ends and another begins. Something for me to think about.}} '''The Tree of Wisdoms''' is one of the main gameplay mechanics in ''The Book of Hours.'' The Librarian commits [[Skills|skills]] of the relevant aspects to each of the nine branches: [[Illumination]], [[Hushery]], [[Nyctodromy]], [[Skolekosophy]], [[The Bosk]], [[Preservation]], [[Birdsong]], [[Horomachistry]], and [[Ithastry]]. Each wisdom is connected to three [[Principles]], and one of the three categories of Arts: Bright Arts, Night Arts, and Arts Unregarded. Each skill can be committed to one of two specific branches of the tree, which upon doing so grants a corresponding [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]]. Keep in mind that for the same slot on the tree, different skills might give different Elements of the Soul. Having committed the skill to the tree, it can be used to [[Elements of the Soul#Evolution|evolve]] two of those same Element of the Soul cards into one upgraded card of the next level. Evolution requires the use of an appropriate [[Workstations|Workstation]] with: * 2 soul cards of the same level that you wish to upgrade; and, * The skill that you wish to use; and, * The "Evolve via..." aspect: provided either by the Workstation itself, or by a particular [[Memory]]. With the use of an appropriate Memory, or the innate "Evolve via..." aspect of a particular Workstation, all [[Skill|skill]] cards can be used to upgrade soul cards, no matter where in the '''Tree''' you have committed them. == Wisdoms and Elements of the Soul == {| class="wikitable sortable" |+ style="white-space:nowrap; text-align:left" | Wisdom details ! Principles.title: Principles
Principles.text:
The '''Principles''' are 13 unique [[Aspects]] that embody the archetypal characteristics, ideas, or influences that underpin the entirety of the invisible arts. Power can be drawn from the veneration of a Principle, or through the interaction of multiple Principles. Each Hour can be said to personify at least one Principle, and typically no more than three. Each Principle has [[Skills]] associated with it, and each Skill can have two different Principles - a primary one, which has a power of two of that Principle, and a secondary one, which has a power of one of a different Principle. {| class="sortable article-table" ! scope="col"| Name !class=unsortable|Description !class=unsortable|Elements

The Beginning.title: The Beginning
The Beginning.text:
{{Quote|
Brancrug, March 7th, 1936,

'There has been no Librarian at Hush House since the fire - seven years now. Suitable candidates are very difficult to find, but perhaps we have found one in you. Take care on your journey - the seas around Brancrug are treacherous...'

There was a storm. It smashed the ship like an egg. But I seized this book as the sea seized me... then the sea brought me here to Brancrug. And Brancrug is where I wanted to be. But it's hard to remember why. What else did I lose in the storm?}}
The game begins with the [[Librarians|Librarian]] washed up on the shores of [[St. Brandan's Cove|St Brandan's Cove]] after a storm, half-drowned, but in possession of a [[Journal|A Drowned Book]]. [[Consider]]ing the [[Memory: Storm|Memory of the storm]] with the help of the book will start the soul creation phase. == Soul Creation == The Librarian will be given two chances to select the [[Elements of the Soul|Elements of their Soul]]. The elements that are not selected will be discarded, but they can be gained later on. Firstly, the Librarian may choose one of {{ES|Shapt}}, {{ES|Chor}}, or {{ES|Fet}}. Secondly, the Librarian may choose one of {{ES|Mettle}}, {{ES|Wist}}, {{ES|Phost}}, or {{ES|Ereb}}. === Journal === The Librarian possesses A Drowned Book, which will later become [[Journals|one of nine possible Journals]], depending on which Elements of the Soul were chosen. The Journal will dictate some of the available [[Endings]] for this playthrough. Below is a table showing which Element selections will lead to which Librarian: {| class="fandom-table" |- |[[File:Element_of_the_Soul.png|20px]] [[Elements of the Soul|Element]] |{{ES|Chor}} |{{ES|Fet}} |{{ES|Shapt}} |- |{{ES|Ereb}} |[[File:Memories.artist.png|20px]] [[The Artist]] |[[File:Memories.artist.png|20px]] [[The Artist]] |[[File:Memories.artist.png|20px]] [[The Artist]] |- |{{ES|Mettle}} |[[File:Memories.executioner.png|20px]] [[The Executioner]] |[[File:Memories.revolutionary.png|20px]] [[The Revolutionary]] |[[File:Memories.archaeologist.png|20px]] [[The Archaeologist]] |- |{{ES|Wist}} |[[File:Memories.symurgist.png|20px]] [[The Symurgist]] |[[File:Memories.magnate.png|20px]] [[The Magnate]] |[[File:Memories.archaeologist.png|20px]] [[The Archaeologist]] |- |{{ES|Phost}} |[[File:Memories.prodigal.png|20px]] [[The Prodigal]] |[[File:Memories.cartographer.png|20px]] [[The Cartographer]] |[[File:Memories.twiceborn.png|20px]] [[The Twice-Born]] |} ==Shelter== After choosing, a new Verb will appear - [[Talk]], along with a [[Memory: Fear]], as well as [[An Old Friend's Address]]. The Librarian can now use a Soul Element to seek help. A [[The Fisherman|Fisherman]] from the nearby village of [[Brancrug Village|Brancrug]] will answer the calls for help, but not without first confirming someone in the village can vouch for them. With his suspicions allayed, the Fisherman can lead the Librarian to Brancrug Village. Depending on the choices made in the [[The Beginning#Soul Creation|Soul Creation]] process, the Librarian will have access to one of three different locations - [[The Smithy]], [[The Rectory]] or [[Mrs and Mr Kille]]. Interacting with that location using the Address and the Half-Drowned (or Freezing) {{ES|Health}} Element will start the game proper.

Talk.title: Talk
Talk.text:
[[File:Talk icon.png|right]] {{Quote|Speak to visitors, assistants, strangers, friends... To someone else, usually.}}
The '''Talk''' Verb on the left side of the screen can be used to communicate with [[Assistants]], [[Visitors]], and [[Beast|Beasts]]. Talking to Beasts will generate various [[Memory|Memories]]. Talking to a hungry Beast requires food, so that they can be fed. Talking to Visitors allows you to provide a consult, discuss an [[Incident]], or obtain a lesson in a [[Skills#Languages|Language]] you don't know yet. Some Visitors also have hidden interactions with [[Readable|Books]] they have written or have a connection to. To hire an unusual helper, they must be spoken to and provided with [[Pence|24p]]. Talking to Assistants with nothing in the "Collaborate" slot will produce a Memory. Which Memories can be generated depends on the Assistant. Talking to assistants with an [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]], [[Beverage]], [[Sustenance]], [[Memory]], or [[Tools|Tool]] will increase their [[Principles]] for the rest of the day. Some assistants also have unique collaborations such as [[Wood]], [[Flower]]s, [[Candle]]s, and [[Fabric]]. [[Category:Verb]]

Garden.title: Garden
Garden.text:
Garden is a type of [[Workstation]]note that while it can't be used for crafting, it is technically still called "Workstation" in-game, accepting any {{Lore|Nectar}} skill and a [[Heart]] [[Principles|Principle]] effort, giving a [[Flower]] or [[Sustenance]] in return. It's also a common theme for locations providing those Workstations. The results of collection vary strongly depending on season, and can provide exceptionally strong items during [[Numa]]. Beehive.title: Beehive
Beehive.text:
{{Workstation
|image1=[[File:Beehive.png]]
|principles={{Lore|Nectar}}, {{Lore|Scale}}
|location=[[Kitchen Garden]]}}
{{Quote|Bees, like librarians, are not to be trifled with.}}
__NOTOC__
The '''Beehive''' is a [[Gathering|Gathering station]], located in the [[Kitchen Garden]].

==Slots==
* <abbr title="Also required by the slots.">'''Principles of this workstation'''</abbr>: {{lore|Nectar}}, {{lore|Scale}}
* '''Effort''':
** '''Essential''': [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]]
** '''Forbidden''': [[Elements of the Soul#Fatigue|Fatigued]], [[Elements of the Soul#Maladies|Malady]]
* '''Knowledge''':
** '''Essential''': [[Skill]]
** '''Required''': [[The Affair of the God in the Wood|Lyterion]]

Per the Quotes section below, the Librarian will not begin gathering from the hive at night. [[Health]] is the only Element of the Soul that qualifies for gathering.

==Outcomes==
Gathering at the Beehive draws a single card from one of the [[Decks]] below, according to the [[Season]].

[[Honey]] and [[Beeswax]] can be obtained in Spring and Summer, and [[Memory|Memories]] in Autumn and Winter. In [[Numa]], something more special might be gathered: [[Cuckoo-Honey]].

===Decks===
{{#lst:Decks|beehive}}
With the ''[[House of Light]]'' DLC, specific choices for the [[Further Stories]] of [[The Affair of the God in the Wood]] will change the Beehive gathering deck, permitting it to occasionally produce Cuckoo-Honey even outside of Numa.
{{#lst:Decks|beehive_liselotte}}

Beachcombing.title: Beachcombing
Beachcombing.text:
{{Workstation |image1=[[File:Crowcross_Sands.png]] |principles={{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Moon}}, {{Lore|Rose}} |location=[[Crowcross Sands]]}} {{quote|Take a long walk along the ocean's side. If I know what to look for, I might find something the ocean has forsaken.}} __NOTOC__'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Gathering]] station, located in [[Crowcross Sands]]. ==Gathering== You can use an [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]] and a [[Skill]] ({{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Moon}}, {{Lore|Rose}}) to obtain an item.
The possible reward depends on the [[Season]]. You can only gather during the day. {{#lst:Decks|beach}} {| class="mw-collapsed mw-collapsible article-table" |+ Quotes !Action !Quote |- |Trying to Gather at Night||This is a bad way to find things and a good way to drown. I should come back tomorrow. |- |Gathering in Normal Seasons||What has the sea ceded today? |- |Gathering End||Sea-strewn salt-snared stuff. |- |Gathering in Numa||The Numa-fog is thick here. |- |Gathering in Numa End||Tide-wracked treasures. |- |Finding the Hush House Key||Something half-buried in the sand... A familiar iron key has washed up on the beach. |} ==Trivia == *Like all [[Gathering]] activities, the item is drawn from a deck that is only reset when exhausted. Seasons changing switches which deck is being drawn from. Some items appear multiple times in a deck, making them more likely to be drawn from a full deck, but eventually the deck is emptied, and every item will be drawn before already-drawn items become available again. Percentages are approximate for a full deck. [[Category:Gathering]]

A Walk on the Moor.title: A Walk on the Moor
A Walk on the Moor.text:
{{Workstation |image1=[[File:Moor.png]] |principles={{Lore|Heart}}, {{Lore|Rose}}, {{Lore|Scale}}}} {{Quote|Clamber up into the long reaches of the moors behind the village. Lean into the wind's fluttering fist. If I know what to look for, I might find something among the rocks.}}
South-east of [[Brancrug Village]], the Librarian can go for '''A Walk on the Moor'''. This is a [[Gathering]] action that can yield various [[Material]]s and a chance of finding the [[Dog]]. ==Gathering== An [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]] and a [[Skills|Skill]] must be provided to gather from the moor. It is only possible to gather during the day and requires 90 seconds. The following table gives an overview of what can be gathered in each [[Season]]. {{#lst:Decks|moor}} {| class="mw-collapsed mw-collapsible article-table" |+Quotes !Action !Quote |- |Trying to Gather at Night||''At night? I'll fall off something, into something, or both. Tomorrow is soon enough.'' |- |Gathering in Spring||''The gorse is bright on the land's nape.'' |- |Gathering in Summer||''The wind's almost warm.'' |- |Gathering in Autumn||''The last leaves toss and scutter.'' |- |Gathering in Winter||''Rime rims the moor-tarns.'' |- |Gathering End||''Unexpected finds in the folds of earth and sky.'' |- |Gathering in Numa||''Is it wise to walk on the moors in this season? Let's find out.'' |- |Gathering in Numa End||''Much is lost, but much remains...'' |} [[Category:Gathering]]

The possible reward depends on the [[Season]]. You can only gather during the day. {{#lst:Decks|nests}} {| class="mw-collapsed mw-collapsible article-table" |+ Quotes !Action !Quote |- |Trying to Gather at Night || ''I am quite clearly not intending to climb the cliffs of Brancrug Isle
in the middle of the night. I'm just speculating about the possibility.'' |- |Gather in Spring || ''The birds are furiously vigilant.'' |- |Gather in Summer || ''The sea rolls below.'' |- |Gather in Autumn || ''Fierce yellow eyes watch my every move.'' |- |Gather in Winter || ''The wind is bitter today.'' |- |Gather in Numa || ''What pilgrims pass in Numa?'' |- |Gathering End ||''Scraps from the isle's edge.'' |- |Gathering End Numa || ''Much is lost, but much remains...'' |- |Hush House Key||''A metallic wink of light... A familiar iron key is caught in a crevice.'' |} [[Category:Gathering]]

The Sea-Caves.title: The Sea-Caves
The Sea-Caves.text:
{{Workstation |image1=[[File:The Sea-Caves.png]] |principles={{Lore|Moon}}, {{Lore|Scale}} |location=[[Sea-Caves]]}} {{Quote|Splash cautiously through the shallower tunnels.}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' are a [[Gathering]] station. They are located in the [[Sea-Caves]]. ==Gathering== You can use an [[Elements of the Soul|Element of the Soul]] and a [[Skill]] ({{Lore|Moon}}, {{Lore|Scale}}) to obtain an item.
The possible reward depends on the [[Season]]. You can only gather during the day. {{#lst:Decks|caves}} {| class="mw-collapsed mw-collapsible article-table" |+ Quotes !Action !Quote |- |Trying to Gather at Night || ''If I go to the caves at night, either I'll drown when the tide
comes in, or I'll drown when it doesn't.'' |- |Gather in Normal Seasons || ''Echoes in the endless night...'' |- |Gather in Numa || ''What has Numa brought?'' |- |Gathering End ||''Gleanings from the darkness.'' |- |Gathering End Numa || ''Much is lost, but much remains...'' |- |Hush House Key|| ''A metallic wink of light...
A familiar iron key lies in a shallow rock-pool.'' |} [[Category:Gathering]]

Fekri's Herbary.title: Fekri's Herbary
Fekri's Herbary.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=Fekri's Herbary|mystery=6|category=Book|tally_price=3|language=[[Aramaic]]|type=[[Readable]], [[Thing]], [[Codex]]|principles={{Lore|Nectar}}|Period=[[Baronial]]|image1=Fekri's Herbary.png}}

'''Fekri's Herbary''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Nectar}} principle.

==Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:{{quote|The early wisdom of Ehsan Fekri, at that point a travelling healer, much later the Secretary Salvant of the Curia of the Isle.|}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|As a skaptodon, Ehsan may consume only that which is found in the earth, so he's best with root-lore...|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Ehsan identifies a pale sea-weed found on the beaches of Cornwall as a useful source of Rose and Winter aspect. His tone here is a little guilty - perhaps because he's showing an interest in sea-produce, which might be thought unwise for a skaptodon, and perhaps because his proposal to name it 'Eva's Locks' suggests a tiny crush on the Pale Lady of Brancrug...|I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates [[Herbs & Infusions|Lesson: Herbs & Infusions]]. Reading always provides [[Memory: Satisfaction|Satisfaction]].

== Additional interactions ==
If [[Mr Ehsan Fekri|Ehsan Fekhri]] is shown this book while visiting, he will give an additional [[Herbs & Infusions|Lesson: Herbs & Infusions]]. Unlike other visitor interactions, he will not leave afterward.[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Nectar]]
[[Category:Baronial]]

Just Verse.title: Just Verse

Musgrave's Sketches.title: Musgrave's Sketches
Musgrave's Sketches.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=Musgrave's Sketches|mystery=8|type=[[Codex]]|tally_price=2|image1=[[File:MusgravesSketches.png|thumb]]|principles=[[Winter]]|Period=[[Curia]]|memory=[[Bittersweet Certainty]]|skill=[[Sights & Sensations]]}}'''Musgrave's Sketches''' is a [[book]] of the [[Winter]] principle.

== Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:{{Quote|Musgrave, 4th Baron Brancrug, was widely mocked as 'the Bleating Baron' and 'the Lamb Dewulf', but these sketches reveal a complex, sombre inner life.|}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|"Art begins in Colours; grows Dappled; finally is either mostly Darkness, or mostly Light."|I'm Reading...}}After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|Musgrave discusses the temptation of the perfectly minimal 'palest painting'. He has so far managed to resist this temptation, but does guiltily describe success in using Sights and Sensations with Winter-aspect to create first a 'chilly elixir' from flowers, which he believes he can refine further into a 'final pigment'...|I've Read...}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of the book generates 2x [[Sights & Sensations|Lesson: Sights & Sensations]]. Reading it always provides [[Bittersweet Certainty|Memory: Bittersweet Certainty]].
[[Category:Book]]

Key of Night.title: Key of Night

The Book of Thrones.title: The Book of Thrones
The Book of Thrones.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=The Book of Thrones|mystery=12|category=[[Readable]]|tally_price=2|language=[[Phrygian]]|type=[[Codex]]|principles=[[Edge]]|image1=The Book of Thrones.png|skill=[[Auroral Contemplations]]|memory=[[Memory: Contradiction|Contradiction]]|period=[[Curia]]}}

'''''The Book of Thrones''''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Edge}} principle written in [[Phrygian]] by [[Alexander Peterhans]]. 

==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:

{{quote|A legend of the Shadowless Empire, transcribed by Alexander Peterhans from annals at a secret shrine in Anatolia.|}}

Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|In 'the first and greatest history', a subject of the Shadowless Empire of Persia travels to the West, to the kingdom of the Perseids. There he becomes a protégé of the tutelary Perseid deity, the Scarred Man who lives in the dark. He returns after seven years to put his skills at the service of the Shadowless Empire, becoming their Golden General... |I'm Reading...}}

After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|After many years of peace, the heirs of the Perseids move against the King of Kings and the Shadowless Empire. The Golden General will not take arms against the blood of his mentor, until the King of Kings whispers 'a great secret of betrayal' in his ear. He breaks his sword, forswears his oath to both the Empire and the Scarred Man, and enters 'the Temple behind the World', leaving his life behind. |I've Read...}}

==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book provides [[Auroral Contemplations|Lesson: Auroral Contemplations]] x2. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Contradiction]].

==Trivia==

* The act of shattering his sword (an act that invokes the Forge principle) caused the man to ascend as the Hour known as [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/The_Lionsmith the Lionsmith].
* The ''Scarred man'' is a reference to [https://secret-histories.fandom.com/wiki/The_Colonel the Colonel].

[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Edge]]

The Fallen Cross.title: The Fallen Cross
The Fallen Cross.text:
{{Book_(BoH)|title1=The Fallen Cross|mystery=6|type=[[Codex]]|tally_price=3|image1=The Fallen Cross.png|principles=[[Sky]]|Period=[[Baronial]]|memory=[[Memory: Regret]]|skill=[[Ouranoscopy]]}}'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[book]] of the [[Sky]].

== Description ==
Selecting the book provides the following description:{{Quote|In which [[Julian Coseley]], magus, immortal, occasional anarchist, argues that through language the Carapace Cross decayed to seed the lives of our ancestors.|Description}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|"Speech is a Wound; Silence is Silver. There is no Silver Door, nor can there be, even in the Moon's House…"|I'm Reading...}}After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|"Without Language there can be no Wordes. Without Wordes there can be no Message. But only in Silence can there be no Error; and Lo, even in that beginning, in that First of Messages, an Error. Thus did we enter the House."|I've Read}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of the book generates [[Ouranoscopy|Lesson: Ouranoscopy]] and [[Memory: Regret]]. Reading it again provides [[Memory: Regret]].
[[Category:Book]]

The Lion and the Glass.title: The Lion and the Glass
The Lion and the Glass.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=The Lion and the Glass|mystery=12|category=[[Readable]]|tally_price=5|language=[[Deep Mandaic]]|type=[[Codex]]|principles={{Lore|Sky}}|image1=[[File:TheLionandtheGlass.png|thumb]]|period=[[Dawn Period|Dawn]]}}

''The Lion and the Glass'' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} principle written by [[Omar, the Blaze]].
==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:{{quote|An early work by Omar the Blaze, a novice or apprentice at the Labyrinth of Lions.|}}Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Omar describes his progress in mastering the Illumination techniques that rely on the 'Truths of Glass'.|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Omar divulges a glassmaker's secret: that 'the Ichor Vitreous' can be filtered and enriched (with enough Lantern Aspect) to become the ink ashartine, which resists untruths…|I've Read...}}

== Rewards ==
Completing mastery of the book generates 2x [[Glaziery & Lightsmithing|Lesson: Glaziery & Lightsmithing]]. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Revelation|Memory: Revelation]].
[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Sky]]

The Focus of Amber.title: The Focus of Amber
The Focus of Amber.text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=The Focus of Amber|mystery=16|category=Readable|tally_price=5|language=[[Deep Mandaic]]|type=Codex|principles={{Lore|Sky}}|Period=[[Dawn]]|image1=The Focus of Amber.png}}'''The Focus of Amber''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Sky}} principle written by [[Omar, the Blaze]].
==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{Quote|Omar, the Blaze, spent seven years manning a lighthouse in Tyre, in atonement for the extinguishing of a sacred flame. By the end of his stint, he was so terrified of fire that he could not stand to share a room with a candle. This work was written in partial penance.|}}


Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|Omar claims that the Hour called Watchman is both a god-who-was-flesh - an Hour who was mortal - and also a god-from-Light - an Hour who descended from the Glory - but adds, finally, that the Watchman's origin is triple, and that 'in essence, he is Amber.'|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:
{{Quote|The Watchman, according to Omar, was once another Hour entirely, who ascended into the Glory to escape efforts by other Hours to send him to Nowhere. It may be that Omar's sense of persecution creeps into the narrative at this point: certainly it grows less coherent, and the last part is devoted to attempts to prove that eyes, eggs and the Sun are all in some sense conjunct.|I've Read...}}
==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates 3 [[Glaziery & Lightsmithing|Lesson: Glaziery & Lightsmithing]]. Reading it always provides [[Memory: Revelation]].
[[Category:Book]]
[[Category:Sky]]

The Radical Measure (Glossed).title: The Radical Measure (Glossed)
The Radical Measure (Glossed).text:
{{Book (BoH)|title1=The Radical Measure (Glossed)|mystery={{Lore|Rose}} 12|category=Book|tally_price=1|language=N/A|type=Codex|image1=The Radical Measure (Glossed).png}}'''The Radical Measure (Glossed)''' is a [[Books|book]] of the {{Lore|Rose}} principle written by [[Dr Arun Peel]] and edited by [[Christopher Illopoly]].
==Description==
Selecting the book provides the following description:
{{quote|The original 'Radical Measures' was a manifesto for experimental poetry with occult properties, written in the nineteenth century by Dr Arun Peel. The original is notoriously incoherent - much later, Christopher Illopoly took on the task of editing and glossing it. He has taken some liberties, but the updated version is generally well regarded.|}}
Upon choosing to master the book, either at a [[Desk]] or with the [[Consider]] verb, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|'The Hours have little time for poetry,' Dr Peel avers, 'but they have a tremendous amount of time for poets.' (Illopoly has added a note suggesting this should in fact be be 'the most tremendous time with poets'.)|I'm Reading...}}
After completing mastery, the Librarian learns:{{Quote|'As the Rose opens,' Dr Peel explains, 'Enduring Memory opens to the Horizon. This is a way of saying something that cannot otherwise be said, and is best only written with one's eyes firmly closed.' (Illopoly's gloss reads: Horizon-Sight synthesis method. Reverse procedure, with Knock, to elaborate Gervinite in the Chronsicord mode.)|I've Read...}}
==Rewards==
Completing mastery of the book generates 2 [[Preliminal Meter|Lesson: Preliminal Meter]] and [[Memory: Pattern]].

Talking to Dr. Arun Peel about the book (talk with no subject, give him the book afterwards) will result in him paying a Silver Spinatria for studying the book.
